Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation to develop or identify and implement a training program for transportation sector employees on the identification and reporting of suspected human trafficking victims; requiring transportation sector employers to certify by January 1, 2027, and each year thereafter that certain employees have completed the training program; requiring new employees to receive training within 90 days of hiring; removing civil and criminal liability for reporting of suspected trafficking; etc.
Title: Department of Transportation - Human Trafficking Awareness, Training, and Response (See Someone, Save Someone Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to develop or identify and implement a human trafficking training program. Covers State employees and contractors working at transit stations, airports, port facilities, highway rest stops, or transit services. Mandates employers to certify employee training completion annually by January 1, 2027, and train new hires within 90 days. Requires employers to establish reporting procedures and implement a human trafficking prevention policy. Protects employers and employees from civil or criminal liability for reporting or responding in good faith. Requires the Department to mandate frequent English and Spanish public service announcements at specified transportation facilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: State employees working at transit stations, airports, port facilities, or highway rest stops; State and contractual transit service workers; transportation sector employers; human trafficking victims
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $262,500 in FY 2026 and $137,500 in FY 2027 for online course development and employee shift-coverage overtime. State revenues are unaffected, and local government operations and finances experience no material effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing, identifying, and administering the human trafficking training program, setting employer certification requirements, and overseeing public service announcements at transportation facilities.

As a modal administration of MDOT providing transit service and operating transit stations, MTA employees represent the primary workforce affected, and MTA is projected to incur costs to develop the online training curriculum and cover employee shift coverage.
MAA operates state airports whose personnel must undergo the required human trafficking awareness training and where safety public service announcements must be broadcast.
MPA operates state port facilities where qualifying employees must complete human trafficking identification and reporting training and where safety announcements must be implemented.
MDOT SHA oversees highway operations, including state highway rest stops where qualifying personnel must receive the training and safety announcements must be displayed or broadcast.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates reporting procedures that connect suspected trafficking incidents to designated regional navigators, a specialized victim-services network funded and overseen by GOCPP under the Safe Harbor program.

Synopsis: Clarifying the definition of "physical therapist assistant" as used in the Maryland Physical Therapy Act to mean an individual licensed by the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners; increasing the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9; and requiring the Board to send renewal notices to licensees by electronic means, rather than first-class mail, unless the licensee requests to receive the renewal notice by first-class mail.
Title: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Clarifies the definition of physical therapist assistant to require licensure by the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners. Expands the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from eight members to nine members. Adds a second licensed physical therapist assistant practicing limited physical therapy in Maryland to the Board. Requires the Board to send license renewal notices to licensees by electronic means instead of first-class mail. Mandates first-class mail notices upon licensee request or when electronic notices are returned as undeliverable.
responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapist assistants, and consumer members
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal 2026, Board special fund expenditures decrease by up to $3,500 annually due to estimated mailing savings of $5,000 partially offset by $1,500 in compensation for the additional board member. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the board's composition, updates its licensing definitions and notification procedures, and has a direct fiscal impact on its special funds.
The bill expands the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9, requiring the Governor to appoint an additional licensed physical therapist assistant member.

The Office of Appointments vets, processes, and recommends candidates for appointment by the Governor to state boards and commissions, including the additional seat created on the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a restriction on land use that increases the cost of installing a solar collector system by at least 5% over a certain cost or that reduces the efficiency of the system by at least 10% under a certain energy generation level; authorizing a community association to impose certain restrictions on the installation of solar collector systems in common areas or common elements; authorizing a community association to install a solar collector system in common areas or common elements under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Restrictions on Use - Solar Collector Systems - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Renewable Energy Sources -see also- Geotherm; Solar; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits land use restrictions that increase solar collector system installation costs by at least 5% over initial projected costs. Prohibits restrictions that reduce solar collector system energy generation by at least 10% below initial projections. Requires property owners to document unreasonable restrictions using a qualified independent solar panel design specialist. Authorizes community associations to prohibit or reasonably restrict solar collector installations in common areas or common elements. Authorizes community association boards of directors to install solar collector systems in common areas or common elements.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: property owners, community associations (including condominium and homeowners associations), and independent solar panel design specialists
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially impact State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration advises on renewable energy policy and promotes solar energy adoption across the state, making statutory changes regarding solar collector system restrictions and installation standards relevant to its core mission.

Disputes arising between property owners and community associations regarding covenants and unreasonable restrictions on solar collector systems are subject to adjudication in the Maryland court system.

The statute contains a specific exemption for historic properties listed or determined eligible by the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is administered within the Department of Planning.

Synopsis: Altering certain definitions related to the Food Resiliency Council; defining what constitutes "healthy food priority areas" as predominantly lower-income areas that have limited access to retail outlets that sell affordable, healthy foods; defining "wasted food" as food not used for its intended purpose; requiring the Council to make recommendations to increase the availability of local foods, create market opportunities for Maryland food businesses, and expand access to small scale food production infrastructure; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Food System Resiliency Council - Definitions and Reports

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Alters the duties and reporting requirements of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council. Defines healthy food priority areas as lower-income areas with limited access to affordable, healthy food retail. Defines wasted food as unused food managed through donation, animal feed, composting, digestion, or disposal. Requires the Council to develop policy recommendations targeting healthy food priority areas and wasted food reduction. Incorporates local food production, procurement, and market expansion strategies into the Council's ongoing policy recommendations. Requires the Council to include appropriate policy and legislative changes in its annual reports.
responsible_party: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: residents in healthy food priority areas, Maryland food businesses, local food council organizations, and public schools and institutions procuring local food
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), which provides staff support and operational oversight for the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory definitions, duties, ongoing goals, and reporting requirements of the Food System Resiliency Council, a state-mandated advisory body.

Synopsis: Repealing the June 30, 2025, termination date for certain provisions of law related to referrals to and reimbursement of specialists and nonphysician specialists who are not part of a carrier's provider panel; prohibiting certain carriers from imposing utilization review requirements other than would be required if the covered benefit was provided by a provider on the carrier's provider panel under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Access to Nonparticipating Providers - Referrals, Additional Assistance, and Coverage

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the termination date for laws governing referrals to and coverage of nonparticipating specialists. Requires health insurance carriers to assist members in identifying and arranging out-of-network mental health or substance use disorder coverage. Prohibits carriers from imposing utilization review requirements exceeding those applied to in-network providers on approved referrals. Mandates that covered mental health or substance use disorder services remain at in-network cost-sharing for the treatment plan's duration. Incorporates regulatory appointment waiting time and travel distance standards into referral access determinations for behavioral health services.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, insured individuals seeking specialized or mental health and substance use disorder care, and nonparticipating specialists and nonphysician specialists.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Workload on the administration is expected to be handled with existing budgeted resources. No impact on local government finances or the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator responsible for enforcing the Insurance Article, reviewing carrier form filings, and ensuring compliance with the referral and coverage requirements for nonparticipating mental health and substance use disorder providers.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and was evaluated for potential fiscal impact regarding health benefit plan mandates, though no fiscal impact was found.
MDH licenses behavioral health programs recognized as nonphysician specialists under the statute and oversees statewide mental health and substance use disorder policies.

Synopsis: Authorizing the officers and employees of the Field Enforcement Division of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to issue a citation for a violation of §10-108 of the Criminal Law Article; prohibiting the sale or distribution of certain products that contain tetrahydrocannabinol or are advertised as containing tetrahydrocannabinol; authorizing the Executive Director of the Commission to seize, destroy, or confiscate a certain unlawful product; etc.
Title: Cannabis - Sale and Distribution - Tetrahydrocannabinol Offenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits the sale or distribution of products containing tetrahydrocannabinol that violate statutory potency, packaging, or labeling requirements. Prohibits selling or distributing products advertised as containing tetrahydrocannabinol amounts exceeding statutory limits. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to seize, destroy, or confiscate unlawful products. Establishes that displaying or offering tetrahydrocannabinol for sale is prima facie evidence of selling without a license. Subjects unlicensed violators to misdemeanor fines up to $5,000 and licensed cannabis businesses to administrative disciplinary action. Authorizes Field Enforcement Division officers to issue citations for distributing certain tetrahydrocannabinol products to individuals under age 21.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: Licensed cannabis businesses, unlicensed sellers and distributors of cannabis or tetrahydrocannabinol products, and adult consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2026 from District Court fines. The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, the Maryland Cannabis Administration, and the District Court can handle implementation with existing budgeted resources. No material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA), as it authorizes MCA to take disciplinary action against licensed cannabis businesses that violate new restrictions concerning tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) potency, packaging, labeling, and advertising.

The bill creates new misdemeanor offenses charged by citation for non-licensees, alters evidentiary standards regarding prima facie evidence of selling THC, and impacts District Court caseloads and fine collection.
The bill references ongoing coordination between the Field Enforcement Division and the Office of the Comptroller regarding enforcement of laws related to cannabis taxes and unlicensed distribution.
As a primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is consulted and impacted by changes to criminal law enforcement regarding citations and unlicensed THC distribution.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal citations and misdemeanor offenses for the illicit sale of THC products, which may impact caseload intake and representation across the justice system.

Synopsis: Authorizing the formation of limited worker cooperative associations; and establishing rules and procedures for the formation, governance, conversion, and dissolution of limited worker cooperative associations.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Limited Worker Cooperative Associations - Authorization (Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Association Act)

bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland limited liability companies to elect status as limited worker cooperative associations or collective worker cooperatives. Establishes statutory procedures governing association formation, governance, capital accounts, profit allocations, conversion, and dissolution. Requires a limited worker cooperative association to have at least three worker members to begin business. Directs workers' compensation insurers to calculate premiums for covered employee members based on actual payroll value. Requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce workers' compensation premium calculation standards for associations. Exempts membership interests and patronage refunds issued by associations from state securities registration requirements.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Maryland limited liability companies electing worker cooperative status, cooperative worker members and investor members, and commercial workers' compensation insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $278,400 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming costs at the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. State special fund revenues may increase minimally from business document filing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Insurance Article and adds provisions requiring the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce requirements regarding how insurers calculate workers' compensation premiums for covered employee members of limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill amends several sections of the Tax - General Article to extend personal liability for motor fuel taxes, sales and use taxes, income tax withholding, and admissions and amusement taxes to individuals exercising fiscal management over limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill provides exemptions from the securities and broker-dealer registration requirements of Title 11 of the Corporations and Associations Article (the Maryland Securities Act), which is administered and enforced by the Securities Division within the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill was reviewed by the Judiciary and establishes legal standards regarding service of process under the Maryland Rules and judicial dissolution proceedings involving limited worker cooperative associations.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law relating to the inspection of recorded images apply to recorded images produced by a noise abatement monitoring system; and extending by 2 years the reporting and termination dates of the noise abatement monitoring systems pilot programs in Montgomery County and Prince George's County.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Noise Abatement Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - Inspection and Extension

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Extends the noise abatement monitoring systems pilot programs in Montgomery County and Prince George's County through June 30, 2028. Requires participating counties to submit a program evaluation report to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2027. Requires custodians of public records to deny public inspection of recorded images produced by noise abatement monitoring systems. Permits inspection of these images by cited individuals, their attorneys of record, or authorized agency personnel.
responsible_party: Montgomery County; Prince George's County; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers in Montgomery County and Prince George's County; custodians of public records; law enforcement agencies in Montgomery County and Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2027 and FY 2028 from contested citations in District Court. Local revenues and expenditures increase for Montgomery County and Prince George's County in FY 2027 and FY 2028 if they continue operating their pilot programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Contested citations issued by the noise abatement monitoring systems are adjudicated in the District Court, which prescribes the uniform citation form and collects fine revenues for contested cases.

The bill extends the deadline for participating counties to submit comprehensive reports to the Governor on the operation, costs, revenues, and effectiveness of the noise abatement monitoring pilot programs.
The pilot program operates under the Maryland Transportation Article and authorizes noise abatement monitoring on State and local highways.
The monitoring systems may be deployed along State highways managed and maintained by the State Highway Administration.
The department oversees statewide noise pollution standards and vehicle sound limit guidelines, and served as an information source regarding the pilot extension.
MSP is responsible for enforcing vehicle equipment and noise laws on state roadways and served as an informational source for automated enforcement.

Synopsis: Expanding the purpose of the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff; requiring the Department to prioritize funding for nurses or nursing support staff who practice in an area with a shortage of nurses or nursing support staff or who practice in a specialty where a shortage has been identified; altering certain education requirements for licensure; repealing a certain requirement that the State Board of Nursing approve certain nursing assistant training program sites within a certain time period; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Nursing - Loan Repayment, Education, and Sunset Extension (Building Opportunities for Nurses Act of 2025)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory authority of the State Board of Nursing by five years to July 1, 2030. Expands the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program to include nurses and nursing support staff in qualifying for-profit shortage areas. Alters education and endorsement qualifications for registered nursing licensure while removing certain training site approval requirements. Extends income tax credits for nurse, physician, and physician assistant preceptorship programs through June 30, 2030. Delays the implementation date for certified nursing assistant tier designations until April 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, certified nursing assistants, clinical preceptors, and nursing training program providers
fiscal_impact_summary: Board of Nursing special fund expenditures increase by approximately $440,000 in FY 2025 to cover infrastructure operations. General fund revenues decrease by up to $100,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2030, while Maryland Department of Health special fund revenues and expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2026 and $300,000 annually thereafter due to preceptorship tax credit extensions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary department impacted by the bill. The bill extends the sunset date of the State Board of Nursing (housed within MDH), continues the Secretary of Health's operational and infrastructure authority over the Board, expands the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff administered by MDH, and extends health professional preceptorship tax credit programs administered by MDH.

The bill extends through 2030 several state income tax credits for preceptorship programs (nurse practitioners, physicians, physician assistants, LPNs, and RNs) and alters rotation requirements, impacting the Comptroller's administration and processing of state income tax returns and revenues.

The statutory provisions amended by the bill require MDH to consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to identify geographic areas of the State with health care workforce shortages for the purpose of qualifying preceptors for income tax credits.

MHEC works in conjunction with the State Board of Nursing to approve nursing assistant training programs and develop applicable regulations as set forth in the Health Occupations Article amended by the bill, and was consulted on the legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to conduct an annual study examining and comparing certain data regarding an individual's residence prior to incarceration and on release from a State correctional facility; and requiring the Department by October 1, 2026, and each October 1 thereafter, to report the results of the study to certain committees of the General Assembly.
Title: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services - Study on Location of Individuals Prior to and Following Incarceration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to conduct an annual study on individual incarceration locations. Directs the department to track where individuals resided before incarceration and where they are released. Mandates collecting data on intake county residence, release county, and the timing of pre-release facility transfers. Requires comparisons between release counties, pre-incarceration residences, conviction counties, and incarceration counties at release. Directs the department to submit annual reports to specified legislative committees beginning October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals incarcerated in and released from State correctional facilities and Maryland county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal impact; the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can conduct the annual study and submit required reports using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 22 directly mandates the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) to conduct an annual study examining data on the location and residence of individuals prior to and following incarceration in State correctional facilities and to submit an annual report to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Establishing the Reservoir Augmentation Program in the Department of the Environment; defining "reservoir augmentation" as the planned placement of reclaimed water into a surface water reservoir used as a source for a drinking water treatment facility; requiring a person to obtain a permit from the Department to perform reservoir augmentation; establishing an Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program in the Department to make recommendations on whether the program should be extended or made permanent and any statutory or regulatory changes necessary; etc.
Title: Environment – Reservoir Augmentation Permit – Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment. Prohibits performing reservoir augmentation without an approved permit from the Department. Restricts reservoir augmentation permit terms to a maximum duration of five years. Requires applicants to submit feasibility studies unless previously approved under the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program. Mandates the adoption of regulations setting program standards and reasonable application fees. Extends the termination date of the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program to June 30, 2030.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: public water systems, municipal and local governments, drinking water treatment facilities, and public water consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $97,300 in FY 2026, $85,800 in FY 2027, and $89,500 in FY 2028 for contractual staff. Special fund revenues increase by $75,000 in FY 2030 from permit application fees. Voluntary local expenditures increase for participating local governments that pay permit fees and implement water treatment processes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program within MDE, requiring the department to adopt regulations, review applications, issue and enforce permits, collect fees, manage a dedicated special fund, and submit regular implementation reports.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to MDE and is statutorily responsible for prosecuting civil and criminal enforcement actions and defending agency permitting decisions under Title 9, Subtitle 3 of the Environment Article.

The bill mandates that MDE submit reports to the Governor regarding the implementation of the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program by December 31, 2029, and the Reservoir Augmentation Program by December 31, 2035, and every five years thereafter.

Synopsis: Clarifying the commissions that a guardian of the property may charge; authorizing a trustee of a trust to charge compensation that is reasonable under the circumstances; and authorizing trustees who are financial institutions or members of the Maryland Bar to charge compensation that is reasonable under the circumstances and calculated in accordance with a schedule of rates filed with an appropriate agency.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Compensation of Guardians of Property and Trustees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a trustee to receive compensation that is reasonable under the circumstances when trust terms do not specify compensation. Repeals the specific statutory commission rate schedules previously applied to trustees. Preserves the application of specific statutory commission rate schedules for guardians of property. Establishes statutory factors for courts to consider when determining whether trustee compensation is reasonable. Requires regular compensation for trustees and custodial or investment advisors to be allocated equally between income and principal. Authorizes courts to adjust compensation specified in trust terms under certain circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Commissioner of Financial Regulation; State Director of the Division of Savings and Loan Associations
stakeholders: trustees, trust beneficiaries, guardians of the property of minors and disabled persons, and financial institutions or attorneys serving as fiduciaries
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues may be affected if trust assets shift to trustees' personal or business income via compensation changes, but the impact cannot be reliably estimated and is likely limited. Expenditures are not materially affected, and local finances experience no effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends statutory provisions regarding court proceedings for the approval, increase, decrease, and determination of reasonable compensation for guardians of property and trustees, affecting the operations and adjudication responsibilities of Maryland circuit courts and trust clerks.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administrations, fiduciary filings, and probate matters within the Estates and Trusts Article, which are directly touched by the statutory changes governing guardian and trustee compensation.

The bill references statutory filings of fee and commission schedules for financial institutions and corporate trustees with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, an agency housed within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The Comptroller is noted in the fiscal analysis regarding minor potential effects on State income tax collections if trustee compensation adjustments shift trust assets into taxable personal or business income.

Synopsis: Requiring, in order to make repairs to powered wheelchairs, that a certain manufacturer make available certain documentation, parts, embedded software, firmware, and tools to a certain independent repair provider or owner of a powered wheelchair; providing that a violation of the Act constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to certain enforcement and penalty provisions; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Consumer Protection - Right to Repair - Powered Wheelchairs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires powered wheelchair manufacturers to provide documentation, parts, embedded software, firmware, and tools to independent repair providers and owners. Mandates that manufacturers offer these repair resources on fair and reasonable terms and costs. Limits covered components to batteries, chargers, nonprogrammable joysticks, wheel assemblies, and other specified nonpositioning parts. Requires manufacturers to make available documentation and tools needed to reset disabled security locks or functions. Establishes that violations are unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: powered wheelchair owners, independent repair providers, authorized repair providers, and powered wheelchair manufacturers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected; the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of the bill's powered wheelchair right-to-repair provisions are designated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill regulates the maintenance and repair of powered wheelchairs, directly impacting the accessibility and affordability of assistive technology for Maryland residents with physical disabilities, an area coordinated by the Department of Disabilities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish a forensic review board at facilities that have charge of persons who have been committed to the facility as not criminally responsible; authorizing a forensic review board to make recommendations relating to the release or rehabilitation of a committed person; requiring the board to give notice at least 10 days before a meeting concerning the committed person; requiring the board to give consideration to a written statement offered by the committed person to the board; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Forensic Review Board - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a forensic review board at each facility housing committed persons. Directs each board of licensed health care providers to review each committed person's release eligibility at least annually. Authorizes boards to determine by majority vote whether to recommend discharge or conditional release to the court. Permits committed persons to appoint an authorized agent to attend board meetings, while prohibiting counsel from attending. Requires facility treatment teams to implement board recommendations and arrange necessary rehabilitative treatment.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: persons committed to Maryland Department of Health facilities as not criminally responsible, facility treatment teams, and licensed health care providers serving on forensic review boards
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with establishing forensic review boards at facilities caring for individuals committed as not criminally responsible, implementing the board recommendations, and adopting regulations to administer the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents committed individuals in criminal and involuntary commitment matters; the bill provides procedural rights to committed persons and their counsel, including mandatory meeting notices, record access, and allowing social workers or nonlegal representatives from the attorney's office to serve as authorized agents.

The courts receive recommendations and records from the forensic review boards regarding conditional release or discharge eligibility and preside over judicial release hearings where board representatives may testify.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates administrative release hearings and reviews concerning committed persons under Title 3 of the Criminal Procedure Article and was consulted regarding operational impacts.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Department of Service and Civic Innovation; renaming the Governor's Volunteer Council to be the Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism; altering certain requirements relating to qualifications for applicants and compensation for participants in the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway; altering certain reporting requirements; and repealing the Executive Fellows Program.

bill_summary: Alters eligibility, compensation, and funding provisions for the Maryland Corps Program Service Year Option Pathways. Requires participant stipends to equal at least the applicable county or State minimum wage, whichever is greater. Restricts the $6,000 program completion award to a cash stipend, repealing Maryland 529 account deposits. Limits the Young Adult pathway to Maryland residents who are at least 18 and under 25 years old. Authorizes pathway funds to pay stipends for participants across the entire Maryland Corps Program. Repeals the Executive Fellows Program and renames the Governor's Volunteer Council.
responsible_party: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
stakeholders: Applicants and participants in the Maryland Corps Program, including the Young Adult Service Year Option and Maryland Service Year Option pathways
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in special fund expenditures to the extent county minimum wages exceed the State minimum wage. Potential decrease in general fund expenditures and an offsetting decrease in general fund reversions due to expanded cross-pathway fund usage beginning in fiscal 2027, with no net effect on the general fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is the primary implementing agency of the bill, which amends the Maryland Corps Program pathways (Young Adult and Maryland Service Year pathways), repeals the Executive Fellows Program, and adjusts fund administration and reporting requirements.

The bill explicitly repeals statutory authorization for Maryland Corps completion awards to be deposited directly into a tax-exempt Maryland 529 account due to plan rules prohibiting third-party deposits.

The Treasurer oversees the Maryland 529 program affected by the removal of the completion award deposit option and is statutorily designated to hold and invest the Young Adult and Maryland Service Year Pathway Funds.
The bill amends statutory provisions to formally reflect the transfer of the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism out of GOCI and into DSCI.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally renames the Governor's Volunteer Council to be the Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism and alters the statutory staff support duties.
The bill is an administration initiative concerning executive branch service programs and reports directly to the Governor regarding Maryland Corps Program metrics.
The bill statutorily subjects the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund to audit by OLA.

bill_summary: Repeals the Interagency Committee on Aging Services and separate statutory mandates for senior congregate housing and assisted living programs. Transfers service coordination authority to the Department of Aging to consolidate programs under a unified aging services framework. Requires the Department to establish, coordinate, and supervise a single point of entry program in each planning and service area. Mandates that area agencies on aging operate single points of entry to assess older adults and caregivers. Authorizes services including home modifications, personal care, meal coordination, hazard resilience improvements, and assisted living subsidies.
responsible_party: Department of Aging; Area Agencies on Aging
stakeholders: older adults, caregivers, area agencies on aging, assisted living providers, and congregate housing services providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative requirements can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. In fiscal 2026, $20.1 million in general funds across three existing programs will be consolidated into the unified program beginning in fiscal 2027. State general fund expenditures and local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the Department enters into new agreements or contracts to coordinate services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary implementing agency for HB 36. The bill repeals several of its existing program statutes (Senior Care, Senior Assisted Living Subsidy, and Congregate Housing Services) to consolidate them into a unified aging services program, transfers functions of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services to the department, and tasks it with stakeholder engagement, single points of entry oversight, and transition planning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals the statutory Interagency Committee on Aging Services, transferring its responsibilities and program coordination oversight directly to the Department of Aging.

The Department of Aging will coordinate with DBM to restructure and consolidate three separate state budget line items totaling approximately $20.1 million into a single unified funding stream for the reorganized program.

The Secretary of Health is a statutory member of the Interagency Committee on Aging Services that is repealed under the bill. In addition, the bill touches on assisted living program definitions and long-term services and health supports for older adults.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services, and the bill alters programs addressing congregate housing services, housing opportunities, and facility resilience for older adults.

The Secretary of Human Services serves on the Interagency Committee on Aging Services repealed by the bill, and local departments of social services coordinate closely with aging services and adult protective/supportive care.
The Secretary of Disabilities is a statutory member of the Interagency Committee on Aging Services that is abolished under the bill.

bill_summary: Repeals the criminal prohibition against knowingly transferring or attempting to transfer the human immunodeficiency virus to another individual. Eliminates the misdemeanor penalty of imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to $2,500, or both. Removes the specific statutory offense from the Health - General Article. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Judiciary
stakeholders: individuals living with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), criminal defense attorneys, and State prosecutors
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local governmental finances or operations, including the workload of the District Court.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 18-601.1 of the Health - General Article concerning the criminal transfer of HIV, directly impacting state public health policy and disease prevention initiatives overseen by MDH.
The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor offense, which affects the caseload, case management, and charge processing across Maryland District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill decriminalizes conduct that carried a potential incarceration penalty of up to three years, directly eliminating potential misdemeanor charges against indigent defendants represented by OPD.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal of an offense carrying up to three years of imprisonment marginally impacts potential intake, incarceration, or community supervision requirements managed by DPSCS.
As the State's chief legal officer providing counsel to state health agencies and handling state criminal appeals, OAG is affected by the repeal of this criminal statutory provision.
As a statewide law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating criminal violations and will no longer investigate or charge individuals under this repealed statute.

Repeals the trout stamp exemption for holders of resident consolidated senior sport fishing licenses. Raises the annual resident senior sport fishing license fee from $5 to $12. Increases the annual resident angler's license fee to $32 and the nonresident annual fee to at least $55. Sets annual trout stamp fees at $20 for residents and $30 for nonresidents.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Resident and nonresident recreational anglers, senior anglers age 65 and older, trout anglers, and authorized license sales agents
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $565,800 in FY 2025 and by approximately $3.0 million ($2,977,800) annually in FY 2026 and future years. General fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount through FY 2028 due to interest earnings on fund balances. State expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 40 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) that alters fees for senior sport fishing licenses, angler's licenses, and trout stamps administered by the department. The bill directly increases DNR special fund revenues for fisheries management and protection by approximately $3 million annually.

Synopsis: Altering the time periods during which a petition for the formation of a new political party or additional signatures to a petition may not be filed; and prohibiting signatures submitted with a petition that was officially determined as not meeting certain legal requirements from being resubmitted with a subsequent petition.
Title: Election Law - Petitions for the Formation of a New Political Party - Process
bill_summary: Alters the time periods during which petitions to form a new political party may not be filed. Expands the filing blackout period in presidential and gubernatorial election years. Prohibits filing petitions or additional signatures after the first Monday in July until voter registration reopens after the general election. Prohibits signatures submitted with a petition officially determined to have failed statutory requirements from being resubmitted with a subsequent petition. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: political organizations seeking recognition as a new Maryland political party and registered voters who sign party formation petitions
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 41 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE). It modifies election administration procedures by moving the deadline for submitting petitions or additional signatures to form a new political party from the first Monday in August to the first Monday in July, and prohibits resubmission of rejected signatures.

Specifies that acquired land must be for the construction or use of a federally qualified health center. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: counties, municipal corporations, and nonprofit organizations operating or establishing federally qualified health centers
fiscal_impact_summary: Alters the purposes for which existing grant funds may be used with no net effect on total state expenditures. The Board of Public Works and Maryland Department of Health can implement administrative changes using existing budgeted resources. Local revenues and expenditures may increase if local entities apply for and receive grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHC) Grant Program and the Secretary of Health is responsible for recommending grant awards for the acquisition of land to the Board of Public Works.
The Board of Public Works is directly authorized by the bill to award grants under the FQHC Grant Program for land acquisition upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health.

The bill formally adds the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity within the Maryland Cannabis Administration to the advisory council and updates statutory references to the Maryland Cannabis Administration.
MDOT requested this departmental legislation to ensure transportation safety and impaired driving considerations are represented on the council through its modal administration, the MVA.
The Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council is established under the Health - General Article and is staffed and provided technical assistance by the Maryland Department of Health.

bill_summary: Alters state building energy performance standards regulations administered by the Department of the Environment. Excludes hospitals and certain manufacturing buildings from the definition of covered buildings. Requires regulations to credit on-site renewable energy and biomethane while excluding steam sterilization and emergency backup power. Exempts certain covered buildings containing permanent sensitive compartmented information facilities from energy use intensity targets. Establishes a $100 annual reporting fee per covered building, adjusted for inflation, to fund program administrative costs. Requires the Department to certify qualifying county standards and complete a cost-benefit analysis by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners of commercial and multifamily residential buildings, hospitals, manufacturing facilities, defense and intelligence contractors, and local governments including Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Maryland Clean Air Fund increase by an estimated $690,000 in FY 2026 from the new $100 annual reporting fee, rising with inflation in subsequent years. Total MDE expenditures increase by $1,033,800 in FY 2026 ($690,000 in special funds and $343,800 in general funds) to support five staff positions and contractual studies. State agencies and local governments that own covered buildings incur ongoing annual costs to pay the reporting fee.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for adopting Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) regulations, establishing exclusions and crediting mechanisms, certifying county BEPS programs, collecting the annual reporting fee, and conducting the comprehensive cost-benefit analysis due by December 31, 2026.

DGS manages and operates state-owned facilities. Because state-owned buildings of 35,000 square feet or more are classified as covered buildings, DGS is directly impacted by BEPS compliance requirements, exemptions, and the payment of annual reporting fees.
The bill requires MDE to submit its cost-benefit analysis and policy recommendations regarding building energy performance standards scenarios to the Governor on or before December 31, 2026.

MEA coordinates statewide energy policy, efficiency programs, and renewable energy adoption. The bill's provisions on energy use intensity targets, crediting renewable generation, and overall BEPS directly interface with state energy transition planning overseen in part by MEA.
USM owns and manages numerous campus facilities meeting the covered building threshold, making them subject to BEPS regulations, laboratory and operational considerations, and annual reporting fees.

As an independent public university owning large state facilities subject to the 35,000 square foot covered building threshold, MSU is impacted by BEPS standards and the associated annual reporting fees.
MDOT oversees extensive infrastructure and state-owned facilities across its modal administrations that meet the size threshold for covered buildings, requiring compliance reporting and fee payments.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date for a certain provision of law related to the maximum amount of total user fees that may be assessed on hospitals and related institutions by the Health Services Cost Review Commission.

bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2025, termination date on the user fee assessment formula for the Health Services Cost Review Commission. Maintains the cap at the greater of 0.1% of budgeted gross hospital revenue or the preceding five-year maximum. Authorizes the Commission to continue assessing user fees on rate-approved hospitals and related institutions under this formula. Requires fee collections to be paid into the Health Services Cost Review Commission Fund. Restricts expenditures exclusively to actual direct costs of fulfilling the Commission's statutory and regulatory duties.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: hospitals and related institutions with rates approved by the Health Services Cost Review Commission, and the Maryland Medicaid program
fiscal_impact_summary: Health Services Cost Review Commission special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $1.6 million in FY 2026, rising to $4.8 million in FY 2030. State Medicaid expenditures increase by up to $315,409 in FY 2026 and $963,267 in FY 2030 (40% general funds, 60% federal funds) because of higher hospital rates, with federal matching revenues increasing correspondingly. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 54 directly affects the Health Services Cost Review Commission by repealing the sunset date on the calculation formula for its user fee assessments on hospitals, allowing the Commission to maintain its special fund revenue levels and support its regulatory duties and implementation of the AHEAD model.

The Maryland Department of Health requested this departmental bill, houses HSCRC administratively, and will experience an increase in Medicaid expenditures (state and federal funds) resulting from the hospital rate adjustments associated with higher HSCRC user fees.

bill_summary: Alters statutory procedures governing property tax sales, redemption, and notice requirements statewide. Requires tax collectors to withhold owner-occupied properties and heir-occupied properties from sale when taxes are under $1,000. Prohibits taxes, interest, and penalties accruing after a tax sale from inclusion in owner-occupied redemption payments. Caps the annual rate of redemption for owner-occupied residential property at 10%. Requires each county to establish a registry for interested parties or the Ombudsman to designate withheld properties. Expands eligibility for the Homeowner Protection Program to include estates, personal representatives, and heirs of deceased homeowners.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; State Tax Sale Ombudsman
stakeholders: Homeowners and heirs facing property tax sales, tenants residing in foreclosed properties, private tax sale certificate purchasers, and local government tax collectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues may decrease by up to $92,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026. Local government tax revenues may decrease by up to $1.1 million annually due to the $1,000 tax sale threshold and the 10% redemption rate cap. Local expenditures may increase by an unquantified amount for programming adjustments and maintaining property withholding registries.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 59 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) designed to protect vulnerable homeowners, prevent displacement, preserve homeownership, and facilitate the return of vacant and abandoned properties to productive use.

The bill alters statutory procedures and timelines governing judicial actions to foreclose the right of redemption in circuit courts, including notice requirements to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman and tenants, as well as the issuance and execution of writs of possession.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Public Accountancy in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2030, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; and requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a certain report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee on or before July 1, 2028.

bill_summary: Extends the statutory termination date for the State Board of Public Accountancy to July 1, 2030. Continues the regulatory and licensing authority of the Board over certified public accountants and accountancy firms. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report regarding the Board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Mandates submission of the report on or before July 1, 2028. Directs that the report include information determined by the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Licensed certified public accountants and public accountancy firms in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Public Accountancy from fiscal 2026 through 2030. Reporting requirements are absorbable with existing Maryland Department of Labor resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the Board's statutory and regulatory authority through July 1, 2030, and requires the Department to submit an evaluation report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2028.

Local school system revenues and expenditures increase by up to $50,000 annually in total depending on grants awarded.

The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $50,000 beginning in FY 2027, which impacts state budget development and fiscal planning overseen by DBM.

Synopsis: Increasing the noncompetitive threshold for State leases of real property from less than 2,500 square feet to up to 5,000 square feet; altering the time frame during which the State is required to advertise the need for rental of building space from at least 30 days to 20 days before proposals for lease are due; requiring the advertisement to be in certain newspapers providing notice to at least the people of the affected locality; and requiring the notice to be posted on the Department's website and eMaryland Marketplace.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - State Leasing of Real Property
bill_summary: Increases the noncompetitive threshold for State real property leases from less than 2,500 square feet to up to 5,000 square feet. Reduces the advance advertising period for State building rental needs from 30 days to 20 days before lease proposals are due. Repeals the requirement that the Department of General Services advertise proposed leases in newspapers. Requires the Department to advertise proposed leases by posting on its website and on eMaryland Marketplace. Mandates that lease advertisements state the proposed square footage and desired general area.
responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: commercial real estate property owners, landlords, prospective bidders on State lease contracts, and State agencies seeking building space
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Changes in Department of General Services leasing and procurement activities do not materially affect State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 73 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of General Services (DGS). It directly alters DGS's real property leasing processes by increasing the threshold for noncompetitive leases from 2,500 to 5,000 square feet, shortening the required advertising window from 30 to 20 days, and codifying posting requirements on the DGS website and eMaryland Marketplace.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for the oversight and approval of State property leases and contracts. Changes to the competitive thresholds and procurement procedures for State real property leases affect the lease acquisition workflow and submissions that may come before the Board.

Requires special election dates to be at least 90 days after council resolution adoption. Prohibits setting a special election date within 120 days of a regularly scheduled election. Requires the State Administrator of Elections to resolve local law conflicts by applying State law and regulations. Increases the deadline to mail ballots in mail-in special elections from 14 days to 30 days. Exempts local election boards from mailing specimen ballots and authorizes voters to use ballot drop boxes.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: Registered voters in Maryland counties conducting special elections, candidates for county council or county executive vacancies, and local election officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances. Local expenditures may be indirectly affected depending on whether special elections must be held independently or concurrently with regularly scheduled elections.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 75 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE). It modifies requirements for scheduling and conducting special elections, empowers the State Administrator of Elections to resolve statutory and regulatory conflicts with local charters, and alters vote-by-mail procedures for special elections.

Synopsis: Specifying the manner in which notice regarding an exercise of the decanting power or the sending of a document under the Maryland Trust Decanting Act is required to be provided.

bill_summary: Specifies permissible methods for delivering notice or transmittal documents under the Maryland Trust Decanting Act. Requires transmittals to be reasonably suitable under the circumstances and likely to result in receipt. Mandates notice by personal service, certified or first-class mail with return receipt, or courier service. Authorizes alternative notice by regular mail, facsimile, or email if the recipient agrees in writing. Requires standard delivery methods if the fiduciary knows or should know alternative notice was not received.
responsible_party: Authorized fiduciaries
stakeholders: Authorized fiduciaries, trustees, and trust beneficiaries entitled to notice under the Maryland Trust Decanting Act
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

The Register of Wills administers estate matters and acts as clerk to the Orphans' Court, making them relevant to statutory revisions within the Estates and Trusts Article governing fiduciary notices.

bill_summary: Establishes that each animal harmed in a violation of crimes relating to animals constitutes a separate offense. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 136 is a departmental bill requested by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP). It updates Maryland statute to formally codify that GOCPP, rather than the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, is directly responsible for reimbursing physicians, health care providers, and hospitals for sexual assault forensic exams, treatments, and follow-up care.

Synopsis: Authorizing the trustee of a trust to resign under the Maryland Trust Act on 30 days' notice to qualified beneficiaries, the settlor, if living, all cotrustees, and any person that has a right to replace or appoint a successor to the resigning trustee.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Resignation of Trustee - Notice
bill_summary: Authorizes a trustee to resign under the Maryland Trust Act without court approval by providing at least 30 days' notice. Requires notice to qualified beneficiaries, the living settlor, all cotrustees, and persons authorized to appoint a successor trustee. Retains court approval as an alternative method for a trustee to resign. Specifies that resignation does not discharge liability of the trustee or surety for prior acts or omissions. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Trustees, trust settlors, cotrustees, qualified beneficiaries, and persons with the right to appoint successor trustees
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows trustees under the Maryland Trust Act to resign by providing 30 days' written notice to specified parties rather than requiring court approval, potentially reducing court filings and proceedings related to trustee resignations handled by the Maryland Judicial Branch.

Synopsis: Altering a requirement that a child care center that has 20 or more children have in attendance a certain ratio, set by the Department, of staff to children who hold a certificate in first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation under certain circumstances.
Title: Child Care Centers - Certificated Staff Ratio Requirement - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland State Department of Education to establish certificated staff-to-child ratios for certain child care centers. Applies to child care centers that serve more than 20 children. Alters the prior statutory requirement of one certified staff member for every 20 children. Retains the requirement that at least one supervisor certified in first aid and CPR be present at all times. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Board of Education
stakeholders: licensed child care centers, child care center staff, and children attending child care centers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected. Small business child care centers may experience operational cost savings through reduced staff training requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 150 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It alters the statutory first aid and CPR certified staff-to-child ratio requirement for child care centers and authorizes MSDE to establish the required ratio through its licensing rules and regulations.

Synopsis: Renaming the Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program to be the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program; providing that the purpose of the program is to provide regular, direct communication from the Department of Aging or the Department's designee to an eligible participant to promote wellness and purposeful social engagement; authorizing the integration of services between the Program and Telecommunications Access of Maryland to promote awareness of the availability of accessible telecommunications equipment; etc.
Title: Department of Aging - Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program

bill_summary: Renames the Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program to the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program. Expands eligibility to Maryland older adults at risk of social isolation who would benefit from purposeful social engagement and wellness checks. Broadens program communications beyond telephone calls to include text messages and web-based, virtual, video, or in-person interactions. Requires the Maryland Department of Aging to integrate services with the Telecommunications Access of Maryland program. Authorizes the department to contract with private vendors, nonprofit organizations, local villages, and area agencies on aging. Extends liability protections to participating entities and contractors for reasonable acts or omissions under the program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Older Maryland adults at risk of social isolation, deaf and hard of hearing older adults, Area Agencies on Aging, local senior villages, and participating contractors and nonprofit organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State finances, as existing Universal Service Trust Fund special fund allocations ($419,967 in fiscal 2026) and existing staff resources will support the program. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local entities and Area Agencies on Aging enter into agreements or contracts to provide program services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 158 is a departmental bill for the Department of Aging that renames, broadens, and administers the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program to provide regular wellness and social engagement communication to eligible older adults.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Aging to integrate program services with the Telecommunications Access of Maryland (TAM) program, which is housed within the Department of Disabilities, by promoting accessible equipment and using TAM outreach materials.

bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt curriculum guides and courses of study aligned with State content standards. Directs the Maryland State Department of Education to develop content standards for each subject at each grade level. Requires the State Superintendent of Schools to issue a written notice of discrepancy when local curricula fail to align. Requires county superintendents to meet with the State Superintendent within 30 days to develop an approved corrective plan. Requires local boards that fail to satisfactorily implement the corrective plan to adopt State curriculum standards and resources. Directs the State Superintendent to withhold State funds if a local board fails to adopt the required curriculum.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Superintendent of Schools
stakeholders: county boards of education, county superintendents, public school teachers, and public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education and the Comptroller can implement requirements using existing resources. Local board of education expenditures may increase minimally to align curriculum guides and courses of study with State content standards. State aid may be withheld from noncompliant local boards, though this is expected to occur rarely.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing statewide content standards across subjects and grade levels. Additionally, the State Superintendent of Schools is tasked with identifying discrepancies in local school board curriculum guides, establishing corrective plans, mandating state curriculum standards where plans fail, and withholding state education funds for noncompliance.

The Comptroller is responsible for withholding State education funding disbursements to local school boards if directed by the State Superintendent of Schools for noncompliance with curriculum standards.

Synopsis: Establishing the reciprocal out-of-state motor home and recreational trailer vehicle show permit, to be issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration, authorizing the holder to display motor homes and recreational vehicles at vehicle shows in Worcester County; and requiring a permit holder, after the permit is approved, to file a bond with the Administration.
Title: Motor Home and Recreational Vehicle Shows in Worcester County - Permit for Out-of-State Dealers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds

bill_summary: Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue vehicle show permits to qualifying out-of-state dealers of motor homes and recreational trailers. Limits permit eligibility to dealers licensed in states that grant reciprocal display privileges to Maryland dealers. Allows permit holders to display or exhibit motor homes or recreational trailers at vehicle shows in Worcester County. Prohibits permit holders from executing a buyer's order or accepting a deposit. Requires approved permit holders to file a surety bond in an amount determined by the Administration. Authorizes the Administration to determine permit duration and suspend or revoke permits for noncompliance.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: out-of-state dealers of motor homes and recreational trailers, Maryland motor home and recreational trailer dealers, and vehicle show operators and attendees in Worcester County
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is directly responsible for administering the new law, including issuing the reciprocal vehicle show permits to out-of-state dealers, approving bonds, determining permit duration and bond amounts, and enforcing compliance.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent cabinet department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is tasked with executing and implementing the permitting program established by the bill.
