Synopsis: Altering from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2027, the date through which the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund may be used for expenses associated with maternal and child health population health improvements.
Title: Health - Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund - Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg

bill_summary: Extends the date through which the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund may be used. Allows the Maryland Department of Health to spend remaining fund balances through December 31, 2027. Permits continued expenditures for maternal and child health population health improvements through designated state administrations. Requires fund expenditures to align with the State budget and receive approval from the Health Services Cost Review Commission. Maintains that expended funds must supplement rather than supplant funding appropriated for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Mothers, infants, and children in Maryland receiving Medicaid or participating in public health initiatives; Maryland hospitals subject to rate assessments
fiscal_impact_summary: No new revenues are generated. Allows up to $24.1 million in unspent special fund balances to continue being expended through the first half of fiscal 2028 instead of ending in calendar 2025, continuing to be used in lieu of general funds and potentially drawing federal Medicaid matching funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health co-administers the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund and is the primary entity that expends monies from the fund to support maternal and child health programs in Medicaid and the Prevention and Health Promotion Administration.

The Health Services Cost Review Commission co-administers the Fund alongside MDH, approves expenditures from the Fund by majority vote, and previously authorized the hospital rate assessment providing the funding.
Under the governing statute, the State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Fund separately, investing the money of the Fund, and crediting interest earnings back to the Fund.
The statute specifies that the Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for accounting for the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund.
The statute explicitly provides that the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

Synopsis: Requiring the Correctional Training Commission to adopt regulations for the training, issuance, and use of body-worn cameras by January 1, 2026; establishing the Public Employees' Safety and Health Unit in the Division of Labor and Industry to administer and enforce certain duties regarding the oversight of workplace safety and health of employees of certain public bodies; establishing and applying certain civil and criminal penalties to public bodies and persons in government; etc.
Title: Davis Martinez Public Employee Safety and Health Act

bill_summary: Establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health Unit within the Division of Labor and Industry. Subjects public bodies to occupational safety and health civil penalties, while exempting public body elevator units. Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to adopt workplace violence prevention standards for public bodies by October 1, 2026. Directs the Correctional Training Commission to adopt regulations for correctional officer body-worn cameras by January 1, 2026. Authorizes uniformed correctional officers to intercept oral communications using body-worn digital recording devices under specified conditions. Allocates civil penalties assessed against public bodies to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Correctional Training Commission; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: State and local public bodies, public employees, correctional officers, correctional units, and participants in the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $535,400 in general funds and $69,400 in special funds in FY 2026 for agency personnel and correctional body-worn camera procurement. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program increase by an estimated $30,000 in FY 2026 and $40,000 annually thereafter from civil penalties assessed against public bodies. Local expenditures may increase for safety compliance and potential penalty assessments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 176 establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health (PESH) Unit within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry. MD Labor is charged with administering and enforcing workplace safety standards for public bodies, adopting workplace violence regulations, conducting inspections, issuing citations and civil penalties, and directing penalty revenues to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts DPSCS by requiring the Correctional Training Commission to adopt regulations for body-worn cameras (BWCs) and requiring correctional units to establish written BWC policies. Furthermore, the bill triggers $428,790 in contingent general fund expenditures for DPSCS in FY 2026 to procure BWCs for correctional and supervision staff.

The bill requires the Attorney General to prioritize and expedite reviews of administrative search warrant applications from PESH, provide formal notices when taking enforcement actions against public bodies, and represent the State in contested citation hearings, which requires an additional Assistant Attorney General position.

As a correctional unit under Maryland law, DJS is subject to the bill's provisions requiring each correctional unit to develop and maintain written policies consistent with state regulations for the use of body-worn cameras by correctional staff.

The bill requires the Attorney General and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to formally notify the Governor whenever legal action is initiated against a public body or when a public body fails to pay assessed workplace safety civil penalties.

Synopsis: Providing that multiple thefts committed by the same person in multiple counties under one scheme or continuing course of conduct may be joined and prosecuted in any county in which any one of the thefts occurred; prohibiting one or more persons from committing a series of thefts from retail merchants over a 90-day period with an aggregate value exceeding $1,500; requiring a court to make a finding as to whether a certain crime is organized retail theft under certain circumstances for a certain purpose; etc.
Title: Organized Retail Theft Act of 2025

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes the felony offense of organized retail theft of merchandise exceeding $1,500 in aggregate value over a 90-day period. Expands property value calculations to include repair, replacement, or restocking costs and damaged property values. Authorizes multi-county thefts committed under one scheme to be joined and prosecuted in any county where a theft occurred. Imposes graduated penalties up to 20 years imprisonment and mandates restitution or restoration of stolen property. Requires courts, upon request by the State's Attorney, to make factual findings regarding organized retail theft for state criminal records. Merges organized retail theft convictions into general theft convictions for sentencing purposes when arising from identical acts.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; State's Attorneys; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Retail merchants, individuals charged with or convicted of retail theft crimes, State's Attorneys, and criminal defense attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal decrease in State general fund revenues and potential minimal increase in local revenues due to cases shifting from the District Court to circuit courts. Potential minimal increase in State general fund incarceration expenditures from longer prison sentences. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new felony offense of organized retail theft, alters venue and joinder rules across county jurisdictions, and requires the court to make specific findings of fact regarding whether an offense constitutes organized retail theft upon request, impacting District Court and Circuit Court caseloads and procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes felony penalties that may increase state incarceration expenditures and bed days in state correctional facilities, and mandates that court findings of organized retail theft be reported to the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository operated by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense and allows misdemeanor thefts to be aggregated and joined across jurisdictions into felony charges, shifting case defense workloads to more experienced circuit court public defenders.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Adjutant General instead of the Governor to appoint certain staff in the Military Department; and establishing that certain staff in the Military Department serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General instead of the Governor.
Title: Military Department – Chief of Staff and Aides – Appointment Authority

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Adjutant General instead of the Governor to appoint a chief of staff and aides in the Military Department. Establishes that the appointed chief of staff and aides serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General. Aligns statutory appointment authority with current administrative practice within the Military Department. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department; Adjutant General
stakeholders: chief of staff, aides, and executive leadership within the Maryland Military Department
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations because the change conforms statute to existing administrative practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly grants the Adjutant General the statutory authority to appoint the chief of staff and aides within the Military Department, establishing that these individuals serve at the Adjutant General's pleasure.

The bill alters gubernatorial appointment authority by transferring the statutory responsibility to appoint the Military Department's chief of staff and aides from the Governor to the Adjutant General.
The Maryland National Guard operates under the Military Department, where the affected chief of staff and aides serve on State active duty status and assist with department operations.

Synopsis: Altering the penalties for a civil citation issued as a result of a recorded image produced by a speed monitoring system; requiring the State Highway Administration to convene a workgroup to study best practices regarding speed monitoring systems in school zones; and requiring the workgroup to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Penalties

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Replaces the flat $40 maximum civil penalty for speed monitoring system violations with an escalating penalty structure. Sets penalties from $40 for exceeding limits by 12 to 15 miles per hour up to $425 for 40 or more. Requires the District Court to prescribe a uniform citation form. Requires the State Highway Administration to convene a workgroup on speed monitoring system best practices in school zones. Requires the administration to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers cited by speed monitoring systems, local governments, and local law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 due to higher civil penalties and contested citations in District Court. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2026 for workgroup consultant costs, and general fund expenditures increase by $33,596 in FY 2026 for Judiciary citation programming. Local expenditures increase correspondingly as jurisdictions direct net camera revenues toward local public safety programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the State Highway Administration to convene a workgroup to study best practices regarding speed monitoring systems in school zones and submit a report by December 1, 2025. Additionally, SHA receives and expends revenues generated from speed cameras on MD Route 210.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, MDOT experiences direct fiscal impacts through Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures, including consultant costs for the workgroup and safety improvement expenditures.

The District Court of Maryland must prescribe the uniform citation form and modify its penalty schedule to implement the escalating tiered fines, incurring one-time programming expenditures and adjudicating an anticipated increase in contested citations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a specialized study workgroup composed of state and local stakeholders to evaluate and recommend best practices regarding speed monitoring systems in school zones.
The State Highway Administration is required to submit the findings and recommendations of the school zone speed monitoring study to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

Synopsis: Altering the fiscal years to include fiscal year 2027 through fiscal year 2029, during which the Governor is required to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $3,700,000 to the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program.
Title: Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program - Funding - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Reestablishes a mandated annual appropriation of $3,700,000 for the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program. Requires the Governor to include the appropriation in the State budget for fiscal years 2027 through 2029. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to administer the program and award grants annually by August 15. Allocates grant funding among existing providers for ongoing and additional services and providers enrolling additional children. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Therapeutic child care and early childhood education providers, and children under age six with developmental delays, physical disabilities, or social, emotional, or behavioral functioning delays
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.2 million annually in fiscal years 2027 through 2029 to meet the $3.7 million mandated appropriation above baseline funding. No fiscal impact occurs in fiscal 2026. Revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary administering agency for the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program and is responsible for awarding grants to providers serving children under age six with developmental delays and disabilities.
DBM oversees the development of the state budget and fiscal planning, and the bill establishes a mandated general fund appropriation of $3.7 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an appropriation of $3,700,000 to the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to disqualify any individual from driving a commercial motor vehicle for 1 year if the individual, while holding a commercial instructional permit or commercial driver's license, drives or attempts to drive any motor vehicle while the alcohol concentration of the person's blood or breath is 0.08 or greater.
Title: Drunk Driving - Commercial Driver's Licenses - Disqualification From Driving

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to disqualify an individual from driving a commercial motor vehicle for one year. Applies when a commercial instructional permit or commercial driver's license holder drives or attempts to drive any motor vehicle. Requires the person's blood or breath alcohol concentration to be 0.08 or greater. Extends the disqualification to three years if transporting hazardous material required to be placarded. Disqualifies any person for life for two or more violations arising from separate incidents. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Holders of a commercial driver's license or commercial instructional permit
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. Reprogramming and procedural changes can be handled using existing resources. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency directly tasked by the bill with disqualifying individuals holding a commercial instructional permit or commercial driver's license from driving a commercial motor vehicle if they drive any vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 or greater.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and sponsored this departmental legislation.
Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicate administrative per se hearing appeals resulting from MVA disqualifications and suspensions.
The Maryland State Police enforce impaired driving laws, administer breath and chemical tests that determine BAC levels, and serve as an information source on the bill's enforcement impacts.
Listed as an information source in the fiscal note; the court system handles judicial proceedings related to underlying impaired driving offenses.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person who tows or removes a vehicle from a parking lot to provide electronic notice of the tow or removal to the vehicle owner through the Motor Vehicle Administration under certain circumstances; and authorizing a police department that takes an abandoned vehicle into custody to send an electronic notice to the last known registered owner of the vehicle through the Administration under certain circumstances.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Towed, Removed, or Abandoned Vehicles - Electronic Notice to Owner

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Authorizes towing businesses and police departments to notify vehicle owners of towed or abandoned vehicles electronically through the Motor Vehicle Administration. Requires the Administration to send the electronic notice using the email address the owner provided in Administration records. Requires notice by certified and first-class mail if the owner does not respond within seven days. Requires the Administration to adopt regulations governing electronic notifications to vehicle owners. Requires a police department to post notice in the circuit court if electronic notice is unacknowledged or undeliverable.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Registered vehicle owners, commercial towing businesses, local and State police departments, vehicle insurers, and secured parties
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Motor Vehicle Administration will develop an electronic notification web portal funded by charging nominal fees to towing businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with adopting regulations for electronic notifications, maintaining an electronic database of insurers, transmitting electronic notices to vehicle owners using email addresses in its records, and creating a web portal for towers.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the implementation of vehicle laws, administrative regulations, and state transportation databases affected by this bill.

As the primary state law enforcement agency that takes abandoned vehicles into custody along state roadways, the Maryland State Police is authorized to use the new electronic notification procedure through the Motor Vehicle Administration to notify vehicle owners.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to develop a comprehensive plan by July 1, 2026, for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools which integrate restorative practices into daily practices and activities of the whole school; requiring a county board of education to use the comprehensive plan if the county board chooses to establish a Restorative Practices School; and requiring the Department to report to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, on the comprehensive plan for Restorative Practices Schools.
Title: Public Schools - Restorative Practices Schools - Comprehensive Plan

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to develop a comprehensive plan for establishing Restorative Practices Schools by July 1, 2026. Replaces the statutory term restorative approaches with restorative practices throughout student discipline provisions. Directs the Department to consult with experienced educators, administrators, and organizations when developing the plan. Requires county boards of education to use the comprehensive plan if they choose to establish a Restorative Practices School. Requires the State Board of Education to provide technical assistance upon request to county boards establishing these schools. Mandates a report by the Department to the Governor and General Assembly on the plan by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland State Board of Education
stakeholders: Public school students, public school teachers, school administrators, and county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2026 for contractual support to help develop the comprehensive plan. Local school board finances are not directly affected because establishing a restorative practices school remains discretionary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing the comprehensive plan for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools, providing technical assistance and model training materials to local school boards, and submitting required reports. The bill also has a fiscal impact on MSDE of $100,000 in FY 2026 for contractual support.
The bill mandates that the State Department of Education submit its comprehensive plan report for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools to the Governor on or before December 1, 2026.

Synopsis: Altering the time before an election when a certain notice is required to be sent to each voter who is on the permanent absentee ballot list; repealing a requirement that the notice be sent to each voter who is on the permanent absentee ballot list as of a certain date; and altering the action the State Board of Elections is required to take if the State Board is unable to contact a voter who is on the permanent absentee ballot list using the method of communication chosen by the voter.
Title: Election Law - Notice to Permanent Absentee Voters
bill_summary: Alters the timeframe for notifying voters on the permanent absentee ballot list before an election. Requires the State Board of Elections to send written communication between 120 and 90 days before an election. Repeals the restriction limiting notices to voters registered on the list at least 90 days prior. Requires the Board to attempt contact using another method if a voter's preferred communication method fails. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: registered voters in Maryland on the permanent absentee ballot list
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 199 is a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections that alters statutory requirements and timeframes governing SBE's pre-election notices and communications to voters on the permanent absentee ballot list.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person that is a seller from advertising or offering for sale a digital good using certain terminology unless, before executing the sale, a certain affirmative acknowledgment is received from the purchaser or a certain clear and conspicuous statement is provided by the seller; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to certain enforcement and penalty provisions.
Title: Consumer Protection – False Advertising – Digital Goods

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: Prohibits sellers from advertising or offering digital goods using terms conferring unrestricted ownership without meeting disclosure requirements. Requires sellers before executing a sale to receive an affirmative purchaser acknowledgment or provide a clear disclosure statement. Mandates that the acknowledgment or statement appear distinctly and separately from other terms and conditions. Exempts subscription services, free digital goods, and goods available for permanent offline download. Classifies a violation as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under Maryland consumer protection law. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Sellers of digital goods and Maryland consumers purchasing digital goods
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division, can handle the requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that misrepresenting ownership terms in the sale or advertising of digital goods constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is the primary agency responsible for investigating and enforcing violations of this Act.

Enforcement actions, injunctions, and civil penalty proceedings initiated under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act are adjudicated within the state court system administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

SponsorPrimary: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Sponsors.Name: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Synopsis: Repealing a duplicative provision of law requiring each county government, local school system, and local health department, in consultation with the local emergency manager, to create or update a cybersecurity preparedness and response plan and complete a cybersecurity preparedness assessment in a manner and frequency established by the Department of Information Technology.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - Local Cybersecurity Preparedness and Response Plan and Assessment - Repeal
bill_summary: Repeals a duplicative statutory provision governing local cybersecurity preparedness and response plans and assessments. The repealed section applied to each county government, local school system, and local health department. The requirement excluded municipal governments. Substantially similar requirements remain codified in another section of the State Finance and Procurement Article. Renumbers existing provisions within the State Finance and Procurement Article accordingly. The Act takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: county governments, local school systems, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is technical in nature and repeals a duplicative statutory requirement that remains codified in another section of state law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 209 is a departmental bill submitted on behalf of the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to clean up duplicative provisions in its governing statute under the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding local cybersecurity preparedness plans and assessments.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Assistive Technology Program in the Department of Disabilities; providing the purpose of the Program is to increase access to assistive technology services and devices for individuals with disabilities, support the State's efforts to provide assistive technology services and devices to persons with disabilities of all ages, including underrepresented populations, and ensure statewide access to assistive technology lending libraries; establishing the Assistive Technology Services Fund; etc.
Title: Human Services - Maryland Assistive Technology Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Assistive Technology Program in the Department of Disabilities. Directs the program to increase access to assistive technology devices and services for individuals with disabilities. Requires statewide access to lending libraries allowing individuals and their supporters to borrow assistive technology devices. Establishes the Assistive Technology Services Fund to receive revenue generated from program services. Restricts fund expenditures solely to supporting program operations, including purchasing assistive technology devices. Authorizes the Secretary of Disabilities to adopt regulations to implement the program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, support networks of individuals with disabilities, and local government entities utilizing assistive technology services
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $25,000 in fiscal 2026, growing to $38,300 by fiscal 2030. General fund revenues increase minimally through fiscal 2028 from interest earnings before interest accrues to the special fund in fiscal 2029. Local expenditures may increase minimally if local governments purchase fee-based assistive technology services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 214 is a departmental bill that formally codifies the Maryland Assistive Technology Program within the Department of Disabilities, and establishes the Assistive Technology Services Fund under the administration of the Secretary of Disabilities.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Assistive Technology Services Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Assistive Technology Services Fund.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the sale, offer for sale, transfer, or distribution of non-arc-resistant jacketed corrugated stainless steel tubing; providing a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for a violation of the Act; and requiring the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal, by September 1, 2026, to submit a final report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly with recommendations related to preventing the fire hazards associated with commonly used fuel gas piping systems.
Title: Public Safety - Fuel Gas Piping Systems and Corrugated Stainless Steel Tubing - Prohibitions and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: Prohibits selling, offering for sale, transferring, or distributing non-arc-resistant jacketed corrugated stainless steel tubing failing specified safety standards. Restricts tubing used in natural gas or liquefied propane piping systems to products meeting the LC1027 standard. Establishes a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for sales or installation violations. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal to study piping fire hazards. Mandates submission of an interim report by December 1, 2025, and a final report by September 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of the State Fire Marshal
stakeholders: Manufacturers, sellers, distributors, and installers of corrugated stainless steel tubing and fuel gas piping systems, building contractors, and residential and commercial property owners
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,983 in FY 2026 and $22,124 in FY 2027 to hire one contractual engineer to conduct the required study and produce reports. State general fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties up to $1,000. Local government inspection entities can consult within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor, in conjunction with the Office of the State Fire Marshal, conduct a comprehensive study and issue interim and final reports on fire hazards associated with fuel gas piping systems and corrugated stainless steel tubing. The department incurs direct fiscal impacts to hire a contractual engineer to carry out the study.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are divisions within the Maryland Department of State Police. The bill explicitly charges the State Fire Marshal with co-leading the study, consulting with the State Fire Prevention Commission, and reporting recommendations on fuel gas piping fire hazards.

The bill requires the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal to submit both an interim report (by December 1, 2025) and a final report (by September 1, 2026) directly to the Governor regarding fuel gas piping system safety and regulatory recommendations.

The bill establishes civil penalties of up to $1,000 for the unlawful sale, transfer, distribution, or installation of prohibited corrugated stainless steel tubing, which may be adjudicated in the District Court system.

Synopsis: Creating an exception for vehicles carrying fluid milk products to the prohibition against driving a vehicle subject to an exceptional hauling permit on the interstate highway system; altering certain weight limits and tolerances under an exceptional hauling permit; altering the preventive maintenance documents that an individual operating under an exceptional hauling permit must possess; and altering certain record-keeping requirements and the application of certain administrative penalties under an exceptional hauling permit.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Exceptional Hauling Permits for Farm Products

NarrowSubjects.Name: Farmers and Farming -see also- Agriculture; Farmland
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes vehicles carrying fluid milk products under an exceptional hauling permit to operate on the interstate highway system. Modifies vehicle axle configuration and spacing eligibility criteria for combinations carrying farm products. Sets maximum gross weights at 88,000 pounds for five-axle combinations and 95,000 pounds for combinations with six or more axles. Repeals statutory load limit tolerances for gross combination weight and axle weights. Permits drivers to possess electronic permit copies and alters preventive maintenance inspection documentation requirements. Authorizes the State Highway Administration to suspend permit eligibility for noncompliant permit holders and motor carriers.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: motor carriers and commercial drivers transporting farm products, dairy farmers and agricultural producers, and law enforcement officers enforcing vehicle weight laws
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Transportation Trust Fund may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from additional permit application fees. State and local roadway preservation and maintenance expenditures may experience minimal and indeterminate impacts from changes in vehicle wear and tear.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SHA is the primary agency responsible for administering, issuing, and enforcing exceptional hauling permits for farm products, as well as promulgating implementing regulations and reviewing violations or revocations.
MDOT is the parent department of SHA and MDTA, submitted the bill as a departmental initiative, and exceptional hauling permit revenues accrue to the Transportation Trust Fund.

MSP officers and authorized personnel enforce commercial vehicle weight restrictions, are authorized to confiscate noncompliant permits, and the Secretary of State Police must be consulted by SHA on implementing regulations.
Maryland Transportation Authority Police officers are specifically authorized under the bill to immediately confiscate exceptional hauling permits for weight violations exceeding 5,000 pounds.
The bill directly modifies hauling permits and transport weight/route regulations for Maryland farm products and fluid milk, and MDA served as an information source on the legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to operate all schools within the county using a scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days to allow for less than 180 school days if the minimal hours of attendance are met; requiring the board, if it elects to use a scheduling model that results in a school in the county being open for less than 180 days, to offer certain school employees an opportunity to make up the lost wages; and requiring the Board to make a report on the schools using an alternative scheduling model.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Public Schools – School Schedule Options

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to operate all county public schools under an alternative scheduling model. Permits the model to eliminate early dismissal days and operate for fewer than 180 school days. Requires all schools using the model to meet regulatory minimal hours of attendance. Requires the county board to offer hourly school employees opportunities to make up lost wages through other duties. Mandates annual reports on alternative school schedules to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education; Maryland State Board of Education
stakeholders: Public school students, parents, teachers, and hourly school employees in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. There is no direct fiscal impact on Anne Arundel County because the bill is authorizing, and the school system can implement an alternative schedule using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts public school calendar and attendance requirements governed by state education law and regulations, and specifically mandates that the Anne Arundel County Board of Education report on the operation of any alternative school scheduling models to the State Board of Education.

Synopsis: Providing that certain unclaimed money held by an electric cooperative and due to a past member is not considered abandoned property; and authorizing an electric cooperative to use this money only to assist members of the cooperative or make donations to nonprofit, charitable organizations.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Electric Cooperatives - Nonescheat Capital Credits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: Exempts unclaimed nonescheat capital credits held by an electric cooperative from Maryland's abandoned property presumption. Defines nonescheat capital credits as unclaimed patronage funds retired at least five years earlier. Authorizes an electric cooperative to use these funds only to assist members or donate to approved nonprofit charities. Requires an electric cooperative to refund nonescheat capital credits upon application of a past member. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: electric cooperatives, past members of electric cooperatives, and nonprofit charitable organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential indeterminate decrease in Unclaimed Property Fund and General Fund revenues because nonescheat capital credits held by electric cooperatives will no longer be presumed abandoned and transferred to the State. State expenditures and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the State's abandoned property program under Title 17 of the Commercial Law Article. The bill amends this title to exempt nonescheat capital credits held by electric cooperatives from being presumed abandoned property, directly impacting the reporting and transfer of unclaimed property to the Comptroller and potentially reducing revenues to the Unclaimed Property Fund.

Synopsis: Expanding the purposes of the Maryland Veterans Trust to include providing monetary and other assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families; and authorizing the Maryland Veterans Trust to expend money from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to provide loans and grants to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families.
Title: Maryland Veterans Trust – Assistance to Members of the Maryland National Guard

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans

bill_summary: Expands the purposes of the Maryland Veterans Trust to assist members of the Maryland National Guard and their families. Authorizes the Trust to expend Maryland Veterans Trust Fund money for grants or loans to those individuals. Preserves existing authority to fund public and private programs supporting veterans and their families. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Veterans Trust; Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Veterans Trust Fund nonbudgeted expenditures increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2026 to provide additional grants and loans. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Veterans Trust is staffed by the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF), which processes grant and loan applications and will oversee the expanded eligibility and distribution of funds to Maryland National Guard members and their families.

The bill directly impacts members of the Maryland National Guard and their families by expanding the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund's eligibility criteria to provide them with monetary assistance, grants, and loans during temporary financial hardship.

The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, which submitted the departmental request for this legislation to secure financial assistance resources for Guard members under their command.

Synopsis: Altering the format and content of training on the requirements of the Maryland Public Ethics Law provided by the State Ethics Commission to certain State employees and regulated lobbyists to be either through online training or live presentation on the conflict of interest, financial disclosure, relevant administrative, and other applicable requirements of the law; and altering the scope of disclosure for the employment of an individual or a member of the individual's immediate family reported in a financial disclosure statement.
Title: Maryland Public Ethics Law - Training and Financial Disclosure Requirements - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Alters ethics training formats and financial disclosure requirements under the Maryland Public Ethics Law. Authorizes the State Ethics Commission to deliver required training through online training or live presentation. Repeals the mandate that ethics training courses for specified officials be at least two hours. Requires financial disclosure statements to list each source of compensated employment rather than salaried employment. Applies this disclosure obligation to employment of the individual and their immediate family members.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: State officials, public officials, candidates for State office, and regulated lobbyists
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact, as the State Ethics Commission can implement the bill with existing resources. Minimal local fiscal impact if local governments update their ethics laws.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 230 is a departmental bill requested by the State Ethics Commission. It directly alters the required format and duration of ethics training courses that the Commission conducts for public officials and regulated lobbyists, and expands the financial disclosure reporting requirements that the Commission administers and oversees.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Cyber Preparedness Unit in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management; altering the duties of the Office of Security Management in the Department of Information Technology; requiring the Office to submit a yearly report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly on the State's cybersecurity expenditures and recommendations for changes to the budget; and altering the responsibilities of the Secretary of Information Technology with regard to information technology policies.
Title: State Government - Information Technology - Cybersecurity Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the cybersecurity responsibilities of the Cyber Preparedness Unit and the Office of Security Management. Transfers the duty to support local government vulnerability and cyber assessments to the Office of Security Management. Expands the Office's authority to mitigate cybersecurity threats affecting or potentially affecting connected network entities. Requires the Secretary of Information Technology to implement information technology policies and a statewide cybersecurity strategy. Establishes a separate January annual reporting requirement on State cybersecurity expenditures and budget recommendations.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: units of State government and local governments, including local school systems, local school boards, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency; the bill alters the statutory duties of its Office of Security Management, shifts vulnerability assessment responsibilities to DoIT, revises annual reporting requirements, and expands the Secretary of Information Technology's responsibilities for statewide cybersecurity strategy implementation.

The bill directly alters the statutory duties of the Cyber Preparedness Unit within MDEM, transferring certain vulnerability assessment responsibilities to DoIT and refining its focus on local emergency planning, resources, and consequence management.

The bill mandates annual reporting directly to the Governor regarding state cybersecurity expenditures, budget recommendations, and preparedness across state and local entities, including special reporting timelines in years with a newly elected Governor.
The Maryland National Guard is explicitly designated in statute to coordinate with MDEM and DoIT when conducting regional cybersecurity preparedness exercises.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the National Guard, the Adjutant General's command coordinates with emergency management and IT officials for regional cybersecurity preparedness exercises.

Synopsis: Expanding the relief that may be included in a final peace order; altering the acts that constitute criminal harassment to include certain visual surveillance of an area of another person's residence where the other has a reasonable expectation of privacy; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction for a first offense is subject to imprisonment of up to 90 days or a fine of $500 or both, and for a second or subsequent offense, imprisonment of up to 180 days or a fine of $1,000 or both.
Title: Peace Orders and Criminal Harassment - Intentional Visual Surveillance
bill_summary: Expands criminal harassment to include visual surveillance of a residence where another has a reasonable expectation of privacy. Imposes misdemeanor penalties of up to 90 days imprisonment and a $500 fine for a first offense. Imposes up to 180 days imprisonment and a $1,000 fine for second or subsequent offenses. Authorizes courts issuing final peace orders for visual surveillance to order device removal or repositioning within 15 days. Permits final peace orders to require respondents to refrain from further visual surveillance.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Petitioners and respondents in peace order proceedings, residential occupants, and individuals accused of criminal harassment
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $29,600 in FY 2026 only for Judiciary software updates. Local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary and court operations by expanding peace order relief options and altering peace order proceedings. The fiscal note identifies a general fund expenditure increase of $29,600 in FY 2026 for programming changes to update court computer systems and peace order forms.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of criminal harassment under § 3-803 of the Criminal Law Article, which carries potential penalties of up to 90 or 180 days imprisonment. The Office of the Public Defender provides legal defense to indigent individuals facing incarcerable criminal charges and was consulted as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Secretary of State to suspend payment of certain late fees assessed to certain charitable organizations that fail to file an annual report under certain circumstances; and authorizing the Secretary of State to cancel a charitable organization's registration or reinstate a charitable organization's canceled registration under certain circumstances.
Title: Charitable Organizations - Late Fees and Registration - Suspension and Cancellation Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of State to suspend or waive late fees assessed against charitable organizations failing to file annual reports. Prohibits treating assessed late fees as delinquent debts requiring referral to the Central Collection Unit. Authorizes the Secretary of State to cancel the registration of a charitable organization that fails to submit required reports for three years. Requires the Secretary of State to send notice of cancellation to the organization's last known address and email address. Establishes requirements for a charitable organization to request reinstatement of a canceled registration.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
stakeholders: charitable organizations registered or required to register in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected because the provisions governing late fee suspensions and waivers conform statute to current administrative practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary administering agency of the bill. It authorizes the Secretary of State to suspend or waive charitable organization late fees, adopt implementing regulations, cancel registrations after three years of noncompliance, and process reinstatement requests.

The Department of Budget and Management houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU). The bill explicitly provides that charitable late fees assessed under the subtitle are not deemed delinquent debts requiring referral to CCU for collection.

The Office of the Attorney General partners with the Secretary of State on charitable enforcement actions and shares distributions from the Charitable Enforcement Fund, which is funded in part by the late fees addressed in the bill.

Synopsis: Clarifying that "spouse" includes a former spouse for purposes of disclosure of confidential communications occurring during marriage; and establishing that a spouse, who is the alleged victim, is competent to disclose a confidential communication between spouses occurring during their marriage in a criminal action in which one spouse is charged with a crime against the other spouse.
Title: Marriage - Confidential Communication

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Clarifies that spouse includes a former spouse regarding confidential communications occurring during marriage. Establishes that an alleged victim spouse is competent to disclose confidential marital communications in certain criminal actions. Applies this exception when one spouse faces criminal charges for a crime against the other spouse. Prohibits compelling a spouse to testify to a confidential communication under this exception. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Spouses and former spouses who are alleged victims or criminal defendants, prosecutors, and criminal defense attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: Procedural measure with no anticipated material effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters evidentiary rules and spousal competency regarding confidential marital communications in criminal proceedings overseen by the state court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an exception to the marital communications privilege in criminal cases where a spouse is an alleged victim, directly impacting criminal defense strategies and trial proceedings for public defender clients.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals where evidentiary questions regarding the marital communications privilege and spousal competency are litigated.

Synopsis: Limiting the requirement that a petitioner's spouse join in the petition for adoption to apply only when the prospective adoptee is a minor; authorizing a petitioner's spouse to join in the petition for adoption if the prospective adoptee is an adult; establishing that certain provisions of law requiring the issuance and service of a show-cause order on a prospective adoptee's parents do not apply if the prospective adoptee is an adult; etc.
Title: Family Law - Adoption of an Adult

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- FamLaw; FosterCare; ParentsGuardians
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Alters independent adoption procedures when the prospective adoptee is an adult. Limits the requirement that a petitioner's spouse join the petition strictly to adoptions of minors. Authorizes a petitioner's spouse to join an adoption petition if the prospective adoptee is an adult. Exempts adult adoptions from parental consent requirements and mandatory show-cause orders to biological parents. Authorizes a court to order pre-ruling investigations in adult adoptions only for good cause shown.
responsible_party: Maryland Circuit Courts
stakeholders: adult adoptees, prospective adoptive parents, and spouses of adoption petitioners
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters judicial procedures for independent adoption proceedings in the circuit courts when the prospective adoptee is an adult, removing parental consent and show-cause order requirements and restricting pre-ruling investigations to cases where good cause is shown.

DHS oversees state adoption policy and child placement services and maintains the website used for public notices under certain adoption proceedings; the bill exempts adult adoptions from these show-cause notice and parental consent requirements.

Synopsis: Specifying that certain provisions of law relating to confidentiality do not prohibit the disclosure of certain information relating to adult protective services or the disclosure of the identity of certain persons making certain reports under certain circumstances; expanding the definition of "health practitioner" to include certain emergency medical providers; and authorizing individuals who are required in specific instances to report information regarding alleged vulnerable adults to make a report by calling the statewide reporting hotline.
Title: Human Services - Adult Protective Services

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Authorizes disclosure of adult protective services information to federal, state, or local government investigators when relevant to an official investigation. Permits disclosing the identity of an individual reporting vulnerable adult abuse or neglect under the same disclosure standards. Expands the definition of health practitioner to include emergency medical services providers while excluding emergency medical dispatchers. Designates covered emergency medical services providers as mandatory reporters of suspected vulnerable adult abuse, neglect, or exploitation. Authorizes mandatory reporters to submit reports by calling the statewide reporting hotline.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
stakeholders: alleged vulnerable adults, emergency medical services providers (excluding emergency medical dispatchers), health practitioners, human service workers, and government investigators
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local entities involved in investigations regarding vulnerable adults may experience operational efficiencies, but the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS requested this departmental bill and administers the Adult Protective Services (APS) program through local departments of social services, which will directly implement the updated disclosure exceptions and reporting hotline procedures.

The Department of Aging advocates for older and vulnerable adults, oversees the Long-Term Care Ombudsman program (referenced in the statute), and collaborates closely with local APS programs on investigations and protective services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the definition of 'health practitioner' to include EMS providers licensed or certified under § 13-516 of the Education Article (excluding dispatchers), making EMS personnel regulated under MIEMSS mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse.
MDH regulates health professionals who are mandatory reporters under the Health Occupations Article and provides behavioral health and public health oversight for vulnerable adults.

State Police officers are mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse and frequently conduct joint or related investigations with APS, benefiting from the clarified confidentiality and information-sharing provisions.
The judiciary handles court-ordered disclosures of confidential APS records and criminal or civil proceedings arising from vulnerable adult abuse investigations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a local jurisdiction from enforcing a law or ordinance that limits the summoning of law enforcement or emergency services to a residential property by establishing a certain threshold or penalty.
Title: Residential Real Property - Local Limits on Summoning Law Enforcement or Emergency Services

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Prohibits county and municipal governing bodies from enforcing local laws that limit summoning law enforcement or emergency services. Bars enforcing ordinances that designate a residential property as a nuisance based on emergency call thresholds. Prohibits penalizing operators, owners, owner-occupants, or tenants when someone summons emergency or police assistance to a residential property. Authorizes affected operators, owners, owner-occupants, or tenants to raise violations as legal defenses or claims for damages. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Residential property owners, operators, owner-occupants, tenants, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows property owners, operators, and tenants to raise violations of the statute as a defense or as an affirmative claim for damages in court, authorizing the courts to adjudicate these claims and award damages, attorney's fees, and other relief.

Synopsis: Altering the frequency, from once every 3 years to an interval of once every 4 years unless it is determined on a case-by-case basis that an audit occur at an interval of 3 years, with which the Office of the Inspector General in the Department of Human Services conducts or contracts for financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services.
Title: Human Services – Local Departments of Social Services – Audits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the frequency of financial and compliance audits for local departments of social services. Sets the standard audit interval conducted by the Office of the Inspector General at four years. Authorizes the Office to determine on a case-by-case basis that an audit occur every three years. Requires the Office to evaluate materiality, fiscal risk profiles, and prior audit findings when determining intervals. Mandates the distribution of written audit reports to the local board and local governing authority. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

bill_summary: Restructures the West North Avenue Development Authority as an instrumentality of the State to revitalize designated corridors in Baltimore City. Establishes a board of directors to manage the Authority and carry out specified development powers. Creates the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund for administrative expenses. Exempts the Authority from state and local transfer and recordation taxes and general state procurement law. Requires the Authority to become self-sustaining beginning in fiscal year 2028. Extends the termination date of the Authority to September 30, 2029.
responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and commercial businesses in the West North Avenue corridor in Baltimore City, as well as community development corporations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $82,614 in FY 2026 from a contingent appropriation, and may increase by at least $21.2 million in FY 2027 based on discretionary funding expectations. Special fund expenditures increase by at least $260,000 in FY 2027. Baltimore City finances may be affected through discretionary city contributions and property tax base alterations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or the Secretary's designee) is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the West North Avenue Development Authority.
The Secretary of Transportation (or the Secretary's designee) is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Secretary of Commerce (or the Secretary's designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the West North Avenue Development Authority, and the agency provided information for the fiscal analysis.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or the Executive Director's designee) is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Authority.

The President of Coppin State University (a member institution of the University System of Maryland), or the President's designee, is designated by statute to serve as a member and the chair of the Board of Directors of the Authority.
The bill creates the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest the fund's monies.
The bill creates the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and assigns responsibility to the Comptroller to account for the fund.
The Governor is authorized to appoint one member to the Authority's Board of Directors and is authorized to include discretionary appropriations to the Authority in the annual State budget bill.

The bill specifically exempts the Authority from Title 3 (Budget and Management) and allows the Authority to set salaries outside the State Personnel and Pension System, directly impacting state budget and personnel oversight.
The bill explicitly exempts the Authority from Title 4 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which governs the Department of General Services.

The bill explicitly exempts the Authority from Title 5A of the State Finance and Procurement Article (Division of Historical and Cultural Programs), which resides within the Maryland Department of Planning.

The bill explicitly exempts the Authority from Title 10 of the State Finance and Procurement Article (Board of Public Works - Miscellaneous Provisions) as well as standard state procurement requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Authority is subject to Title 14, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article governing the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program, which the office oversees.
The bill explicitly specifies that the Authority, its officers, and its employees are subject to the Maryland Public Ethics Law enforced by the State Ethics Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain DNA sample to be collected in a certain manner from an individual who is required to register as a sex offender; requiring a DNA sample to be collected by a certain individual or at a certain location under certain circumstances; requiring a custodial agency or correctional facility to ensure a DNA sample is collected in a certain manner; prohibiting a DNA sample from being tested and placed in a certain statewide DNA database system until certain conditions are met; etc.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires DNA sample collection from individuals required to register as sex offenders at initial registration. Mandates custodial agencies and correctional facilities to ensure required DNA collection before releasing individuals from custody. Restricts DNA testing for charged individuals until probable cause is found, an arrest warrant issues, or formal charges are filed. Prohibits an individual from refusing to provide a required DNA sample, establishing a misdemeanor with a maximum $1,000 fine. Requires automatic expungement and destruction of qualifying untested DNA samples that fail testing requirements after two years.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Individuals required to register as sex offenders, criminal defendants charged with or convicted of qualifying offenses, correctional facilities, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected and implementation is expected to be handled within existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are unaffected; most local jurisdictions can implement the bill with existing resources, though Montgomery County reported potential local expenditure increases of approximately $200,000 annually for correctional staff.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of State Police. The DSP Forensic Sciences Division (Crime Laboratory) administers the Statewide DNA Database System, establishes regulations for DNA collection and testing, and is directly responsible for processing, storing, expunging, and destroying DNA samples.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates state correctional facilities and community supervision units. The bill mandates that correctional facilities collect DNA samples at intake, custodial agencies ensure samples are collected prior to an individual's release, and supervising authorities collect samples from individuals required to register as sex offenders.

The bill shifts the trigger for testing arrestee DNA samples to judicial determinations of probable cause by District Court commissioners or judges, allows sample collection at circuit courts following sentencing, and involves court orders regarding expungements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants charged with qualifying offenses who are required to submit DNA samples. The bill affects client rights regarding DNA collection, testing consent prior to probable cause determinations, notifications of sample destruction or expungement, and establishes a misdemeanor offense for refusal to provide a sample.

The OAG acts as primary legal counsel to the Department of State Police, advising the Crime Laboratory on statutory interpretations and compliance regarding the legal testing, retention, and expungement of arrestee DNA samples.

bill_summary: Reduces criminal penalties for drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia offenses throughout the State. Decreases subsequent violation penalties for drug paraphernalia possession, delivery, or sale to one year imprisonment and a $1,000 fine. Repeals the misdemeanor prohibition against possessing controlled paraphernalia intended for illegally administering a controlled dangerous substance. Establishes a maximum fine of $500 for a first controlled paraphernalia offense without incarceration. Lowers subsequent penalties for controlled paraphernalia violations to one year imprisonment and a $1,000 maximum fine. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: individuals charged with or convicted of drug paraphernalia or controlled paraphernalia offenses; law enforcement officers; criminal defense attorneys; state prosecutors
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected due to the low number of convictions for the altered offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters criminal penalties for drug and controlled paraphernalia offenses, creating a fine-only penalty for a first violation of § 5-620. As the agency that provides legal defense when incarceration is a possibility, OPD experiences reduced eligible caseloads for these offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reduces maximum terms of imprisonment for subsequent drug paraphernalia offenses and controlled paraphernalia offenses, directly affecting individuals committed to state correctional facilities or supervised by the Division of Parole and Probation.

The bill modifies criminal penalties, elements of offenses, and sentencing maximums for drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia cases adjudicated across Maryland's District and Circuit courts.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing criminal laws, State Police troopers are operationally impacted by changes to paraphernalia offenses and charging protocols, such as issuing criminal citations for fine-only first violations.

Synopsis: Prioritizing the payment of unpaid child support over certain other claims on an estate of a decedent with insufficient assets to pay all claims in full.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Priority of Claims on an Estate - Unpaid Child Support

NarrowSubjects.Name: Family Law -see also- Adoption; Alimony; Annulment; etc.

bill_summary: Prioritizes the payment of unpaid child support due by a decedent over certain other estate claims. Places unpaid child support sixth in the statutory order of priority for claims against an estate. Ranks child support claims immediately after family allowances and ahead of taxes due by the decedent. Requires personal representatives to satisfy claims according to this order when estate assets cannot cover all debts. Prohibits preferences between claims of the same class or claims not yet due.
responsible_party: Personal representatives; Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Custodial parents and children owed child support by decedents, personal representatives of estates, and estate creditors including state and local tax authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential but likely limited decrease in State and local revenues if prioritizing child support reduces payments for taxes or public assistance recovery. Expenditures are unaffected, and specific revenue estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills oversees the administrative probate of decedents' estates, where claims against an estate and the statutory priority order of payments under § 8-105 of the Estates and Trusts Article are directly applied and reviewed.

The Department of Human Services administers child support enforcement services across Maryland, which directly benefits from unpaid child support claims receiving higher priority. DHS also administers the Public Assistance to Adults Program, which ranks lower in the statutory order of estate claims.

As the state's tax collector, the Comptroller may experience a reduction in recovered delinquent state taxes from insolvent estates because the bill places unpaid child support ahead of 'taxes due by the decedent'.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Orphans' Courts and Circuit Courts, which adjudicate contested estate claims, creditor priorities, and child support arrearage enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

The Governor is responsible for appointing the majority of the members to the Maryland Agricultural Commission under the revised statutory categories.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, which includes the reconstituted membership categories on the Maryland Agricultural Commission.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland designates an ex officio member to serve as the principal administrative official for agricultural affairs on the Maryland Agricultural Commission.
