bill_summary: Expands eligibility for Higher Education Loan Assistance Grants under the Maryland Dent-Care Program to part-time dentists and dental hygienists. Requires the Office of Student Financial Assistance and the Maryland Department of Health to establish prorated grant amounts. Permits recipients to hold the grant for up to three years while employed full time or part time. Requires participating practitioners to maintain a patient caseload of at least 30% Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Part-time dentists, part-time dental hygienists, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $6,000 in fiscal 2026 for one-time computer aid processing system modifications at the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The Maryland Department of Health can handle additional applicant processing with existing resources. No effect on local finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program and the Higher Education Loan Assistance Grants. The bill requires MHEC to expand eligibility to part-time dentists and dental hygienists, update award systems, and adopt regulations establishing prorated grant amounts in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health.

MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary state entity responsible for administering higher education loan assistance grants under the Maryland Dent-Care Program, updating award rules, and collaborating with MDH on establishing prorated award amounts for part-time participants.

The Maryland Department of Health (specifically its Office of Oral Health) is statutory partner in the Maryland Dent-Care Program, responsible for processing applications, verifying practice requirements, notifying OSFA for awards, and collaborating with MHEC to determine prorated grant amounts and adopt regulations.

Synopsis: Altering provisions of law related to a hospital's financial assistance and collection of debts policies; specifying the percentage by which a hospital is required to reduce a patient's out-of-pocket expenses under certain circumstances; adding to the notice requirements relating to a hospital's financial assistance policy; prohibiting a hospital from filing a civil action to collect a debt against a patient whose outstanding debt is at or below $500; etc.
Title: Hospitals - Financial Assistance and Collection of Debts - Policies

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: Alters hospital financial assistance and medical debt collection requirements across Maryland. Requires hospitals to reduce out-of-pocket expenses by specified percentages for eligible patients with incomes up to 500% of the federal poverty level. Prohibits hospitals from filing civil debt collection actions for outstanding patient balances at or below $500. Extends the minimum timeframe before hospitals may assess interest or file collection lawsuits from 180 to 240 days. Excludes hospital consumer debt contracts under seal from the 12-year statute of limitations for specialties.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Acute care and chronic care hospitals, hospital patients with medical debt, low-income patients, debt collection agencies, commercial health insurers, and Medicaid recipients
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State Medicaid expenditures (40% general funds, 60% federal funds) and federal matching revenues beginning as early as FY 2026, driven by potential increases in hospital rates to fund additional uncompensated care. Administrative workloads for the Health Services Cost Review Commission can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing the bill, which requires HSCRC to establish guidelines for hospital income-based payment plans, review hospital debt collection and financial assistance policies, compile annual medical debt reports, and adjust hospital rate structures to account for uncompensated care.

HSCRC is an independent commission housed within MDH. Additionally, MDH administers the Medicaid program, which is anticipated to see an increase in state and federal expenditures beginning as early as FY 2026 due to hospital rate adjustments resulting from increased uncompensated care.

The bill statutorily requires hospitals to provide contact information for the Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) within the Office of the Attorney General on notices and bills, directing consumers to HEAU for assistance and mediation regarding medical debt and financial assistance denials.

The bill alters the statute of limitations under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article for certain consumer debt arising from hospital services and establishes new evidentiary and procedural requirements, restrictions, and timelines for hospitals filing civil debt collection actions in state courts.

Limits county plan reviews submitted by the Department of the Environment to water and sewerage proposals only. Requires the Department of Planning to prepare municipal population projections only on request of a municipal corporation. Restricts the Department's real property repository obligations solely to State-owned real property. Repeals statutory provisions regarding capital facilities land entry, regional planning funding allocations, and statewide geographic classification standards.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; State Administrator of Elections; Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Planning; local boards of elections; municipal corporations; county governments; regional planning councils
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 272 is a departmental modernization bill specifically revising and streamlining the statutory duties, reporting obligations, population projection schedules, and property data repositories of the Department of Planning.

The bill establishes a statutory requirement directing the State Administrator of Elections to electronically transmit maps and descriptions of new or modified precinct boundaries to the Secretary of Planning upon receipt from local boards.

The bill alters statutory requirements governing the Department of the Environment's county plan review process, limiting the required submission of county plans to the Department of Planning to water and sewerage proposals only.

Synopsis: Altering a prohibition concerning the maximum penalty for the late payment of rent that a landlord may charge in a residential lease to prohibit a penalty in excess of 5% of the amount of the unpaid rent rather than of the amount due.
Title: Residential Leases - Late Payment Penalties - Calculation
bill_summary: Prohibits residential landlords from including lease provisions charging late fees over 5% of the unpaid rent. Changes the penalty calculation basis from the total rent due to the delinquent unpaid rent amount. Retains the late penalty limits for weekly rental installments at $3 per week or $12 per month. Renders prohibited lease provisions unenforceable by the landlord. Authorizes tenants to recover actual damages and reasonable attorney's fees if landlords attempt to enforce prohibited provisions. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts); Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: residential tenants, residential landlords, and property management companies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces consumer protection and landlord-tenant statutes regarding unfair or deceptive trade practices, including illegal lease provisions and unauthorized fee assessments under the Real Property Article.

The Maryland Judiciary handles residential landlord-tenant dispute cases, including actions for failure to pay rent and civil actions brought by tenants seeking damages for prohibited lease provisions.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "adjusted actual income" under the State child support guidelines by requiring the deduction, from actual income, of an allowance for support for each child in the parent's home for whom the parent owes a legal duty of support but who is not subject to a support order; requiring that the amount of a certain allowance be subtracted from a parent's actual income before the court determines the amount of a child support award; etc.
Title: Family Law - Child Support - Multifamily Adjustment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Alters the definition of adjusted actual income under the State child support guidelines. Establishes a deduction for each additional child living in a parent's home not subject to the support order. Applies this deduction if the child spends more than 92 overnights per year in the parent's home. Calculates the allowance by multiplying 75% by the basic child support obligation using only that parent's actual income. Requires the court to decline the allowance if the deduction would be unjust or inappropriate. Alters factors courts may consider in determining whether applying the child support guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Judiciary
stakeholders: Parents paying or receiving child support, children subject to child support orders, and additional dependent children living in a parent's household.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by up to $297,600 in FY 2026 ($101,200 general funds and $196,400 federal funds) for Department of Human Services computer system programming costs, offset by $196,400 in matching federal fund revenues. Ongoing maintenance costs are estimated at $56,500 annually beginning in FY 2027 ($19,200 general funds and $37,300 federal funds). Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees the State's Child Support Enforcement Administration. The bill alters the statutory child support calculation formula, requiring system reprogramming and maintenance costs estimated at up to $297,600 in FY 2026 and $56,500 annually thereafter.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch. State judges and court masters must apply the altered child support guidelines and new multifamily adjustment formulas when establishing or modifying child support orders.

bill_summary: Requires installation of a water bottle filling station or combined unit in certain new construction and renovations. Mandates these fixtures at locations where plumbing codes require drinking fountains, beginning October 1, 2025. Requires replacing drinking fountains with filling stations during renovations that involve replacing those fountains. Exempts certain commercial or industrial buildings that have alternative potable water sources or replace fountains without other renovations. Directs the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Commercial and residential property owners, building developers, plumbing contractors, and building occupants
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures and revenues are not significantly affected. The Maryland Department of Labor can adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 277 explicitly directs the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt regulations to implement and carry out the provisions requiring water bottle filling stations in new construction and specified renovations, directly interfacing with the State Plumbing Code and the State Board of Plumbing overseen by the department.

The bill adds a new subtitle to the Environment Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland governing water bottle filling stations connected to potable water distribution systems, which falls within the broad statutory domain administered by the Department of the Environment.

The Department of General Services is responsible for the planning, design, construction, and maintenance of state-owned facilities, and will need to ensure that future state building projects and major renovations comply with the new plumbing fixture requirements.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities annexing property; Maryland Department of Planning; property owners and businesses in annexed municipal areas
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 279 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Planning. It specifically adds the department to the list of entities that must receive municipal annexation resolutions within 10 days of taking effect, and mandates that the department keep them on record and make them available for public inspection.

SponsorPrimary: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Sponsors.Name: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Synopsis: Specifying that fees collected for electronic transactions for procurements are those due to the State and not any fees due to a third party.
Title: Procurement – Electronic Transactions – Clarification of Fees Due

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Clarifies that only electronic procurement transaction fees due to the State must be deposited into the Operations Revenue Fund. Permits private contractors furnishing electronic procurement systems to retain their own service fees. Retains requirements for fee approval by the Chief Procurement Officer and the Board of Public Works. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Board of Public Works; Chief Procurement Officer
stakeholders: Private contractors furnishing electronic procurement systems, bidders and offerors on State procurement contracts, and primary State procurement units
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill is clarifying in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT requested this departmental legislation to resolve statutory ambiguities regarding third-party vendor fees, enabling the department to continue using its preferred electronic procurement platform (BidX) for transportation-related procurements.

DGS houses the Office of State Procurement and the Chief Procurement Officer, who must approve electronic procurement fees, and administers the Operations Revenue Fund where state-due fees are deposited.

The Board of Public Works must approve any fees charged for conducting electronic procurements under the statute and previously advised MDOT that continued use of third-party platforms could be prohibited without this statutory clarification.

Synopsis: Providing certain planning principles that are collectively intended to create sustainable communities and to protect the environment utilizing active public participation; altering the State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy to consist of planning principles for advancing sustainable growth in the State; and requiring the publisher of the Annotated Code of Maryland, along with the Department of Legislative Services, to correct cross-references and terminology in the Code that are rendered incorrect by the Act.
Title: Local Comprehensive Planning and State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy - Planning Principles

Smart Growth -see also- Zoning and Planning

bill_summary: Replaces the 12 statutory planning visions for local comprehensive planning and State growth policy with eight planning principles. Identifies the eight planning principles as land, transportation, housing, economy, equity, resilience, place, and ecology. Requires local planning commissions to implement the principles through local comprehensive plans. Updates criteria for Board of Public Works approval of growth-related transportation projects outside priority funding areas. Directs the code publisher and the Department of Legislative Services to correct resulting statutory cross-references.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; Board of Public Works; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: County and municipal governments, local planning commissions, land use planners, property owners, and Maryland small businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not expected to have a direct, material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Departmental sponsor of the bill; MDP oversees state planning policy, coordinates local comprehensive planning guidelines, and jointly evaluates transportation projects outside priority funding areas against the newly established planning principles.

Statutorily tasked under § 5-7B-05, in conjunction with the Department of Planning, to determine whether growth-related transportation projects connecting priority funding areas comply with the updated State planning principles.

Directly referenced in statute as the approval authority for transportation projects connecting priority funding areas, evaluated in accordance with the revised State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy.
The multi-agency initiative is grounded in the State's statutory planning visions, which this bill directly amends by repealing the 12 visions and replacing them with 8 planning principles.

Synopsis: Increasing from 180 days to 300 days the maximum duration of an emergency status determination authorizing the temporary adjustment of tolls, fees, or other charges by the Maryland Transportation Authority.
Title: Maryland Transportation Authority – Tolls, Fees, and Other Charges – Temporary Adjustments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Increases the maximum duration of an emergency status determination by the Maryland Transportation Authority from 180 days to 300 days. Authorizes the Authority to maintain temporary adjustments to tolls, fees, mileage rate ranges, pricing periods, and toll zones during emergency status. Requires the Authority to post website notice and immediately begin public comment procedures upon adopting emergency adjustments. Terminates temporary adjustments adopted under an emergency determination immediately when the emergency status expires. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
stakeholders: Motorists and commercial vehicle operators using Maryland Transportation Authority toll facilities, MDTA bondholders, and state and local government agencies that pay toll charges
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential indeterminate increase in MDTA nonbudgeted revenues as early as FY 2026 due to emergency rate increases persisting up to 120 days longer. State and local government expenditures may also increase if fleet vehicles incur emergency tolls or fees for an extended duration.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 288 directly amends the statutory powers of the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) by extending the maximum duration of an emergency status determination for temporary toll and fee adjustments from 180 days to 300 days, allowing MDTA sufficient time to complete statutory public notice and comment requirements during emergencies.
The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) encompasses and coordinates with MDTA, submitted the legislation as a departmental bill, and prepared the accompanying economic impact analyses.

Synopsis: Requiring that certain funds for certain reserve accounts be deposited on or before the last day of each fiscal year; requiring the governing body of a cooperative housing corporation, a residential condominium, or a homeowners association to prepare a certain funding plan subject to certain requirements; authorizing a reasonable deviation from certain reserve funding requirements following a certain financial hardship determination; requiring that certain updated reserve studies be prepared by a certain person; etc.
Title: Cooperative Housing Corporations, Condominiums, and Homeowners Associations - Funding of Reserve Accounts and Preparation of Funding Plans

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Alters reserve account funding and reserve study requirements for cooperative housing corporations, residential condominiums, and homeowners associations. Extends the timeframe to attain recommended reserve funding levels from three to five fiscal years following an initial study. Authorizes governing bodies to deviate from reserve funding requirements for one fiscal year upon determining financial hardship. Requires governing bodies to develop a reserve funding plan prioritizing essential repairs, occupant safety, and structural integrity. Requires depositing designated reserve funds on or before the last day of each fiscal year. Authorizes using reserve funds for other purposes if the funds are repaid within five years.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of cooperative housing corporations, residential condominiums, and homeowners associations
stakeholders: Cooperative housing corporations, residential condominiums, homeowners associations, and their members, unit owners, and lot owners
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces consumer protection laws and handles complaints and disputes related to common ownership communities, including condominiums, cooperatives, and homeowners associations governed by these reserve requirements.

The Department of Labor oversees professional licensing boards, including the State Board of Architects and the State Board for Professional Engineers, whose licensees are explicitly qualified under the bill to prepare reserve studies and consult on funding plans.

The Secretary of State holds regulatory and registration responsibilities regarding residential condominiums in Maryland, which are directly subject to the reserve study and funding plan provisions amended by the bill.

Synopsis: Altering a certain requirement under which a court is authorized to order that the testimony of a child victim be taken outside a courtroom and shown in the courtroom by closed circuit television in certain child abuse cases; requiring the testimony of a child victim taken by closed circuit television within the courthouse be in a setting that reasonably mitigates the likelihood the child victim will suffer emotional distress; etc.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Child Victims - Testimony in Child Abuse Cases

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Alters the standard for allowing a child victim to testify outside the courtroom by closed circuit television. Repeals the requirement that the child victim's serious emotional distress prevent reasonable communication. Requires closed circuit testimony to occur within the courthouse in a setting that mitigates emotional distress. Requires a means for defendants or child respondents to communicate privately, orally, and in real time with counsel. Prohibits courts from ordering any procedure that allows a child victim to see or hear the defendant.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Child victims of abuse, criminal defendants, child respondents, prosecutors, and defense attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: Not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures regarding when and how child abuse victims may testify outside the courtroom via closed-circuit television or remote technology, requiring courthouses to accommodate suitable settings and technology for real-time private attorney-client communication.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts defense practice in child abuse and juvenile delinquency cases, altering the legal standard for allowing closed-circuit testimony of child victims and requiring that defense attorneys have the means to communicate privately in real time with their clients during such testimony.

The bill governs testimony in child abuse cases under Title 5, Subtitle 7 of the Family Law Article and Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings, which are initiated and managed by local departments of social services under the Department of Human Services.

Synopsis: Renaming the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program to be the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program; repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law that establish and govern the funding for the Program; authorizing rather than requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to establish and implement the Program; and prohibiting the Exchange from implementing the Program if certain funds are not available.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program - Sunset Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Repeals the termination date of the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program, making the program permanent. Renames the pilot program by removing reference to its pilot status. Authorizes rather than requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to establish and implement the program. Prohibits the Exchange from implementing the program in calendar years when provider fee assessment funds are unavailable. Authorizes the Exchange to designate funds from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund for annual subsidies beginning in calendar year 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: young adults ages 18 through 40 purchasing individual health benefit plans in Maryland with household incomes between 133% and 400% of the federal poverty level
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $13.0 million in FY 2026, $26.0 million each in FY 2027 and FY 2028, and $13.0 million in FY 2029 to provide subsidies through calendar 2028. Funding is drawn from the 1% health insurance provider fee assessment and prior program reserves. Special fund revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill permanently authorizes and governs the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program, which is administered and operated directly by the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange using special funds from the MHBE Fund.

The Maryland Insurance Administration, headed by the Insurance Commissioner, is statutorily required to be consulted by MHBE when establishing subsidy eligibility, payment parameters, and designating fund amounts for the program.

Synopsis: Altering the rate at which nonprofit organizations receiving State-funded grants or contracts may be reimbursed for indirect costs to match the rate established under relevant federal guidelines; requiring the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council to study and make certain recommendations to the Department of Budget and Management regarding the entire grants life cycle; requiring the Council to submit a report on its full recommendations to the Department and the General Assembly by July 1, 2027; etc.
Title: State Government - Grants and Contracts - Reimbursement of Indirect Costs

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the reimbursement rate for indirect costs on certain State-funded grants and contracts awarded to nonprofit organizations. Applies to nonprofits providing services funded wholly or partially with State funds without a negotiated indirect cost rate. Sets the reimbursement rate at the greater of the federal de minimis rate or 15% of modified total direct costs. Replaces the previous statutory minimum reimbursement rate of 10%. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Tax-exempt nonprofit organizations receiving State-funded grants or contracts, State grant-making agencies, and local government pass-through entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on total State revenues or expenditures. State agencies and local pass-through entities must allow eligible nonprofit grantees to allocate at least 5% more of award funding toward indirect costs, likely with no material diminution in services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is explicitly referenced in the bill as the department receiving recommendations from the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council regarding uniform guidance regulations and statewide grants management. In addition, DBM oversees state fiscal planning, budget execution, and overall efficiency in state operations.

The Governor's Grants Office serves as the state's central resource for grant management standards, compliance, and best practices for state agencies and nonprofits, directly aligning with this bill's changes to indirect cost reimbursement rates and OMB Uniform Guidance standards.

DGS is the state's central procurement authority responsible for policies and oversight governing state contracts, which are directly impacted by statutory rules regarding nonprofit contract cost reimbursements under the State Finance and Procurement Article.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts and expenditures, which must comply with state procurement laws governing indirect cost reimbursement rates for nonprofit contractors and grantees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, an executive council established to examine the grants life cycle and recommend uniform guidance regulations, is referenced and directly tasked with ongoing reporting requirements under Section 2-210.

Synopsis: Altering and clarifying the requirement that a sworn affidavit for judicial authorization to initiate forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search (FGGS) assert that the reasonable investigative leads have been pursued and failed to identify the perpetrator and instead requiring that a sworn affidavit for judicial authorization assert that identity of the perpetrator is unknown.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Forensic Genetic Genealogical DNA Analysis and Search - Affidavit for Judicial Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Alters requirements for judicial authorization to initiate a forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search. Requires a law enforcement agent's sworn affidavit to assert that the perpetrator's identity is unknown. Repeals the prior requirement to assert that reasonable investigative leads were pursued and failed. Clarifies that investigators are not required to exhaust all investigative leads before seeking authorization. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of State Police; State's Attorneys' Offices
stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, State's Attorneys, criminal investigators, criminal defendants, and crime victims.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency investigating homicides, sexual assaults, and other severe crimes, MSP investigators submit sworn affidavits seeking judicial authorization to initiate forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and searches.
The bill alters the statutory standards and affidavit contents required for state courts to grant judicial authorization for forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and searches.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in serious criminal proceedings where FGGS evidence may be introduced, and its attorneys evaluate compliance with statutory affidavit and authorization requirements.

The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals and advises on state criminal procedure laws, which may involve challenges to the legality of judicial authorizations granted under altered affidavit standards.

Synopsis: Expanding certain provisions of law relating to a certain investigation and recommendation by a State's Attorney concerning the filing of a statement of charges against certain professionals to include certain human service workers.
Title: Courts and Judicial Proceedings - Statement of Charges - Human Service Workers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Extends pre-charge investigation protections to adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers. Requires District Court applications for charges against these workers for job-related offenses to go immediately to the State's Attorney. Directs the State's Attorney to investigate the matter and recommend whether to file a statement of charges. Requires the State's Attorney to recommend whether a summons or warrant should issue if charges are recommended. Prohibits filing a statement of charges until the State's Attorney completes the investigation and recommendations.
responsible_party: Office of the State's Attorney; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers facing criminal allegations arising from their official duties
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local finances or operations, including the Judiciary, circuit courts, and State's Attorneys' offices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides procedural protections against criminal charges filed in District Court for adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers acting in the course of their duties, both of which are core employment categories within DHS and its local departments.

The bill governs the procedural requirements for District Court Commissioners and judges when applications for statements of charges are filed against covered human service workers, requiring referral to the State's Attorney prior to issuing charges.

Synopsis: Establishing certain confidentiality requirements for peer support counseling programs for law enforcement agencies; prohibiting a peer support specialist from  disclosing the contents of any written or oral communication regarding a peer support interaction; and providing certain exceptions.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement Agencies - Peer Support Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Prohibits peer support specialists and program participants from disclosing communications regarding a peer support interaction. Applies to peer support counseling programs provided by law enforcement agencies or the Fraternal Order of Police. Requires peer support specialists to inform participants in writing about confidentiality rules before the initial interaction. Permits disclosure for threats of suicide, imminent serious bodily harm, or admissions of criminal conduct. Allows disclosure when mandated by a court order or authorized by all participating parties.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: law enforcement officers, peer support specialists, law enforcement agencies, and the Fraternal Order of Police
fiscal_impact_summary: State law enforcement agencies can implement requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local expenditures may minimally increase if local agencies must modify existing programs. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police directly employs law enforcement officers and operates peer support and employee assistance programs subject to the bill's confidentiality and notification requirements.
The Department oversees the Maryland Natural Resources Police, whose officers and peer support programs are directly governed by the confidentiality mandates established in the bill.
The Department oversees modal administrations with sworn law enforcement agencies (such as the Maryland Transit Administration Police), requiring its peer support operations to comply with the bill.
The MDTA operates its own nationally accredited police force, which must implement the bill's confidentiality protocols and written notification requirements for officer peer support interactions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department employs sworn personnel and law enforcement officers who participate in agency employee assistance and peer counseling programs covered by the bill.
The Department houses the Maryland Capitol Police, a state law enforcement agency whose peer support specialists and participating officers must adhere to the bill's confidentiality rules.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS operates the State Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) team, which provides volunteer peer support and training to law enforcement agencies across the state.
The Comptroller employs sworn law enforcement officers within its Field Enforcement Division, making its peer support interactions subject to the statutory confidentiality requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund, which provides grants to local law enforcement agencies for peer support and mental health crisis training.
Member institutions within the USM maintain campus police departments whose officers and peer support counseling services fall under the bill's provisions.
Morgan State University maintains an independent campus police department, and any peer support interactions for its law enforcement officers must comply with the bill.
The college maintains its own public safety and law enforcement officers, subjecting its peer counseling and employee support services to the bill's standards.

Synopsis: Repealing the time limitation within which the Motor Vehicle Administration is required to make available specially designed vintage reproduction registration plates; and requiring the Administration to charge a fee of $100 for the initial issuance and $25 for the renewal of a specially designed vintage reproduction registration plate.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Specially Designed Vintage Reproduction Registration Plates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the one-year limitation on the Motor Vehicle Administration issuing vintage reproduction registration plates. Makes permanent the requirement to provide plates resembling the 1910 black lettering on yellow background design. Establishes a $100 initial issuance fee and a $25 renewal fee for the plates. Authorizes owners and lessees of Class A, Class E, Class L, Class M, and Class N vehicles to apply. Directs collected fees to recover administrative costs and credit the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Owners and lessees of Class A (passenger), Class E (truck), Class L (historic), Class M (multipurpose), and Class N (street rod) vehicles
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase by an illustrative $135,000 in FY 2026 and expenditures increase by $12,500 for plate production costs, resulting in a net increase of $122,500. Out-year net revenues are projected to range between $90,000 and $146,250 annually through FY 2030. Local highway user revenues distributed from the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account experience a negligible increase beginning in FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with permanently issuing specially designed vintage reproduction registration plates, establishing production processes, and collecting initial and renewal registration fees.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a modal unit of the Department of Transportation, and fee revenues and cost recovery expenditures under the bill directly affect the state Transportation Trust Fund and the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland to examine and analyze the efficiency, uniformity, and quality of fiduciary adjudication in Maryland and make recommendations; requiring the orphans' courts, circuit courts, registers of wills, and Administrative Office of the Courts to comply with certain requests of the Task Force; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and make recommendations on or before January 1, 2026.
Title: Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland. Directs the task force to examine judicial qualifications, procedures, and jurisdictions of orphans' courts and circuit courts. Requires orphans' courts, circuit courts, registers of wills, and the Administrative Office of the Courts to provide requested data. Requires the task force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland; Department of Legislative Services; Maryland State Bar Association
stakeholders: judges of orphans' courts and circuit courts, registers of wills, estate and trust attorneys, and Maryland residents involved in probate and fiduciary proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented with existing State resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly studies fiduciary adjudication in the circuit and orphans' courts and statutorily requires the Administrative Office of the Courts to comply with all reasonable requests by the Task Force for data and information.

The bill includes two registers of wills as members of the Task Force, examines probate adjudication and procedures, and statutorily requires registers of wills to comply with all reasonable requests by the Task Force for information and data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland as a temporary advisory body to study fiduciary adjudication and submit findings and recommendations.
The Governor appoints one member with expertise in budgeting and personnel matters, designates the chair of the Task Force, and receives the final report and recommendations by January 1, 2026.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing the gubernatorial appointment to the Task Force.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Administrator of Elections to enter into memoranda of understanding with municipal corporations that allow the State Administrator to work collaboratively with a municipal corporation to support the administration of the municipal corporation's elections; authorizing the State Administrator to lease a voting system or other equipment used to administer an election for use in a municipal election; repealing the authority of a local board to lease a voting system to certain entities within the county; etc.
Title: Election Law - Municipal Elections - Administration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to enter into memoranda of understanding with municipal corporations to support election administration. Authorizes the State Administrator to lease a voting system or other election equipment to a municipal corporation. Requires the State Administrator to determine lease terms and distribute lease proceeds to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. Repeals authority of local boards of elections to lease voting systems to entities within the county. Alters the deadline for municipal requests for ballot inclusion from 18 months to 9 months before candidate filing. Requires requesting municipalities to certify consistent deadlines and procedures for voter registration and voting.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; State Board of Elections
stakeholders: municipal corporations in Maryland; local boards of elections; municipal election voters
fiscal_impact_summary: Fair Campaign Financing Fund special fund revenues may increase annually beginning in FY 2025 from voting equipment lease proceeds. Municipal expenditures may increase annually for municipalities leasing voting equipment. State Board of Elections expenditures and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 322 directly empowers the State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections to enter into MOUs with municipal corporations, lease voting systems and equipment, manage lease proceeds for the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, and oversee the inclusion of municipal offices and ballot questions on statewide ballots.

Synopsis: Clarifying required information for registering a domestic partnership or obtaining a marriage license; and requiring a declaration of domestic partnership filed with the register of wills to include the Social Security number of each domestic partner who has a Social Security number.
Title: Domestic Partnership and Marriage - Required Information

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Clarifies information requirements for registering a domestic partnership or obtaining a marriage license. Requires declarations and marriage license applications to state each party's full legal name and date of birth. Mandates that a declaration of domestic partnership include the Social Security number of each partner who has one. Prohibits disclosing a partner's Social Security number in public records, subject to specific statutory exceptions. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Registers of Wills; Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Individuals registering domestic partnerships, individuals applying for marriage licenses, county registers of wills, and circuit court clerks
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on local finances. May protect federal child support enforcement grant funding by ensuring Maryland statutes comply with federal requirements; specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Estates and Trusts Article governing declarations of domestic partnership filed with the Register of Wills, requiring the collection of full legal names, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers, while restricting the public disclosure of those Social Security numbers.
The bill amends procedures for marriage license applications handled by the clerks of the circuit courts, requiring applicants to provide full legal names and dates of birth rather than simply age.

The bill helps protect federal funding for the state's child support enforcement program, administered by DHS's Child Support Administration, by ensuring state law complies with federal requirements to record Social Security numbers.

Synopsis: Requiring each member of a county board of education to complete certain antibias training at least once during the member's term.
Title: County Boards of Education - Antibias Training for Members - Requirement (County Board Member Antibias Training Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Requires each member of a county board of education to complete antibias training at least once during their term. Mandates that members complete the training developed by the local board based on state guidelines. Requires board member training to be conducted separately from the training provided to public school employees. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: County Boards of Education
stakeholders: Members of county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local school systems can comply with the requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state public education system and establishes the underlying guidelines and standards for antibias training that local school boards must develop and implement for board members.

The Commission enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws and was consulted as an information source on the legislation, although it has no direct statutory enforcement or administrative mandates under the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to allow an individual to choose to take all components of the General Educational Development Test in either English or Spanish; and requiring the Department to study the feasibility and cost of offering the examination in additional languages and to report its findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
Title: Adult Education - High School Diploma by Examination - Requirements and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to allow individuals to take all high school diploma examination components in either English or Spanish. Directs the Department to identify other appropriate languages for offering the General Educational Development Test to adult learners. Requires the Department to study the feasibility and cost of offering the examination in additional languages. Mandates a report with study findings and recommendations to two legislative committees by December 1, 2026. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary authorizing and executing authority for the issuance of general obligation bonds, capital project approvals, grant encumbrances, and loan fund allocations under the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan.

The Treasurer receives the cash proceeds from bond sales, pays the expenses of bond issuance and delivery, determines the allocation of bond sale premiums to the Annuity Bond Fund, and receives certifications regarding matching funds.

The IAC is directly allocated and tasked with administering hundreds of millions of dollars in capital grants for public school construction, healthy school facilities, aging schools, and supplemental enrollment growth programs.

DHCD is responsible for administering extensive capital funding allocations across its Division of Neighborhood Revitalization and Division of Development Finance, including rental housing programs, demolition funds, and community revitalization initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS receives major capital bond appropriations and preauthorizations for high-value projects, including the Baltimore Therapeutic Treatment Center, perimeter security at Roxbury, and facility upgrades across multiple correctional institutions.

USM and its constituent campuses receive substantial capital funding and preauthorizations for major academic buildings, infrastructure improvements, student services facilities, and deferred maintenance.

Morgan State University receives tens of millions in direct capital appropriations and multi-year preauthorizations for its New Science Center, campus electrical infrastructure upgrades, and the demolition of Lake Clifton High School.
The Comptroller credits bond proceeds, maintains expenditure accounts, executes transfers and reconciliations, and is authorized to advance funds to loan accounts.

DBM exercises supervisory and fiscal oversight by approving project programs, preliminary plans, budget adjustments, shifts between design and construction appropriations, and transfers to the Construction Contingency Fund.

DGS oversees the Facilities Renewal Fund for State-owned facilities, handles capital construction support, and is explicitly directed to record correct grantee identification and descriptions in grant agreements.

MDH administers capital grant programs for community health facilities and Federally Qualified Health Centers, and receives direct capital appropriations for state healthcare institutions including Clifton T. Perkins Hospital Center.

MDE receives capital appropriations to administer the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program, the Maryland Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund, and the Maryland Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund.
DNR receives capital bond funding for Community Parks and Playgrounds, the Oyster Restoration Program, the Waterway Improvement Fund, and capital development on DNR properties.

MDP oversees capital appropriations administered through the Maryland Historical Trust for historical preservation, the African American Heritage Preservation Program, and capital improvements at Jefferson Patterson Park and Museum.
MSDE co-administers capital programs including the Senator James E. 'Ed' DeGrange Nonpublic Aging Schools Program and oversees public school facilities funding frameworks.
MHEC administers multi-million dollar grants for the Community College Construction Grant Program and Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program across local subdivisions.
MDOT receives major capital funding for Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) upgrades and modal administration projects.
MPA receives a $31.5 million capital appropriation to complete construction and rail infrastructure improvements for the Howard Street Tunnel project.
MSP receives capital bond funding and preauthorizations for design and construction of replacement barracks and garages at Waterloo, Annapolis, and Forestville.
MSD receives substantial capital appropriations and multi-year preauthorizations for new student residences, a student center, and facilities renewal at both its Frederick and Columbia campuses.

The Adjutant General heads the Military Department, which receives capital appropriations for readiness center renovations in Glen Burnie, White Oak, and Frederick, as well as a new Joint Force Headquarters at Camp Fretterd.
DoIT receives a $14.9 million capital appropriation to continue construction of the Maryland FiRST statewide unified public safety radio communications system.
DJS receives capital funding to design the renovation and expansion of the Maryland Youth Residence Center in Baltimore City and manages adjustments to prior authorizations.
MES receives funding through the State Water and Sewer Infrastructure Improvement Fund to design, construct, and equip water and wastewater facility improvements at state institutions.
The Maryland State Library Agency administers the $7.5 million Public Library Capital Grant Program to assist local jurisdictions with public library facilities.
DVMF receives capital funding for the Crownsville Veterans Cemetery expansion and has contingent capital matching fund authorizations allocated for the New State Veterans Home in Sykesville.
The Department of Disabilities receives $1.027 million for the Access Maryland program to finance architectural modifications improving accessibility at State-owned facilities.
The Department of Commerce administers the Maryland Arts Capital Grant Program ($3,000,000) through its Division of Marketing, Tourism, and the Arts.
HSMCC receives capital funds to begin design work on the visitor center conversion and expansion for the Education Center and Artisan Center Complex.

Judicial branch facilities supporting the courts system, notably the construction of a new Supreme Court of Maryland Building in Annapolis and District Court additions, are authorized and funded in this bill.
MEDCO is designated as the recipient of capital grants for specific economic development projects, including the Viva White Oak project and the Principio Rail Spur.
SHA is explicitly named alongside Montgomery County to carry out capital improvements for crosswalks on Route 108 funded via a legislative grant.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments executing capital bond projects and proposes the capital budget that this legislation enacts.

Synopsis: Establishing or altering certain administrative penalties; altering or repealing certain required appropriations; authorizing the use of certain funds for certain purposes; establishing certain funds; authorizing, requiring, or altering the distribution of certain revenue; altering the rates and rate brackets under the State income tax on certain income of individuals; increasing the cap on the percentage that may be deducted from all open purses and paid to a certain organization; etc.
Title: Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025
