bill_summary: Enacts statutory changes to balance the State budget by adjusting tax rates, mandated appropriations, and fund allocations. Increases the top individual income tax rate to 6.50% and imposes a 2% surtax on net capital gains. Raises the vehicle excise tax to 6.5% and levies a 3% sales tax on data and information technology services. Requires county governments to fund 90% of property valuation expenses and share teacher pension obligations starting in fiscal 2026. Reduces or restructures State mandated appropriations for nonpublic special education placements and community college scholarships.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Budget and Management; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland individual and corporate taxpayers; motor vehicle purchasers, owners, and rental operators; data and information technology consumers; adult-use cannabis consumers and retailers; county governments and Baltimore City; local school systems; community college students; healthcare and human services providers
fiscal_impact_summary: Increases State general fund revenues by $765.6 million in FY 2025 and $1.57 billion in FY 2026, while decreasing general fund expenditures by $104.7 million in FY 2025 and $897.9 million in FY 2026. Special fund revenues increase by $19.5 million in FY 2025 and decrease by $80.1 million in FY 2026, while special fund expenditures increase by $94.5 million in FY 2025 and $366.7 million in FY 2026. Total net State budgetary improvement is estimated at $795.2 million in FY 2025 and $2.04 billion in FY 2026. Local government expenditures increase by over $157.5 million in FY 2026 due to cost-shifting mandates, partially offset by an estimated $28.2 million increase in local income tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Removes the Judicial Branch's exemption from review and performance evaluations by the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability (OPEGA) and authorizes a $20 million transfer from the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund to the General Fund.
Requires BPW to periodically notify counties of their 50% cost share for erroneous conviction compensation awards and reduces BPW's unexpended grant appropriation for the Artscape Festival.

Administers extensive tax alterations including individual income tax rate and bracket restructuring, net capital gains surtax, sales and use tax expansions (IT/data services, precious metals, snack foods), cannabis sales tax adjustments, tire fees, and fund distributions from the Local Income Tax Reserve Account.

Increases nursery inspection and certification fees, modifies commercial weights and measures registration and fee setting, reduces the mandated appropriation for tree planting on agricultural land, and redirects agricultural land preservation funding to the General Fund.

Oversees State expenditure reductions, coordinates budget transfers, waives across-the-board reduction reporting requirements for FY 2026, and is mandated to certify and report on federal revenue reductions exceeding $1 billion.

Reduces the annual film production activity tax credit cap, alters the More Jobs for Marylanders Tax Credit Reserve Fund, transfers funds from the Innovation Investment Incentive Tax Credit, and reallocates Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account balances.

Increases local cost shares for nonpublic placements of special education students, phases out teacher retirement supplemental grants, alters Safe Schools Fund mandate structures, and participates in the Interagency Rates Committee provider rate freeze.
Authorizes the transfer of $9.0 million from the Resilient Maryland Revolving Loan Fund to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
Withdraws a $12 million FY 2024 capital pay-as-you-go general fund grant for Lansdowne Library improvements and oversees State Center relocation funding.

Increases the hospital Medicaid Deficit Assessment, establishes the Medicaid Primary Care Program Fund, adjusts Developmental Disabilities Administration funding and support services caps, alters Behavioral Health Administration grant reversions, transfers licensing board balances, and authorizes delegation of nursing home surveys to Montgomery County.

Authorizes the $50 million mandated appropriation for the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund (Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative) to be met via general obligation bonds in the capital budget instead of only the operating budget.

Imposes a $30 million annual cap on the restoration of benefits lost due to Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card theft and is subject to the Interagency Rates Committee rate freeze for foster care maintenance payments.

Repeals the requirement to set aside at least 20% of IT Investment Fund appropriations for expedited projects and transfers cybersecurity appropriations from the Dedicated Purpose Account to the General Fund.
Subject to the Interagency Rates Committee rate freeze for provider payments in FY 2026.

Imposes a 0.15% unemployment insurance administrative fee to fund the Special Administrative Expense Fund, transfers $80 million from the State UI reserve account, receives a $37.3 million transfer for the Division of Paid Leave from LITRA, and reduces funding mandates for several workforce development and grant programs.

Redirects Program Open Space and Rural Legacy transfer tax revenues to the General Fund, authorizes up to $10.5 million from the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund and up to $16.4 million from POS fund balances for DNR operating expenses, and increases Waterway Improvement Fund spending for the Natural Resources Police.
Reduces mandated funding for the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Reserve Fund and authorizes $340,000 in Maryland Heritage Areas Authority POS funds for MDP operating expenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Authorizes the use of Opioid Restitution Funds for medication-assisted opioid treatment in correctional facilities and authorizes the transfer of $5.0 million from the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund to the General Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Adjusts statutory participation targets for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and reduces the mandated FY 2026 appropriation to the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund.

Authorizes new fees for erosion and sediment control certification, increases Wetlands and Waterways Program fees, increases rental property lead registration and certification fees, increases Voluntary Cleanup Program fees, alters tire recycling fees, increases surface mining fees, and receives SEIF funding for the Air and Radiation Administration.

Increases the Consolidated Transportation Bond debt cap to $5.0 billion, expands GARVEE bond uses to light rail rehabilitation, alters the TTF operating forecast formula, receives dedicated revenues from vehicle excise tax, titling fees, and tire fees, and coordinates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.
Transfers $62.9 million in capital PAYGO funding previously designated in the Dedicated Purpose Account for the construction of a new State veterans home to the General Fund.
Provides the statutory framework for the Governor's executive budget proposals, fund balance transfers, mandated appropriation relief, and expenditure reductions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Reduces mandated grant funding for warrant apprehension efforts, authorizes up to $1.0 million from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to support the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman, and transfers $4.9 million from the Violence Intervention and Prevention Program Fund to the General Fund.
Implements the increased Medicaid Deficit Assessment on hospitals and administers assessments to fund the Medicaid Primary Care Program Fund under the AHEAD model.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Eliminates the $500,000 mandated appropriation for the Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program in FY 2026.
Expands allowable uses of the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund to fund the $5.0 million Social Equity Partnership Grant Program and adjusts cannabis sales tax distribution provisions.
Modifies Safe Schools Fund provisions and the mandated funding mechanism for School Resource Officer grants.
Designated as the successor entity to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority for the operation of racing and community development projects.

Redirects SEIF interest earnings and transfers $230 million from the RPS/ACP account to the General Fund, while expanding authorized uses of ACP revenues for local clean energy and State solar projects.
Increases the statutory caps on project contingency funds for State-owned facility projects, including the Eastern Correctional Institution turbine project.
Repeals the annual $1.0 million mandated appropriation for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund, converting it into a discretionary appropriation.

Reduces mandated appropriations for the Community College Promise Scholarship, police and probation agent loan repayment and scholarship programs, and caps the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit at $9 million for tax year 2025.

Designated as the successor entity to MTROA for the planning, design, construction, and ownership of racing and community development projects, and transfers $3.0 million of interest from RCDFF to the General Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Increases the tax rate on mobile sports wagering from 15% to 20%, redirects a portion to the General Fund, and alters lottery revenue distribution to the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.
Expands allowable uses of the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF) in FY 2025 and FY 2026 to support general operations of the Aviation Command.

Repeals the $50 million annual supplemental pension contribution, eliminates the surplus pension sweeper mandate, and shifts $97.7 million in annual TRS/TPS employer pension contributions from the State to local governments.

Authorizes the transfer of funds from the Rainy Day Fund to the Annuity Bond Fund if necessary to pay State debt service, and oversees various State fund balances and investments affected by the bill.
Provides $7.5 million annually from unspent SMWOBA allocations to TEDCO's Pre-Seed Builder Fund for FY 2026 through FY 2028.
Delays the mandate to purchase only zero-emission buses from FY 2027 to FY 2032 and authorizes GARVEE bond proceeds to finance major light rail rehabilitation.
Authorizes the transfer of $10.0 million in capital PAYGO deferred maintenance funds from the Dedicated Purpose Account to the General Fund (replaced with GO bond funds).

Increases cost recovery requirements for miscellaneous vehicle fees, accelerates registration fee increases for multiple vehicle classes, equalizes rental car registration fees, doubles certificate of title fees, increases VEIP testing fees, and restricts the historic motor vehicle definition.
Consults on the development and scope of the independent audit required for the Prince George's County Board of Education.

Replaces general funds with special funds for the Consumer Protection Division, authorizes Securities Act Registration Fund revenues to support OAG general operations, and expands permissible uses of the Mortgage Loan Servicing Practices Settlement Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the registration fee requirement for the Community Association Registry; permitting the County Executive to establish the registration fee; prohibiting a person or entity who fails to register from filing a dispute; and requiring the Prince George's County Office of Community Relations to provide revenue from annual community association registration fees to fund the administrative hearing process for disputes between community associations and owners in Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Community Associations - Registration Fees for Administrative Hearing Process PG 408-25

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alternative Dispute Resolution -see also- Arbitra; Mediation
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires each condominium, homeowners association, and cooperative housing corporation in Prince George's County to register annually with the county registry. Directs the County Executive to establish an annual registration fee sufficient to fund an administrative hearing process. Authorizes additional fees for administrative hearing services and a per-unit charge on developers when recording association documents. Requires collected fee revenues to fund the county administrative hearing process and related technical assistance. Prohibits any person who fails to register or provides false statements from filing disputes under the hearing process.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Office of Community Relations; Prince George's County Executive; Commission on Common Ownership Communities in Prince George’s County
stakeholders: condominiums, homeowners associations, cooperative housing corporations, community association managers, unit and lot owners, and residential property developers in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Prince George's County expenditures increase by approximately $400,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026 for three additional Office of Community Relations staff to manage hearings and investigations, fully offset by new registration and hearing fee revenues.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a health occupations board from requiring additional evidence of English proficiency as a condition for licensure, certification, or registration if an applicant holds a valid, unrestricted license, certification, or registration from another state that requires evidence of English proficiency; requiring each health occupations board that requires evidence of English proficiency to post a statement on their website that an applicant may not be required to provide additional evidence of proficiency; etc.
Title: Health Occupations Boards - English Proficiency Requirements and Licensure by Endorsement for Nursing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants

bill_summary: Prohibits health occupations boards from requiring additional evidence of English proficiency under specified circumstances. Applies when an applicant holds a valid, unrestricted credential from another state that requires English proficiency. Requires affected health occupations boards to prominently post an informational statement on their websites. Expands acceptable proof of English proficiency for registered nursing and licensed practical nursing applicants. Authorizes nurses holding an unencumbered multistate compact license to qualify for licensure by endorsement. Removes the requirement that another state's English proficiency examination component be similar to Maryland's standards.
responsible_party: Health Occupations Boards; State Board of Nursing; State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Applicants for health occupation licensure, certification, or registration; out-of-state licensed health care professionals; registered nurses; licensed practical nurses; pharmacists
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health regulates health care professionals and houses the State's health occupations boards, including the State Board of Nursing and State Board of Pharmacy, which are directly required to implement the bill's changes to English proficiency requirements and licensure by endorsement procedures.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination of certain provisions of law establishing the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority.
Title: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority - Sunset Repeal PG 403-25
bill_summary: Repeals the statutory termination date for the Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority, making the entity permanent. Retains the authority's mandate to support a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan within designated Prince George’s County municipalities. Covers the target area encompassing Mount Rainier, Brentwood, Cottage City, Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood. Maintains the requirement to report a comprehensive revitalization strategy to the Governor and General Assembly committees by October 31, 2025. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority; Prince George’s County Redevelopment Authority; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and municipal governments in the City of Mount Rainier, Town of Brentwood, Town of Cottage City, City of Bladensburg, Town of Colmar Manor, and Town of North Brentwood
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or Prince George’s County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, and the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority provides operational support in consultation with DHCD.
Under the Economic Development Article, the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority.
The Prince George's Gateway Development Authority is statutorily required to submit its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report to the Governor.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to ride a bicycle, play vehicle, or unicycle on a sidewalk or sidewalk area unless prohibited by local ordinance; and requiring a person riding a bicycle, play vehicle, or unicycle on a sidewalk or sidewalk area or in or through a crosswalk to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian or a person using an electric personal assistive mobility device.
Title: Bicycles, Play Vehicles, and Unicycles - Authorizations and Requirements (Jay's Law)

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes a person to ride a bicycle, play vehicle, or unicycle on a sidewalk or sidewalk area unless prohibited by local ordinance. Excludes mopeds from the definition of a bicycle for sidewalk riding. Requires riders on sidewalks, sidewalk areas, or crosswalks to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians. Requires operators to also yield to individuals on electric personal assistive mobility devices. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Individuals operating bicycles, play vehicles, unicycles, or electric personal assistive mobility devices, pedestrians, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal decrease in State general fund revenues if fewer citations are issued. State and local law enforcement and local governments can implement the changes with existing resources, with no local revenue impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article regarding the operation of bicycles, play vehicles, and unicycles on sidewalks and crosswalks, directly impacting the department's transportation policy, safety guidelines, and multi-modal roadway planning.

As the modal agency responsible for state roadways, sidewalk networks, pedestrian facilities, and crosswalks, MDOT SHA is impacted by the shift to permitting bicycles on sidewalks and regulations concerning crosswalk right-of-way.
The MVA is responsible for driver safety guidance and the assessment of points on driving records for violations of sidewalk driving regulations under the Maryland Vehicle Law.
MSP troopers enforce state motor vehicle and traffic laws, including citations for sidewalk and crosswalk right-of-way infractions under the Transportation Article.
The District Court of Maryland processes traffic citations and prepayment penalties for violations of pedestrian, bicycle, and sidewalk laws.

SponsorPrimary: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Sponsors.Name: Chair, Health and Government Operations Committee

Synopsis: Altering the selection of the membership and chair of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council; requiring beginning on October 1, 2025, and every 2 years thereafter, the Council to elect a chair and vice chair from among the members of the Council; requiring the Council, working with certain entities, to assess and address cybersecurity threats and associated risks from artificial intelligence and quantum computing; etc.
Title: Maryland Cybersecurity Council - Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the membership, leadership selection, and statutory duties of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council. Requires the Council, beginning October 1, 2025, to elect a chair and vice chair every two years. Mandates that one leader be a State employee and the other be a non-State employee. Expands Council membership to include specified representatives from higher education, utilities, industry sectors, and nonprofit organizations. Directs the Council to assess and address cybersecurity threats from artificial intelligence and quantum computing. Requires the Council to address sensitive privacy interests of State residents related to cybersecurity risks.
responsible_party: Maryland Cybersecurity Council
stakeholders: Maryland cybersecurity businesses, higher education institutions, critical infrastructure operators, public utilities, and State residents
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as Council duties and member reimbursements can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the membership structure, leadership selection process, and statutory responsibilities of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council, which is an executive advisory body.

Under current law, the Attorney General or their designee chairs the Council and appoints certain members. The bill removes the Attorney General as the mandatory chair and alters appointment authorities, while retaining the Attorney General as a member.

The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the Council, and the bill expands the Council's responsibilities to address artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and critical cyber infrastructure.
The bill adds the People's Counsel, or their designee, as a newly designated statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.

The bill explicitly designates seats on the Council for presidents/deans of multiple USM institutions (Bowie State University, UMB, UMBC, UMCP, and UMGC) and authorizes the USM Chancellor to designate two additional representatives.
The bill specifies that the President of Morgan State University, or the President's designee, is a member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Chief Executive Officer of TEDCO, or their designee, is a designated statutory member of the Council.
The State Administrator of Elections, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Emergency Management, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of State Police, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Adjutant General, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Commerce, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council.

Synopsis: Imposing assessments of 12 points for certain subsequent drunk and drugged driving violations.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Drunk and Drugged Driving - Points Assessments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to assess 12 points against drivers convicted of specified repeat drunk or drugged driving violations. Mandates the assessment for violations committed after two prior impaired driving or boating convictions. Mandates the assessment for violations committed after three or more prior convictions or prior vehicular homicide convictions. Subjects convicted drivers to administrative driver's license revocation following the 12-point assessment. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Drivers convicted of repeat drunk or drugged driving offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the MVA to assess 12 points on the driver's license of an individual convicted of subsequent drunk or drugged driving violations under § 21-902(h) or (i) of the Transportation Article, resulting in mandatory driver's license revocation procedures.
As the parent cabinet agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Maryland Transportation Article and state vehicle regulations.
State courts adjudicate criminal violations of § 21-902 and transmit conviction records to the MVA for the assessment of points against drivers' licenses.
OAH employs Administrative Law Judges who conduct administrative hearings on contested cases, including appeals of driver's license revocations and suspensions resulting from point accumulations.

Synopsis: Exempting personal property used in connection with certain large family child care homes from valuation and taxation; authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or a municipal corporation to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the real property tax owed on the portion of real property used for certain large family child care homes; increasing the maximum amount of a property tax credit that may be granted for certain child care homes and centers and day care centers; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Day Care Centers, Child Care Homes, and Child Care Centers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Exempts personal property used in connection with a registered large family child care home from valuation and property tax. Repeals completion date requirements for real property improvements dedicated to day care centers and child care centers. Authorizes local governing bodies to grant property tax credits for real property used for large family child care homes. Increases the maximum annual property tax credit for eligible day care centers from $3,000 to $10,000. Establishes a maximum annual property tax credit of $10,000 for qualifying employer-owned child care facilities.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Operators and owners of registered large family child care homes, family child care homes, child care centers, adult and elderly day care centers, qualifying businesses, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 due to the expanded personal property tax exemption and local real property tax credits, though the statewide revenue reduction is expected to be minimal. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE licenses and registers family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, which establishes the eligibility criteria for the personal property tax exemption and local property tax credits addressed in the bill.

PTAAB hears appeals regarding personal property assessments, tax exemptions, and property tax credits, which could be impacted by the expanded exemption for large family child care homes and modifications to local property tax credit limits.

The bill references day care centers for the elderly and adults licensed under Title 14 of the Health - General Article, which fall under the regulatory and licensing purview of the Maryland Department of Health, as eligible facilities for the local property tax credits.

Synopsis: Authorizing an owner of real property used for rental housing and the governing body of a county to enter into a payment in lieu of taxes agreement for maintaining at least 25% of the rental housing units located at the real property as affordable dwelling units for at least 15 years; and authorizing the governing body of the county to require the owner of real property to maintain a higher percentage of rental housing units as affordable dwelling units than the minimum percentage specified in the Act.
Title: Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Authorizes county governing bodies and owners of rental housing real property to enter into payment in lieu of taxes agreements. Exempts qualifying rental housing real property from county property taxes upon execution of the agreement. Requires property owners to maintain at least 25% of units as affordable dwelling units for at least 15 years. Authorizes county governing bodies to require an affordable dwelling unit percentage higher than 25%. Defines affordable dwelling units as units affordable to households earning 60% or less of area median income.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties
stakeholders: Owners of real property used for rental housing, county governments, and households earning 60% or less of area median income
fiscal_impact_summary: County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent rental properties receive exemptions, though decreases are mitigated by negotiated payments in lieu of taxes. Specific local revenue impacts are indeterminate and depend on local participation. State revenues and expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands local Payment In Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) authority for affordable rental housing, establishing standards for affordable dwelling unit percentages and duration. While executed at the county level, this directly impacts affordable housing development, preservation, and financing, which is the core mission and policy area of the Department of Housing and Community Development.

Synopsis: Altering a certain loan program to authorize the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation to provide loans in an amount up to $25,000 for certain seasonal full-time jobs; and reducing, from 5 years to 3 years, the number of years that a person must have been a licensed seafood dealer in order to be eligible to receive financing under the loan program.

bill_summary: Alters the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation. Increases the maximum loan amount from $10,000 to $25,000 for each projected seasonal full-time job created or retained. Reduces the required experience for a licensed seafood dealer to receive financing from five years to three years. Maintains the maximum loan limit of up to $250,000 for eligible seafood processing projects. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
stakeholders: licensed seafood dealers, oyster processing businesses, and seasonal seafood processing workers
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in nonbudgeted expenditures and nonbudgeted loan repayment revenues for MARBIDCO beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent lending activity increases from existing program funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing entity for the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program. The bill directly alters MARBIDCO's loan terms by increasing the allowable loan amount per seasonal full-time job to $25,000 and lowering the dealer experience requirement from five years to three years, impacting its nonbudgeted loan expenditures and revenues.

Under the loan program statute amended by the bill, loan forgiveness is conditioned on recipients returning oyster shells to the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) or planting spat-on-shell on public fishery bottoms as verified by DNR.

bill_summary: Increases the scholarship award for the student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education from $8,000 to $15,000. Takes effect June 1, 2025.

stakeholders: Student members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund the increased scholarship amount. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the compensation/scholarship for the student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education, which falls under the broader public education system overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education, though the fiscal impact is entirely local.

responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists; Governor; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: licensed hearing aid dispensers in Maryland; State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists; Hearing Society of Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Delaware

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is a health occupations regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and the Secretary of Health advises the Governor on these appointments.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the hearing aid dispenser members to the Board from the list of nominees submitted by the Board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in managing the recruitment, vetting, and appointment process for members serving on state boards and commissions, including this regulatory board.

bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the part-time deputy chief inspector in Anne Arundel County from $9,000 to $18,000. stakeholders: part-time deputy chief inspector employed by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County; Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $9,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026 to fund the salary increase. County revenues are not affected.

responsible_party: Maryland State Archives
stakeholders: Maryland residents, historians, educators, and mineral enthusiasts
fiscal_impact_summary: Designating a State mineral does not materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives serves as the official record keeper for state symbols and maintains the Maryland Manual On-Line, which catalogues official state designations such as the newly designated State mineral.

Synopsis: Requiring each local board of elections to make available on its website each open meeting agenda, a summary of any finalized documents, certain written testimony, and other materials on which the  board will be voting; requiring each local board to provide live video streaming of each open meeting and to maintain a complete and unedited archived video recording of each open meeting for 5 years; requiring the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations to ensure that the streaming requirements are met in a certain manner; etc.

bill_summary: Requires each local board of elections to make open meeting agendas and voting materials publicly available on its website. Mandates publication at least 48 hours before each meeting, or as soon as practicable during emergencies. Directs local boards of elections to provide live video streaming of open meetings. Excludes off-site meetings, project site visits, and inspections from live video streaming requirements. Requires local boards of elections to maintain unedited archived recordings for at least 5 years. Requires the State Board of Elections to adopt implementing regulations by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local boards of elections, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local expenditures increase for certain counties to purchase livestreaming equipment, provide technical support, and maintain video storage archives.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Board of Elections adopt regulations on or before December 1, 2025, to ensure that the open meeting live streaming requirements established for local boards of elections are implemented in a manner that maximizes transparency.

bill_summary: Authorizes an individual at least 21 years old to manufacture personal use amounts of cannabis products at a private residence without volatile solvents. Reduces criminal penalties for volume dealer and drug kingpin offenses involving 50 pounds or more of cannabis. Authorizes certain incarcerated individuals serving mandatory minimum terms for cannabis or cocaine base offenses to apply for sentence reductions. Reclassifies specified firearm offenses from misdemeanors to felonies and establishes imprisonment penalties for illegal handgun manufacturing and sales.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Public Defender; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals incarcerated for cannabis or cocaine base offenses, adults manufacturing cannabis for personal use, individuals charged with firearm or controlled dangerous substance offenses, defense attorneys, and State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $95,700 in FY 2026 and up to $130,500 by FY 2030 for the Office of the Public Defender to handle sentence modification caseloads. State finances and local revenues and expenditures are otherwise not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an application process for incarcerated individuals to seek sentence reductions or modifications for certain past mandatory minimum convictions and alters firearm penalty classifications, creating a direct operational and fiscal impact requiring additional defense attorney staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill eliminates mandatory minimums and reduces penalties for cannabis volume dealers and drug kingpins, authorizes sentence modifications for current inmates, and elevates several firearm misdemeanors to felonies, impacting state correctional intake and sentence lengths.

The bill requires circuit courts to receive sentence modification applications, provide notices to prosecutors, and conduct mandatory hearings, in addition to shifting cases between the District Court and Circuit Courts due to penalty reclassifications.

The bill amends the Public Safety Article regarding firearms offenses (including handgun roster violations, stolen regulated firearms, and firearm serial number registrations overseen by the Secretary of State Police) and impacts criminal law enforcement regarding controlled dangerous substances.

The bill amends state cannabis policy by establishing guidelines and exceptions for non-commercial personal-use manufacturing of cannabis concentrates and products at private residences and reducing statutory cannabis trafficking penalties.

Synopsis: Establishing the Family Literacy Pilot Program administered by the State Library Agency in consultation with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Correctional Education Council to enable certain incarcerated individuals to read aloud to their children by preparing a recording; and requiring the State Library Agency to submit a certain report on or before December 1, 2028.
Title: State Library Agency - Family Literacy Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes the Family Literacy Pilot Program administered by the Maryland State Library Agency. Requires the agency to select four State correctional facility libraries or prerelease centers across Western, Central, and Eastern Maryland. Requires participating sites to include at least one facility serving female incarcerated individuals and one serving male incarcerated individuals. Enables participating incarcerated individuals to select children's books and record themselves reading aloud to their children. Mandates that participation and book distribution remain free of charge with custodial parent or guardian written permission. Requires the agency to report program results to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Correctional Education Council
stakeholders: incarcerated individuals in State correctional facilities and prerelease centers, their children, and custodial parents or guardians
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $69,207 in FY 2026, $70,800 in FY 2027, $73,800 in FY 2028, and $38,500 in FY 2029 to fund one contractual program administrator within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and program supplies for the Maryland State Library Agency. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSLA is the primary administering agency responsible for developing, managing, and reporting on the Family Literacy Pilot Program, including selecting books, purchasing equipment, and establishing participation processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS must be consulted to select four correctional facilities or prerelease centers and establish operational processes; it incurs direct fiscal impacts to hire a contractual program administrator to facilitate the program within its facilities.
MD Labor houses the Correctional Education Council (jointly administered with DPSCS), which must be consulted on selecting correctional facility sites and establishing program procedures.

Synopsis: Altering the defined term "auto-injectable epinephrine" to be "emergency use epinephrine" and to include certain drug delivery devices and products; and altering the name of the Emergency Use Auto-Injectable Epinephrine Program to be the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program.
Title: Education and Health - Emergency Use Epinephrine - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: Replaces the statutory term auto-injectable epinephrine with emergency use epinephrine throughout the Education, Health-General, and Health Occupations articles. Expands the definition to include any portable, disposable drug delivery device or product approved by the FDA. Renames the Emergency Use Auto-Injectable Epinephrine Program as the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program. Authorizes public and nonpublic school personnel, youth camp operators, and participating facilities to store and administer emergency use epinephrine. Extends existing civil liability protections to individuals who administer, prescribe, or dispense emergency use epinephrine in good faith.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education; State Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Students, public and nonpublic school personnel, child care providers, youth camp operators and campers, participating food service and recreation facility staff, and licensed health care practitioners
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Health can update existing regulations, program materials, and procedures using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program and the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program for youth camps. It will need to update program regulations, training guidelines, and reporting materials to incorporate non-injectable forms of FDA-approved epinephrine.

MSDE oversees public school and child care policies and reporting requirements concerning emergency epinephrine administration. Under the bill, MSDE's definitions, guidelines, and incident reporting forms for schools and child care facilities are updated from auto-injectable epinephrine to emergency use epinephrine.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund for certain expenditures that support the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline; and altering a certain restriction on the use of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to prohibit funds from being used for expenses solely related to the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline, instead of preventing the use of funds for any costs associated with the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline.
Title: Public Safety - 9-1-1 Trust Fund - 9-8-8 Suicide Prevention Hotline

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Authorizes the use of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund for operational costs shared between 9-1-1 activities and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline. Permits funding for shared expenditures including software interfaces and joint training. Prohibits the use of 9-1-1 Trust Fund money for costs that solely support the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline. Repeals the former restriction prohibiting 9-1-1 funds from being used for any purpose associated with the hotline. Maintains prohibitions against using fund money for communications centers other than public safety answering points.
responsible_party: Maryland 9-1-1 Board; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: public safety answering points, 9-1-1 specialists and dispatch personnel, 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline operators, behavioral health crisis service callers, and Maryland telecommunications subscribers paying 9-1-1 fees
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the 9-1-1 Trust Fund increase minimally as shared activities and projects receive funding. Special fund expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund may decrease due to administrative efficiencies and eliminated duplication. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and administers the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. This bill directly expands the authorized uses of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to include shared expenditures supporting both 9-1-1 activities and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the state's behavioral health crisis services, including the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline and the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. The bill allows joint training and software integration costs between 9-1-1 and 9-8-8 systems to be paid from the 9-1-1 Trust Fund, potentially reducing expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland 9-1-1 Board to adopt regulations to implement and enforce certain responsibilities of the Board; and authorizing the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to adopt regulations to implement and enforce the responsibilities of the Department.
Title: Public Safety - Maryland 9-1-1 Board and Maryland Department of Emergency Management - Regulatory Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland 9-1-1 Board to adopt regulations to implement and enforce statutory provisions governing 9-1-1 systems. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to adopt regulations to implement and enforce emergency management statutory responsibilities. Clarifies the regulatory authority of both entities to oversee operational standards, planning, and enforcement. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland 9-1-1 Board; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: Maryland 9-1-1 Board, Maryland Department of Emergency Management, county emergency management agencies, and local public safety answering points
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Emergency Management and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 423 directly authorizes the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board (which operates within MDEM) to adopt regulations to implement and enforce their statutory responsibilities.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council; requiring the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, under certain circumstances, to establish a process for setting upper payment limits for purchases and payor reimbursements of prescription drug products that the Board determines have led or will lead to affordability challenges; authorizing the Board to reconsider an upper payment limit for a drug that becomes a current shortage; and altering requirements related to the setting of upper payment limits.
Title: Prescription Drug Affordability Board - Authority and Stakeholder Council Membership (Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for All Marylanders Now Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council to include rare disease, oncology, and patient advocacy representatives. Requires the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to determine whether setting upper payment limits for prescription drugs serves the State. Requires the Board to establish a limit-setting process if it makes an affirmative determination. Prohibits the Board from applying new limits to drugs in a current shortage or to pharmacy dispensing fees. Requires the Board to confer with the Maryland Medical Assistance Program before establishing an upper payment limit for Medicaid. Contingently requires statewide upper payment limits if the Board maintains limits on two prescription drugs for one year.
responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: prescription drug manufacturers, pharmacy benefit managers, health insurance carriers, wholesale distributors, retail and independent pharmacies, healthcare providers, Maryland Medical Assistance Program participants, and Maryland prescription drug consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $106,700 in FY 2026 and reach $146,300 by FY 2030 for one assistant attorney general to provide legal support. Prescription Drug Affordability Board special fund expenditures increase by at least $264,900 annually beginning in FY 2027 for staff and consulting, offset by a corresponding increase in annual fee assessment revenues. Local governments may realize minimal savings on employee health plan pharmaceutical spending.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) incurs a direct fiscal impact from the bill, requiring $106,700 in general funds in FY 2026 to hire an Assistant Attorney General to provide legal counsel, assist in drafting regulations, and handle potential litigation arising from expanded upper payment limits. Additionally, the Attorney General serves as a secondary approval authority for the Board's plan of action.

The bill requires the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to confer directly with MDH's Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) before establishing any upper payment limit applicable to the program, assessing potential conflicts with the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program and budget impacts.

DBM has statutory representation on the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council and oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which purchases prescription drugs potentially subject to upper payment limits.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council (including a representative of a patient advocacy organization) and acts jointly with the Attorney General to review and approve the Board's plan of action if the Legislative Policy Committee does not.
MIA regulates private commercial health insurance carriers in the state, which are directly affected by provisions establishing upper payment limits on payor reimbursements for prescription drugs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory composition, membership, and advisory responsibilities of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council.
The bill repeals obsolete statutory language regarding the repayment of startup funding from the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to the Maryland Health Care Commission.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting candidates for gubernatorial appointments to state boards and councils, including the newly added seat on the Stakeholder Council.

bill_summary: Excludes licensed auctioneers from the definition of vessel dealer under the State Boat Act under specified conditions. Applies when the auctioneer acts on behalf of a seller, secured party, or owner. Requires that title does not pass to the auctioneer. Requires that the auction is not conducted to avoid statutory requirements. Removes auctioneers who sell vessels under commercial lien provisions from the definition of dealer. responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: licensed auctioneers selling vessels on behalf of sellers, secured parties, or owners; vessel owners and buyers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources administers the State Boat Act, licenses boat dealers, and oversees the collection and remittance of the vessel excise tax, which are directly impacted by exempting certain auctioneers from the definition of 'dealer.'

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections, in collaboration with the local boards of elections, to conduct a risk-limiting audit after each statewide election; authorizing the State Board, in collaboration with the local boards, to conduct a risk-limiting audit after a special general election; authorizing the State Board, in collaboration with the local boards, to conduct an automated software audit after a statewide election; authorizing a local board to conduct a risk-limiting audit of a local contest under certain circumstances; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Elections and local boards of elections to conduct risk-limiting audits after each statewide election. Authorizes risk-limiting audits after special general elections and allows local boards to audit local contests at their discretion. Directs the manual examination of voter-verifiable paper records until meeting the risk limit or confirming the outcome. Requires completing the risk-limiting audit before the Board of State Canvassers transmits certified election results. Alters the automated software audit requirement to an authorization and repeals the existing post-general election manual audit mandate.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local election directors and staff, local boards of canvassers, and candidates in statewide and local elections
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,000 in fiscal 2026, $72,000 in fiscal 2027, and $51,000 annually thereafter for audit software and consultant support. Local government expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2026 for personnel and supplies to conduct the audits, potentially offset in general election years by repealing the prior manual audit mandate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary implementing agency responsible for conducting risk-limiting postelection tabulation audits in collaboration with local election boards, adopting regulations, and procuring the necessary software and consulting services, with a direct fiscal impact on general fund expenditures.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Public Accountancy to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; and requiring the Board to reinstate the license of an individual who is on emeritus status under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Public Accountancy to place a qualifying licensee on emeritus status. Requires an applicant to be retired and meet specified experience and age thresholds without pending disciplinary actions. Exempts licensees on emeritus status from continuing education requirements and reinstatement fees. Prohibits an emeritus licensee from practicing certified public accountancy, certifying financial statements, or providing attestation services. Permits emeritus licensees to use the titles "Certified Public Accountant Emeritus" or "CPA Emeritus".
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
stakeholders: Retired and long-practicing certified public accountants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Public Accountancy are likely not materially affected, as the bill is assumed to apply in a limited number of cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is an occupational licensing regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is directly responsible for administering the new emeritus status licensing category, processing applications, issuing certificates, and enforcing practice restrictions.

Synopsis: Establishing certain requirements for a complaint for a money judgment; defining "medical debt" as a debt owed by a consumer to a provider of medical services, products, or devices, but does not include debt charged to a credit card except under certain circumstances; prohibiting the creation of a lien on owner-occupied residential property by contract or as a result of a breach of contract for the payment of medical debt; and applying the Act prospectively.

bill_summary: Prohibits creating a lien on owner-occupied residential property by contract or breach of contract for medical debt. Requires complaints seeking a money judgment to indicate whether the judgment sought is for medical debt. Mandates that complaints seeking a money judgment for medical debt include the defendant's primary residence address. Requires a court to remove any lien created in violation of these provisions. Excludes credit card debt unless the credit plan is offered solely for health care services. Applies prospectively only to complaints filed on or after October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Circuit Courts of Maryland
stakeholders: Consumers owing medical debt, owners of owner-occupied residential property, healthcare providers, and medical debt collection entities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by establishing specific pleading requirements for civil complaints seeking money judgments for medical debt, governing how money judgments create liens on land, and directing the courts to remove liens created on owner-occupied residential property in violation of the Act.

The Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General enforces statutory consumer protections against unlawful debt collection practices and contract liens, and the agency was consulted in the analysis of the bill.

The Department of Health regulates health care providers and facilities whose medical billing and debt collection practices are impacted by restrictions on pursuing contract liens against residential property.

bill_summary: Prohibits consumer contracts from setting a shorter time to bring an action than required by State law. Declares any such provision against State public policy, illegal, and void. Prohibits courts from enforcing the provision or allowing defenses based on shorter limitation periods. Excludes certain authorized businesses, specified utility-regulated services, and licensed security system providers. Classifies a violation as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under Maryland consumer protection law. Applies prospectively to consumer contracts entered into on or after June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers entering into consumer contracts; businesses providing goods or services for personal, family, or household purposes
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that a violation of the prohibition against shortening limitation periods in consumer contracts constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill directly instructs state courts that they may not give effect to shortened limitation period provisions in consumer contracts and that a defense to liability may not be based on such provisions in civil actions.
The bill explicitly excludes services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission from the provisions restricting contract limitation periods.

bill_summary: Authorizes indefinite validity for medical exemptions allowing enhanced vehicle window tinting for owners with permanent medical conditions. Repeals the previous two-year limitation when a licensed physician determines an owner's condition is permanent. Requires the vehicle owner to keep the physician's written certification inside the vehicle. Applies to aftermarket window tinting materials that allow less than 35% light transmittance. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Vehicle owners with medical conditions requiring protection from the sun, licensed Maryland physicians, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Department of State Police, which is responsible for specifying the manner and format of the medical certification required for enhanced tinted windows and oversees safety equipment repair orders.

The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates motor vehicle equipment standards, driver/vehicle compliance, and the Motor Vehicle Administrator retains authority regarding regulations governing vehicle windows.
As the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and the Maryland Transportation Article, MDOT is directly concerned with changes to state vehicle equipment laws.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court, which processes citations and adjudicates traffic offenses related to vehicle equipment and window tint violations.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "private place" as it relates to the prohibition on conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent of an individual without the consent of the individual to include a residence; and altering the prohibition against conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent.
Title: Criminal Law - Visual Surveillance With Prurient Intent - Modifications
bill_summary: Alters the definition of "private place" under criminal prohibitions against visual surveillance with prurient intent. Adds residences and other places of private use or accommodation to the scope of protected private places. Prohibits nonconsensual camera surveillance of an individual's private area regardless of the location of the individual. Subjects violators to misdemeanor penalties of up to one year of imprisonment, a $2,500 fine, or both. Preserves a civil cause of action allowing affected individuals to recover actual damages and reasonable attorney's fees.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Judiciary
stakeholders: individuals in private residences and places of private accommodation, victims of nonconsensual visual surveillance, and individuals prosecuted for visual surveillance offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures from expanded application of existing misdemeanor incarceration and monetary penalty provisions; specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands a criminal offense (visual surveillance with prurient intent) and provides for a civil cause of action, which impacts the caseload, fine collection, and judicial proceedings handled in the District Court and Circuit Courts managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill expands the scope of an existing misdemeanor offense that carries a penalty of up to one year imprisonment, the Office of the Public Defender may see an increase in indigent criminal defense representation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly responsible for state-level incarceration (such as at the Baltimore Pretrial Complex) and community supervision via the Division of Parole and Probation for individuals convicted of this misdemeanor.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing criminal laws and conducting criminal investigations, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating violations of visual surveillance statutes.

Synopsis: Increasing from $10,000 to $25,000 the maximum amount of compensatory damages that may be awarded to an owner of a pet from a person who tortiously causes an injury to or death of the pet while acting individually or through an animal under the person's ownership, direction, or control.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum compensatory damages awarded to a pet owner for tortious pet injury or death from $10,000 to $25,000. Applies when a person acts individually or through an animal under the person's ownership, direction, or control. Defines compensatory damages as reasonable and necessary veterinary care costs, plus fair market value in fatal cases. Excludes livestock from the definition of a pet. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Pet owners seeking damages for injured or killed pets and individuals liable for tortious harm to pets
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory caps on compensatory damages in civil tort claims regarding the injury or death of a pet, which are adjudicated in the Maryland court system supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Expanding the evidentiary rule on the admissibility of out of court statements made by child victims or witnesses to make admissible an out of court statement made by a child to a forensic interviewer.

bill_summary: Expands an evidentiary hearsay exception to admit out-of-court statements made by child victims and witnesses to forensic interviewers. Defines a forensic interviewer as a trained professional employed by or under contract with a child advocacy center. Excludes law enforcement officers from the definition of a forensic interviewer. Applies to statements by children under age 13 in juvenile court and criminal proceedings concerning specified offenses. Requires the court to find particularized guarantees of trustworthiness before admitting any statement into evidence. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Child victims and witnesses under age 13, child advocacy centers, forensic interviewers, prosecutors, defense attorneys, criminal defendants, and juvenile respondents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural and is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory rules of evidence in criminal and juvenile court proceedings, requiring judges to conduct trustworthiness hearings, examine child witnesses or recordings, and oversee deposition procedures for forensic interviewers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Public defenders represent indigent defendants and juvenile respondents in criminal and juvenile proceedings where statements to forensic interviewers may now be admitted into evidence, requiring defense counsel to review notices and conduct depositions.

Local departments of social services work directly with Child Advocacy Centers where forensic interviewers operate and initiate Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings where these hearsay exceptions apply.
The bill alters evidentiary rules applicable to juvenile court proceedings involving juvenile respondents facing allegations of abuse, neglect, or crimes of violence.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals, which frequently involve challenges to the admissibility of evidence under statutory hearsay exceptions.

stakeholders: Operators and staff of public safety answering points, 9-1-1 emergency callers, law enforcement agencies, and individuals prosecuted for unauthorized computer access offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the incarceration and community supervision of individuals convicted under the bill's newly established felony offense carrying up to five years of imprisonment.

MSP is the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations, including criminal cyber interference targeting emergency dispatch and public safety answering points.
AOC provides operational and administrative support for the state court system, which will adjudicate new felony charges and proceedings established under this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD provides legal representation for indigent defendants who are charged with the newly established felony offense under § 7-302 of the Criminal Law Article.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires DNR to establish and implement the pilot program in coordination with the Invasive Catfish Advisory Committee, an executive advisory body.

stakeholders: Habitat for Humanity of the Chesapeake, Incorporated; Anne Arundel County; municipal corporations in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Anne Arundel County and municipal property tax revenues decrease to the extent eligible properties receive the credit, depending on assessed values and credit terms established by local governing bodies. Local expenditures are unaffected.

bill_summary: Aligns Maryland statutory definitions of military and veteran terms with federal standards across multiple state codes. Expands eligibility for burial in State veterans' cemeteries to qualified reserve members, their eligible dependents, and uniformed service officers. Repeals the state residency requirement for veterans seeking burial in a State veterans' cemetery. Requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to collect a burial fee for qualified reserve members and dependents. Mandates that the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families develop coordinated policies to assist service members and families through transitions. Extends anti-discrimination protections in housing and employment to reserve components of all uniformed services.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Maryland veterans, active-duty service members, members of reserve components and the uniformed services (including the Public Health Service and NOAA), and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in Department of Veterans and Military Families general and federal fund expenditures and revenues beginning in FY 2026 from additional cemetery burials and plot allowance fee collections; net impact is partially offset by federal reimbursements and NCA plot allowance fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is centered around the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF). It expands eligibility for burial in State veterans' cemeteries (creating operational and fiscal impacts), establishes definitions and hiring preferences at veterans' homes, mandates the development of policies for life transitions, and alters the Secretary's annual reporting requirements.

The bill amends the Election Law Article regarding definitions of 'active duty' and 'uniformed services', the use of Common Access Cards for voter registration, and rules allowing members of the uniformed services to file certificates of candidacy remotely.

The bill amends Title 20 of the State Government Article by expanding the definition of 'military status'—a protected class under Maryland's anti-discrimination laws for housing and employment enforced by the Commission on Civil Rights—to include members of a reserve component of the uniformed services.

The bill amends statutory language governing the Governor's role as commander-in-chief of the State militia relative to active service in the uniformed services, and requires the Secretary of DVMF to submit an expanded annual report to the Governor.

The bill updates statutory provisions and definitions relating to the State militia, reserve components, active duty, and the commander-in-chief chain of command for State military forces overseen by the Adjutant General.

stakeholders: permanently disabled transit riders enrolled in the Maryland Transit Administration's Disability Reduced Fare Program
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected, as the Maryland Transit Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Transit Administration to automatically renew the Disability Reduced Fare Program certification for permanently disabled enrollees and adopt implementing regulations.

The Maryland Transit Administration is a modal unit within MDOT, making the department directly responsible for the overarching administration and operation of state transit policy amended by this legislation.
The Department of Disabilities coordinates and improves services, including accessible transportation, for Marylanders with disabilities, and served as an information source for the legislation.
