bill_summary: Prohibits using State funds for permanent outdoor luminaires on State parks and trails unless specific standards are met. Requires state-funded luminaires to have a correlated light temperature at or below 3,000 Kelvins, excluding Department of Transportation installations. Exempts luminaires used to illuminate the field of play at a sports facility. Authorizes the Board of Public Works or its designee to waive the color temperature requirement. Requires the Maryland Green Building Council to update or develop outdoor lighting purchase guidance by October 1, 2026. Requires the Department of Transportation to conduct a review of highway lighting practices by September 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Green Building Council; Maryland Department of Transportation; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State agencies acquiring or maintaining outdoor lighting for State buildings, facilities, parks, or trails; Maryland Department of Transportation; sports facility operators
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State expenditures due to existing waiver procedures and prospective application; the Maryland Department of Transportation can conduct the highway lighting review using existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Green Building Council, which is mandated by the bill to update or develop guidance for outdoor lighting fixture purchases. DGS also manages State-owned facilities, handles State procurement, and serves as a designated authority for lighting waiver requests under Board of Public Works regulations.

MDOT is explicitly named in the bill; it is exempted from the Maryland Green Building Council guidelines and the 3,000 Kelvin temperature limit, and it is required by Section 2 to conduct a comprehensive review of highway lighting practices against FHWA guidelines by September 30, 2026.

The bill explicitly tasks the Board of Public Works (or its designee) with establishing waiver requirements and reviewing waiver requests for state-funded outdoor luminaire color temperature and uplight restrictions.
The bill expands restrictions on State-funded outdoor lighting to include State parks and trails, which are owned and managed by the Department of Natural Resources.
As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for non-toll highways, SHA is directly responsible for highway lighting and implementing the highway lighting review mandated by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directs the Maryland Green Building Council (an advisory/interagency body) to develop or update outdoor lighting guidance considering American Medical Association recommendations.

USM owns and manages extensive public campus grounds and facilities affected by State funding lighting standards, and holds delegated authority from the Board of Public Works to grant lighting waivers.

The bill explicitly exempts luminaires used to illuminate the field of play at a sports facility from state-funded outdoor lighting restrictions, which directly relates to MSA's sports venue development and management responsibilities.

Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to establish the program in cooperation with the Behavioral Health Administration. Mandates instruction on signs, signals, pavement markings, dangerous driving behaviors, and work zone safety. Requires instruction on impairment hazards, alcohol and drug penalties, and the Maryland points system. Requires certain license applicants who never held a Maryland or other state license to complete the course. Directs the Administration to adopt regulations establishing certification criteria for private entities offering the program.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Behavioral Health Administration
stakeholders: Driver's license applicants who have never held a Maryland or other state license, driver education students, and private driving education providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing resources, with no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing and administering the 3-hour Roadway Safety Driving Education Program, defining curriculum requirements, and adopting regulations to certify private course providers.
The Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the state's transportation operations, policies, and regulations.

Statute requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to establish the 3-hour educational program in cooperation with the Behavioral Health Administration, an administration within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing public health, the regulation of health occupations, and housing vouchers and assistance to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.

bill_summary: Expands statutory military definitions across Maryland law to cover all uniformed services rather than only the armed forces. Extends vital record fee exemptions and Medicaid waiver registry protections to all uniformed service members and their dependents. Requires health occupations boards to expedite credentialing and credit relevant training for active service members and eligible spouses. Prioritizes all eligible veterans equally for state housing vouchers and housing assistance payments. Authorizes health occupations boards to discipline practitioners disciplined by any branch of the uniformed services.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Health Occupations Boards; Department of Housing and Community Development; Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Members, veterans, and military families of the uniformed services, including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the provisions apply to a relatively small group of individuals, allowing any impact to be absorbed within existing agency resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes substantial amendments to the Health-General and Health Occupations Articles, directly affecting MDH operations including vital records fee exemptions, the Sheila E. Hixson Behavioral Health Services Matching Grant Program, DDA and Medicaid waiver eligibility, and expedited licensing/disciplinary procedures across health occupation boards.

The bill updates the core statutory definitions of veterans, uniformed services, and military families in Title 9, Subtitle 9 of the State Government Article (which governs DVMF) and amends provisions concerning veteran residency requirements and collaboration on behavioral health service coordination.
The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article to alter the definition and prioritization of housing vouchers and assistance payments for veterans and uniformed service members.
The bill updates eligibility and registry retention provisions for the Autism Waiver, which is administered jointly by the Maryland State Department of Education.
The bill modifies the Certificate of Need exception criteria for comprehensive care health care facilities serving veterans and service members, which is regulated by MHCC.
The bill names the Maryland National Guard as a required collaborative partner with MDH for providing behavioral health service coordination to eligible service members and veterans.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing both the Maryland National Guard and Maryland Defense Force, the Adjutant General is implicated in the interagency behavioral health coordination mandated under the bill.

Requires Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc. to submit an annual hotel tax usage report by November 1. Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Auditor to audit the organization's financial records. fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local finances and operations in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis are not materially affected.

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from obscuring or modifying a vehicle registration plate in a manner that may prevent identification. Authorizes police officers to enforce the plate obscuring prohibition only as a secondary action. Alters the definition of registration plate cover by removing clear objects. Prohibits advertising or promoting unlawful registration plate covers by falsely claiming they are lawful in Maryland. Classifies false advertising of registration plate covers as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice.
responsible_party: Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General; Department of State Police
stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and owners; sellers, manufacturers, and advertisers of registration plate covers; consumers; law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not materially affected. The bill can be implemented and enforced using existing budgeted State resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the false advertising or promotion of unlawful registration plate covers as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The MVA oversees vehicle registration, issues registration plates, and maintains driving records, including assessing driver's license points for moving violations like obscuring or modifying a registration plate.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle and traffic laws, MSP is directly responsible for enforcing the bill's secondary violation provisions regarding obscured or modified registration plates.
MDOT oversees state transportation policies and the Maryland Vehicle Law, serving as the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration.
The District Court processes citations, prepayable fines, and hearings for vehicle law violations related to registration plates and covers.

Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - 45th Alcoholic Beverages District - Licenses
bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C license on East Oliver Street. Restricts the license to on-premises consumption, prohibits conversion to other classes, and requires a community association agreement. Limits outdoor alcohol service to patrons seated at tables or standing in a courtyard area. Prohibits sales before 10 a.m. for the new Class C license. Establishes restricted sales hours from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. in a specified boundary of the district. Applies these restricted hours to Class A, Class B-D-7, and certain other alcoholic beverages license holders.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in the 45th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City, patrons, and the Greenmount West Community Association
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Local finances and operations in Baltimore City are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and collects applicable alcohol sales and excise taxes. Although this bill specifically concerns retail licensing and hours of sale administered locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it falls within the broader statutory framework of alcoholic beverages regulation in Maryland.

bill_summary: Establishes uniform definitions across Maryland law for terms including uniformed services, active duty, and veteran. Expands eligibility for special registration plates to recipients of high-level noncombat uniformed services medals. Removes armed forces restrictions on special disabled veteran registration plates to include any qualifying disabled veteran. Extends driver licensing exemptions, temporary identification renewals, and vehicle emissions exemptions to all uniformed services members. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to consult specified federal agencies and adopt regulations identifying qualifying medals.

stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services, including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, their families, and veterans
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances, including the Transportation Trust Fund, are not materially affected because the bill applies in a limited number of cases. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the bill's changes to driver's licensing, vehicle registration exemptions, special military and disabled veteran license plates, parking placards, temporary ID renewals, and emissions inspection exemptions.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the Maryland Vehicle Law and the Transportation Trust Fund, which are affected by the standardized military service definitions and fee/registration provisions.

The bill directly amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article, which provides core statutory definitions governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families, standardizing definitions of veterans, service members, and military families.

The Department of the Environment jointly administers the state's vehicle emissions inspection program with the Motor Vehicle Administration, which includes the updated exemption criteria for deployed uniformed service members.

Synopsis: Altering the quota for the number of Class A alcoholic beverages licenses that may be issued in the 8th election district in St. Mary's County.
Title: St. Mary's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class A License Quota
bill_summary: Alters the quota for Class A alcoholic beverages licenses in the 8th election district of St. Mary's County. Sets the quota in the 8th election district to one license for every 4,000 residents. Maintains the existing quota of one license for every 1,350 individuals in all other election districts. Prohibits transferring a license between election districts if the transfer exceeds the applicable quota. Requires the Board of License Commissioners to maintain quotas using County Planning Commission annual report population statistics.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Current and prospective Class A alcoholic beverages license holders and retail businesses in the 8th election district of St. Mary's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. St. Mary's County revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent fewer Class A licenses are issued under the reduced quota limit; specific figures are unavailable. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. Although this bill specifically alters local alcoholic beverage licensing quotas administered by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader regulatory domain of alcoholic beverages overseen by the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to conduct a thorough analysis of the State's regulatory framework for child care facilities with particular emphasis on regulations that limit a person's ability to register a child care facility, receive a license to operate a child care center, or operate a child care facility in a profitable manner while providing quality care; and requiring an interim and final report be submitted to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, and September 1, 2026, respectively.

bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Education to conduct a comprehensive analysis of Maryland's regulatory requirements for child care facilities. Directs the department to focus on regulations affecting facility registration, licensing, staffing, physical standards, and profitable operation. Mandates comparisons with child care regulatory frameworks in other states and regions. Requires consultation with advisory councils, private child care providers, and provider-representing unions and nonprofit organizations. Requires an interim report to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026. Mandates a final report with recommended regulatory changes by September 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: operators and staff of child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can handle the required analysis and reporting using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Education is the primary agency responsible for conducting the comprehensive analysis of child care facility regulations, consulting with required stakeholders, and submitting the interim and final reports.

Allows off-campus authority when complying with a memorandum of understanding with another law enforcement agency with jurisdiction. Clarifies that the expanded authority does not supersede the jurisdiction of the Washington County Sheriff's Office or other law enforcement agencies. Preserves the college police force's statewide enforcement authority regarding controlled dangerous substances.
responsible_party: Hagerstown Community College Police Force; Hagerstown Community College Board of Trustees
stakeholders: Hagerstown Community College police officers, Washington County Sheriff's Office, other law enforcement agencies with jurisdiction, and Washington County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. The bill affects local government operations but is not anticipated to materially affect local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill relates to the jurisdiction and operational standards of the Hagerstown Community College Police Force, which by statute consults with the Secretary of State Police regarding standards and qualifications comparable to the Department of State Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, housed within DPSCS, is referenced in existing statutory provisions maintained by the bill regarding the adoption of training and performance standards for campus police officers.

The bill references statutory authority allowing campus police officers to exercise extraterritorial police powers if ordered to do so by the Governor, and the office was consulted in the fiscal analysis.

stakeholders: St. Mary's County local government, developers, and property owners seeking new or expanded public sewerage and water supply systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. The bill creates operational efficiencies for St. Mary's County with minimal impact on local finances.

Synopsis: Adding programs, a day reporting program, an in-patient treatment program, and a pretrial release supervision program, that the St. Mary's County Sheriff is authorized to establish; repealing a requirement that the Sheriff or the Sheriff's designee collect the earnings of a certain individual participating in a certain program; and authorizing the Sheriff or the Sheriff's designee to direct an individual participating in a certain program to provide proof that the individual has made payments toward certain obligations.

stakeholders: Individuals court-ordered to the custody of the St. Mary's County Sheriff participating in detention, release, and treatment programs

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees correctional policy and statutes under the Correctional Services Article. agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent indigent defendants in St. Mary's County who may be court-ordered to participate in these alternative correctional and pretrial supervision programs or face sanctions and loss of diminution credits upon alleged violations.

responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for St. Mary’s County

Directs the Department to consult with specified fire service representatives, a higher education fire engineer, and housing advocates. Requires the Department to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Multifamily housing developers, affordable housing advocates, professional and volunteer firefighters, and local building code officials

The Department of Labor is required to submit its final study findings and recommendations regarding single-staircase building code changes to the Governor on or before December 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill's substantive provisions, which alter regulations and fee requirements for hunting and fishing licenses, clarify license lapse protections for deployed service members, and establish free day-use and per-vehicle entry to State parks for active service members, veterans, and Maryland National Guard members.

The bill directly amends § 9-901 of the State Government Article, which sets the statutory definitions governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families, updating and standardizing definitions for veteran, military family, active service member, uniformed services, and reserve components.

The bill amends Natural Resources § 1-405 governing the Healing Hunting and Fishing Fund administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust, altering the scope of eligible grant-funded outdoor and therapeutic opportunities to apply to all service members rather than solely members of the armed forces.
The bill explicitly grants all members of the Maryland National Guard, upon presentation of valid uniformed services identification, free day-use and per-vehicle entry to Maryland State parks.

bill_summary: Prohibits youth transportation companies from using visual impairment or mechanical restraints when transporting children to residential child care programs. Restricts physical restraints to situations involving a substantial likelihood of imminent serious physical harm. Prohibits picking up children between 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., unless under contract with the Department of Human Services. Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief and statutory damages for violations. Authorizes individuals to bring civil actions for restitution, damages, and reasonable attorney's fees within 10 years of majority.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: youth transportation companies, children transported to residential child care programs, and residential child care programs
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local governmental operations or finances. The Office of the Attorney General can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil enforcement actions against youth transportation companies for violations of restraint and transport restrictions, seeking injunctive relief and statutory damages.

The bill regulates the transportation of children to residential child care programs and explicitly provides an exemption from nighttime pickup restrictions for transportation companies under contract with the Department of Human Services. DHS also licenses residential child care programs.
The bill cross-references residential child care programs licensed by the Maryland Department of Health that serve children with behavioral, mental health, developmental, and substance use needs.
The bill cross-references residential child care programs licensed by the Department of Juvenile Services that provide specialized residential care and behavioral intervention for youth.

bill_summary: Revises State procurement laws governing agency oversight, preference programs, master contracting, and contract administration. Requires Executive Branch procurements valued at $1,000,000 or less to be designated for the Small Business Reserve program. Requires awarded contractors on covered procurements to utilize registered apprenticeship programs and, at $1,000,000 or more, internship programs. Establishes a technical evaluation factor in competitive sealed proposals for businesses demonstrating good labor practices. Requires the State to pay Small Business Reserve contract invoices within 15 days of receipt.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Chief Procurement Officer; Department of Information Technology; Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Transportation; Board of Public Works; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: State procurement vendors and contractors; certified minority business enterprises; small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; student interns; registered apprentices
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $840,800 in FY 2026, rising to $1.16 million by FY 2030, for legal and IT procurement personnel at the Office of the Attorney General and the Department of Information Technology. Other agencies can implement requirements with existing resources. State procurement costs may face an indeterminate increase across all funds due to compliance costs and potential reductions in vendor competition. No direct effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 500 significantly restructures State procurement law, expanding the powers of the Chief Procurement Officer (CPO) housed within DGS, altering DGS's procurement authority over equipment and services, adjusting master contracting rules, and delegating various administrative authorities.

The bill mandates that DoIT establish a technical procurement team with expertise in IT and agile procurement to collaborate with DGS on templates and assist agencies with IT procurement. The fiscal note provides dedicated funding and six new positions for DoIT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the Employment Works Program to GOSBA, transfers regulatory authority over small business qualification criteria and bidder lists from BPW to GOSBA, assigns GOSBA oversight and data collection for the new Veteran-Owned Small Business Reserve, and tasks GOSBA with adopting regulations for workforce and supplier diversity plans.

The bill creates an internship and registered apprenticeship requirement for covered procurements, placing enforcement, penalty determination, and regulation under the Secretary of Labor and funding the State Apprenticeship Training Fund. It also tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry with maintaining the list of businesses qualifying for the Good Labor Practices evaluation factor.

MDOT is granted independent procurement authority for transportation-related supplies and services, including IT, without DGS oversight. MDOT is also consulted on statewide MBE goals and sits on the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers.

Along with MDOT, MDTA is explicitly granted authority to procure supplies and services (including IT supplies and services) for transportation-related activities without approval of other primary procurement units.

The bill requires the Procurement Advisor to the BPW to conduct a comprehensive study on instituting an in-State preference for Maryland vendors, directs BPW to update regulations on expedited change orders, requires reports on expedited procurements, and shifts small business definition authority from BPW to GOSBA.

OAG receives reports of alleged apprenticeship/internship program violations to determine whether to bring civil actions, is consulted on MBE and VSBE regulations and goals, and receives general fund support in the fiscal note for an additional Assistant Attorney General position.
The bill creates a dedicated Veteran-Owned Small Business Reserve Program specifically applying to procurements conducted by DVMF (and the Military Department).

As head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General's agency procurements are specifically designated and made subject to the new Veteran-Owned Small Business Reserve Program established under § 14-602.1.

The bill codifies pay-for-success contracting provisions and explicitly requires MES to review and evaluate the results of all pay-for-success contracts completed by state units every three years and receive reimbursement for these reviews.

The bill amends § 14-205 to require the Department of Commerce to assist the Special Secretary for GOSBA in establishing procedures for compiling small business bidder lists and locating potential MBE sources.
The Department of Agriculture is one of the designated state agencies expressly authorized to enter into pay-for-success contracts for environmental outcomes under § 13-228.
MDE is specifically enumerated as one of the agencies authorized to execute pay-for-success environmental outcomes contracts under § 13-228.
DNR is specifically designated under § 13-228 as authorized to enter into pay-for-success environmental outcome procurements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services (or designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers under § 14-106.
The Assistant Secretary for Vocational Rehabilitation within MSDE is designated by statute as a member of the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers under § 14-106.
The bill alters authority over noncompetitive negotiation approval by transferring it from the Department of Budget and Management to the Chief Procurement Officer.

The bill updates the mandatory statutory nondiscrimination contract clause under § 19-116, which requires contractors to cooperate with investigations and provide records upon request of the Commission on Civil Rights.

The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees state procurement rules, approves CPO source selection methods, and receives reports and the in-State preference study required by the bill.
The State Treasurer is a designated primary procurement unit under § 11-101 and a member of the Board of Public Works reviewing procurement policies and contracts affected by the bill.
As a primary procurement unit under State Finance and Procurement law, USM is subject to the altered threshold requirements for small business reserves, task orders, and contract modifications.
As an independent primary procurement unit, Morgan State University is directly impacted by the revised procurement rules, reporting requirements, and Small Business Reserve thresholds.
As a primary procurement unit under Division II, St. Mary's College is subject to the bill's standardized procurement thresholds, master contracting rules, and small business reserve requirements.

The Maryland Port Commission/Administration is a designated primary procurement unit whose procurement jurisdictions and general procurement procedures are governed under Division II as amended by this bill.

The bill is an Administration initiative affecting executive branch procurement policies, and the Governor serves as the presiding member of the Board of Public Works receiving the study and reports mandated by the bill.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency managing state employee policies, recruitment, and benefits, DBM is directly impacted by state workforce hiring, retention, and career advancement initiatives for individuals with disabilities across state government.

The bill is an Administration bill that authorizes the Governor to include a $250,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill beginning in FY 2027 and mandates an annual report on the initiative's progress and recommendations to the Governor.

bill_summary: Modifies funding formulas and implementation timelines under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. Reduces the target per pupil foundation amount and adjusts mandated appropriations for coordinated community supports. Delays the required phase-in of teacher collaborative time and classroom teaching requirements under the career ladder. Establishes the Academic Excellence Program and the Maryland Teacher Relocation Incentive Grant within the State Department of Education. Alters eligibility, distribution, and allowable uses under the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program. Authorizes county governing bodies to exceed local property tax limitations to fund teacher pension and retirement payments.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board
stakeholders: Public school students, teachers and teacher candidates, school administrators, local school systems, county governing bodies, and local workforce development boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures decrease by $29.5 million in FY 2026 and by $156.1 million by FY 2030 due to reductions in the target per pupil foundation amount and community support appropriations. Special fund revenues increase by $602,700 in FY 2026 and $2.8 million in FY 2027 from interest earnings. County expenditures and local school system revenues decrease substantially beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which restructures major public school funding formulas under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, establishes the Academic Excellence Program and Fund, modifies the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program, oversees community school implementation plans, conducts a special education funding study, and administers new teacher recruitment and relocation initiatives.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and supervision, and the bill significantly reduces and restructures multi-year mandated state education appropriations (including the foundation formulas and the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund), institutes fiscal triggers limiting funding increases based on revenue estimates, and requires MSDE to report free and reduced-price meal eligibility data to DBM annually.

The bill is an Administration priority measure that alters statutory mandates governing the Governor's annual budget submissions—including appropriations for public schools, the Accountability and Implementation Board, and behavioral health supports—and establishes revenue downturn trigger mechanisms that require the Governor to freeze certain education aid increases.

The bill alters statutory mandated annual state budget appropriations to the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, which is administered within MDH (via the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports) to deliver holistic behavioral health services to public school students.

Under Maryland law, the Secretary of Disabilities jointly oversees accessibility specifications for digital education tools with MSDE. The bill enacts a temporary three-year exemption from accessibility procurement standards for digital tools that utilize artificial intelligence to support student learning.

The bill specifically amends Education Article provisions (§ 8-3A-09) that dictate the statutory per-pupil funding growth formulas and foundation calculation parameters governing state appropriations for the Maryland School for the Deaf.

The bill establishes the Academic Excellence Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund held and invested by the State Treasurer, with interest earnings directed to be credited to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
The bill directs the Comptroller to account for the newly established Academic Excellence Fund and its interest allocations pursuant to the State Finance and Procurement Article.

The bill extends mandated local education funding distributions to local workforce development boards through fiscal year 2028 to support middle and high school career counseling and registered apprenticeship pathways, which fall under the workforce development purview of the Maryland Department of Labor.

GWDB and its Career and Technical Education Committee are responsible for evaluating and coordinating middle and high school career counseling agreements and workforce readiness initiatives that receive extended funding under this legislation.

Public higher education institutions within USM participate in teacher preparation collaboratives under the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program, are eligible for Academic Excellence Fund grants, and are consulted by MSDE regarding community schools research and program evaluations.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Leaders in Environmentally Engaged Farming (LEEF) Program and its special fund in the Department of Agriculture. Directs the Governor to appropriate at least $900,000 annually to the fund starting in fiscal year 2026. Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to lease State land for healthy soils and regenerative agricultural practices. Exempts licensed commercial finfish harvesters using the ike jime dispatch method from food establishment licensing requirements. Establishes the Water Quality Monitoring Program within the Department of Natural Resources. Requires the Department of the Environment to certify water quality trading credits for government-funded oyster restoration projects.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers, commercial finfish harvesters, aquaculture leaseholders, restaurants, recreational anglers, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in fiscal 2026 and by $900,000 annually from fiscal 2027 through 2030 to support the LEEF Program Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures match these amounts annually through fiscal 2030. Indeterminate special fund revenue increases for the Department of Natural Resources from aquaculture advertising and survey fees as well as potential water quality trading credits from oyster restoration projects. Local government revenues may increase if they generate water quality trading credits from oyster restoration projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 506 establishes and tasks the Department of Agriculture with administering the new Maryland Leaders in Environmentally Engaged Farming (LEEF) Program and the associated special fund, alters the definition of healthy soils to include regenerative practices, and requires consultation on agricultural leases on Department of Natural Resources land.

HB 506 establishes the Water Quality Monitoring Program within DNR, alters statutory fishery management plan requirements, modifies aquaculture lease procedures and fees, authorizes long-term agricultural leases on DNR land for regenerative practices, and coordinates expedited permitting under the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.

The bill requires MDE to authorize oyster restoration projects to generate water quality trading credits and certify them by December 31, 2025. It also clarifies permitting applicability for stream and floodplain restoration projects and involves MDE in permitting coordination under the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.
The bill exempts certain commercial fishers who harvest and process finfish on a vessel using the ikejime method for direct sale to restaurants from obtaining a food establishment license from MDH.

The bill directs MEA to coordinate with the Department of Agriculture, Department of Natural Resources, and Department of the Environment to establish incentives for participation in the LEEF Program.

The Department of Planning is a statutory member of the State management team for the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership, which HB 506 tasks with developing expedited project permitting plans and tracking dashboards.
The bill alters procedures for contested aquaculture and submerged land lease protests, authorizing mediation by DNR before transmitting protests to OAH for administrative hearings.
HB 506 establishes the Maryland Leaders in Environmentally Engaged Farming (LEEF) Program Fund and statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Maryland Leaders in Environmentally Engaged Farming (LEEF) Program Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.

This Administration bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of at least $900,000 in the State budget for the LEEF Program Fund beginning in FY 2026.
DBM is responsible for overseeing the state budget and implementing the mandated annual general fund appropriation of at least $900,000 for the LEEF Program Fund starting in FY 2027.

The University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES), a USM institution, coordinates with DNR on science-based modeling and recommendations for the oyster fishery management plan as maintained in statute, and higher education institutions are consulted for LEEF conservation practices.

Synopsis: Clarifying a prohibition on including in State contracts provisions pertaining to limitations of liability for damage to real or tangible personal property; and clarifying a prohibition on including in State contracts provisions limiting the recovery of costs related to the use of replacement contractors under certain circumstances.
Title: State Contracts - Prohibited Provisions
bill_summary: Clarifies prohibitions against including certain liability and cost-recovery limitations in State contracts. Narrows the liability limitation ban specifically to direct loss from damage to real property or tangible personal property. Prohibits contract terms limiting the State's recovery of replacement contractor costs under specified conditions. Applies this restriction when combined payments to original and replacement contractors exceed the original contract amount. Renders any prohibited terms void and unenforceable while leaving the remainder of the contract in effect. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of General Services; Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: State contractors and vendors, replacement service contractors, and Maryland State procurement units
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central procurement and operational support agency, DGS is responsible for awarding and managing state contracts for goods, services, and facilities, and must ensure that standard contract terms comply with prohibited liability and replacement contractor restrictions.

The Board of Public Works reviews and approves major State procurements and contracts, ensuring they adhere to statutory requirements regarding prohibited clauses such as indemnification and liability limitations.
The OAG reviews State contracts for legal form and sufficiency, enforces contract terms, and represents the State in breach of contract and recovery disputes involving replacement contractors.
MDOT enters into significant capital, infrastructure, and operational contracts that must comply with statutory limits on liability provisions and replacement contractor recovery language.
DoIT manages major technology procurements and contracts, which frequently involve standard commercial vendor liability and indemnification terms that are directly impacted by this statute.
DBM oversees statewide budget execution, fiscal planning, and certain statewide procurement and service contracts affected by statutory contract limitations.

The State Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works and manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and state risk management, which intersect with limits on liability for property damage and contractor default recovery.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Contract Appeals adjudicates contract disputes between the State and contractors, including claims that turn on the enforceability of contract provisions rendered void ab initio under this law.

The bill explicitly references and maintains the statutory exception under § 2-901(a-1) for contracts relating to racing or training facilities defined under Economic Development Article § 10-601, which are overseen and developed by the Maryland Stadium Authority.

Synopsis: Requiring a State or State aided or controlled entity to require a prime contractor to procure certain janitorial products packaged or repackaged by Blind Industries and Services of Maryland.
Title: State Procurement Preferences - Blind Industries and Services of Maryland - Packaging and Repackaging

NarrowSubjects.Name: Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

bill_summary: Expands procurement requirements for State maintenance contracts that include housekeeping or janitorial services. Requires State and State-aided or controlled entities to mandate prime contractor purchases from Blind Industries and Services of Maryland. Applies to available janitorial products packaged or repackaged by the organization, to the extent practicable. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State or State aided or controlled entities; Department of General Services; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Blind Industries and Services of Maryland, prime contractors on State maintenance contracts, and small business janitorial suppliers
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances, although State procurement units may experience a minimal operational impact. No material effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services serves as the state's central procurement authority and manages the operation and maintenance of state-owned facilities. As such, it will be directly responsible for incorporating the expanded preference for products packaged or repackaged by Blind Industries and Services of Maryland into state housekeeping and janitorial maintenance contracts.

The Department of Budget and Management was consulted for the fiscal analysis and plays a key role in statewide fiscal planning, budget supervision, and operational efficiency across executive branch procurements.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts and ensures compliance with Maryland procurement law, including statutory procurement preferences.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Inventory of Cemeteries and Burial Sites Workgroup for the purpose of studying issues related to the establishment and maintenance of a State cemetery inventory system; and requiring the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Inventory of Cemeteries and Burial Sites Workgroup to study issues regarding a State cemetery inventory system. Requires the Maryland Historical Trust to provide staff for the Workgroup. Directs the Workgroup to review statutory definitions and evaluate cemetery documentation practices across Maryland. Requires the Workgroup to determine costs, funding sources, and system functions for a State cemetery inventory. Mandates evaluating the feasibility of a grant program to assist governmental entities and nonprofit organizations. Requires the Workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust; Maryland Inventory of Cemeteries and Burial Sites Workgroup
stakeholders: local governments, nonprofit preservation organizations, genealogical and historical organizations, cemetery operators, and descendant communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $42,200 in FY 2026 only for the Maryland Historical Trust to hire one temporary contractual employee to staff the workgroup from July through December 2025. Revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), which is a unit within the Department of Planning, is tasked with providing staff for the workgroup. The Director of MHT serves on the workgroup, and the department incurs a general fund expenditure of $42,178 in FY 2026 to hire contractual staff to support the workgroup.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Office of Cemetery Oversight (housed within the Department of Labor) is a designated member of the workgroup, and the Secretary of Labor is responsible for appointing several workgroup members representing local governments, genealogical organizations, descendant communities, and cemeteries.
The Chief of the Office of Cultural Resources within the Maryland Department of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup.
The Maryland State Archivist (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Inventory of Cemeteries and Burial Sites Workgroup as a temporary advisory body to study and make recommendations on a statewide cemetery inventory system.
According to the fiscal note, any legal research and analysis associated with the workgroup's responsibilities will be handled with existing budgeted resources of the Office of the Attorney General.
The workgroup is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

Synopsis: Increasing from 5 to 6.5 ounces of wine by the glass that a holder of a barbershop or beauty salon beer and wine license in Frederick County may provide to a certain customer for on-premises consumption.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum amount of wine provided to a customer from 5 to 6.5 ounces by the glass. Applies to holders of a barbershop or beauty salon beer and wine license in Frederick County. Authorizes license holders to provide wine or up to 12 ounces of beer for on-premises consumption. Limits service to customers receiving eligible services or attending permitted fund-raising events. Prohibits the service of beer and wine later than 9 p.m. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners; Frederick County Department of Permits and Inspections
stakeholders: Barbershop and beauty salon beer and wine license holders and their customers in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Frederick County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically alters serving size limits for local Frederick County retail licenses administered by the local liquor board, it relates to the broader regulation and administration of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulatory boards that issue barbershop and beauty salon permits under the Business Occupations and Professions Article referenced by the bill, though the legislation only modifies the volume of wine permitted to be served under local alcoholic beverage licenses.

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from keeping an individually maintained rooster movement-constrained using an enclosure or tether beginning January 1, 2027. Excludes commercial poultry producers, state-funded schools, government-operated animal shelters, and animal welfare organizations. Excludes qualifying 4-H or Future Farmers of America members and owners keeping more adult hens than roosters. Establishes that violations are civil offenses subject to warnings and civil penalties up to $1,000 per rooster. Authorizes enforcement by any State or local law enforcement officer or local animal control authority.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; local law enforcement agencies; local animal control authorities
stakeholders: rooster owners and keepers, commercial poultry producers, 4-H and Future Farmers of America members, animal shelters and welfare organizations, and local animal control authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from civil penalties. State enforcement can be absorbed within existing resources. Local government expenditures for animal control and law enforcement agencies may increase minimally in some jurisdictions, while local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes restrictions on keeping roosters movement-constrained and specifies that its provisions may be enforced by any State or local law enforcement officer.
The bill creates a civil offense with monetary penalties for unlawful rooster confinement, which are processed and adjudicated through the Maryland District Court system.

The department oversees avian health and poultry regulations in Maryland. The bill incorporates definitions from the Agriculture Article to exempt commercial poultry producers and directly addresses agricultural practices related to poultry keeping.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law governing the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners and the practice of chiropractic in the State related to Board membership, licensure of chiropractors, the discipline of chiropractors, and the denial of licenses to applicants; authorizing the Board to inspect chiropractor offices under certain circumstances; and requiring the Board to require a licensee or applicant to submit to an examination by a health care provider under certain circumstances.
Title: Health Occupations - State Board of Chiropractic Examiners - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Alters governance, licensing, and disciplinary standards under the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners. Authorizes the Board to conduct unannounced inspections of chiropractor offices regarding infection control complaints. Requires licensees or applicants to submit to health care provider examinations when objective evidence indicates potential harm. Replaces extern licenses with temporary licenses and creates an exemption for students in approved preceptorships. Modifies examination criteria and repeals bachelor's degree mandates for chiropractic licensure applicants.
responsible_party: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners
stakeholders: licensed chiropractors, chiropractic license applicants, chiropractic students, and chiropractic patients in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from civil penalties of up to $5,000. Potential minimal special fund expenditure savings from repealed examination publication mandates offset any Board-paid examination costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Chiropractic Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly modifies the board's licensing qualifications, disciplinary powers, inspection authority, examination administration, and regulations governing chiropractors in Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires applicants for newly established temporary chiropractic licenses to complete a state and national criminal history records check, which is processed by the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR).
The bill alters the statutory appointment criteria and nominating procedures by which the Governor selects chiropractor members to serve on the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners.

The office vets and processes appointments to state boards and commissions on behalf of the Governor and will need to apply the revised nomination requirements and list size parameters for appointments to the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain holder of a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in Anne Arundel County to convert the license to a Class C (veterans' organization) license; reducing from $400 to $300 the annual license fee for a Class C (veterans' organization) license; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to provide application and administrative fee discounts to certain licensees and applicants; and authorizing a Class C (veterans' organization) licensee to operate on Sunday without a Sunday license.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Veterans' Organizations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Authorizes qualifying Class C beer, wine, and liquor licensees in Anne Arundel County to convert to veterans' organization licenses. Classifies the license conversion and issuance as a license renewal rather than an issuance of a new license. Reduces the annual fee for a Class C veterans' organization license from $400 to $300. Authorizes the local licensing board to offer application and administrative fee discounts to eligible veterans' organizations. Permits license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor on Sundays without obtaining a separate Sunday license.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Veterans' organizations and Class C alcoholic beverages licensees in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County license fee revenues decrease by an estimated $2,400 annually beginning in FY 2026 due to lower license fees and eliminated Sunday permit fees. County expenditures and State finances are not affected.

Synopsis: Requiring a custodian of recorded images produced by certain automated enforcement systems to deny inspection of the images, subject to certain exceptions; prohibiting certain State and local agencies from using a recorded image or associated data from an automated enforcement system subject to certain exceptions; and establishing certain requirements and authorizations for the removal and destruction of recorded images and associated data produced by an automated enforcement system.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Automated Enforcement Programs - Privacy Protections

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road
