Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes privacy protections and data retention limits for automated traffic enforcement programs across Maryland. Prohibits State and local agencies from accessing recorded images without a warrant, subpoena, or court order, subject to exceptions. Requires agencies to immediately destroy recorded images and associated data that do not evidence a traffic violation. Permits retaining violation records until the earlier of one year after proceedings conclude or five years after capture. Prohibits automated enforcement systems from using biometric identifying technology, including facial recognition technology. Imposes a fine not exceeding $1,000 per violation on any agency that knowingly violates access restrictions.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; State Highway Administration; local police departments; local agencies operating automated enforcement programs; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and owners; State and local law enforcement agencies; automated enforcement vendors and program operators; individuals issued citations under automated traffic enforcement systems
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential indeterminate increase in administrative and operational expenditures for State and local agencies managing automated enforcement systems to update procedures, audit processes, and data-destruction workflows. The Judiciary expects to absorb any increase in warrant, subpoena, or court order requests within existing budgeted resources. Potential minimal revenue gain from civil fines of up to $1,000 per violation imposed on agencies that knowingly violate access requirements; specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the State Highway Administration as an agency subject to the new standards, requiring it to comply with privacy protections, independent data storage rules, audit procedures, and strict retention and destruction timelines for automated enforcement programs such as work zone speed control systems.

The bill explicitly defines a State police department as an implementing agency and places stringent limits on how law enforcement agencies may access, retain, use, and destroy recorded images and data from automated traffic enforcement systems.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration and oversees the state's transportation infrastructure and policies governing automated traffic enforcement under the Transportation Article.

The bill mandates that the Chief Judge of the District Court adopt procedures for the issuance of citations, trials, and collections of civil penalties in alignment with the newly established privacy standards, and the Judiciary will handle requests for warrants, subpoenas, and court orders.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration to study reorganizing the Maryland Transit Administration; requiring the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2025; and requiring the Department of Transportation, in consultation with the Department of Legislative Services, to submit to the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House draft legislation to effectuate the recommendations of the Workgroup.
Title: Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration. Directs the workgroup to study reorganizing the administration and the Maryland Department of Transportation. Requires evaluation of options allowing the administration to continue local Baltimore City transit services. Prohibits any considered reorganization plan from reducing funding for local Baltimore City transit services. Mandates a final report and implementing draft legislation by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration; Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland Transit Administration passengers, Baltimore City transit riders, and Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Transit Administration personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by an estimated $324,000 in both FY 2026 and FY 2027 for expert consultant services to evaluate contracts, budgets, and federal funding implications. Revenues are unaffected. Member expense reimbursements and staffing by the Department of Legislative Services are absorbable within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is directly responsible for co-staffing the Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration, the Secretary of Transportation serves on the workgroup and designates its chair, and MDOT must submit draft legislation based on the workgroup's findings. MDOT also incurs the fiscal impact of consultant costs via the Transportation Trust Fund.

MTA is the central subject of the reorganization study and potential restructuring evaluated by the workgroup, and the Maryland Transit Administrator (or designee) serves as a member of the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory, temporary study body—the Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration—to study transit reorganization options and report recommendations.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the workgroup who regularly use MTA services, and the workgroup must submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state task forces and advisory groups, including the two transit riders appointed to this workgroup.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transit Administration to develop and implement a program providing for the first month after transit service begins on the Purple Line, free ridership on Purple Line transit vehicles to individuals residing within a one-quarter-mile radius of the Purple Line track; and requiring the Administration to include, beginning on October 1, 2025, for 3 months after service on the Purple Lines begins promotional materials and services at no cost to small businesses located within a one-quarter-mile radius of the Purple Line track.
Title: Maryland Transit Administration - Purple Line - Free Ridership and Promotional Materials and Services

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to develop and implement a transit and promotional assistance program. Mandates free Purple Line ridership for individuals residing within a one-quarter-mile radius during the first operational month. Requires free promotional materials and services for small businesses located within a one-quarter-mile radius of the track. Directs business promotional services to run from October 1, 2025, through three months after service begins. Instructs the Administration to use internal resources, including agency websites and printing and design services. Requires the Administration to adopt regulations to implement the program.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Individuals residing within a one-quarter-mile radius of the Purple Line track and small businesses located within a one-quarter-mile radius of the Purple Line track
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by $75,000 in fiscal 2028 due to foregone fare revenues. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures likely increase from fiscal 2026 through 2028 to provide promotional materials and services, but specific cost figures depend on program scope and cannot be predicted in advance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 527 directly mandates that the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) develop, implement, and adopt regulations for a program offering free ridership on the Purple Line for eligible nearby residents and free promotional materials/services to nearby small businesses, utilizing its internal resources.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation will experience a direct fiscal impact through decreased Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) fare revenues and increased TTF expenditures to support the promotional program.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, from October 1, 2025, to July 1, 2028, a person from driving a motor vehicle in violation of certain provisions of the Maryland Vehicle Law on private roadways in a certain residential community in Baltimore County; authorizing, from October 1, 2025, to July 1, 2028, a police officer to enforce the vehicle law on private roadways in a certain residential community in Baltimore County; and prohibiting a person from driving a motor vehicle in violation of the Act on any roadway located in certain areas of Calvert County.
Title: Baltimore County - Vehicle Laws - Private Roadways in Residential Communities

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits driving a motor vehicle in violation of Maryland Vehicle Law on private roadways in Queen Anne Village in Owings Mills. Authorizes a police officer to enforce Maryland Vehicle Law on those private roadways from October 1, 2025, through July 1, 2028. Requires the Baltimore County Police Department to report on implementation and compliance to the county legislative delegation by September 1, 2028. Abrogates the statutory authority and requirements on September 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Police Department
stakeholders: Motor vehicle drivers and residents within the Queen Anne Village community in Owings Mills
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Baltimore County can likely conduct enforcement with existing police resources, and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes police officers in Baltimore County to enforce the Maryland Vehicle Law on private roadways within a specified residential community. As a statewide law enforcement agency with concurrent jurisdiction in Baltimore County, Maryland State Police troopers possess the authority to enforce these provisions, though primary enforcement is expected to be conducted by the Baltimore County Police Department.

The bill amends the Transportation Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland governing the application of the Maryland Vehicle Law to private roadways. MDOT is responsible for the overarching administration of transportation statutes and policies in Maryland, although the bill does not materially impact its operations or budget.

Synopsis: Authorizing a judge to consider whether a military protection order has been issued against a respondent when determining whether to grant a temporary peace order or a temporary protective order; and requiring a law enforcement officer to notify a certain law enforcement agency that an individual may have violated a military protection order under certain circumstances.
Title: Peace Orders and Protective Orders – Military Protection Orders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Authorizes a judge to consider whether a military protection order was issued against a respondent for similar conduct. Applies this authority when determining reasonable grounds to issue a temporary peace order or temporary protective order. Defines military protection orders issued under federal law in the uniformed services or National Guard. Requires an officer arresting an order violator to report suspected military protection order violations. Directs notice to the law enforcement agency that entered the order into the federal database.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: petitioners and respondents in peace order and protective order proceedings, military service members subject to military protection orders, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $99,900 in FY 2026 only for one-time computer programming costs. The bill has no effect on state revenues and no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by authorizing District Court and Circuit Court judges to consider military protection orders when determining whether to issue temporary peace or protective orders. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs a direct fiscal impact of $99,900 in FY 2026 for one-time system programming and updates.

The bill imposes a statutory requirement on law enforcement officers—including state troopers—who arrest individuals for violating peace or protective orders to determine whether the individual is a service member in violation of an active military protection order in NCIC and notify the agency that entered the order.
The legislation specifically defines military protection orders to include those issued against members of the Maryland National Guard by commanding officers under federal law (10 U.S.C. § 1567).

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the state's military forces and discipline, the Adjutant General is consulted on military protection orders and policies involving members under National Guard command.

Synopsis: Establishing the Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund to provide for the care, preservation, maintenance, and restoration of abandoned and neglected cemeteries in the State; authorizing the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $250,000 to the fund; and requiring an annual report by September 30 to the General Assembly on the donations to the Fund and promotional efforts undertaken by money from the Fund.
Title: Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes the Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor. Directs the Secretary of Labor to administer the Fund to care for, preserve, maintain, and restore qualifying cemeteries. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation of $250,000 to the Fund. Limits expenditures for promoting donations to no more than 5% of the Fund's net proceeds. Requires the Secretary to report annually by September 30 to the General Assembly on the administration of the Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Secretary of Labor
stakeholders: Communities with deteriorating burial grounds, owners and caretakers of neglected cemeteries, and descendants of individuals interred in abandoned or neglected cemeteries
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026, assuming the Governor provides the discretionary appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor increase correspondingly by $250,000 each year. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund to be administered by the Secretary of Labor and used to support cemetery care, preservation, and restoration, with annual reporting requirements submitted by the Secretary.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer must hold the Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund separately and invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of up to $250,000 to the Abandoned and Neglected Cemeteries Fund in the annual budget bill.

As the agency responsible for formulating the state budget and managing state funds, DBM would handle the inclusion and administration of any $250,000 general fund appropriation to the fund in the executive budget.

Synopsis: Requiring the Family Investment Administration in the Department of Human Services to be the central coordinating and directing agency of the federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program using certain funds and resources; and repealing the requirement that the Secretary of Aging administer the Program.
Title: Department of Human Services - Federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program - Administration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services' Family Investment Administration to coordinate and direct the federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program. Repeals the statutory mandate that the Secretary of Aging administer the program. Specifies the use of funds and resources received from the United States Department of Agriculture. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services, Family Investment Administration; Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Low-income individuals aged 60 and older eligible for food assistance, Department of Human Services, Maryland Department of Aging, and partner food distribution organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $22,000 in FY 2026 and $29,000 annually thereafter for the Maryland Department of Aging to maintain coordinator salary previously supported by federal funds. Federal fund revenues and expenditures of $225,000 in FY 2026 and $300,000 annually thereafter transfer from the Department of Aging to the Department of Human Services, resulting in no net change in federal funds. Local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 538 requires the Family Investment Administration within the Department of Human Services to serve as the central coordinating and directing agency for the federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program, transferring program administration and corresponding federal funds to the department.

The bill removes the statutory requirement that the Secretary of Aging administer the federal Commodity Supplemental Food Program, transferring federal funding from the Department of Aging to DHS and requiring an increase in general fund expenditures to cover existing administrative personnel costs.

Synopsis: Establishing a nonprofit organizations navigator within the Department of Commerce to provide technical assistance and work with nonprofits and units of State government to resolve complexities and delays in State grant-making processes, collect and share certain information, and represent nonprofit organizations' interests and concerns as a member of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council; and requiring the Department to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the implementation of the navigator.
Title: Department of Commerce - Nonprofit Organizations Navigator - Established

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes a nonprofit organizations navigator within the Department of Commerce. Requires the Secretary of Commerce to designate the navigator. Directs the navigator to provide technical assistance to nonprofits applying for State grants and resolve procedural delays. Adds the navigator as a nonvoting member of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council. Requires the Department of Commerce to report on navigator assistance and grant outcomes by January 1, 2027. Abrogates the navigator provisions on June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations seeking or receiving government grants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $80,400 in FY 2026 and $69,800 in FY 2027 for the Department of Commerce to hire one contractual navigator position. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes a nonprofit organizations navigator within the Department of Commerce, requiring the Secretary of Commerce to designate the position and requiring the Department to report data and recommendations to the General Assembly regarding the navigator's assistance, with direct general fund expenditures.

The Secretary of Budget and Management chairs the Maryland Efficient Grant Application (MEGA) Council, and the bill repeals existing statutory study and reporting requirements previously imposed on the Council and DBM regarding the potential designation of a State Grants Ombudsperson.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership and statutory duties of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application (MEGA) Council by adding the nonprofit organizations navigator as a nonvoting member and repealing the council's requirement to study and make recommendations regarding a State Grants Ombudsperson.

Synopsis: Authorizing a local department of social services to request assistance from federal law enforcement officers in an investigation relating to an alleged vulnerable adult; and altering certain provisions relating to the disclosure of certain information concerning human services to include adult protective services.
Title: Adult Protective Services - Investigations and Disclosure of Information

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Authorizes a local department of social services to request assistance from federal law enforcement officers during vulnerable adult investigations. Expands confidentiality protections to prohibit unauthorized disclosure of information concerning applicants for or recipients of adult protective services. Permits disclosing adult protective services information to administer adult protective services programs under specified official exceptions. Maintains misdemeanor penalties of up to 90 days imprisonment and a fine of up to $500 for violations. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, applicants for or recipients of adult protective services, local departments of social services, and federal law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local entities involved in investigations may experience operational efficiencies; however, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees Adult Protective Services (APS) and the local departments of social services. The bill directly impacts DHS by authorizing local departments to request assistance from federal law enforcement officers during vulnerable adult investigations and amending the confidentiality provisions governing social services records to explicitly protect APS records.

The Department of Aging collaborates closely with local departments of social services and local offices on aging in the protection and investigation of alleged vulnerable and older adults. The agency was an information source for the fiscal note regarding operational efficiencies in vulnerable adult investigations.

Synopsis: Establishing a certain appeal process for persons who are subject to the digital advertising gross revenues tax and receive a notice of assessment from the Comptroller; authorizing the Comptroller or the Comptroller's designee to issue an order to correct an erroneous assessment of the digital advertising gross revenues tax, subject to certain conditions; and applying the Act to assessments of the digital advertising gross revenues tax made after December 31, 2025.
Title: Digital Advertising Gross Revenues Tax - Assessments - Appeals and Corrections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer

bill_summary: Establishes an appeals process for persons assessed the digital advertising gross revenues tax. Authorizes an assessed person or governmental unit to submit an application for revision or refund claim within 30 days. Requires the Comptroller to promptly hold an informal hearing and mail a notice of final determination. Authorizes the Comptroller to issue an order decreasing or abating an erroneous assessment despite an untimely application. Specifies that orders or refusals regarding these abatements are final and not subject to appeal. Applies to digital advertising gross revenues tax assessments made after December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Persons and entities subject to Maryland's digital advertising gross revenues tax who receive an assessment notice
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $132,100 in FY 2026 to hire two senior tax attorneys in the Comptroller's Office to handle appeals, reflecting a 180-day start-up delay. Ongoing personnel and operating costs increase to $229,400 in FY 2027 and reach $260,900 by FY 2030. State revenues are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the tax appeals and assessment revision process administered by the Comptroller for the digital advertising gross revenues tax. The Comptroller's Office is responsible for conducting informal hearings, determining revisions, and issuing orders to correct erroneous assessments, requiring two new positions and an estimated $132,100 in expenditures in FY 2026.

The Maryland Tax Court is the quasi-judicial body hearing appeals from final determinations made by the Comptroller. By establishing formal statutory procedures for assessments, administrative revisions, and final determinations under the Comptroller for the digital advertising tax, this bill clarifies and directly affects the administrative process that precedes appeals to the Tax Court.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on January 1, 2026, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide coverage for self-measured blood pressure monitoring for certain eligible Program recipients; and requiring reimbursement of health care provider and other staff time used for patient training, transmission of blood pressure data, interpretation of blood pressure readings and reporting, remote patient monitoring, and the delivery of co-interventions, including educational materials or classes.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Maternal Health Self-Measured Blood Pressure Monitoring

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to cover self-measured blood pressure monitoring beginning January 1, 2026. Applies to recipients who are pregnant, postpartum, or diagnosed with chronic kidney disease, diabetes, heart disease, or cardiometabolic disease. Mandates coverage for validated home blood pressure monitors. Requires reimbursement for provider time spent on training, data transmission, interpretation, remote monitoring, and educational co-interventions. Subjects required coverage to the limitations of the State budget and federal law.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients who are pregnant, postpartum, or diagnosed with chronic kidney disease, diabetes, heart disease, or cardiometabolic disease, along with participating health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No meaningful State fiscal impact because Medicaid already covers self-measured blood pressure monitoring across qualifying diagnoses based on medical necessity. Local health department providers may receive reimbursement for qualifying monitoring services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill directly mandates Medicaid coverage for self-measured blood pressure monitoring for pregnant, postpartum, and other eligible recipients, and requires the Department to submit an annual report on program outcomes and cost savings.

Synopsis: Authorizing food establishments that are businesses that conduct agritourism, Class 4 limited wineries, or Class 8 farm breweries to comply with the requirement to provide a convenient lavatory by providing a portable chemical toilet that is supplied with approved hand drying devices, kept in a sanitary condition, is properly ventilated, and is placed at least 25 feet from a well.
Title: Food Establishments - Portable Chemical Toilets
bill_summary: Authorizes specified food establishments to meet lavatory requirements by providing a portable chemical toilet. Applies specifically to businesses that conduct agritourism, Class 4 limited wineries, and Class 8 farm breweries. Requires the portable chemical toilet to be supplied with soap, water, and towels or other approved hand drying devices. Mandates that the portable chemical toilet be kept sanitary, properly ventilated, and placed at least 25 feet from a well. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; local health departments
stakeholders: businesses that conduct agritourism, licensed Class 4 limited wineries, licensed Class 8 farm breweries, and their patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Health can update regulations and provide guidance to local health departments within existing budgeted resources. Local health departments can handle complaint responses and inspections within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly oversees food establishment regulations and public health standards under the Health - General Article. MDH is responsible for updating regulations and providing compliance and inspection guidance to local health departments.

MDE regulates chemical toilets and oversees groundwater and wellhead protection standards, which intersect directly with the bill's requirement that portable chemical toilets be situated at least 25 feet from a well.

MDA supports and promotes agricultural operations, agritourism activities, and on-farm alcohol production (farm breweries and limited wineries) that are specifically targeted for regulatory relief under the bill.

Synopsis: Altering from four to three the number of members elected from each councilmanic district of Baltimore County to the Baltimore County Republican Party Central Committee; and altering the number of members elected from each legislative district of Baltimore County to the Baltimore County Democratic Party Central Committee.
Title: Baltimore County - Political Party Central Committee - Elections
bill_summary: Reduces the number of members elected to the Baltimore County Republican Party Central Committee from four to three per councilmanic district. Alters the composition and district apportionment of the Baltimore County Democratic Party Central Committee. Allots ten Democratic members across legislative districts 11A, 42A, 42B, 43B, and 44A, electing two from each district. Apportions twelve Democratic members among legislative districts 7A, 11B, and 44B, electing four from each district. Designates eighteen Democratic members from legislative districts 6, 8, and 10, electing six from each district.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Baltimore County Board of Elections
stakeholders: Baltimore County Republican Party Central Committee; Baltimore County Democratic Party Central Committee; candidates for party central committees; registered Republican and Democratic voters in Baltimore County

bill_summary: Establishes binding arbitration for negotiations between the State and BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department uniformed fire employees. Exempts these negotiations from general statutory fact-finding procedures. Requires the parties to reach a collective bargaining agreement by September 30 of the expiration year. Directs the arbitrator to select one party's last, best, and final offer on or before December 15. Makes the arbitrator's decision binding, but subjects wage determinations to State budget limitations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Budget and Management

fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund and potentially general fund expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 due to shared arbitrator fees and potential labor relations staffing needs. State revenues and local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department operates directly under the Maryland Aviation Administration, meaning its uniformed fire employees are MAA personnel directly subject to the bill's collective bargaining and binding arbitration requirements.

As the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration, MDOT funds these positions through the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), participates in labor negotiations, and will bear the fiscal and operational costs of arbitration and potential compensation adjustments.

DBM is the State's central personnel and budget agency, works in conjunction with MDOT during labor negotiations, oversees state personnel policies, and must account for budget limitations and fiscal impacts resulting from binding arbitration awards.

PERB administers public sector collective bargaining across Maryland and is operationally impacted by statutory changes to dispute resolution mechanisms and potential jurisdictional overlap with arbitrators.
The Governor serves as the statutory party representing the State in collective bargaining negotiations, designates bargaining representatives, and executes final memoranda of understanding.

bill_summary: Expands educational, professional licensing, and scholarship benefits previously limited to armed forces personnel to all uniformed services members. Establishes uniform statutory definitions for military terms across education, general provisions, and state government laws. Requires the State Superintendent of Schools to expedite educator licensing for active service members, eligible veterans, and eligible spouses. Broadens nonresident tuition exemptions at public higher education institutions to all eligible active service members, veterans, and dependents. Extends the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to dependents of uniformed services personnel.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Emergency Medical Services Board
stakeholders: Active service members and veterans across all uniformed services (including the U.S. Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Officer Corps), their spouses and dependent children, and Maryland public schools and higher education institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an estimated $9,200 per scholarship award annually under the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program beginning in FY 2026, but the total number of additional awards cannot be reliably estimated. Public higher education institutions may experience a minimal loss of tuition revenue from expanded in-state tuition eligibility. Local school systems and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for state-administered higher education financial aid and scholarships, including the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship, to members of the uniformed services and their dependents, directly impacting program administration and potential expenditures.

The bill requires the State Superintendent to expedite educator licensing for active service members of the uniformed services and their spouses, and broadens public school enrollment hardship exceptions and the Purple Star Schools Program criteria to cover all uniformed services.

The bill updates foundational definitions within the Department of Veterans and Military Families subtitle of the State Government Article, including terms such as active duty, active service member, military family, and uniformed services, standardizing their application across state law.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the EMS Board within MIEMSS to credit relevant experience and training completed in the uniformed services (including NOAA and the Public Health Service) toward state licensure or certification requirements.
USM institutions are required to extend in-state tuition eligibility and priority course registration to active service members of all uniformed services, their spouses, and their dependent children.

As an independent public university, Morgan State University must extend nonresident tuition exemptions and priority course registration to service members of the uniformed services and their dependents.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland must grant in-state tuition exemptions and priority course registration to eligible active service members of the uniformed services and their qualifying dependents.

The bill amends the Maryland Disability Employment Tax Credit provisions under Education § 21-309, involving MD Labor's determination of service-connected disabilities for individuals discharged from the uniformed services.

The bill amends Education § 18-1910 to allow time spent on active duty in any of the uniformed services to be added to the allowable benefit period for prepaid contracts before termination under the Maryland Prepaid College Trust.

The Treasurer's Office oversees and administers the Maryland 529 program and its legacy Prepaid College Trust, which is amended by the bill regarding contract benefit period extensions for active service members.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority to authorize the provision of a guaranty under the Small Business Guaranty Fund in an irrevocable letter of credit, an official treasurer's check, funds on deposit in an escrow or other depository account, or any other legal instrument promising a financial institution restitution or reimbursement for its loan losses, within the limits of the guaranty.
Title: Economic Development - Small Business Guaranty Fund - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority to provide small business loan guaranties in specified forms. Permits guaranties via irrevocable letters of credit, official treasurer's checks, or escrow or depository account funds. Allows any other legal instrument promising restitution or reimbursement to a financial institution for loan losses. Prohibits governing terms and conditions from being so onerous as to discourage lenders from offering loans. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority; Department of Commerce
stakeholders: small businesses seeking long-term commercial loans; financial institutions participating in the Long-term Guaranty Program
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures are not materially affected, and revenues are unaffected due to historically limited program activity. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) and its financing programs, including the Long-Term Guaranty Program and Small Business Guaranty Fund, are administered by and housed within the Department of Commerce.

The bill authorizes specific financial instruments, such as official treasurer's checks, letters of credit, and escrow/depository accounts for state loan guarantees, implicating state treasury and banking practices on which the Treasurer's Office was consulted.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Nursing to hold discussions with Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia to pursue reciprocity agreements for advanced practice nursing licensure and specialty certification; and requiring the Board, by November 1, 2025, and each November 1 for the following 4 years, to submit a report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the status of the discussions, agreements reached, challenges in the negotiations, and any legislative recommendations.
Title: State Board of Nursing - Advanced Practice Nursing Licensure and Specialty Certification - Reciprocity Discussions (Maryland Border States Advanced Practice Nursing Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Nursing to discuss reciprocity agreements with specified neighboring nursing licensing boards. Covers licensing boards in Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia. Directs the Board to pursue reciprocity for advanced practice nursing licensure and specialty certification. Aims to enhance licensure portability, expand telehealth access, and increase access to qualified advanced practice registered nurses. Requires the Board to submit annual progress reports to designated legislative committees through 2029.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: advanced practice registered nurses, patients utilizing telehealth services, and nursing licensing boards in Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Nursing special fund expenditures can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources, though contractual staffing could cost approximately $90,000 if additional personnel are needed. Board special fund revenues may experience a minimal decrease if out-of-state advanced practice registered nurses no longer require Maryland licensure under future reciprocity agreements. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing (MBON) is a health occupations licensing board operating within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly tasks MBON with holding reciprocity discussions with nursing boards in neighboring jurisdictions and submitting annual reports on those efforts.

Synopsis: Altering the method by which the Comptroller must provide notice of the maximum income eligibility for the earned income tax credit for the calendar year to all employers in the State to include an electronic means of notification.
Title: Earned Income Tax Credit - Notice of Eligibility - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to provide required earned income tax credit eligibility notices to employers by mail or electronic means. Retains the requirement for the Comptroller to publish maximum income eligibility thresholds annually by January 1. Requires employers to continue providing notice by December 31 to employees who may be eligible for the credit. Allows employers to notify all employees or only those meeting wage eligibility thresholds. Prohibits employees from pursuing a private cause of action against an employer for failing to provide notice. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees potentially eligible for the federal or State earned income tax credit
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 due to reduced mailing costs. Fiscal 2026 savings are likely offset by one-time programming costs, but out-year expenditures may decrease by more than $100,000 annually. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which was requested by the Comptroller's Office. The bill authorizes the Comptroller to distribute the annual Earned Income Tax Credit notice to Maryland employers electronically rather than exclusively by mail, generating ongoing operational efficiencies and an estimated general fund expenditure reduction exceeding $100,000 annually.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a county's applicable income tax rate is the tax rate used to calculate the local earned income tax credit that certain individuals may claim against the county income tax; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
Title: Local Earned Income Tax Credit - Calculation - County Income Tax Rate

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Clarifies the county income tax rate used to calculate local earned income tax credits. Sets the rate as the lowest marginal rate for counties imposing marginal income tax rates. Sets the rate as the rate applicable to a taxpayer's income and filing status for flat-rate counties. Applies these calculations to nonrefundable local credits and optional refundable county earned income credits. Takes effect July 1, 2025, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers claiming the local earned income tax credit, particularly in counties with bracket-based or graduated flat income tax rates, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues or expenditures; the Comptroller's Office can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources. No direct impact on local income tax revenues because the legislation codifies existing administrative practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced at the request of the Office of the Comptroller. As the state's tax collector and administrator of personal income taxes, the Comptroller is directly responsible for administering the local earned income tax credit, receiving required county notices, and processing returns using the clarified tax rates.

Synopsis: Extending from 1 year to 3 years the statute of limitations for prosecutions relating to destroying funerary objects and other elements of a cemetery to begin at the time local authorities knew or reasonably should have known of the violation; and prohibiting a person from willfully destroying, damaging, defacing, or removing any part of the grounds of a cemetery.
Title: Criminal Law - Destroying Funerary Objects and Cemetery Elements - Statute of Limitations and Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Extends the statute of limitations for criminal prosecutions involving the destruction of funerary objects and cemetery elements. Requires prosecutors to institute charges within three years after local authorities knew or reasonably should have known of the violation. Prohibits a person from willfully destroying, damaging, defacing, or removing landscaping or any other part of cemetery grounds. Authorizes removing grounds or landscaping for repair or replacement with permission from cemetery managers or descendants. Subjects violators of these cemetery grounds prohibitions to misdemeanor penalties of up to five years imprisonment and a $10,000 fine.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; local law enforcement agencies; Office of the State's Attorney
stakeholders: Cemetery owners and operators, descendants and heirs of deceased individuals interred in cemeteries, and individuals prosecuted for property damage in cemeteries
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of criminal offenses relating to the destruction of cemetery grounds and extends the statute of limitations for prosecution, directly impacting judicial branch caseloads, filings, and court proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the misdemeanor offense of damaging or defacing cemetery elements and extends the prosecution statute of limitations to three years, potentially affecting criminal defense caseloads for indigent defendants facing penalties of up to five years in prison.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation, which manage individuals convicted and sentenced to incarceration or probation under the expanded cemetery destruction offenses.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates criminal property damage and enforces state criminal laws, including the newly expanded prohibitions regarding cemetery destruction.

The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for representing the State in criminal appeals resulting from convictions under the amended statute and providing legal guidance on statutory interpretations.

Synopsis: Clarifying which telephone calls the Comptroller of the State may record and monitor for training, quality control, and employee safety purposes; and providing that the Comptroller may monitor and record calls to the Comptroller's call centers only.
Title: Comptroller - Recording and Monitoring Telephone Calls - Clarification

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Clarifies that the Comptroller may record or monitor incoming calls to the Comptroller's call centers only. Replaces statutory references to automated call distribution systems with call centers. Prohibits recording or monitoring calls to or from direct individual lines in the Comptroller's Office. Maintains caller notification rules and restrictions on using call recordings in legal proceedings. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Callers contacting the Comptroller's call centers, Maryland taxpayers, and employees of the Comptroller's Office
fiscal_impact_summary: None. The bill does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Comptroller's Office or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental legislation directly clarifies and updates the statutory authority of the Comptroller of Maryland regarding the recording and monitoring of incoming calls to the agency's call centers for quality control, training, and employee safety purposes.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to allow the establishment of a system or program that allows an individual to purchase a State lottery subscription plan through an electronic device that connects to the Internet, such as a personal computer or mobile device; and requiring the Agency to report by December 1, 2026, to certain committees of the General Assembly on State lottery subscription sales.
Title: State Lottery - Internet Sales of Subscription Plans - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to allow individuals to purchase lottery subscriptions through the Internet. Applies to subscriptions for multijurisdictional or jackpot lottery games played across a specified number of consecutive drawings. Authorizes the Agency to allow licensed agents to sell vouchers that fund subscription purchases. Requires the Agency to pay licensed agents statutory commissions on voucher sales and eligible 24-month renewals. Requires the Agency to report subscription sales data to specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
stakeholders: Lottery players purchasing subscriptions and licensed State lottery sales agents
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from online lottery subscription sales. The State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency can implement the program and reporting mandates using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to implement an internet-based subscription sales program, oversee licensed agent voucher sales and commissions, and submit a mandated report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

As the state's chief financial officer responsible for receiving state revenue deposits and accounting for the General Fund, the Comptroller is minimally impacted by net increases in State lottery proceeds flowing into the General Fund.

Synopsis: Expanding the exemption from the sales and use tax for certain cannabis sales to include sales between certain licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries.
Title: Sales and Use Tax - Sales Between Cannabis Businesses and Cannabis Nurseries - Exemption
bill_summary: Expands the sales and use tax exemption for certain cannabis transactions. Applies the tax exemption to cannabis sales between licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries. Conforms business-to-business transaction rules under the State sales and use tax law. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances because the bill is clarifying in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's chief tax collector responsible for administering and collecting the sales and use tax. This departmental bill requested by the Comptroller clarifies sales and use tax exemptions on cannabis transactions between licensed cannabis businesses and registered nurseries.

The Maryland Cannabis Administration regulates the cannabis industry under Title 36 of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, including licensing cannabis businesses and registering cannabis nurseries involved in the tax-exempt transactions addressed by the bill.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "slot machine" to provide that certain skills-based amusement devices excluded from the definition may award merchandise, tickets, tokens, or other objects that do not exceed a certain minimal value per play and may be accumulated and exchanged for noncash merchandise or prizes of value that is similar to the cumulated value of the objects exchanged, and does not exceed a minimal wholesale value of $599.
Title: Gaming - Slot Machines - Skills-Based Amusement Devices

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the definition of 'slot machine' under Maryland criminal law. Excludes certain skills-based amusement devices that award merchandise, tickets, tokens, or other objects. Limits the per-play award to minimal value approved by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission. Permits awarded objects to be accumulated and exchanged for noncash merchandise or prizes. Requires the exchanged noncash items to have similar value and not exceed a $599 minimal wholesale value. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: businesses operating skills-based amusement devices and consumers playing skills-based amusement devices
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Enforcement can be handled with existing agency resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing skills-based amusement devices excluded from the definition of a slot machine, explicitly referencing standards and minimal values established and approved by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission through regulation.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing criminal laws, the Maryland State Police investigates illegal gambling and unauthorized slot machines under the Criminal Law Article, which this bill amends.

Synopsis: Establishing the Income Tax Reconciliation Program in the State to allow certain justice-involved individuals to establish installment payment plans and receive a waiver of any interest and penalties that accrue for unpaid income tax due for a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024, but before January 1, 2030; requiring the Comptroller to administer the Program; requiring the Comptroller, in collaboration with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, to develop an awareness campaign about the Program; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Income Tax Reconciliation Program - Established (Maryland Fair Taxation for Justice-Involved Individuals Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes the Income Tax Reconciliation Program administered by the Comptroller for eligible justice-involved individuals. Allows eligible individuals unable to file returns while incarcerated to enter installment payment plans up to 10 years. Requires the Comptroller to waive accrued interest and penalties on unpaid taxes for taxable years 2025 through 2029. Requires sentencing courts to inform defendants imprisoned between six months and 10 years about the program. Directs the Comptroller and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to develop a public awareness campaign.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Justice-involved individuals incarcerated for six months to 10 years in State or federal correctional facilities with unpaid State income tax
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2026 due to forgone interest and penalty collections. The Comptroller can administer the program with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 634 requires the Comptroller to administer the newly created Income Tax Reconciliation Program, establish installment payment plans, waive accrued interest and penalties for eligible justice-involved individuals, adopt regulations, and submit annual reports to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to collaborate with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to develop an awareness campaign informing justice-involved individuals and the public about the program.

The bill adds Section 6-237 to the Criminal Procedure Article requiring the court to inform qualifying convicted or pleading defendants about the Income Tax Reconciliation Program at sentencing, directly impacting court operations and procedures managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Expanding the eligibility for the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program to include individuals who received a certain degree from an accredited veterinary school and provided veterinary services in the State for not less than 5 years or provided volunteer veterinary services at certain animal shelters for 3 years and to include individuals who provided veterinary technician services for not less than 5 years or provided volunteer veterinary technician services at certain animal shelters over a 3-year period.
Title: Higher Education - Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program - Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program to include veterinary practitioners and veterinary technicians. Requires eligible applicants to hold a degree from an accredited veterinary college or university. Requires individuals to provide services as a Maryland employee for at least five years. Alternatively authorizes eligibility for volunteering at least 100 hours annually for three years at qualifying animal shelters. Covers shelters owned by local governments, contracted animal control organizations, or Spay and Neuter Grants Program recipients.
responsible_party: Office of Student Financial Assistance; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: veterinary practitioners, veterinary technicians, local government animal shelters, and animal welfare organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $8,000 in fiscal 2026 for one-time system enhancements at the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Expanding program eligibility does not mandate additional spending, but additional loan assistance repayment awards average approximately $5,800 per recipient if funds are available. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, directly administers the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program. MHEC will implement the expanded eligibility criteria for veterinary professionals and incur costs to upgrade its processing system.

The Commission oversees state student financial aid programs, including the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program, which this bill modifies to include veterinary practitioners and technicians.

The bill references organizations that were recipients of the Maryland Spay and Neuter Grants Program, a program established under and administered in accordance with Maryland Department of Agriculture guidelines.

Synopsis: Extending the deadline for the reporting requirement for the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services to be October 31, 2026; and extending the termination date for the Task Force to be June 30, 2027.
Title: Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services - Extension of Report Deadline and Task Force
bill_summary: Extends the reporting deadline for the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services. Requires the Task Force to submit its report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by October 31, 2026. Postpones the termination date of the Task Force from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2027. Allows the Task Force to continue assessing existing reentry services and identifying service gaps.
responsible_party: Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Returning citizens and individuals released from incarceration in Maryland; members of the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Additional expense reimbursements for task force members and staffing costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local finances and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for staffing the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services, which is tasked with studying and developing a plan to establish a new Division of Returning Citizens within DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the operational life and reporting deadline of the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services.

Synopsis: Establishing a temporary to-go event permit in Wicomico County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County to issue a temporary to-go event permit to a holder of a Class B beer, wine, and liquor license; establishing a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license in the county; authorizing the Board to issue a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license to a municipality in the county; requiring the Board to adopt certain regulations; etc.
Title: Wicomico County - Alcoholic Beverages - Temporary To-Go Event Permit and Class C Per Diem Municipal To-Go Beer, Wine, and Liquor License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a temporary to-go event permit and a Class C per diem municipal to-go license in Wicomico County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County to issue the per diem license to municipalities. Authorizes the Board to issue temporary to-go event permits to eligible Class B license holders adjacent to event areas. Permits participating Class B license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor in approved to-go cups. Sets fees of $45 per day for the municipal license and $20 per day for the permit. Requires the Board to adopt regulations concerning designated areas, hours of sale, and public safety.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County
stakeholders: Municipalities in Wicomico County and Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Wicomico County revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2026 from the $45 daily license fee and $20 daily permit fee, though the total increase cannot be reliably estimated. Local monitoring can be handled with existing county resources.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Secretary of Higher Education and the State Superintendent of Schools to select a designee to serve on the Juvenile Services Education Board; altering the terms of membership for the Board; and altering certain requirements for meetings of the Board.
Title: Juvenile Services Education Board - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Higher Education and the State Superintendent of Schools to designate representatives on the Juvenile Services Education Board. Staggers the four-year terms of appointed board members and limits members to two consecutive terms. Allows members appointed mid-term to remain eligible for reappointment to two consecutive full terms. Reduces mandatory public meetings from once monthly to at least 10 times per year. Authorizes special meetings called by a majority of members, the chair, or the Secretary. Phases in staggered terms through 2028 based on length of service or randomized lotteries.
responsible_party: Juvenile Services Education Board; Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Appointed and ex officio members of the Juvenile Services Education Board, Department of Juvenile Services staff, and State educators in juvenile residential facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and has no direct effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Juvenile Services Education Board, which oversees educational services in DJS-operated facilities. DJS is responsible for staffing the Board, and the Secretary of Juvenile Services is a statutory member with the authority to call meetings.
The bill directly amends the composition of the Juvenile Services Education Board to allow the State Superintendent of Schools to designate a representative to serve on the Board.
The bill directly amends the composition of the Juvenile Services Education Board by authorizing the Secretary of Higher Education to designate an individual to serve on the Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the governance, meeting schedules, term limits, and staggering of terms for the Juvenile Services Education Board, which is a state advisory and governing board.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing members to state boards and commissions, which is affected by the bill's changes to term staggering, term expirations, and vacancies for appointed members on the Board.

The Governor appoints the public and superintendent members of the Board with the advice and consent of the Senate, fills vacancies, and may remove members for cause under the altered term provisions.
The Attorney General or their designee is an ex officio statutory member of the Juvenile Services Education Board.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the State Board of Nursing may deny a license or grant a license, including a license subject to a reprimand, probation, or suspension, if an applicant for a license to practice direct-entry midwifery or a licensed direct-entry midwife violates a ground for discipline.
Title: Health Occupations - Licensed Direct-Entry Midwives - Disciplinary Actions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Nursing to grant a license subject to reprimand, probation, or suspension to direct-entry midwifery applicants. Clarifies disciplinary actions the Board may take against applicants and licensed direct-entry midwives who violate statutory grounds. Maintains the Board's authority to deny, suspend, or revoke a license, or place a licensee on probation. Retains established disciplinary grounds, including fraud, gross negligence, criminal convictions, and professional incompetence.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: Licensed direct-entry midwives and applicants for a direct-entry midwife license in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal or operational impact on the State Board of Nursing and no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing, which licenses and disciplines direct-entry midwives and is the primary regulatory entity affected by this bill, operates within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide coverage in accordance with the most recent guidelines issued by the American College of Cardiology that expand the scope of preventive care services for the benefit of consumers; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2026.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Calcium Score Testing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, managed care organizations, and certain health insurance carriers to cover calcium score testing. Requires coverage in accordance with American College of Cardiology guidelines that expand preventive care services for consumers. Applies to individuals with high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or family history of premature coronary artery disease. Applies to all health benefit plans and insurance policies issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: enrollees in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, commercial health insurance policyholders, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in fiscal 2026 from rate and form filing fees. Potential minimal increase in Medicaid expenditures (split equally between general and federal funds) to the extent utilization increases, though the service is already covered. Local government expenditures may increase minimally for jurisdictions that purchase fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is explicitly required by the bill to cover calcium score testing for eligible participants beginning January 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Alters the administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development. Authorizes public housing agencies to administer the program in accordance with their local administrative plans. Authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to project-base up to 100% of its authorized voucher units. Removes the requirement that public housing agencies equally prioritize vouchers across specified demographic groups. Replaces annual unit inspections with an initial inspection and at least biennial inspections thereafter. Increases the annual state funding distribution to public housing agencies to defray administrative staffing expenses.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income households seeking rental assistance, local public housing agencies, and rental property owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because overall funding for the program remains unchanged. Local revenues increase as public housing agencies receive an increased share of state program funds to defray administrative and staffing expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 716 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Department of Housing and Community Development's (DHCD) administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program. It includes DHCD in the definition of public housing agency, allows project-basing of voucher units, modifies inspection schedules and standards, and alters administrative funding distribution formulas to local public housing agencies.

Synopsis: Altering provisions of law regarding the acquisition of real property by the Department of Natural Resources; establishing a Land and Property Management Program in the Department to process certain  transactions; authorizing the Department and the Natural Resources Police to establish affiliated foundations; authorizing the Governor to transfer certain Program Open Space funds to the Department under certain circumstances; altering and repealing certain provisions of law regarding the use of Program Open Space local funding; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Public Lands - Acquisition, Staffing, Operations, and Funding
