bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to establish affiliated foundations to solicit funds and promote conservation and recreation. Establishes a Land and Property Management Program within the department to process real property transactions and departmental housing leases. Requires the department to request one permanent classified position per 400 acres of newly acquired fee simple land. Authorizes the Governor to transfer Program Open Space land acquisition funds above an $80,000,000 balance to cover operating costs. Allows qualifying local jurisdictions meeting acquisition goals to allocate up to 100% of their local apportionment to development projects.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Board of Public Works; Department of Budget and Management; State Ethics Commission; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland public lands, local governments administering Program Open Space funds, Department of Natural Resources personnel, and conservation partners
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $212,543 in fiscal 2026 for two positions in the Land and Property Management Program, rising to nearly $1.9 million by fiscal 2030 to support additional staff. Special fund spending may further increase if Program Open Space balances exceeding $80.0 million are transferred to cover operating costs. Local governments gain greater flexibility to use Program Open Space allocations for development projects and local plan updates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which restructures real property acquisition processes, creates the Land and Property Management Program, establishes affiliated foundations, modifies staffing formulas based on acquired acreage, and alters the use of Program Open Space funds.

The Board of Public Works must approve real property interest acquisitions, easement valuation systems, property disposals and exchanges, and continues to supervise acquisition expenditures under the Natural Resources Article.

DNR is required to submit budget requests directly to DBM to fund and create new permanent, classified positions based on the ratio of at least one position per 400 acres of newly acquired fee simple land.

The Department of Planning, in conjunction with DNR, is responsible for certifying whether local jurisdictions have met their acquisition goals in approved local land preservation and recreation plans, which dictates the local allocation of Program Open Space funds.
The Attorney General is required to review policies developed by DNR for operating affiliated foundations for form and legal sufficiency and approve them if appropriate.

The State Ethics Commission must review and approve conflict-of-interest policies for affiliated foundations, receive notifications and annual reports regarding DNR staff serving on foundation boards, and register any objections.
DNR is required to consult with DGS when developing the system for appraisal review included in regulations for real property interest acquisitions.

The Governor is authorized to execute fund transfers from the Program Open Space State land acquisition balance to DNR when statutory threshold conditions are met, and receives annual reports on DNR affiliated foundations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor and assess the impact of potential and actual federal changes to specified health care programs and to provide recommendations for State and local action to protect the access of residents of the State to affordable health coverage; and requiring the Commission to submit a report of its findings and recommendations, including any legislative proposals, to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31 each year.
Title: Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor and assess federal health care changes. Tasks the Commission with reviewing changes to the ACA, MHPAEA, Medicaid, MCHP, Medicare, and the Maryland All-Payer Model. Requires the Commission to recommend State and local actions to protect resident access to affordable health coverage. Authorizes the Commission to hold public meetings across the State and convene stakeholder workgroups. Mandates annual reporting of findings and legislative proposals to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission
stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking affordable health coverage, health insurance carriers, healthcare and behavioral health providers, hospitals, nursing homes, and employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources by the Department of Legislative Services, the Maryland Department of Health, and the Maryland Insurance Administration. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission, and the Department is explicitly tasked with co-staffing the commission alongside MIA and DLS. Additionally, the commission monitors programs administered by MDH, including Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) serves as a member of the commission, and the agency is mandated to jointly provide staffing and operational support for the commission with MDH and DLS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a statutory multi-stakeholder commission—the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission—to study, monitor, and advise on federal health care policy changes and health coverage in the state.

The Executive Director of the Health Services Cost Review Commission (or designee) is a designated member of the commission, which is specifically tasked with monitoring and assessing impacts on the Maryland All-Payer Model administered by HSCRC.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (or designee) is a designated member of the commission, whose core charge involves monitoring ACA changes and ensuring Marylanders retain access to affordable health coverage through individual and small group markets.
The Attorney General (or designee) is an ex officio member of the established commission to evaluate legal and federal policy impacts on health care coverage.

The Governor is responsible for appointing four members of the commission (an employer, a nursing home industry representative, a public member, and an HMO representative) and will receive annual reports and legislative recommendations from the commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees to the newly re-established commission.

Synopsis: Repealing certain advertising and public hearing requirements for proposed regulations implementing the State Boat Act; increasing certain funding thresholds for certain projects financed by the Waterway Improvement Fund; and altering the fees for manufacturer and dealer licenses, certificates of number, Maryland use stickers, and the issuance of certificates of title, transfer of title, or duplicate or corrected certificates of title.
Title: Natural Resources - State Boat Act - Alterations

bill_summary: Alters fee structures, safety standards, financing thresholds, and regulatory procedures under the State Boat Act. Increases fees for certificates of title, vessel certificates of number, Maryland use stickers, and manufacturer or dealer licenses. Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to establish temporary speed zones or restricted areas by public notice during emergencies. Raises Waterway Improvement Fund complete financing limits to $500,000 for boating construction and $1,000,000 for public marina projects. Permits owners of qualifying nonmotorized vessels to apply for a two-year vessel decal for a $12 fee. Repeals newspaper advertising and citizen petition hearing requirements for proposed Department regulations implementing the Act.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: vessel owners, boat manufacturers and dealers, livery vessel owners, recreational boaters, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Natural Resources special fund revenues increase by approximately $4.9 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 due to higher vessel registration, titling, and license fees. Special fund expenditures are expected to increase by $100,000 or more annually beginning in fiscal 2026 from higher spending caps on Waterway Improvement Fund small projects, partially offset by modest advertising savings. Local governments gain access to higher funding limits for local marina and waterway construction projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency for the State Boat Act. The bill directly alters DNR's vessel titling, numbering, and dealer licensing fees, modifies definitions enforced by DNR, updates funding limits for DNR's Waterway Improvement Fund, authorizes DNR to establish speed zones and offer nonmotorized vessel decals, and generates approximately $4.9 million annually in special fund revenues for DNR.

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law relating to the Somers Cove Marina Commission, the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund, and the operation of Somers Cove Marina; requiring the Secretary to develop a master plan for the operation and improvement of services at Somers Cove Marina by October 1, 2027; requiring all revenue received by the Department from activities associated with Somers Cove Marina be deposited in the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund; establishing the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Repeal of Somers Cove Marina Commission and Improvement Fund and Alteration of Operations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals provisions governing the Somers Cove Marina Commission and the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund. Transfers operations and management of Somers Cove Marina to the Department of Natural Resources. Authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to execute leases, procure contracts, employ staff, and assess fees. Requires the Secretary to develop an initial marina master plan by October 1, 2027. Establishes the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission within the Department of Natural Resources. Directs all marina revenues into the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Secretary of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Somers Cove Marina slip holders, boat owners, commercial fishers, local businesses in Somerset County and the City of Crisfield, and marina staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase and special fund expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2026, potentially by over $1.0 million annually if DNR operates the marina directly. The remaining balance of the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund transfers to the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund on October 1, 2025. General fund interest earnings increase minimally through fiscal 2028. Local finances in Somerset County and Crisfield are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the management, operations, maintenance, and development of Somers Cove Marina to the Department of Natural Resources, authorizing the Secretary to hire staff, execute leases and contracts, set fees, develop master plans, and administer the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the statutory Somers Cove Marina Commission and establishes a new advisory body, the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission, to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources on marina management and operations.

The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold and invest money in the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund separately, crediting interest earnings directly to the fund pursuant to an amendment to the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund and handle the accounting of related revenues and interest.
The bill authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to employ and set compensation for marina staff and a marina manager, which interacts with state personnel and budget oversight managed by DBM.

The bill alters leasing, contracting, and property maintenance provisions for state-owned land and facilities at Somers Cove Marina, areas subject to general procurement and state property lease review by the Board of Public Works.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports on or before December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, to the Senate Finance Committee, the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, the House Health and Government Operations Committee, and the House Appropriations Committee on the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs and recovery residences.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Report on Oversight of Substance Use Disorder Treatment Programs and Recovery Residences

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to report on the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs and recovery residences. Mandates submission of the reports to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026. Requires the reports to detail revisions to COMAR 10.63 and improvements to recovery residence certification and monitoring procedures. Directs the Department to analyze how regulatory changes will prevent events similar to those reported regarding PHA Healthcare. Specifies that this analysis must address patient relapse and death among individuals housed in provider-owned buildings.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Substance use disorder treatment programs, recovery residences, and patients receiving substance use disorder treatment while residing in provider-owned housing
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 722 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, regarding the revision of COMAR 10.63, improvements to the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs, and certification/monitoring procedures for recovery residences.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Dental Examiners to issue a license or certification to certain applicants licensed or certified by another state within 15 business days after receiving the completed application; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop a plan for a temporary or permanent authorization to practice a health occupation in the State for certain individuals who left employment with a federal agency after January 20, 2025; requiring the Department to submit the plan by October 1, 2025 to certain committees; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Authorization to Practice for Former Federal Employees and Dental Applicants Licensed or Certified in Another State

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to issue licenses or certificates to qualified out-of-state applicants within 15 business days. Establishes certification criteria for dental radiation technologists authorized to practice in another state. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to develop an authorization plan for certain former federal health care workers. Applies the plan to individuals holding equivalent out-of-state credentials who left federal employment after January 20, 2025. Requires the Department to submit the plan to specified legislative committees by October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed dentists, dental hygienists, and dental radiation technologists; former federal employees in health occupations who left service after January 20, 2025
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the State Board of Dental Examiners and Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues for health occupations boards may increase minimally and indeterminately from additional application and renewal fees. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its State Board of Dental Examiners with expedited licensing requirements for out-of-state dental professionals, and explicitly mandates that MDH develop and submit a plan to authorize certain former federal employees to practice health occupations in Maryland.

Synopsis: Altering the allowable uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to provide funds for the operating expenses and personnel costs for investigations, enforcement actions, and other activities conducted by the Opioids Enforcement Unit within the Office of the Attorney General that are related to the recovery of funds from opioid-related judgments or settlements; and requiring, beginning October 1, 2025, the Office of the Attorney General to report annually to the General Assembly on the status of activity of the Opioids Enforcement Unit.
Title: Opioid Restitution Fund - Authorized Uses

bill_summary: Expands the allowable uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to include operating expenses and personnel costs for the Opioids Enforcement Unit. Authorizes funding specifically for investigations, enforcement actions, and activities related to recovering opioid judgments or settlements. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to submit an annual report on unit activity beginning October 1, 2025. Mandates reporting to the Governor and the General Assembly on investigations, lawsuits filed, and lawsuit dispositions. Takes effect July 1, 2025, and terminates on June 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Opioids Enforcement Unit, Maryland's Office of Overdose Response, and community-based organizations providing substance use disorder recovery services
fiscal_impact_summary: Likely no net impact on total Opioid Restitution Fund expenditures or State revenues. The fiscal 2026 State budget provides $1.5 million in special funds from the Opioid Restitution Fund to the Office of the Attorney General annually through fiscal 2029, offsetting an equivalent amount of funding previously available for other discretionary opioid abatement grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of the Attorney General by authorizing the use of Opioid Restitution Fund monies for the operating expenses and personnel costs of its Opioids Enforcement Unit ($1.5 million annually), and mandates that the office submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly detailing its investigations and litigation.

The Maryland Department of Health and its affiliated Office of Overdose Response administer the Opioid Restitution Fund. Allocating $1.5 million annually from the fund to the Office of the Attorney General directly decreases the amount of discretionary fund monies available to the department for other opioid prevention, treatment, and abatement grants.

Beginning October 1, 2025, and annually thereafter through 2028, the Office of the Attorney General is required to submit an annual report directly to the Governor on the operational status, investigations, and lawsuit dispositions of the Opioids Enforcement Unit.

Synopsis: Altering the training that the Maryland Department of Health is authorized to provide under the Overdose Response Program to include emphasis on the restoration of breathing, avoiding withdrawal, and compassionate postoverdose support and care; clarifying that the use of the Opioid Restitution Fund is subject to certain restrictions; and altering the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund so as to include the addressing of racial disparities in access to prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services.
Title: Public Health - Use of Opioid Restitution Fund and Training Under the Overdose Response Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Opioids -see also- Controlled Dangerous Substances; Drugs

bill_summary: Aligns authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund with purposes specified in opioid-related settlement agreements and court judgments. Repeals the specific statutory list of funded programs while maintaining support for evidence-based prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction. Adds explicit authorization to use fund monies to address racial and socioeconomic disparities in service access. Alters Overdose Response Program training authorized by the Maryland Department of Health. Requires this training to emphasize breathing restoration, avoiding withdrawal, and compassionate postoverdose care.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council
stakeholders: individuals with substance use disorders, overdose response training providers and trainees, community-based nonprofit recovery organizations, and communities experiencing racial or socioeconomic disparities in healthcare access
fiscal_impact_summary: No material state or local fiscal impact. The bill alters allowable uses of existing Opioid Restitution Fund revenues to align with settlement agreements without impacting overall funding levels or existing programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency directly responsible for administering the Overdose Response Program and managing/distributing the Opioid Restitution Fund under the altered statutory guidelines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council is tasked with reviewing, determining emerging evidence for, and approving funding for substance use disorder pilot programs and demonstration studies.
The OAG prosecutes and negotiates the opioid settlement agreements and judgments whose terms define and restrict allowable uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund under this legislation.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Opioid Restitution Fund, whose allowable expenditures and parameters are amended by the bill.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and maintain the Opioid Restitution Fund as a separate, nonlapsing special fund.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Connectivity Coalition to foster collaboration among State and federal agencies, nongovernmental organizations, and other stakeholders for the purpose of protecting endangered wildlife from habitat fragmentation; requiring the State Highway Administration to have final decision-making authority regarding decisions related to placement, funding, or design of wildlife crossings; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Connectivity Coalition to reduce vehicle-wildlife collisions and improve habitat connectivity across the State. Designates the State Highway Administrator as coalition chair with final authority over wildlife crossing placement, funding, and design. Requires the coalition to develop project prioritization criteria, performance metrics, and a public website. Mandates that the State Highway Administration report on wildlife crossings in each Consolidated Transportation Plan. Requires local jurisdictions to consider wildlife movement and habitat connectivity when adopting or amending comprehensive plans. Directs the Maryland Department of Planning to coordinate with State agencies to provide connectivity data to local jurisdictions.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Planning; Maryland Connectivity Coalition
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, local governments, and wildlife conservation organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by an estimated $50,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026 for consultant research and staffing services. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration (SHA) is a primary implementing agency under the bill. The State Highway Administrator serves as the Chair of the newly created Maryland Connectivity Coalition, SHA co-adopts coalition rules with DNR, retains final decision-making authority over wildlife crossings, must report on crossings in the Consolidated Transportation Program, and incurs an estimated $50,000 annual fiscal impact for consultant and staffing support.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the Consolidated Transportation Program (which must include new reporting on wildlife crossings) and administers the Transportation Trust Fund, which will fund the coalition's annual consultant and staffing expenditures.

The Secretary of Natural Resources is designated as a member of the Maryland Connectivity Coalition. DNR is charged with co-adopting operational rules with SHA, adopting regulations, and coordinating with the Department of Planning and SHA to furnish habitat connectivity data to local governments.

The bill amends the Land Use Article to require the Department of Planning to coordinate with DNR and SHA to supply charter counties and local jurisdictions with updated information on habitat connectivity concerns and planned wildlife crossings for their comprehensive plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates a new collaborative entity, the Maryland Connectivity Coalition, composed of agency leadership, legislators, and stakeholders tasked with developing criteria, evaluating performance metrics, and meeting regularly regarding wildlife crossings and habitat connectivity.

Synopsis: Providing that a unit of State government may not purchase, lease, contract for, or rent an information technology service or product unless consistent with the master plan, as determined by the Secretary of Information Technology; providing that the Secretary is responsible for overseeing the implementation of major information technology development projects in the State; establishing the Maryland Office of Digital Experience in the Department to provide oversight, leadership, and strategic modernization for major technology projects; etc.
Title: Department of Information Technology - Major Information Technology Development Projects - Oversight
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 845

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes oversight standards and funding controls for major information technology development projects across units of State government. Authorizes the Secretary of Budget and Management to withhold or reallocate project funds upon the Secretary of Information Technology's recommendation. Establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience, the Maryland Digital Service Unit, and the Major Information Technology Development Project Oversight Division. Requires the Department of Information Technology to publish an online public dashboard tracking major development projects. Establishes the Information Technology Advisory Board to advise the Legislative Policy Committee on State enterprise technology initiatives. Repeals the Modernize Maryland Commission and modifies annual reporting requirements for the Information Technology Investment Fund.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Department of Budget and Management; Department of Legislative Services; Department of General Services
stakeholders: Units of State government, State agency Chief Information Officers, information technology contractors and vendors, and Maryland residents using State digital services
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Information Technology Investment Fund increase by at least $4,300,000 in fiscal 2026 for staffing, with out-year expenditures likely increasing by at least that amount. General funds may be required if special funds are unavailable. Potential agency savings from enterprise efficiencies are indeterminate. No effect on local finances or State revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The legislation substantially expands the Secretary of Information Technology's oversight over major IT development projects, establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience (MODE), the Maryland Digital Service Unit (MDSU), and the Major Information Technology Development Project Oversight Division (MIDPOD) within the department, and mandates the creation and maintenance of a public IT project dashboard.

DBM has direct statutory responsibilities under the bill, including withholding or reallocating unexpended major IT project funds upon recommendation of the Secretary of Information Technology, approving employee compensation structures proposed for MODE, and executing budget amendments and fund transfers.

DGS is required, in consultation with DoIT, to report semiannually to legislative committees on projects over $1,000,000 undertaken by State units under master contracts for Statewide Agile Resources and Teams (START) or work orders approved by the Board of Public Works.

The Governor is authorized to approve budget amendments transferring funds and up to 50 budgeted positions to MODE, receives reports whenever major IT project funds are withheld, and oversees executive branch compliance.

State units managing major IT projects must submit formal notices to BPW within 30 days of contract award affirming DoIT approval and unit head accountability; the bill also monitors and requires reporting on START work orders and contracts approved by BPW.

The bill repeals an uncodified mandate for a study on an April 2024 OLA audit and creates a legislative workgroup tasked with evaluating actions needed to resolve the 2024 audit findings from OLA regarding State IT management.

Members appointed to the newly established Information Technology Advisory Board are subject to the Public Ethics Law and are explicitly required to submit conflict-of-interest and employment disclosures to the State Ethics Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally abolishes and repeals the statutory provisions establishing the Modernize Maryland Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the penalties and points assessments related to the offenses of reckless, negligent, and aggressive driving; and adding certain motor vehicle offenses as elements that may contribute to charges for reckless or aggressive driving.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Reckless, Negligent, and Aggressive Driving (Sergeant Patrick Kepp Act)

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Expands the definition of reckless driving to include traveling at least 30 miles per hour over the posted speed limit. Subjects reckless driving violators to imprisonment for up to 60 days, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Increases maximum fines to $750 for negligent driving and $1,000 for aggressive driving. Lowers the aggressive driving threshold from three offenses to two and expands qualifying violations. Alters driver's license point assessments to two points for negligent driving and six points for excessive speeding.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Motor vehicle drivers in Maryland, law enforcement officers, and indigent defendants facing reckless driving charges
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $534,800 in FY 2026 for the Office of the Public Defender to hire attorneys and support staff for incarcerable reckless driving cases. General fund revenues increase minimally from higher District Court fines. State and local incarceration expenditures may increase minimally.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters point assessments administered by the MVA for negligent driving and excessive speeding (30 mph or more above the posted limit) and will lead to an increase in driver's license suspensions and revocations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes reckless driving an incarcerable offense, requiring OPD to provide legal representation to indigent defendants and creating a significant operational and fiscal impact of over $534,000 annually for additional attorneys and support staff.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and administrator of the Maryland Transportation Article being amended, MDOT oversees state transportation policy and driver licensing systems impacted by the bill.

The bill makes reckless driving an incarcerable offense that requires mandatory court appearances rather than prepayable fines, affecting District Court and Circuit Court traffic case dockets and fine collection.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency enforcing traffic safety laws on state highways, MSP troopers will investigate and enforce the expanded definitions of reckless and aggressive driving.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS may see a minor increase in expenditures and inmate commitments due to the new incarceration penalties for reckless driving convictions in Baltimore City.
OAH adjudicates administrative appeals related to driver's license suspensions and point accumulation hearings resulting from MVA enforcement actions.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists to issue a license to practice behavior analysis to qualified applicants within 30 days of receiving the completed application; requiring the State Board to issue a license within 50 days to an applicant who submitted an incomplete application but has presented additional information; and requiring the State Board to provide a certain e-mail notification regarding the status of an application for a license to practice behavior analysis.

The bill alters judicial timelines and procedures for individuals aggrieved by a decision of the Comptroller to commence a civil action in the circuit courts to establish their abandoned property claims.

It must receive hospital debt collection reports, post debt sale information on its website, monitor hospital compliance with debt collection policies, and treat proceeds from medical debt sales as an offset to uncompensated care in hospital rate setting.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically its Consumer Protection Division, enforces consumer protection and debt collection standards across Maryland, and provided input on the legal protections and restrictions concerning medical debt collection practices in the bill.

responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: family child care providers, cooperative housing corporations, condominium associations, homeowners associations, and local jurisdictions
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances and no direct effect on local finances, though local governments may experience operational impacts regarding zoning and capacity regulation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly relates to the regulation and licensing of family child care homes and large family child care homes, which fall under the jurisdiction of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The bill prohibits common ownership communities and local zoning authorities from limiting child care enrollment below the capacity authorized by MSDE.

The bill amends the Land Use Article to prohibit local jurisdictions and charter counties from restricting the capacity of family child care homes through local zoning laws and ordinances. The Department of Planning provides policy guidance and technical assistance to local governments on comprehensive planning and land use statutes.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Appellate Court of Maryland, in conjunction with the administrations of secondary and postsecondary educational institutions in the State, to hold sessions at certain secondary and postsecondary educational institutions in the State.
Title: Appellate Court of Maryland - Sessions at Educational Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Authorizes the Appellate Court of Maryland to hold sessions at secondary and postsecondary educational institutions in the State. Requires designation by the Chief Judge of the court in conjunction with institutional administrations. Expands existing provisions that allow sessions at designated law schools. Maintains general statutory requirements regarding judicial panel composition and court quorums. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Appellate Court of Maryland; Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Appellate Court of Maryland judges and staff, litigants, and students, faculty, and administrators at secondary and postsecondary educational institutions in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judiciary, including the Appellate Court of Maryland. The bill was requested by the Judiciary and directly authorizes the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court to hold court sessions at secondary and postsecondary educational institutions.
The bill authorizes the Appellate Court to coordinate with the administrations of secondary educational institutions across Maryland to host court sessions for educational and civic purposes.

The bill expands the authority of the Appellate Court to sit at postsecondary institutions statewide beyond its existing statutory authority at the University of Baltimore and the University of Maryland, Baltimore.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that the State Reporter secure copyright for the State of published reports of opinions of the Supreme Court of Maryland and the Appellate Court of Maryland.
Title: Courts - State Reporter - Publication of Cases
bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the State Reporter secure a copyright for the State for published court opinions. Applies to reports of cases decided in the Supreme Court of Maryland and the Appellate Court of Maryland. Maintains the requirement that the State Reporter superintend the proofreading, correction, and publication of the reports. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Reporter
stakeholders: State Reporter, legal researchers, publishers, and members of the public accessing Maryland appellate opinions
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill eliminates an obsolete statutory requirement and reflects current practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory duties of the State Reporter, who operates under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Maryland within the Judicial Branch, by removing the requirement to secure state copyright for published appellate opinions.

Synopsis: Allowing the chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to appoint a former member to temporarily fill a certain vacancy on the Commission; allowing the Governor, on certain request of the chair, to appoint a temporary substitute member or extend the term of an existing member of the Commission; and requiring that any temporary substitute is subject to the same qualifications applicable to the member the substitute is replacing and, if the member is a judge or an attorney, must be a member in good standing of the Maryland bar.
Title: Judiciary Department - Commission on Judicial Disabilities - Temporary Appointment
Status: Assigned a chapter number, enactment subject to constitutional referendum - Chapter 848
bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution concerning temporary appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities. Authorizes the commission chair to recall former members or request temporary appointments upon member recusal, disqualification, or term expiration. Authorizes the Governor, on request, to appoint temporary substitute members or extend current terms until replacements are appointed. Requires temporary substitute members to meet the qualifications of the original seat. Requires judicial and attorney substitutes to be members in good standing of the Maryland Bar. Submits the constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2026 general election.
responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities; Governor
stakeholders: Commission on Judicial Disabilities members and temporary appointees, Maryland judges and justices, and former commission members
fiscal_impact_summary: Operational efficiencies for the Commission on Judicial Disabilities if approved by voters, with no material impact on State finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch and the Commission on Judicial Disabilities by establishing mechanisms for temporary appointments and term extensions to address vacancies and recusals. The bill was proposed by request of the Maryland Judicial Conference.
The bill directly grants the Governor authority, upon request of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities chair, to appoint temporary substitute members or extend an existing member's term.
As a proposed constitutional amendment, the measure must be submitted to Maryland voters on the ballot at the November 2026 general election, which is administered by the State Board of Elections.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to include certain information concerning a certain State installment payment program for property taxes on the Ombudsman's website; requiring the Ombudsman to contract with a vendor to operate an installment payment program for payment of taxes in which any homeowner may enroll; requiring a collector of taxes to include certain information concerning a certain State or local installment payment program for property taxes in a separate insert included with each property tax bill; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Payment Plans - Notice to Taxpayers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Requires tax collectors to include a separate insert about installment payment programs with each property tax bill. Mandates that the insert describe available State or local payment plans and provide enrollment instructions. Directs the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to design the insert unless a local installment program is included. Requires tax collectors and the Ombudsman to publish the installment plan information on their websites. Adds installment payment program notices to separate inserts sent to property owners facing tax sales.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; local tax collectors
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners and real property owners, county tax collectors, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact, as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation can handle requirements using existing resources. County expenditures may increase by approximately $500,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to printing and mailing costs for the required inserts. Local revenues are not directly affected.

Synopsis: Authorizing the County Commissioners of Somerset County to impose an emergency services tax on all property subject to the county property tax to pay costs of emergency services; and prohibiting the county commissioners from initially imposing or subsequently increasing an emergency services tax until after a public hearing is held.
Title: Somerset County - Property Tax - Emergency Services Tax

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Somerset County to impose an annual emergency services property tax on county-taxed property. Funds pay all or part of emergency services costs, including fire, rescue, and emergency medical services. Prohibits initially imposing or subsequently increasing the tax until after holding an advance-noticed public hearing. Requires this hearing to take place at the same time as the annual county budget hearing. Establishes that unpaid taxes become liens and accrue interest and penalties like other unpaid county property taxes.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of Somerset County
stakeholders: Property owners and emergency services providers, including fire, rescue, and emergency medical services organizations, in Somerset County.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Somerset County revenues may increase depending on the special tax rate set by the county commissioners, generating approximately $170,000 per 1 cent increase on real property and $16,825 per 1 cent increase on personal property. County expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that unpaid emergency services taxes in Somerset County may be enforced through property tax sales under Title 14, Subtitle 8 of the Tax - Property Article, which involves circuit court filings and foreclosure proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted regarding court operations, though the overall operational and fiscal impact is negligible.

Synopsis: Approving certain projects for the acquisition, development, and improvement of certain academic facilities for the University System of Maryland; authorizing the issuance of bonds by the University System of Maryland in a total principal amount of $25,000,000 for financing the projects; and providing that the bonds issued under the authority of the Act are not a debt or obligation of the State or any of its subdivisions.
Title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue, sell, and deliver up to $30,000,000 in academic facilities bonds. Approves $5,000,000 in bond financing for campuswide building systems and infrastructure improvements at the University of Maryland, College Park. Approves $25,000,000 in bond financing for systemwide capital facilities renewal projects across constituent institutions and centers. Specifies that the authorized bonds do not constitute a debt or obligation of the State. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland
stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions and centers, students, and faculty
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures from bond proceeds increase by $30.0 million in FY 2026 for academic facilities projects. Higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2027 for 20 years to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 793 is a departmental bill requested by and directly applying to the University System of Maryland, authorizing it to issue $30 million in academic revenue bonds for campuswide infrastructure and systemwide facility renewal projects.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state capital projects, facility renewals, and related major procurement contracts funded through the authorized bonding.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements related to the certification of employment by public service employers under the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program, including requirements regarding determinations of whether employees are full-time; and requiring the Student Loan Ombudsman in the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to develop and disseminate information to increase awareness of and participation in the Program.
Title: Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program - Employee Certification and Awareness Materials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes employment certification requirements for public service employers under the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program. Requires public service employers to adopt policies calculating hours worked to maximize employee full-time eligibility. Mandates that higher education institutions credit adjunct and tenured professors with at least 3.35 hours worked per classroom hour. Requires public service employers to certify employment upon an employee's request or separation without unreasonable delay. Directs the Student Loan Ombudsman to develop awareness materials for employers to distribute to employees. Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Student Loan Ombudsman in the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
stakeholders: Current and former public service employees (including state, local government, public higher education, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit workers, as well as adjunct and tenured professors) and public service employers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the requirements with existing resources. Local public service employer expenditures may increase minimally to conform personnel practices, but costs are likely absorbable. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry with adopting regulations to implement the new subtitle and requires the Student Loan Ombudsman (housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation) to develop, update, and disseminate PSLF informational materials to public service employers.

As the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland, DBM oversees state employee onboarding and personnel policies, requiring it to incorporate the bill's PSLF employee certification standards, hour calculation rules, and required distribution of awareness materials into state onboarding packets and annual distributions.

The bill includes specific statutory requirements for public institutions of higher education regarding how hours are calculated (crediting at least 3.35 hours per classroom/contact hour) and requiring consecutive academic terms to be treated as continuous employment for adjunct and tenured professors under PSLF.

As an independent public institution of higher education outside the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University must implement the bill's specific hour calculation multiplier and continuous employment requirements for its adjunct and tenured faculty.

As an independent public honors college, St. Mary's College of Maryland must conform its human resources and employment certification procedures to the bill's specialized provisions for faculty and higher education employers.

Synopsis: Increasing the filing fee required to accompany an order to docket or a complaint to foreclose a mortgage or deed of trust on residential property from $300 to $450.
Title: Real Property – Filing Fee for Residential Mortgage Foreclosure – Increase

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Increases the filing fee accompanying an order to docket or a residential mortgage foreclosure complaint from $300 to $450. Applies the fee to foreclosures on mortgages and deeds of trust on residential property. Requires payment of this fee in addition to any other filing fees required by law. Directs fee revenue to support housing counseling and foreclosure mediation programs. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Judiciary
stakeholders: Mortgage lenders and secured parties filing residential foreclosure actions, and homeowners seeking foreclosure counseling or mediation
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Department of Housing and Community Development increase by approximately $525,600 in FY 2026 and by $700,800 annually thereafter. General fund revenues increase minimally beginning in FY 2026 due to interest earnings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD administers the Housing Counseling and Foreclosure Mediation Fund, which directly receives the revenues generated by the residential mortgage foreclosure filing fee increased by this bill, resulting in an estimated special fund revenue increase of over $700,000 annually.
The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the court system where orders to docket and complaints to foreclose are filed and where the statutory filing fee is collected.

Revenues from the Housing Counseling and Foreclosure Mediation Fund directly support efforts by the Department of Labor (including the Commissioner of Financial Regulation) to assist homeowners facing foreclosure, and the bill references loss mitigation affidavits prescribed by the Commissioner.
The bill explicitly references prefile mediation reports issued by OAH, and the fund supported by the increased fee assists in covering the costs of foreclosure mediations conducted by OAH.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Office of Overdose Response, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health, to develop and maintain an interactive dashboard on Opioid Restitution Fund spending to share prescription opioid-related settlement information with the public; requiring the dashboard to include links to the State, county, or municipal websites that provide access to additional information on the use of opioid-related settlement funds; etc.
Title: Opioid Restitution Fund - Interactive Dashboard

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Opioids -see also- Controlled Dangerous Substances; Drugs
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Office of Overdose Response and the Maryland Department of Health to develop an interactive settlement spending dashboard. Directs the dashboard to report payment schedules, past spending, spending plans, and funded initiatives by jurisdiction. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an online reporting portal for local governments. Exempts jurisdictions that already fulfill settlement reporting mandates and share data with the appropriate State entity. Requires developing and maintaining the dashboard using appropriations from the Opioid Restitution Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of Overdose Response; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland residents, counties, and municipalities receiving prescription opioid-related settlement funds
fiscal_impact_summary: Opioid Restitution Fund special fund expenditures increase by approximately $70,000 in FY 2026 for contractual development and $2,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 for ongoing maintenance. Total fund spending experiences no net change, as dashboard costs redirect funds from other discretionary uses, which may reduce funding available to local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the Maryland Office of Overdose Response, with developing and maintaining an interactive dashboard on Opioid Restitution Fund spending, establishing an online reporting portal for local governments, and uploading settlement data. MDH will incur special fund expenditures of approximately $70,000 in FY 2026 and $2,000 annually thereafter.

The Maryland Office of Overdose Response (MOOR) operates within the Executive Department / Governor's Office and is designated as the co-lead entity responsible for developing and maintaining the interactive Opioid Restitution Fund spending dashboard.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Innovation Initiative Institution Partnership Extension Program to expand opportunities for technology validation, entrepreneurial development, and industry engagement at eligible institutions; establishing eligibility criteria for project proposals to receive funding under the Program; authorizing the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2027 and 2028 for the Program; and altering the purpose and contents of the Maryland Innovation Initiative Fund.
Title: Economic Development - Maryland Innovation Initiative Institution Partnership Extension Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Innovation Initiative Institution Partnership Extension Program to expand technology validation, entrepreneurial development, and industry engagement. Authorizes Bowie State University, Frostburg State University, and other eligible public or private nonprofit institutions of higher education to participate. Requires an eligible institution to provide a cash match equivalent to 10% of the awarded grant amount. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 for the program in fiscal years 2027 and 2028. Requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to submit comparative and implementation reports to the General Assembly by specified dates.
responsible_party: Maryland Innovation Initiative; Maryland Technology Development Corporation
stakeholders: Bowie State University, Frostburg State University, other public and private nonprofit institutions of higher education in Maryland, and technology-based entrepreneurs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2027 and FY 2028 and by $1.0 million annually thereafter under discretionary budget assumptions, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures in the Maryland Innovation Initiative Fund. Higher education expenditures increase by $15,000 annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 for participating institutions to provide the required 10% cash match.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO houses the Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII), which is responsible for administering the new Institution Partnership Extension Program, establishing proposal evaluation criteria, collaborating with institutions, awarding grants, and submitting required reports.

Bowie State University and Frostburg State University are constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland that are specifically designated as the eligible institutions for the program, requiring them to submit proposals and provide a 10% cash match.
The Governor is authorized to include appropriations for the program in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2027 and 2028 and is a designated recipient of TEDCO's report on program expansion.
DBM oversees the development of the state budget and the allocation of general fund expenditures, which may include the discretionary $250,000 appropriations authorized in the bill.

As the primary economic development agency promoting business creation, commercialization, and industry partnerships in Maryland, the department is an interested stakeholder and was consulted on the fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Requiring a written lease for certain residential or commercial real property in Howard County to include information on the annual charge assessed by the Columbia Association and a description of certain rights and privileges under certain circumstances; requiring a landlord to provide a tenant with a copy of certain covenants and governing documents under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Columbia Association - Lease Requirements and Governing Documents Ho. Co. 14-25

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes lease disclosure and document requirements for residential and commercial rental properties in Howard County subject to Columbia Association covenants. Requires landlords who pass on any annual Columbia Association charge in rent to disclose the amount and calculation method. Mandates written leases to include or direct tenants to descriptions of rights and privileges under association covenants. Requires landlords to provide tenants copies of covenants and governing documents upon lease signing. Authorizes landlords to provide document copies physically, digitally, or through a permanent digital link.
responsible_party: Landlords of residential and commercial real property subject to Columbia Association covenants
stakeholders: Landlords, residential tenants, and commercial tenants of real property in Howard County subject to Columbia Association covenants, as well as the Columbia Association
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or Howard County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General includes the Consumer Protection Division, which enforces state consumer protection and landlord-tenant laws regarding required lease terms and disclosures, and was consulted as an information source for the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual enrolled in an accredited institution of higher education or a residential vocational training program to return to an out-of-home placement provider with whom the individual was previously placed under certain circumstances; requiring an individual to make a request to a local department of social services at least 30 days before the scheduled break; requiring the local department to make a recommendation to the Department of Human Services not later than 21 days before the scheduled break; etc.
Title: Out-of-Home Placement Providers - Individuals Enrolled in Higher Education and Vocational Training Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Authorizes individuals enrolled in accredited higher education institutions or residential vocational training programs to return to previous out-of-home placement providers. Applies when individuals cannot remain on campus during scheduled breaks, temporary closures, or temporary leaves of absence. Requires mutual agreement among the individual, the out-of-home placement provider, and the provider agency. Requires individuals to request approval from a local department at least 30 days before a scheduled break. Requires the local department to make a recommendation to the Department of Human Services at least 21 days before the break. Requires the Department of Human Services to make a final determination at least 14 days before the scheduled break.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
stakeholders: individuals enrolled in accredited institutions of higher education or residential vocational training programs previously placed in out-of-home care, and out-of-home placement providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Human Services can review and determine placement requests using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees child welfare and out-of-home placement programs. The bill specifically tasks DHS and its local departments of social services with receiving requests, making recommendations, and issuing determinations regarding former foster youth returning to out-of-home placement providers during academic breaks or temporary closures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, to convene a workgroup to study and review reimbursement for pharmacists; and requiring the workgroup to submit an interim report by December 31, 2025, and a final report on their findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly by December 31, 2026.
Title: Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Department of Health - Workgroup to Study Pharmacy Benefits Managers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Department of Health to convene a workgroup studying pharmacy benefits managers. Mandates consultation with the Prescription Drug Affordability Board and representation from diverse healthcare and supply chain stakeholders. Directs the workgroup to review pharmacist reimbursement, specialty drug coverage, ERISA preemption issues, and commercial contracting costs. Requires an interim report by December 31, 2025, and a final report by December 31, 2026. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Pharmacy benefits managers; independent and chain community pharmacies; pharmacy services administrative organizations; health insurance carriers; managed care organizations; drug manufacturers and distributors; pharmacists; Medicaid beneficiaries
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by $51,292 in FY 2026 and $21,134 in FY 2027 (split evenly between general funds and federal funds) to hire a part-time health policy analyst to support the workgroup. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly by $25,646 in FY 2026 and $10,567 in FY 2027. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026 and FY 2027 for contractual consultant services. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is one of the two lead agencies tasked with convening the workgroup of stakeholders to study pharmacy benefits managers, potentially hiring consultants, and submitting interim and final reports to legislative committees.

MDH is designated as a co-lead agency alongside MIA to convene the study workgroup, evaluate Medicaid pharmacy benefits and reimbursement structures, hire staff to support the workgroup, and submit required reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary multi-stakeholder workgroup tasked with studying issues related to pharmacy benefits managers, drug pricing, and pharmacist reimbursement, and making policy recommendations to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Juvenile Services to submit an annual report to certain committees of the General Assembly by October 1 detailing efforts by the Department to promote predelinquent programs, including youth service bureaus, efforts by the Department to collaborate with and provide technical assistance to local governments regarding the establishment of youth service bureaus, and an assessment of the programs and activities of the bureaus and any other efforts to prevent youth offenses.
Title: Department of Juvenile Services - Report on Youth Service Bureaus

NarrowSubjects.Name: Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Juvenile Services to submit an annual report on youth service bureaus and delinquency prevention. Mandates submission to the Senate Judicial Proceedings Committee and House Judiciary Committee by October 1 each year. Requires reporting on departmental efforts to promote predelinquent programs, including youth service bureaus. Details agency collaboration and technical assistance provided to local governments regarding youth service bureaus. Requires an assessment of youth service bureau activities and other efforts to prevent youth offenses.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: youth service bureaus, local governments, and youth participating in delinquency prevention programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected because the Department of Juvenile Services can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government operations and finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 814 directly mandates the Department of Juvenile Services to prepare and submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding youth service bureaus, predelinquent programs, technical assistance to local governments, and delinquency prevention efforts.

The Governor's Office for Children oversees the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund, which is the primary source of State grant funding distributed to local management boards that support youth service bureaus.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy funds youth delinquency prevention initiatives and provides grant funding to youth service bureaus evaluated under the scope of this reporting requirement.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland Stadium Authority, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College to establish a certain preference program for certain procurements; authorizing the establishment of a certain evaluation factor for certain proposals by an entity that utilizes certain employee stock ownership plans; requiring contractors to provide certain information to a unit regarding the use of an employee stock ownership plan; etc.
Title: Procurement - Employee Stock Ownership Plan Preference - Pilot

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes certain State entities to establish an evaluation factor for offerors utilizing an employee stock ownership plan. Applies to the Maryland Stadium Authority, Morgan State University, St. Mary’s College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College. Requires Board of Public Works approval for any evaluation factor, capped at 10% of technical points. Limits applicability to covered procurements valued under $80,000,000 solicited on or before June 30, 2030. Requires contractors to submit written verification of their plan's Internal Revenue Service determination letter. Mandates an evaluation report by December 1, 2028, and terminates the program on June 30, 2030.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland; Baltimore City Community College; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Contractors and offerors utilizing an employee stock ownership plan; competing non-ESOP businesses; Maryland Stadium Authority; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland; Baltimore City Community College
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures from general, higher education, and nonbudgeted funds may increase by up to 10% for each contract where the evaluation factor is utilized. A reliable total estimate is unavailable because adoption is optional and the number of future contracts is unknown. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Stadium Authority is directly authorized under the bill to establish a procurement evaluation factor of up to 10% for offerors utilizing an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) and is required to report on the program by December 1, 2028.

Morgan State University is directly authorized under the bill to establish a procurement evaluation factor for ESOP offerors on covered procurements and is mandated to evaluate and submit a report on the program by December 1, 2028.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is specifically authorized under the bill to establish a procurement evaluation factor for ESOP offerors on covered procurements and is required to submit an evaluation report by December 1, 2028.
Under § 14-803 of the bill, the establishment of the ESOP evaluation factor by participating units is subject to the approval of the Board of Public Works.
The University System of Maryland is named under the reporting requirements of § 14-806 to submit a report on ESOP contract awards and program effectiveness by December 1, 2028.

Synopsis: Requiring that certain carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and private review agents ensure that artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools are used in a certain manner when used for conducting utilization review.
Title: Health Insurance - Utilization Review - Use of Artificial Intelligence

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and private review agents to base software determinations on an enrollee's clinical circumstances. Prohibits artificial intelligence, algorithms, or other software tools from denying, delaying, or modifying health care services. Prohibits software tools from replacing the role of a health care provider in utilization review determinations. Requires carriers to report quarterly whether an artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tool contributed to adverse decisions. Requires regulated entities to open all utilization review software tools to inspection and audit by the Commissioner.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, private review agents, health care providers, and health benefit plan enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from private review agent application fees. Special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2026 for contractual compliance audits, though these costs may be recouped from examined entities. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is responsible for reviewing private review agent filings, receiving quarterly reporting on the use of AI in adverse benefit decisions, conducting compliance examinations and audits of AI tools, and drafting implementing regulations.

MDH oversees health care quality and regulations related to health maintenance organizations (HMOs) referenced in the adverse decisions reporting statutory framework (§ 19-705.2 of the Health - General Article), and serves as an information source on utilization review policies.

The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to submit an annual summary report detailing carrier utilization review activities, adverse decisions, and the use of AI tools directly to the Governor.
