responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Child care professionals, child care employers, and child care providers, particularly those accepting Child Care Scholarship vouchers
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026 only, Department of Commerce special fund expenditures increase by $250,000 to transfer funds from the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE). MHBE special fund revenues and expenditures each increase by $250,000 in FY 2026 to conduct the outreach campaign and survey. Ongoing expenses can be absorbed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting an outreach campaign to promote health insurance access for child care professionals, assisting them with enrollment in exchange plans or Medicaid, and conducting a survey on child care health care access.

MSDE is explicitly named in the legislation as a mandatory partner for the outreach effort, prekindergarten provider hubs, and the development and administration of the health care access survey for child care professionals.

Enactment of the bill triggers a contingent budget transfer of $250,000 in special funds in FY 2026 from Commerce's Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to MHBE to fund the outreach campaign and survey.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain common carriers from damaging certain public infrastructure necessitating the closure of the infrastructure; establishing that a violation of the Act is a public nuisance; authorizing the State or a local government to bring a civil action against a common carrier for a violation under the Act; and providing that a common carrier that commits a violation may be liable to the State or local government for civil penalties of $1,000 per day for each day the public nuisance continues.
Title: Public Nuisance - Common Carriers - Damage to Public Infrastructure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Prohibits a common carrier or carrier employee from causing damage to public infrastructure that necessitates infrastructure closure. Establishes that causing such damage constitutes a public nuisance. Authorizes the State or local government designated counsel to bring a civil action against a common carrier. Authorizes the State or local government to seek injunctive relief, declaratory relief, and compensatory damages. Authorizes civil penalties of $1,000 per day until the infrastructure is sufficiently repaired or replaced.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transportation Authority; local governments
stakeholders: Land-based common carriers (including motor bus, railroad, taxicab, transit, and transportation network companies), common carrier employees, local governments, and the State of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in State general fund and local revenues from civil penalties of $1,000 per day. Potential recovery of repair or replacement costs for the Transportation Trust Fund, Maryland Transportation Authority, and local governments through compensatory damages. Potential minimal increase in State litigation expenses and local costs to retain outside counsel.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT owns and maintains State public infrastructure, including highways and bridges. The bill authorizes civil actions against common carriers that damage State infrastructure causing closures, directly impacting the Transportation Trust Fund through potential recovery of repair costs and litigation expenditures.

As the MDOT administration responsible for maintaining and operating non-toll State highways and bridges, SHA is directly impacted when common carriers cause damage necessitating infrastructure closure, and would be directly involved in the repair/replacement assessments and recovery actions.

MDTA operates and maintains Maryland's toll facilities, including major bridges and highways. The fiscal note explicitly identifies that MDTA finances and nonbudgeted expenditures could be impacted if it litigates claims to recover repair or replacement costs for damaged infrastructure.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel and representative for the State and its transportation agencies, and would be tasked with bringing civil actions for public nuisance, injunctive relief, repair costs, and daily civil penalties against common carriers.

The bill creates a new statutory cause of action under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article for public nuisance against common carriers, which will be filed and adjudicated in the Maryland court system managed and supported by the AOC.

Synopsis: Requiring a transportation network company to provide each operator with a weekly fare and earnings summary; requiring a transportation network company to report, on or before February 1 each year, certain information to the Public Service Commission; and providing that the report submitted to the Commission may be made available to the General Assembly on request, provided that the report remain confidential and exempt from public disclosure.
Title: Transportation Network Companies - Weekly Fare and Earnings Summary and Operator Data Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires each transportation network company to provide its operators with a weekly fare and earnings summary. Specifies the summary must detail total fares collected, additional passenger fees charged, and the operator's earnings. Mandates that summaries include operator earnings expressed as percentages of total fares and additional fees collected. Requires companies to report annual aggregated fare, drive-time, and earnings data to the Public Service Commission by February 1. Classifies nonpublic reported information as confidential trade secrets exempt from disclosure under the Public Information Act.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: transportation network companies and transportation network operators
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission regulates transportation network companies (TNCs) in Maryland and is the agency designated to receive annual aggregated reports on TNC operator earnings, fares, and drive time.

Synopsis: Authorizing the transfer of funds from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund if the balance of the Fund has been depleted due to use or transfer or the estimated costs for providing adequate disaster relief for a natural disaster or catastrophic situation are in excess of the Fund's balance; and providing the Legislative Policy Committee has 10 days to review and make comments before the Governor may transfer certain funds from the Account through budget amendment.
Title: Catastrophic Event Account - Transfer of Funds - State Disaster Recovery Fund

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund by budget amendment. Permits the transfer when the State Disaster Recovery Fund balance is depleted from use or transfer. Allows the transfer when estimated costs for adequate disaster relief exceed the fund's balance. Reduces the Legislative Policy Committee review and comment period for fund transfers from 15 days to 10 days. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: Units of Maryland State and local government responding to natural disasters or catastrophic situations, and communities receiving disaster recovery assistance
fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on State finances, as any transfer increases special fund expenditures from the Catastrophic Event Account and increases special fund revenues to the State Disaster Recovery Fund correspondingly. Special fund revenues to the Revenue Stabilization Account may decrease minimally from foregone interest earnings. Local government finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM administers the State Disaster Recovery Fund, which under this bill is authorized to receive direct transfers of funds from the Catastrophic Event Account when its balance is depleted or estimated disaster relief costs exceed available funds.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account within the State Reserve Fund and manages state budget processes, including budget amendments used to transfer funds authorized by the bill.

The bill directly authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund by budget amendment and shortens the review and comment period required before the Legislative Policy Committee.
The Comptroller is statutorily responsible for accounting for the Catastrophic Event Account and tracking fund movements and budget amendments.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to separately hold and invest the monies within the Catastrophic Event Account.

Synopsis: Establishing a Class C (theater) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County; authorizing the manager of the theater or any other official designated by the theater to sign the application for the license; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue the license for use by certain theaters; authorizing the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption, subject to certain limitations; establishing an annual license fee of $150; etc.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Theater) Beer, Wine, and Liquor License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a Class C (theater) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County. Authorizes the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to theaters with seating. Permits a theater manager or designated official to sign the license application. Authorizes sales for on-premises consumption from one hour before to one hour after specified performances or rented events. Sets the annual license fee at $150.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
stakeholders: Theaters with seating in Frederick County, theater patrons, and the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from the $150 annual license fee for each issued license. Frederick County can handle enforcement activities with existing resources. There is no state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers state sales and excise taxes related to alcoholic beverages. While this bill is local to Frederick County and administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it pertains to the regulation and sale of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

Synopsis: Repealing the limitation on the period during which the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations are required to provide reimbursement for certain health care services provided through telehealth on a certain basis and at a certain rate; altering the circumstances under which health care practitioners are authorized to prescribe certain controlled dangerous substances for the treatment of pain through telehealth; etc.
Title: Preserve Telehealth Access Act of 2025

NarrowSubjects.Name: Controlled Dangerous Substances -see also- Drugs; Opioids
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: Establishes permanent coverage and reimbursement parity for telehealth services provided through Medicaid and commercial health insurance. Permanently defines telehealth to include certain audio-only telephone conversations between health care providers and patients. Requires Medicaid and commercial insurers to reimburse appropriate telehealth services at the same rate as in-person care. Authorizes health care practitioners to prescribe Schedule II opiates for pain through telehealth under specified practitioner-patient conditions. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit a telehealth study report every four years beginning December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Medicaid recipients, commercially insured patients, licensed health care practitioners and providers, commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2027 and every four years thereafter for contractual research to complete the required telehealth reports. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues decrease minimally in FY 2026 only. Medicaid expenditures and matching federal revenues for telehealth services continue beyond FY 2025, with an indeterminate net impact on total Medicaid costs. Local government health plans may face indeterminate expenditure increases to maintain telehealth reimbursement parity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) submit a comprehensive report on telehealth advances, delivery modalities, and costs to the Governor and General Assembly every four years beginning December 1, 2026, requiring an estimated $100,000 in special fund expenditures every four years.

The bill permanently mandates telehealth coverage and payment parity (including audio-only services) for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-139 to make permanent the requirement that commercial health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans provide telehealth reimbursement and parity for audio-only services, which the MIA regulates and enforces.

The bill amends Health Occupations § 1-1003 regarding the authorization and statutory conditions under which practitioners may prescribe Schedule II controlled dangerous substances (opiates) for the treatment of pain through telehealth.

The bill explicitly references HSCRC, clarifying that the parity and reimbursement provisions may not be construed to supersede the commission's authority to set hospital rates, including facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was reviewed in the fiscal note regarding any fiscal impact from the permanent telehealth and parity requirements.
The bill requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit its quadrennial telehealth report directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "community benefit" to include a community health worker workforce program which is intended to provide services to patients of a nonprofit hospital and to improve health outcomes; authorizing a nonprofit hospital and a community-based organization to establish a community health worker workforce program; providing that a partnership that establishes a community health worker workforce program may be executed through a memorandum of understanding; establishing requirements for the memorandum of understanding; etc.
Title: Health Services Cost Review Commission - Community Benefits - Community Health Worker Workforce Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Expands the definition of hospital community benefits to include qualified community health worker workforce programs. Authorizes nonprofit hospitals and community-based organizations to establish these workforce programs to improve patient outcomes. Permits partners to execute the program through a memorandum of understanding outlining operational duties and evaluation standards. Authorizes partnerships to offer health insurance coverage to participating community health workers who lack coverage and request it. Authorizes nonprofit hospitals to provide financial support for community-based organizations' administrative capacity costs.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: nonprofit hospitals, community-based organizations, community health workers, and hospital patients
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on state or local government finances. Nonprofit hospitals and community-based organizations may incur voluntary costs to fund programs, provide health benefits, or support administrative capacity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory definition of hospital 'community benefit' under Health - General § 19-303, which the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) administers and tracks through annual nonprofit hospital community benefit reporting and financial reports.

HSCRC is an independent commission operating within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). In addition, the bill incorporates the statutory definition of community health workers who are certified and accredited under programs administered by MDH.

Synopsis: Clarifying the circumstances under which liability for the failure to comply with certain requirements relating to a tenant's right of first refusal to purchase residential property is restricted to the owner of the property and does not attach to the property.
Title: Residential Real Property - Tenants' Right of First Refusal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: Clarifies liability provisions regarding statutory requirements for a tenant's right of first refusal to purchase residential rental property. Restricts noncompliance liability exclusively to the property owner following closing on a sales contract between an owner and a third party. Prohibits failure-to-comply liability from attaching to the residential rental property that is the subject of the contract. Applies to voluntary transfers of residential rental property subject to statutory right of first refusal requirements.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs
stakeholders: residential rental property owners, residential tenants, and third-party purchasers of residential rental property
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statute governing tenants' right of first refusal, which is administratively overseen by the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs (OTLA) housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill clarifies civil liability restrictions regarding failure to comply with tenant right-of-first-refusal requirements and establishes that liability does not attach to real property, affecting real property litigation adjudicated in state courts.

Synopsis: Extending the time for submission of the interim report and final report of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by 3 years; and extending the termination date for the Commission by 3 years.
Title: Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission - Reporting and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2029. Delays the deadline for the Commission's interim report from June 1, 2025, to June 1, 2028. Delays the deadline for the Commission's final report from January 1, 2026, to January 1, 2029. Requires the Commission to submit both reports to the Governor and the General Assembly. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: incarcerated individuals and justice-involved adults and juveniles, education and workforce training providers, and members of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $28,500 in FY 2026, $65,600 in FY 2027, $68,400 in FY 2028, and $42,100 in FY 2029 for the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to maintain one contractual staff position through January 2029. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP provides administrative and operational staff support to the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission and is directly fiscally impacted by having to maintain contractual staff through FY 2029 to support the extended reporting deadlines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the statutory lifespan, operations, and reporting requirements of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission through June 30, 2029.
The Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission is required to submit both its interim and final reports of findings and policy recommendations directly to the Governor.

The Department of Labor is an information source for the legislation, as the commission's underlying mandate involves evaluating workforce, vocational, and adult education programs for justice-involved individuals.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools for the purpose of studying and making recommendations on practices to identify, prevent, and eliminate chronic absenteeism by students from schools in the State; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
Title: Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools. Requires the Task Force to analyze absenteeism data and set a statewide reduction goal. Requires the Task Force to report recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2025. Requires the State Department of Education to update student attendance regulations by December 31, 2025. Requires the Department to distribute an absenteeism toolkit and guidance to local school systems by June 30, 2026. Sunsets all provisions of the Act on December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can staff the Task Force and update regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local school finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for staffing the Task Force, updating regulations on student attendance by December 31, 2025, and distributing the attendance toolkit and guidance to local school systems by June 30, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools to study, make recommendations, and report on strategies and best practices to address chronic absenteeism.

The Governor's Office is required to have a representative appointed to the Task Force by the State Superintendent, and the Task Force must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Phasing in a requirement that all child support received in a month pass through to a family seeking assistance under the Family Investment Program and prohibiting the consideration of child support in computing the amount of assistance received.
Title: Family Investment Program - Child Support

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst

bill_summary: Phases in a requirement that child support collected in a month pass through to families receiving Family Investment Program assistance. Disregards passed-through child support when computing the recipient family's amount of assistance. Sets the passthrough rate at the greater of current statutory minimums or 25% in fiscal 2028. Increases the percentage threshold to 50% in fiscal 2029 and 75% in fiscal 2030. Requires 100% of collected child support to pass through beginning in fiscal 2031.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Families receiving Family Investment Program or Temporary Cash Assistance benefits, and noncustodial parents paying child support.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $406,100 across general and federal funds in fiscal 2027 for IT updates, offset by $268,000 in federal revenues. General fund expenditures increase by $2.4 million in fiscal 2028, rising annually to $13.9 million by fiscal 2031 to offset lost special fund revenues and reimburse federal shares. No material local impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) directly administers the Family Investment Program and the Child Support Administration. The bill phases in an increase in child support pass-through amounts to FIP recipients, requiring major IT system updates to the Child Support Management System and Eligibility and Enrollment System, as well as replacing lost special fund revenues with millions of dollars in general fund expenditures.

Synopsis: Establishing that an individual who, after earning service credit sufficient for a vested allowance in the State Police Retirement System, the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, or the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, separates from service, and subsequently returns to service in a position in the same system under certain circumstances, is subject to the same requirements to which certain members of the same system are subject.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System – Deferred Vested Former Members – Return to Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Allows certain former members of public safety retirement systems who return to service to retain pre-2011 benefit tiers. Applies to the State Police Retirement System, the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System, and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System. Covers qualifying individuals who were members on or before June 30, 2011, without withdrawing contributions or retiring. Requires a separation of four years or less, qualifying military service, or minimum service for a vested allowance. Subjects eligible returning employees to the requirements governing continuous members enrolled before July 1, 2011.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: returning former members of the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers’ Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System who initially joined on or before June 30, 2011
fiscal_impact_summary: Likely no discernible effect on State or participating governmental unit retirement liabilities and contribution rates. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers' Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and is directly responsible for implementing the benefit tier and re-enrollment rules prescribed by the bill.
The bill directly impacts the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) by establishing conditions under which former vested members returning to service can regain pre-2011 pension benefit structures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters rules for the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS), directly impacting personnel and returning officers employed by DPSCS.
DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State and oversees statewide employee benefits and fiscal planning related to State pension obligations.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for an individual licensed as a certified public accountant in another state to practice certified public accountancy in the State by requiring that the individual must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination when qualifying for the license in the other state.
Title: Accountants - Licensed Out-of-State Practice Privileges - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Alters qualifications for out-of-state certified public accountants to practice certified public accountancy in Maryland. Repeals the requirement that NASBA verify substantial equivalence with the Uniform Accountancy Act. Requires instead that an individual passed the Uniform CPA Examination to qualify for licensure in the other state. Repeals NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service review pathways for individuals from non-equivalent states. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
stakeholders: Certified public accountants licensed in other states and accounting firms employing out-of-state practitioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill with existing resources. Special fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses and oversees the State Board of Public Accountancy, which regulates certified public accountants and will implement the revised out-of-state practice privilege qualifications under this bill.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for an initial teacher certificate to include passing a portfolio-based assessment of a nationally accredited teacher preparation program.
Title: Education - Initial Teacher Certification - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Alters qualifications for obtaining an initial teacher certificate in Maryland. Expands qualifying options to include passing a portfolio-based assessment of a nationally accredited teacher preparation program. Applies to graduates of teacher preparation programs and alternative teacher preparation programs. Preserves alternate qualifying pathways, including completing a qualifying local school system teacher induction program. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Board of Education
stakeholders: graduates of teacher preparation programs and alternative teacher preparation programs seeking initial teacher certification, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal effect on State finances or local school systems, though local school systems may see an increased pool of licensed teachers available for hire.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is responsible for certifying and licensing public school educators in Maryland. The bill directly alters the statutory qualification requirements for an initial teacher certificate by allowing candidates to qualify via a portfolio-based assessment from a nationally accredited teacher preparation program.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to suspend for up to 5 years for a first violation, rather than revoke, a person's oyster authorization for knowingly committing certain violations; providing for the reinstatement for certain persons of an oyster authorization and an entitlement to engage or work in the oyster fishery; altering a certain offense related to the use of prohibited gear; and repealing the 90-day time period within which a certain administrative hearing must be held.
Title: Tidal Fish Licenses - Oyster Authorizations - Administrative Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Replaces the revocation penalty with a suspension of up to five years for a first knowing oyster violation. Retains license revocation for a second or subsequent violation. Restricts the prohibited gear offense to violations occurring more than 200 feet within a prohibited area. Repeals the requirement that administrative hearings take place within 90 days after an offense. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to reinstate fishery work entitlements five years after certain pre-July 2025 revocations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial oyster harvesters, tidal fish license holders with oyster authorizations, individuals with prior oyster authorization revocations, and commercial license waitlist applicants.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund expenditures increase annually by approximately $5,300 and $6,200, respectively, beginning in fiscal 2026 for the Department of Natural Resources to conduct additional administrative hearings. Special fund revenues may decrease minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 because suspended authorizations are held rather than reallocated to new licensees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for managing tidal fish licenses, issuing oyster authorizations, enforcing fishery conservation laws, and administering suspensions, revocations, and reinstatements.

OAH conducts the administrative contested hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act before DNR can suspend or revoke an oyster authorization, and is expected to handle additional hearings annually under the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Secretary of Natural Resources to issue an incidental taking permit for the Indiana bat, the northern long-eared bat, the tricolor bat, or the eastern small-footed bat if an applicant submits a certain conservation plan and the Secretary makes certain findings.
Title: Endangered and Threatened Species - Incidental Taking - Bats

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes incidental taking permits for the Indiana bat, northern long-eared bat, tricolored bat, or eastern small-footed bat. Requires permit applicants to submit a conservation plan detailing impacts, mitigation measures, funding, and alternative actions. Requires the Secretary of Natural Resources to find the taking will not appreciably reduce species survival. Requires applicants to obtain any required federal authorization for the incidental taking. Authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to adopt regulations to implement and enforce the provisions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Landowners, project developers, and small businesses conducting activities in areas supporting protected bat species; Indiana bat, northern long-eared bat, tricolored bat, and eastern small-footed bat populations
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and has no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of Natural Resources with establishing, evaluating, and issuing incidental taking permits for specified bat species, reviewing required conservation plans, making statutory determinations, and adopting implementing regulations.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing the regulation of business, economic development, insurance, and labor and employment to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Employment and Insurance Equality for Service Members Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes uniform statutory definitions relating to military and uniformed services across multiple Maryland Code articles. Expands existing legal protections and benefits previously restricted to the armed forces to include all uniformed services. Extends occupational licensing accommodations, fee exemptions, and training credits to all qualifying uniformed service members. Broadens eligibility for small business no-interest loans, employment preferences, and insurance protections to covered members and eligible spouses. Clarifies family temporary disability leave protections and unemployment benefits for individuals connected to uniformed service members.
responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families; Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services (including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration), veterans, military spouses and families, licensed professionals, employers, and insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in fiscal 2026 only due to form filings. State and local government finances and operations are not otherwise materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates the core statutory definitions in the State Government Article governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families (including definitions of active duty, active service member, uniformed services, and veteran) and mandates their consultation on the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program.

The bill makes extensive changes to statutes administered by MD Labor, including occupational and professional licensing exemptions and expedited pathways, financial regulation of mortgage loan originators, unemployment insurance eligibility, and the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program.
The bill alters and expands eligibility for the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program administered by the Department of Commerce.

The bill amends multiple sections of the Insurance Article regarding licensing of producers, travel insurance, long-term care exclusions, and underwriting protections for service members, generating special fund revenue from required insurance form filings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees the State's Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) program, whose statutory eligibility definition of 'veteran' under the State Finance and Procurement Article is amended by the bill.

The bill amends Section 20-502 of the Insurance Article, which directly sets coverage eligibility standards for policies issued by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund for active-duty service members.

The Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General enforces protections under the Maryland Commercial Law Article, which the bill updates regarding credit reporting and protected consumers who are eligible service members.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of a certain property tax exemption for dwelling houses owned by blind individuals or their surviving spouses from $15,000 to $40,000.
Title: Property Tax - Exemption for Blind Individuals - Alteration
bill_summary: Increases the property tax exemption from $15,000 to $40,000 of assessed value for qualifying dwelling houses. Applies the exemption to dwelling houses owned by blind individuals or their unremarried surviving spouses. Requires the supervisor of assessments to prorate the exemption for remaining parts of a taxable year. Takes effect June 1, 2025, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Blind homeowners and their unremarried surviving spouses
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease by approximately $40,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026. Local property tax revenues decrease by an estimated $450,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts blind individuals by increasing the property tax exemption on their dwelling houses from $15,000 to $40,000, aligning with the Department of Disabilities' mission to coordinate policy, support accessible housing, and advance the welfare of Maryland residents with disabilities.

The bill reduces State property tax revenues dedicated to the Annuity Bond Fund by approximately $40,000 annually, which directly impacts the funds used for State debt service overseen and managed by the Treasurer's Office.

The board hears appeals and adjudicates disputes regarding real property assessments and property tax exemptions and credits, which includes dwelling exemptions administered by local assessment supervisors.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals of decisions concerning real property exemptions and assessments.

Synopsis: Increasing from two to four the number of speed monitoring systems that may be placed on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City; limiting to not more than one speed monitoring system in each direction that may be in operation at the same time on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City; and making permanent the authorization to place speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City.
Title: Baltimore City - Speed Monitoring Systems - Interstate 83

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Increases the maximum number of speed monitoring systems authorized on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City from two to four. Limits speed monitoring system operation on Interstate 83 to no more than one system in each direction simultaneously. Repeals the June 30, 2026, abrogation date to permanently authorize speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City, registered vehicle owners cited for speeding violations, and Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate state and local impact. Baltimore City expenditures increase to acquire, install, and maintain additional cameras beginning as early as FY 2025. City revenues may increase beginning in FY 2026 from additional citation issuance. Because the program would have otherwise terminated after FY 2026, City revenues and expenditures increase significantly beginning in FY 2027. State general fund revenues may increase beginning in FY 2026 from contested citations in District Court, which can handle any caseload changes with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Individuals issued speed monitoring citations on Interstate 83 may elect to contest them in the District Court of Maryland, which is administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The agency will absorb the potential increase in contested caseloads and process fine revenues paid directly to the general fund.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding speed monitoring on Interstate 83, an interstate highway corridor within Maryland. MDOT oversees transportation policy and highway safety coordination across the state.

Speed monitoring warning signage must comply with traffic control device standards established by the State Highway Administration, which sets technical and engineering requirements for highway signage.

Under state speed monitoring system laws, if net fine revenues exceed 10% of a jurisdiction's total revenues, the excess balance must be remitted to the Comptroller. The Comptroller also tracks and advises on automated enforcement revenue collections.

Synopsis: Specifying that an individual may consent to the issuance of a permanent protective order against the individual.
Title: Family Law - Permanent Protective Orders - Consent
bill_summary: Authorizes an individual to consent to the issuance of a permanent protective order against themselves. Requires a court to issue the permanent protective order upon consent if an order was previously issued. Mandates that the victim of the alleged abuse must request the permanent protective order. Restricts relief in the permanent order to relief granted in the original protective order. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: victims of domestic abuse and individuals subject to protective orders in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $30,300 in FY 2026 only for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs. No material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by allowing individuals to consent to the issuance of permanent protective orders. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs a direct fiscal impact of $30,300 in FY 2026 for one-time computer programming and court case management updates.

Synopsis: Establishing the Public Health Abortion Grant Program to provide grants to improve access to abortion care clinical services for individuals in the State; establishing the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide grants under the Program; and requiring that certain premium funds collected by health insurance carriers be used to provide certain coverage and to support improving access to abortion care clinical services under certain circumstances.
Title: Public Health Abortion Grant Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and Fund in the Maryland Department of Health. Directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to transfer excess balances from health carriers' federal segregated abortion accounts to the Fund. Requires the Secretary of Health to provide operating grants to eligible organizations providing abortion clinical services. Mandates a two million dollar budget amendment allocation for the program by October 1, 2025. Requires the Governor to include an annual mandated appropriation for the Fund starting in fiscal year 2027. Prohibits the Department of Health from collecting or disclosing identifying information of abortion patients or clinic staff.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health maintenance organizations, eligible abortion care clinical providers, and uninsured, underinsured, or privacy-vulnerable individuals seeking abortion care in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $19.3 million in FY 2026 and $2.5 million annually thereafter from carrier segregated account transfers. Special fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million in FY 2026 and $2.5 million annually thereafter for grants and administrative costs under the mandated appropriation. General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 from interest earnings. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 930 establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund within the Maryland Department of Health, requiring the Secretary of Health to administer the fund, award operating grants to eligible organizations, and establish grant standards.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner are responsible for receiving annual carrier accountings of segregated ACA abortion accounts, issuing orders to transfer excess funds to the newly established special fund, and handling related notifications and appeals.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer must hold the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund separately and invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund.

The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to allocate $2,000,000 to the program by budget amendment by October 1, 2025, and to include a mandated appropriation in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2027.

Parties aggrieved by an order of the Insurance Commissioner transferring segregated account balances have the right to administrative hearings and appeals, which may be adjudicated through the Office of Administrative Hearings.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to place certain interests into a certain certified blind trust or divest of certain interests within 6 months after taking the oath of office; requiring the Governor to enter into a nonparticipation agreement with the State Ethics Commission for any interests not included in a blind trust; authorizing the Ethics Commission to impose a fine of up to $5,000 for each violation of the Act; requiring the Commission to adopt regulations to carry out the Act including standards for types of interests that be exempted; etc.
Title: Public Ethics - Conflicts of Interest and Blind Trust - Governor

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to place private interests into a certified blind trust or divest them within six months of taking office. Requires the Governor to enter into a nonparticipation agreement for any interest not included in a blind trust. Exempts any residence of the Governor from which no income was derived in the immediately preceding year. Requires business entities seeking State grants, awards, or contracts to report qualifying interests held by the Governor or restricted individuals. Directs the Department of General Services to include an ownership check-off box on eMaryland Marketplace procurement notices. Authorizes the State Ethics Commission to fine the Governor up to $5,000 for each violation.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission; Department of General Services
stakeholders: The Governor, Governor-elect, qualifying family and household members of the Governor, and business entities seeking State grants, competitive awards, or contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $95,000 in FY 2026 for contractual IT programming services ($75,000 for the State Ethics Commission and $20,000 for the Department of General Services). Penalties assessed under the bill are not expected to materially affect special fund revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Ethics Commission is the primary implementing and regulatory agency under the bill. It is responsible for approving the Governor's certified blind trust, determining necessary divestitures, administering nonparticipation agreements, receiving business interest disclosures, posting records on its website, adopting new regulations, and enforcing potential fines.

The bill directly governs the actions, financial disclosures, and conflict-of-interest requirements of the Governor and Governor-elect, requiring them to establish a certified blind trust or divest assets, enter into nonparticipation agreements, and submit annual compliance certifications.

The Department of General Services is statutorily required to modify the eMaryland Marketplace system to include a check-off box with each procurement notice indicating ownership interests by the Governor or restricted individuals, requiring an estimated $20,000 in IT expenditures in FY 2026.

The bill directly restricts the Governor from participating in matters before the Board of Public Works involving any non-trust interests and mandates that copies of all nonparticipation agreements be provided to the Executive Secretary and General Counsel of the Board.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to review the cost reports and other data submitted by each nursing home that participates in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; and requiring the Department to report the findings resulting from the review conducted under the Act to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by October 1, 2025, and each October 1 thereafter through 2029.
Title: Nursing Homes - Cost Reports

NarrowSubjects.Name: Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants
Nursing Homes -see also- AsstLiving; ContinCare; LTCare
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data from Medicaid-participating nursing homes. Directs the department to review revenue allocations for contracted nursing care services. Mandates review of wages and salaries for all direct care nonadministrative staff. Requires annual reporting of findings to the Governor and designated legislative committees through 2029. Takes effect June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Nursing homes participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and their direct care nonadministrative staff
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can complete the required reviews and reports using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data submitted by nursing homes participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) regarding contracted nursing services and nonadministrative staff wages, and submit an annual report of its findings from 2025 through 2029.
The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit an annual report detailing the findings of its nursing home cost report review to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring that a carrier provide notice by certain electronic means, in addition to written notice, of cancellation or nonrenewal of a small group market health benefit plan and include information regarding additional health benefit coverage options in the notice; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2026.
Title: Health Insurance - Cancellation and Nonrenewal of Coverage - Required Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Requires small group health insurance carriers to notify enrolled employees within seven days after cancellation or nonrenewal of coverage. Requires delivery of written notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, and compliant electronic notice. Requires notices to include additional coverage options, including available COBRA continuation and Maryland Health Benefit Exchange plans. Applies to policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: health insurance carriers offering small group plans, small employers, and enrolled employees
fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal or operational impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator of commercial health insurance carriers in Maryland and is responsible for enforcing insurance laws, approving form notices, and overseeing carrier compliance with small group market cancellation and nonrenewal rules.

The bill explicitly requires health carriers to provide information regarding coverage options available through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to employees facing cancellation or nonrenewal of small group health plans.

Synopsis: Requiring the appointment of an alternate subscriber member to the governing body of a continuing care provider; and authorizing the alternate subscriber member to attend all meetings of the governing body and vote only if the regular subscriber is unable to fulfill the subscriber's duties as a regular member of the governing body.
Title: Continuing Care Providers - Governing Bodies - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Continuing Care -see also- Long-Term Care; Nursing Homes
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Requires a continuing care provider's governing body with only one subscriber to authorize the appointment of an alternate subscriber. Authorizes the alternate subscriber to serve as a regular member when the regular subscriber cannot fulfill duties. Permits the alternate subscriber to attend all governing body meetings and vote only when the regular subscriber is unable. Requires the governing body to confer with the resident association before the alternate subscriber officially joins. Authorizes the alternate subscriber to report nonconfidential deliberations, actions, and policies to the resident association.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Continuing care providers, governing bodies of continuing care facilities, and continuing care subscribers and resident associations in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues or local government finances. The Maryland Department of Aging can implement necessary document and regulatory updates using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging regulates continuing care retirement communities and providers under Title 10, Subtitle 4 of the Human Services Article. The bill amends governing body requirements for continuing care providers, requiring the department to update relevant documents and regulations using existing resources.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Commission for Women to establish the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control to study access to over-the-counter birth control; and requiring the Collaborative to submit an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027.
Title: Maryland Commission for Women - Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Commission for Women to establish the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control. Charges the collaborative with studying access and coverage options at pharmacies, retail counters, virtual platforms, and vending machines. Requires the collaborative to identify public health initiatives for individuals lacking or unable to access over-the-counter contraception coverage. Directs the collaborative to examine specified federal responses, rules, and policy reports on over-the-counter coverage. Mandates submission of an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report by December 1, 2027. Terminates the collaborative on June 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission for Women; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Individuals seeking over-the-counter birth control, health insurance carriers, pharmacies, retailers, and managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Commission for Women can staff the collaborative using existing budgeted resources. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Commission for Women, housed within the Department of Human Services, to establish and provide staff for the Collaborative, and tasks the Secretary of Human Services with appointing various stakeholders.

The Secretary of Health must designate two representatives to the Collaborative (one representing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and one representing public health), and the Collaborative's work directly impacts public health and reproductive healthcare access.
The Commissioner of the Maryland Insurance Administration must designate a representative to serve as a member of the Collaborative to address insurance coverage of over-the-counter contraception.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must designate a representative with expertise in the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program to serve on the Collaborative.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange must designate a representative to serve on the Collaborative.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new multi-stakeholder body, the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control, which operates for three years before terminating.

The Collaborative includes a representative from the Consumer Health Information Hub at the University of Maryland School of Public Health, as well as a representative of a public higher education institution providing student health insurance.
The Collaborative is required to submit both an interim report and a final report detailing its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from committing a certain crime of malicious or fraudulent burning that causes the death of or serious physical injury to a firefighter; and establishing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a felony and on conviction is subject to imprisonment not to exceed 10 years.
Title: Criminal Law - Crimes of Malicious or Fraudulent Burning - Prohibitions and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from committing a crime of malicious or fraudulent burning that causes death or serious physical injury to a firefighter. Defines applicable crimes as first-degree or second-degree malicious burning of personal property or burning with intent to defraud. Establishes that a violator is guilty of a felony subject to imprisonment for up to 10 years. Authorizes a court to impose a sentence consecutive to or concurrent with a sentence for the underlying offense.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Firefighters; individuals charged with or convicted of malicious or fraudulent burning offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund incarceration expenditures due to the 10-year maximum penalty. Judicial operations and Office of the Public Defender workloads can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and State revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense punishable by up to 10 years of imprisonment, which may result in a minimal increase in incarceration expenditures and commitments to State correctional facilities operated by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants charged with crimes and will be responsible for providing legal defense to clients charged under this new felony statute.

The Maryland Judiciary will handle criminal case filings, court proceedings, and sentencing related to the new criminal offense, with impacts expected to be absorbed using existing budgeted resources.

Synopsis: Altering, from the last Tuesday in June to the fourth Tuesday in June, the date for the primary election in the year of the gubernatorial election.
Title: Election Law - Gubernatorial Primary Election - Date
bill_summary: Alters the date of the statewide primary election in gubernatorial election years. Requires the gubernatorial primary election to occur on the fourth Tuesday in June. Replaces the prior requirement holding the election on the last Tuesday in June. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: voters, candidates for public office, and election administrators in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering and supervising statewide elections in Maryland. The bill directly alters the statutory date of the statewide primary election during gubernatorial election years.

Synopsis: Requiring each collector of taxes that maintains a website to include on the collector's website certain information and a certain link relating to the Homeowner Protection Program; altering the information the State Department of Assessments and Taxation is required to obtain and include in a certain annual report regarding tax sales; requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to take certain actions to maximize enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protection Program - Funding and Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Alters funding and administrative requirements for the Homeowner Protection Program. Requires each tax collector maintaining a website to conspicuously display a program description and application link. Directs the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to prioritize and maximize program enrollment. Prohibits the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from charging interest on unpaid taxes owed by enrolled homeowners. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $250,000 to the Homeowner Protection Fund. Requires county governments collectively to pay $500,000 each fiscal year to the fund.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; State Tax Sale Ombudsman
stakeholders: homeowners facing property tax delinquency or tax lien sales, county tax collectors, county governments, and tax sale purchasers
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to cover debt service in place of diverted property tax interest. Homeowner Protection Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $750,000 annually, reflecting $250,000 from State overdue property tax interest and $500,000 from mandatory collective county payments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $250,000 of the interest on overdue State property tax to the Homeowner Protection Fund for each fiscal year beginning in FY 2027.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning, and is directly responsible for incorporating the mandated $250,000 annual appropriation to the Homeowner Protection Fund into the State budget.
Under Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article, the State Treasurer is statutory custodian of the Homeowner Protection Fund, required to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article statutorily assigns the Comptroller the responsibility to account for the Homeowner Protection Fund.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation; requiring the Workgroup to monitor and make recommendations related to the regulation of artificial intelligence, consumer protection, current private sector use of artificial intelligence, enforcement authority for the Office of the Attorney General's Office of Consumer Protection, and impact in the determination of government benefits; and requiring the Workgroup to make its recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.
Title: Consumer Protection - Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation to monitor issues and make recommendations regarding artificial intelligence. Requires the University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security to staff the workgroup. Directs the workgroup to examine consumer rights, privacy protections, labor impacts, and private sector artificial intelligence use. Requires annual reports of findings and recommendations to specified legislative committees beginning July 1, 2026. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual $100,000 appropriation starting in fiscal year 2027. Terminates the workgroup on June 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation; University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, commercial artificial intelligence developers and deployers, labor and civil rights organizations, and State agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally in fiscal 2026 and by up to $100,000 annually from fiscal 2027 through 2029 to support the workgroup. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security (an academic center within the University System of Maryland) provide staff for the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, and the fiscal note assumes authorized funding ($100,000 annually starting in FY 2027) will be appropriated via the USM budget.

The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically tasked with monitoring and making recommendations regarding enforcement authority for the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary state body, the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, which operates through June 30, 2029, to study AI issues and report recommendations to the General Assembly.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the CEO's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation.

The Governor is responsible for appointing 19 members from diverse sectors to the workgroup and is authorized to include an appropriation of $100,000 annually in the state budget bill starting in FY 2027 to support the workgroup.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and managing the appointment process for the multiple private and public sector representatives appointed by the Governor to this new workgroup.

Synopsis: Specifying that the scope of the Maryland Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry and Referral System includes private and State inpatient and outpatient mental health and substance use services; requiring the Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services, under certain circumstances, to ensure pediatric hospital overstay patients are placed in the least restrictive setting when clinically indicated and when possible; etc.
Title: Public Health - Pediatric Hospital Overstay Patients and Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Overstays

Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes pediatric hospital overstay coordinators within the Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services. Requires both departments to ensure pediatric hospital overstay patients are placed in the least restrictive setting when clinically indicated. Authorizes hospitals to concurrently explore in-state and out-of-state placement options for these patients. Expands the state behavioral health registry to include private and State inpatient and outpatient services. Establishes a workgroup to study children in unlicensed settings and pediatric hospital overstays. Authorizes the Governor to fund staffing for five additional beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services; State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect
stakeholders: pediatric hospital overstay patients, children in unlicensed out-of-home placements, hospitals, and behavioral health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 to staff five additional beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents. Existing agency resources are sufficient for the Maryland Department of Health and Department of Human Services to establish coordinators and for the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect to staff the workgroup. Revenues and local government operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks MDH with expanding the scope of the Maryland Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry and Referral System, establishing an internal Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, transferring pediatric overstay patients to the least restrictive settings, staffing the newly authorized beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents (at a cost of roughly $3 million annually), and serving on the newly established workgroup.

The bill requires DHS to establish an internal Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, ensure that pediatric overstay patients committed to its custody are transferred to the least restrictive setting clinically indicated, and participate as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays to evaluate bed needs, create sustainable resource and implementation plans, and report findings to the General Assembly and Governor. It also tasks the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect with staffing the workgroup.

The Governor is tasked with appointing 11 members to the new workgroup, receiving the workgroup's report, and including budget appropriations for staffing beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services (or their designee) is designated as a mandatory member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Public Defender (or their designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove to study how urban renewal caused the displacement of residents from the Emory Grove community and make recommendations on potential remedies to those who were displaced by urban renewal; requiring the Task Force to submit an interim report by December 15, 2025, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Montgomery County Council, the Montgomery County Executive, the Montgomery County Delegation, and the General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
Title: Montgomery County - Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove MC 5-25

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary coordinating office for the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program.
