agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council as a statutory partner collaborating with MDH on educational and public health outreach initiatives regarding Alzheimer's treatments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting insurance carriers that offer life insurance or disability insurance policies or contracts from unfairly discriminating against an individual by taking certain actions relating to coverage based on medical information; prohibiting certain carriers from accessing sensitive medical information without first obtaining written consent or mandating certain genetic testing or full genome sequencing as a prerequisite for life insurance or disability insurance eligibility or coverage;  etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits life, long-term care, and disability insurers from unfairly discriminating based on medical information without an actuarial risk relationship. Authorizes insurers to establish risk relationships using actuarially sound principles or actual or reasonably anticipated experience. Prohibits life and disability insurers from accessing sensitive medical information, including genetic data, without signed written consent. Prohibits life and disability insurers from mandating genetic testing or full genome sequencing for insurance eligibility or coverage. Forbids insurers, applicants, or policyholders from waiving the prohibition on mandatory genetic testing under any circumstances. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to issue enforcement orders and impose penalties for violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Life, long-term care, and disability insurance carriers; applicants and policyholders for life, long-term care, and disability insurance
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in fiscal 2026 from rate and form filing fees. Any impact on State general fund premium tax revenues cannot be reliably predicted but is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary regulatory body responsible for enforcing Maryland's insurance laws. Under HB 1007, the Insurance Commissioner is granted explicit enforcement authority over life and disability insurers regarding restrictions on the use of genetic tests and sensitive medical information, and MIA will receive form filings and associated fees.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the African American Heritage Preservation Program and Grant Fund to provide funding for African American Heritage Preservation Noncapital Grants for the purpose of preserving or sharing African American history or culture in the State; requiring certain noncapital grants to be made using certain money received by the African American Heritage Preservation (AAHP) Grant Fund; and authorizing the AAHP Grant Fund to receive grants and donations.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Authorizes the African American Heritage Preservation Grant Fund to receive grants and donations. Permits the Secretary of Planning to award noncapital grants for preserving or sharing African American history or culture. Requires these noncapital grants to be funded solely from received grants and donations. Authorizes remaining grant and donation money to fund capital preservation projects after awarding all eligible noncapital grants. Restricts state budget appropriations, bond proceeds, and investment earnings strictly to capital preservation projects. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust; Commission on African American History and Culture; Secretary of Planning
stakeholders: individuals, business entities, nonprofit organizations, and political subdivisions preserving or sharing African American history or culture in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2026 from grants and donations received and noncapital grants disbursed. Specific dollar amounts cannot be reliably estimated. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent localities receive and spend grant awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the African American Heritage Preservation Program and Grant Fund within the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), which is an agency overseen by the Department of Planning. The Secretary of Planning makes the final determination on awards for the newly authorized noncapital grants and adopts regulations to implement the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture (MCAAHC) partners directly with the Maryland Historical Trust to develop and administer the program, review grant applications, establish annual application dates, and recommend grant awards to the Secretary.

bill_summary: Requires the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force to identify funding sources and mechanisms. Mandates studying funding to renovate the Baltimore Convention site and surrounding area, excluding designated Inner Harbor renewal areas. Directs the Task Force to identify funding to establish and sustain operations of an authority. Requires the Task Force to report findings and recommendations to state and city officials by December 1, 2025. Extends the termination date of the Task Force by one year to June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force
stakeholders: convention and tourism industries in Baltimore City, Baltimore City government, and visitors to the Baltimore Convention Center
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by approximately $350,000 in fiscal 2026 for consultant assistance. State revenues are not affected. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce provides primary staff support for the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force and incurs an estimated $350,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2026 to hire specialized consultants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the duties, scope of study, reporting requirements, and termination date of the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force.

The Maryland Stadium Authority holds statutory authority and existing capital and operating agreements regarding the Baltimore Convention Center, and the Task Force's findings directly impact the future governance, redevelopment, and funding of the convention site.
Housed within the Department of Commerce, the office is relevant to the Task Force's focus on convention site redevelopment, tourism marketing, and visitor economy strategies in Baltimore.
The Task Force is required to submit its findings and recommendations on funding sources and mechanisms to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

Synopsis: Requiring banking institutions, credit unions, mortgage lenders, mortgage lending businesses, and mortgage loan originators to include a certain provision in certain conventional home mortgage loans authorizing a certain borrower to purchase the property interest of a certain borrower in connection with a decree of absolute divorce if the lending entity determines that the assuming borrower qualifies for the loan; applying certain provisions of the Act retroactively; etc.
Title: Financial Institutions - Conventional Home Mortgage Loans - Assumption and Required Disclosures

bill_summary: Requires banking institutions, credit unions, and mortgage lenders to include an assumption provision in conventional home mortgage loans. Authorizes an existing borrower to purchase another borrower's property interest in connection with an absolute divorce decree. Conditions the mortgage assumption on the lender determining that the assuming borrower qualifies for the loan. Mandates written disclosure of the assumption provision to loan applicants before completing a loan application. Applies the assumption requirement retroactively to conventional home mortgage loans entered into before October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Mortgage borrowers facing an absolute divorce, banking institutions, credit unions, and licensed mortgage lenders in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which licenses, supervises, and regulates Maryland state-chartered banks, credit unions, and mortgage lenders subject to the bill's mortgage assumption and disclosure requirements.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a consumer reporting agency from furnishing any consumer report containing certain adverse information relating to a consumer's medical debt, or any collection action against a consumer for medical debt, or maintain a file on a consumer related to medical debt or collections; prohibiting a person from using medical debt information from a consumer report for certain purposes; prohibiting a health care facility, a health care practitioner, or an ambulance service from disclosing medical debt to a consumer reporting agency; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Credit Reporting - Medical Debt (Fair Medical Debt Reporting Act)

bill_summary: Prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including adverse medical debt information or debt collection actions in consumer reports. Prohibits persons from using medical debt information in consumer reports to determine a consumer's creditworthiness. Bars medical service, product, or device providers and their agents from disclosing medical debt to consumer reporting agencies. Requires medical providers to prohibit consumer reporting disclosures in debt collection and debt purchase contracts. Voids contracts with collection entities entered into on or after October 1, 2025, that lack this provision. Directs hospitals to instruct consumer reporting agencies by November 1, 2025, to delete previously reported adverse patient information.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission; Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers with medical debt, medical service and device providers, hospitals, medical debt collection entities, and consumer reporting agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Commercial Law Article to restrict credit reporting and creditworthiness determinations regarding medical debt, falling under consumer protection statutes enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The bill amends Health - General § 19-214.2 governing hospital debt collection policies and reporting, which are directly submitted to and overseen by the Health Services Cost Review Commission.

The bill establishes a new subtitle under the Health - General Article (Subtitle 25. Medical Debt Reporting) prohibiting health care facilities, health care practitioners, and medical service providers from disclosing medical debt to credit reporting agencies.
The Department of Labor regulates consumer reporting agencies and debt collection entities through its financial regulatory division and was consulted as an information source on the legislation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors from requiring an applicant to hold a bachelor's degree or higher to qualify for a certain certification or licensure as a real estate appraiser.

bill_summary: Prohibits the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors from requiring a bachelor's degree. Applies the restriction to applicants seeking real estate appraiser licensure or residential real estate appraiser certification. Excludes applicants seeking certification as a general real estate appraiser from this degree prohibition. Maintains other statutory qualification standards, including minimum age, good character, and required trainee hours. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors
stakeholders: Applicants for real estate appraiser licensure and residential real estate appraiser certification
fiscal_impact_summary: The Commission can implement the bill using existing resources. State revenues are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, which oversees the licensing and regulation of real estate appraisers affected by the bill.

Synopsis: Altering in Frederick County the beer and wine consumption permit to be the beer and wine tasting permit and the beer, wine, and liquor consumption permit to be the beer, wine, and liquor tasting permit; and requiring the Board to regulate the quantity of beer and wine served to an individual and the number of bottles or other containers from which the quantity is served.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Tasting Permits
bill_summary: Converts Frederick County alcoholic beverage consumption permits into beer and wine, and beer, wine, and liquor tasting permits. Authorizes the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue tasting permits to Class A license holders. Retains maximum tasting limits of 12 ounces of beer, 6 ounces of wine, and 1.5 ounces of liquor. Repeals statutory restrictions on individual sample serving sizes and combinations. Requires the Board to regulate serving quantities and the number of containers used. Prohibits open containers from leaving licensed premises or being served from drive-through windows.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County and retail tasting patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Frederick County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and collecting excise taxes; however, this bill specifically concerns local tasting permits administered directly by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners, resulting in no direct state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System; requiring the Workgroup to review a certain study completed by the Department of Information Technology in order to establish a plan to implement the recommendations of the study; and requiring the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by November 1, 2025.
Title: Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System
bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System. Designates the Secretary of Information Technology or the Secretary's designee as chair. Requires the Department of Information Technology, assisted by the Department of Legislative Services, to staff the workgroup. Directs the workgroup to review a prior feasibility study and examine implementation options for expanded 3-1-1 services. Requires the workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by November 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System
stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking nonemergency government information and services, local governments, public safety answering points, and telecommunications providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in fiscal 2026 only for the Department of Information Technology to hire a consultant to support the workgroup. No impact on State revenues. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation; the Secretary of Information Technology chairs the workgroup, DoIT provides staff support, and the department incurs a $50,000 fiscal impact in FY 2026 to hire a consultant to support the workgroup and prepare the report.

The Secretary of Emergency Management is a designated member of the workgroup, and MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, whose Executive Director is also a member tasked with appointing a telecommunications industry representative.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state-level workgroup/advisory task force to study 3-1-1 systems and deliver recommendations before terminating in June 2026.
The workgroup is mandated to submit its findings and recommendations report directly to the Governor by November 1, 2025.

bill_summary: Repeals the Objective Criteria Committee of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. Establishes the Compensation and Staffing Committee within the Board of Trustees. Modifies conditions under which the Chief Investment Officer and Investment Division staff receive awarded incentive compensation upon retirement. Requires payment of unpaid awarded incentives after a furlough if an individual retires directly from the division. Authorizes the Board of Trustees to retain a consultant for committee assistance and executive search services.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Chief Investment Officer and Investment Division staff of the State Retirement Agency; members and retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $10,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026, except in fiscal 2029, to retain the required consultant. Expenditures increase further if the consultant is engaged to provide executive search services. There is no effect on state revenues and local effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, repealing the Objective Criteria Committee, establishing the Compensation and Staffing Committee, and altering compensation, incentive pay, and staffing rules for the Investment Division. It also has a direct fiscal impact on the agency's special fund expenditures.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or the Secretary's designee) is designated as a mandatory member of the newly created Compensation and Staffing Committee of the Board of Trustees.
The State Treasurer (or the Treasurer's designee) is an authorized appointee to the newly established Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.
The Comptroller of Maryland (or the Comptroller's designee) may be appointed as a member of the newly established Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Synopsis: Clarifying the membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain employees of certain Maryland Department of Health facilities; and clarifying that certain participating employees who are appointed, promoted, or transferred are members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Membership - Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Expands membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System to specified Maryland Department of Health employees at seven designated facilities. Applies to CAMH associate supervisors and developmental disability associate assistant managers, managers, and supervisors as an employment condition. Requires the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer eligible prior service credit into the system. Permits affected members with pre-July 2008 service credit to opt out of the transfer by June 1, 2026. Authorizes normal service retirement for members who attain a combined total of at least 20 years of eligibility service. Requires the Board to calculate and grant the higher ordinary disability benefit available between the retirement systems.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; Maryland Department of Health; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: specified Maryland Department of Health supervisory and managerial employees at seven state health facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities increase by $470,000, increasing State pension contributions by $53,600 in FY 2028, funded by 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal/other funds, with costs increasing annually thereafter. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Employees' Pension System (EPS). The agency is directly responsible for administering the transfer of service credit, managing member opt-out elections, and calculating adjusted retirement and disability benefits under the bill.

The bill directly alters the retirement plan membership conditions for Maryland Department of Health employees in specified job classifications across seven MDH healthcare facilities, enrolling them into CORS as a condition of employment.

DBM serves as the central personnel and budget agency for the state. The bill creates an increase in state pension liabilities and employer pension contributions beginning in FY 2028 that will impact state personnel budgets and benefit structures.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the maximum average final compensation that certain retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System is to be based on the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale as of January 1 of the preceding calendar year in order to be exempt from a certain reemployment earnings limitation; and adding an average final compensation reemployment exemption for the temporary suspension of a retirement allowance for disability retirees.

bill_summary: Alters the maximum average final compensation threshold for reemployment earnings limitation exemptions in the State Retirement and Pension System. Replaces the fixed $25,000 threshold with the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale. Bases this standard on the pay scale as of January 1 of the preceding calendar year. Exempts qualifying reemployed disability retirees from the temporary suspension of their retirement allowance. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Reemployed service and disability retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System with low average final compensation, and participating public employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates, as the State Retirement and Pension System does not account for foregone offsets. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the calculation, tracking, and enforcement of reemployment earnings limitations, average final compensation thresholds, and benefit suspensions or offsets for retirees.

The Department of Budget and Management serves as the central personnel agency for the state and maintains the standard State pay scale, the minimum annual salary of which establishes the new threshold for reemployment earnings limitation exemptions.

Synopsis: Altering certain due dates of certain reports from the State Retirement and Pension System; and clarifying the eligibility requirements of State Police Retirement System members to participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System – Alterations and Clarifications
bill_summary: Postpones the annual minority business enterprise investment report deadline for the Investment Committee from September 1 to November 1. Extends the Board of Trustees' annual venture capital investment reporting deadline from December 1 to December 31. Links eligibility for the State Police Retirement System Deferred Retirement Option Program to years of employment instead of eligibility service. Applies the employment-based standard to determine maximum program duration for eligible troopers and the Secretary of State Police. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System Board of Trustees; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System, the Secretary of State Police, and minority business enterprise investment firms
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material effect on State governmental operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends reporting deadlines for the State Retirement and Pension System's Investment Committee and Board of Trustees, and clarifies statutory eligibility rules for the State Police Retirement System's Deferred Retirement Option Program administered by the agency.

The bill modifies the eligibility criteria for the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) specifically for members of the State Police Retirement System and the Secretary of State Police, basing eligibility on years of employment rather than eligibility service credit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the statutory recipient of the State Retirement Agency Investment Committee's annual report regarding minority business enterprise brokerage and investment management firms, the submission deadline of which is extended from September 1 to November 1.

bill_summary: Establishes comprehensive regulatory and procurement frameworks for electricity generation, energy storage devices, and gas utility infrastructure. Requires electric companies to file specific rate schedules protecting residential customers from the financial risks of large load customers. Directs the Public Service Commission to implement solicitations for dispatchable energy generation, energy storage, and nuclear generation. Establishes an expedited Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity review process for qualifying dispatchable and storage resources. Authorizes the distribution of Strategic Energy Investment Fund alternative compliance fees as residential electric bill credits in fiscal 2026. Excludes waste-to-energy and refuse-derived fuel from eligibility under the State Tier 1 Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; Office of People's Counsel
stakeholders: investor-owned electric and gas utilities; residential and business utility customers; large load commercial and industrial customers; independent energy generation and storage developers; municipal electric utilities; electric cooperatives; Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $203.3 million in FY 2026, which includes up to $200.0 million transferred from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to provide ratepayer bill credits and $2.5 million for Public Service Commission administrative costs. Office of People's Counsel special fund expenditures increase by $527,541 in FY 2026, with PSC and OPC costs recovered via utility assessments. Department of Natural Resources expenditures increase by $822,795 in FY 2026 and by at least $1.2 million annually thereafter for power plant siting reviews. Local finances are affected through municipal utility mandates and an estimated $12.2 million annual revenue decrease for Montgomery County beginning in FY 2027 from the exclusion of waste-to-energy from the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is the primary regulatory agency tasked with executing most of the bill's provisions, including solicitations for dispatchable energy generation and energy storage, regulating large-load customer rate schedules, overseeing multiyear rate plans and STRIDE gas cost recovery, issuing expedited CPCNs, and distributing $200 million in residential ratepayer credits.

MEA is required to pursue regional nuclear cost-sharing agreements and federal small modular reactor siting agreements, report on nuclear energy procurement, and absorb significant fiscal impacts from the redirection of up to $200 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) to fund utility bill credits.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is heavily involved in reviewing proposals for dispatchable energy generation and large capacity energy resources, recommending projects for expedited CPCN reviews, coordinating on nuclear agreements, and receiving fast-track procurement authority, requiring several new staff and ongoing consultant support.

DHCD is authorized to provide loans in addition to grants for multifamily residential building greenhouse gas reduction projects and can count expanded funding sources toward its EmPOWER Maryland emissions reduction targets, affecting tens of millions of dollars in ratepayer-funded program financing.

OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC. The bill establishes multiple new regulatory and ratemaking dockets requiring OPC to hire additional legal staff and consultants, and grants OPC legislative fast-track procurement authority.

The bill creates a legislative fast-track procurement process where the Chief Procurement Officer (located within DGS) must review and approve qualifying consultant contracts within five business days, creating operational requirements and potential procurement staffing demands.

MD Labor's Commissioner of Labor and Industry sets prevailing wage rates and the department enforces wage and community benefit agreement standards for underground utility work, front-of-the-meter storage projects, and energy generation projects under the bill.

MDE is granted fast-track procurement authority for mandated consultants, provides greenhouse gas emission baseline data utilized by the PSC, and will experience permitting workload increases for new generation and storage facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA, in consultation with the Office of the Attorney General, is required to assist potential applicants and minority investors and establish minority business enterprise participation goals and procedures for approved nuclear generation projects.

DHS is required to submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, regarding legislative and regulatory changes needed to consolidate all State energy assistance programs into a single program.

As the State's certified MBE agency, MDOT may need to conduct a disparity study regarding minority business enterprise utilization in nuclear power facilities to support GOSBA's participation goal-setting mandates.
OAG is required to consult with GOSBA in assisting potential applicants and minority investors and in developing MBE participation plans for nuclear energy generation projects.

The Comptroller is responsible for administering the state income tax subtraction modification established by the bill for legislative energy relief refunds received by residential distribution customers.

bill_summary: Alters the factors the Public Service Commission must consider before approving a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Establishes a distributed generation certificate of public convenience and necessity for certain solar energy generating systems. Prohibits local jurisdictions from adopting laws that ban solar energy generating stations or front-of-the-meter energy storage devices. Requires sellers and lessors of residential rooftop solar energy systems to provide a five-year warranty. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to develop a special solar contractor license. Directs the Public Service Commission to study electricity generation procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Developers and owners of solar energy generating stations and front-of-the-meter energy storage devices, residential rooftop solar sellers and contractors, electric companies, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $2.41 million in FY 2026 across the Public Service Commission, the Department of Natural Resources, and the Maryland Department of Labor, partially offset by $403,385 in public service company assessments. Special fund application fees and contractor license revenues begin in FY 2027. Indeterminate impact on local government finances and operations due to siting restrictions, bond administration, and expedited permitting mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with establishing regulations for the new Distributed Generation Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (DGCPCN), approving energy storage devices, reviewing CPCN and DGCPCN applications under altered criteria, and conducting two major studies.

The department's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is directed to develop standard siting, design, and licensing requirements for DGCPCNs, evaluate individual DGCPCN applications, update the SmartDG+ mapping tool, and complete a comprehensive assessment of State-owned land suitable for solar development.

The Department of Labor is required to establish and administer a new special solar contractor license, set minimum qualifications for installers of residential rooftop solar energy generating systems, and conduct associated enforcement.

The agency is statutorily required to consult with the Department of Natural Resources in updating the SmartDG+ tool and conducting an analysis of State-owned land suitable for solar energy development.

The Department of Planning must consult with DNR on updating the SmartDG+ tool and analyzing State-owned land for solar development, and its work overlaps with the bill's provisions on priority preservation areas and local comprehensive planning.

The Department of the Environment is notified of CPCN applications, required to expedite regulatory reviews and decisions for certain procurement model generation projects, and oversees environmental and stormwater standards impacted by solar expansion.

MDOT is required to consult with DNR on updating the SmartDG+ tool and analyzing State-owned land suitable for solar development, and the bill contains provisions addressing public road rights-of-way.

The bill references MDA's weed control program as the standard for allowable herbicide use on solar and storage project sites and amends statutory definitions relating to agricultural activities and agrivoltaics.

As the advocate for residential utility customers, OPC is an active party in PSC proceedings related to generation procurement models, community solar programs, and rate impacts addressed in the bill.
The bill explicitly references MAA determinations of aviation safety as a required factor for the PSC when evaluating CPCN applications.
The Governor's Office receives the reports from the two studies conducted by the Public Service Commission regarding generation procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.

Synopsis: Updating references to federal law related to family planning services, grandfathered plans, explanation of benefits, summaries of benefits and coverage, medical loss ratios, catastrophic plans, annual limits for cost sharing, prescription drugs, and rescissions; altering the definitions of "legally protected health care" and "sensitive health services" to include gender-affirming care for purposes of law governing the disclosure of information regarding sensitive health services; etc.
Title: Health Insurance, Family Planning Services, and Confidentiality of Medical Records - Consumer Protections - Updates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg

bill_summary: Updates statutory references to federal law across health insurance consumer protections and family planning services to December 31, 2024. Alters the definitions of legally protected health care and sensitive health services to include gender-affirming care. Grants the Maryland Insurance Commissioner concurrent jurisdiction with the Commission on Civil Rights to enforce health insurance anti-discrimination provisions. Authorizes the Commissioner to adopt regulations enforcing anti-discrimination provisions consistent with federal standards in effect December 31, 2024. Updates the baseline date for family planning provider funding and maintenance of effort requirements to December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, Title X family planning providers, patients seeking reproductive and gender-affirming care, and insured consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive fiscal impact on State or local finances, as the bill updates reference dates and aligns regulatory authorities without altering State operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1045 updates federal reference dates across multiple health insurance consumer protection statutes enforced by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, grants the Commissioner authority to adopt regulations, and establishes concurrent jurisdiction with the Commission on Civil Rights over health insurance discrimination provisions.

The bill directly updates references and requirements for MDH's Family Planning Program and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program regarding Title X providers, and updates definitions of 'legally protected health care' and 'sensitive health services' regarding medical records and health care confidentiality under the Health-General Article.

The bill specifically addresses the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights, granting it concurrent jurisdiction with the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce statutory prohibitions against carrier discrimination in health insurance plans.

The bill updates federal statutory and regulatory reference dates governing hardship and affordability exemptions that the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is tasked with establishing via regulation, and requires consultation on benefit and coverage summary standards.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a mechanical repair contract from containing a provision precluding coverage for service to a motor vehicle solely for issues identified in a technical services bulletin and prohibiting the denial of a service claim solely for such an issue by a guarantor or provider.
Title: Mechanical Repair Contracts - Technical Service Bulletins

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Prohibits mechanical repair contracts from precluding coverage solely for motor vehicle issues identified in technical service bulletins. Prohibits guarantors and providers from denying claims solely because a technical service bulletin identified the diagnosed issue. Applies the prohibition to mechanical repair contracts defined under Maryland transportation law. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners who purchase mechanical repair contracts or extended warranties; providers, guarantors, obligors, and licensed vehicle dealers that issue or service mechanical repair contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds provisions to the Maryland Service Contracts and Consumer Products Guaranty Act under the Commercial Law Article prohibiting the exclusion or denial of mechanical repair contract claims based solely on technical service bulletins. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces the Act and may seek court orders or restitution for violations.

Obligors who issue and perform services under mechanical repair contracts are required to register annually with the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, making contract requirements and claim denial standards relevant to the agency's regulatory oversight.
The MVA regulates licensed vehicle dealers and automotive businesses in Maryland, which are among the primary entities authorized to offer and sell mechanical repair contracts governed by the bill.
MDOT oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and provisions of the Transportation Article governing vehicle dealers and mechanical repair contracts referenced in the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of judicial proceedings, corrections, criminal, family, public safety, and real property laws to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Judicial and Public Safety for Service Members Act

Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes uniform statutory definitions related to military service across multiple articles of the Maryland Code. Expands various legal, family, correctional, and public safety provisions to cover all uniformed services members. Broadens court record fee exemptions and jury service exemptions to include NOAA and Public Health Service officers. Protects eligible service members and their spouses regarding residential lease terminations and consumer contract cancellations. Exempts honorably discharged reserve component members of the uniformed services from correctional officer minimum age requirements.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Veterans and Military Families; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Active-duty and reserve service members of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps, and Public Health Service Commissioned Corps), veterans, military families, landlords, and commercial service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in fiscal 2026 only to update the Department of State Police licensing portal. Other state agencies and the Judiciary can absorb any administrative changes within existing resources, and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory exemptions and qualifications for handgun qualification licenses, handgun permits, and firearms transactions to apply to uniformed services members, requiring a $50,000 update to the Department of State Police licensing portal in FY 2026.

The bill updates the core statutory definitions of veterans, service members, and military families in Title 9, Subtitle 9 of the State Government Article governing the department, and tasks the department with presenting state flags to families of uniformed services members killed in the line of duty.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the organized militia, the Maryland Defense Force commissioning requirements, and the Adjutant General's authority to organize honor guards for deceased veterans.

The bill alters statutory requirements for court clerks to provide court and marriage records free of charge to expanded categories of service members, updates prospective juror qualification forms, and impacts judicial proceedings involving service members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article requiring the Secretary to update regulations regarding the minimum hiring age exemption for correctional officers to include honorably discharged reserve component members of the uniformed services.

The bill updates provisions under the State Code of Military Justice, organized militia qualifications, and references to rights posted on the Maryland National Guard's website under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act.
The bill updates the Secretary of State's statutory duty to issue a State flag to the family of any member of the uniformed services killed in the performance of duty.
The bill modifies the definition of 'emergency management' in the Public Safety Article to exclude functions for which the uniformed services are primarily responsible.
The bill updates the Family Law Article regarding out-of-home placement eligibility and exit from foster care due to uniformed services duty for children in need of assistance (CINA).

Synopsis: Establishing that certain project site visits and educational field tours do not constitute open meetings subject to the requirement that the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, respectively, stream live video or audio of their open meetings.
Title: Montgomery County Planning Board and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission - Open Meetings - Live Streaming Requirement MC/PG 101-25
bill_summary: Establishes that project site visits and educational field tours do not constitute open meetings under live streaming mandates. Applies this exclusion to the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission. Excludes these events only when the entity conducts no organizational business during the visit or tour. Limits live streaming mandates to meetings at headquarters or sites hosting at least ten meetings the preceding year. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Planning Board; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
stakeholders: Montgomery County Planning Board, Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, and members of the public observing their proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Montgomery County Planning Board or the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General advises on and assists with the enforcement and interpretation of Maryland's Open Meetings laws, and was consulted as an information source for the bill. However, the legislation specifically targets local and bi-county entities (the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission) and has no state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the board of appeals in Prince George's County to be at least three members; and altering the number of members of the board required to concur in any resolution to a simple majority.
Title: Prince George's County - Board of Appeals - Membership MC/PG 106-25
bill_summary: Requires the County Council of Prince George's County to appoint at least three members to the board of appeals. Replaces the requirement that at least two members concur in any resolution with a simple majority requirement. Maintains four-year terms for members and the requirement that members reside in the county's regional district. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Council; Prince George's County Board of Appeals
stakeholders: Prince George's County Board of Appeals members; residents of the regional district in Prince George's County; Prince George's County Council
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent that additional members are appointed to the board of appeals, but specific figures are unavailable. County revenues are not affected.

Synopsis: Requiring the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to establish a workgroup on the improvement of health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use; requiring the workgroup to make recommendations on changes to State laws, policies and practices needed to mitigate the harm related to criminalization of substance use and related to the discharge of patients from substance use treatment programs; and requiring the workgroup to submit a certain report annually.

bill_summary: Requires the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to establish a workgroup on substance use outcomes. Directs the workgroup to evaluate substance use disorder treatment access, criminal justice involvement, and patient discharge standards. Mandates that the workgroup meet at least two times per year. Requires annual reports and recommendations to the Commission and the Behavioral Health Advisory Council by July 1. Instructs the workgroup to recommend statutory and policy changes regarding substance use criminalization and treatment discharge.
responsible_party: Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: individuals with substance use disorders, behavioral health treatment providers, patients in substance use treatment programs, and individuals involved in the criminal justice system
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health increase by $38,000 in FY 2026 and $39,600 in FY 2027 to hire a part-time contractual health policy analyst to staff the workgroup. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) provides administrative and staffing support to the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access. The bill requires MDH to hire a contractual health policy analyst incurring state general fund expenditures, and mandates that the new workgroup specifically evaluate and review MDH regulations concerning patient discharge standards for substance use treatment programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the statutory duties of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, requiring it to establish an additional workgroup focused on improving health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use, and report annual recommendations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the use of discretionary clauses in life insurance policies, health insurance policies, annuity contracts, and health maintenance organization contracts.
Title: Life and Health Insurance Policies and Annuity and Health Maintenance Organization Contracts - Discretionary Clauses - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: Prohibits carriers from selling, delivering, or issuing life insurance, health insurance, annuity contracts, or health maintenance organization contracts with discretionary clauses. Expands the definition of carrier to include health maintenance organizations alongside insurers and nonprofit health service plans. Bars clauses reserving sole discretion to the carrier to interpret policy terms. Prohibits standards of interpretation or review that are inconsistent with State law. Applies to policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and policyholders and contract holders in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. MIA can handle form reviews with existing budgeted resources. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance policies and contracts sold in the State. The bill prohibits carriers from including discretionary clauses in life, health, HMO, and annuity contracts, requiring MIA to review updated policy forms and collecting rate and form filing fees.
The bill amends the Health - General Article (§ 19-706) regarding health maintenance organizations (HMOs), over which the Maryland Department of Health maintains regulatory and statutory oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to certify certain employer contribution rates each fiscal year; requiring the employer contribution rates to include recognition of certain administrative and operational expenses; repealing a requirement that certain administrative and operational expenses of the State Retirement and Pension System and the State Retirement Agency be funded by charging each participating employer an administrative fee for each system participant; etc.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Administrative Fees - Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that participating employers pay separate administrative fees to the State Retirement and Pension System. Requires normal employer contribution rates to include administrative and operational expenses of the system and State Retirement Agency. Excludes administrative and operational expenses of the Investment Division from that normal contribution rate calculation. Funds system administrative and operational expenses through the pension accumulation fund for fiscal year 2026. Requires participating local employers to pay their certified fiscal year 2025 administrative fees by June 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: State agencies, local school boards, community colleges, and participating governmental units enrolled in the State Retirement and Pension System
fiscal_impact_summary: In fiscal 2026, State Retirement Agency special fund revenues decrease by $21.8 million and general fund expenditures decrease by $5.7 million due to a planned budget reversion. Local employer expenditures decrease by $21.8 million in fiscal 2026 due to the elimination of fee payments. Beginning in fiscal 2027, inclusion of administrative expenses in employer normal contribution rates fully offsets the fee repeal, resulting in no material net effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1072 directly alters how the administrative and operational expenses of the State Retirement and Pension System and the State Retirement Agency are funded, repealing separate administrative fees paid by participating employers and incorporating these costs into the normal employer contribution rate, resulting in significant fiscal and operational impacts on the agency.

The Board of Trustees must annually certify the employer contribution rates to the Secretary of Budget and Management. As the state's central budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits, budget execution, and the general fund reversion resulting from the bill in FY 2026.
The bill requires the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System to certify the recommended rates of employer contributions annually to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord to provide a tenant with certain written notice in a certain manner at least 24 hours in advance of when the landlord intends to enter a leased premises, except in the event of a certain emergency; and authorizing the court to issue a certain injunction or assess certain damages under certain circumstances.
Title: Residential Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Notice of Landlord Entry

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires residential landlords to provide tenants with at least 24 hours written notice before entering leased premises. Limits entry to between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday unless agreed otherwise in writing. Permits entry without notice during emergencies to protect property, occupant safety, or staff and tenant welfare. Authorizes courts to issue injunctions or assess damages against noncompliant landlords. Requires tenants alleging housing code violations to grant landlord access within 24 hours of notification.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: residential landlords and residential tenants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory cause of action allowing tenants to seek judicial relief, authorizing the courts to issue injunctions and award damages against landlords who violate the notice of entry requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General, particularly its Consumer Protection Division, enforces laws protecting consumers and tenants from deceptive or unlawful practices related to residential leases and landlord-tenant relations.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include $200,000,000 in the annual operating or capital budget bill for site redevelopment and transportation infrastructure improvements if the U.S. General Services Administration applies to Prince George's County or the State for a permit associated with the relocation of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters to Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters - Mandated Appropriation
bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation in the annual operating or capital budget bill. Triggers the mandate if the U.S. General Services Administration applies for a relocation permit. Requires the permit application to be submitted to Prince George’s County or the State. Mandates an appropriation of at least $200,000,000 for the project. Dedicates the funding to site redevelopment and transportation infrastructure improvements for the Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters.
responsible_party: Governor
stakeholders: Prince George’s County, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the U.S. General Services Administration
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected assuming $200 million in previously authorized general obligation bond funding fulfills the mandate. If interpreted as requiring new funding, state expenditures increase by up to $200 million in fiscal 2027. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $200,000,000 in the annual operating or capital budget bill if the U.S. General Services Administration applies for a relocation permit.

As the principal agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM must implement and account for the statutory funding mandate in the Governor's annual budget submission.

The mandated appropriation is dedicated to improving transportation infrastructure for the FBI headquarters relocation project, which is programmed within MDOT's Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP).

The transportation improvements funded by the bill include construction of an interchange along I-95/I-495 at the Greenbelt Metro Station, which falls under the planning and construction responsibilities of the State Highway Administration.

Synopsis: Establishing that governmental units may provide disaster service leave with pay to certain employees; establishing that an employee of a governmental unit of a county or a municipality in the State may be entitled to disaster service leave with pay under certain circumstances; authorizing certain governmental units to waive certain requirements for disaster service leave; and authorizing a governmental unit of a county or a municipality to provide leave with pay under certain circumstances.
Title: Local Government - Local Personnel - Leave With Pay

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes governmental units of counties and municipalities to provide disaster service leave with pay to eligible employees. Limits disaster service leave to 30 days in a 12-month period upon governmental unit approval. Authorizes local governmental units to waive approval requirements and increase leave days during prolonged or recurrent disasters. Authorizes local governmental units to provide paid leave for jury duty, employee organization events, and subpoena compliance. Authorizes paid leave for up to 30 days of uniformed services training or active duty. Authorizes paid administrative leave when safety threats or extraordinary circumstances require removing an employee from work.
responsible_party: County and municipal governmental units
stakeholders: Employees of county and municipal governmental units in Maryland, volunteer emergency personnel, military reservists, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local government expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, to the extent that counties and municipalities elect to provide additional paid leave. Specific figures are unavailable because granting leave is discretionary. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local governments to grant paid disaster service leave to employees participating in disaster response organizations (such as CERT, VOAD, Red Cross, and volunteer fire/EMS). While there is no direct state fiscal impact, this policy intersects with MDEM's coordination of disaster preparedness, response, and volunteer emergency operations across local jurisdictions.

The bill authorizes county and municipal governments to provide up to 30 days of paid leave for local employees participating in uniformed services training or active duty in the organized militia, which falls under the leadership and readiness oversight of the Adjutant General.

Synopsis: Establishing the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program to provide subsidies to individuals in the State to mitigate the impact of a reduction in certain federal advance premium tax credits for calendar years 2026 through 2028; and requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to implement the Program under certain circumstances.
Title: Health Insurance - Individual Market Stabilization - Establishment of the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Establishes the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program to mitigate reductions in federal advance premium tax credits. Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in consultation with the Insurance Commissioner, to implement the program. Targets individuals facing higher premium contribution percentages for individual health plans in calendar years 2026 and 2027. Authorizes the Exchange to designate money from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund in fiscal years 2026 through 2028. Requires the Exchange to track program expenditures monthly and adopt implementing regulations. Abrogates the program if the federal government extends advance premium tax credits for calendar years 2026 and 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland residents purchasing individual health benefit plans through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; health insurance carriers offering plans in the individual market
fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming federal advance premium tax credits are not extended, Maryland Health Benefit Exchange special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate but significant amount (potentially up to $75.0 million in FY 2026, $150.0 million in FY 2027, and $75.0 million in FY 2028) to provide subsidies. Administrative costs are absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected. If federal credits are extended, the bill terminates without fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing, administering, and funding the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program, adopting regulations, setting subsidy eligibility and payment parameters, and tracking monthly expenditures.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must be consulted by MHBE to establish program eligibility and payment parameters, and is tasked with notifying the Department of Legislative Services if federal premium tax credits are extended.
The Comptroller accounts for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, which receives and expends designated funds under the program.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the moneys of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund pursuant to state statute.

Synopsis: Requiring the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, through its workgroup, to implement Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment requirements; requiring the workgroup to provide recommendations to implement recommendations in a certain Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services State Health Official letter; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
Title: Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access - Plan to Implement Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to provide implementation recommendations. Directs the bodies to implement federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services best practices for children. Requires evaluation of screening conditions, community-based services, crisis needs, and diagnostic tools for patients under age five. Mandates consultation with behavioral health clinicians, childhood specialists, advocates, affected children, and experienced caregivers. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Advisory Council; Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
stakeholders: Medicaid-eligible children and youth with behavioral health needs; families and caregivers navigating the behavioral health system; pediatric behavioral health clinicians and specialists
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the advisory council, commission, and Maryland Department of Health can formulate recommendations and submit the report using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the state's Medicaid program (including the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment Program) and is statutorily required under the bill to submit the final report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that two executive advisory bodies—the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access—collaborate through a designated workgroup to develop and provide the required recommendations.

Synopsis: Exempting certain real property owned by certain nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities from State and local property taxation; directing certain nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities to make payment in lieu of taxes that may be set by mutual agreement with a political subdivision; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
Title: Housing Authorities - Tax-Exempt Status - Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Exempts real property owned by certain nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities from State and local property taxation. Expands the property tax exemption statewide beyond Baltimore City, Howard County, and Montgomery County. Applies the exemption to property used, planned, or under construction for housing persons of eligible income. Directs qualifying housing authority entities to make payments in lieu of taxes established by mutual agreement with political subdivisions. Caps the negotiated payments at the amount of regular taxes levied on similar property. Takes effect June 1, 2025, applying to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Public housing authorities across Maryland, nonprofit subsidiary entities created by public housing authorities, persons of eligible income seeking affordable housing, and local political subdivisions
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal decrease in State and local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2026 to the extent public housing authorities establish qualifying nonprofit entities. State and local expenditures are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article to extend property tax exemptions to real property owned by nonprofit entities established by public housing authorities statewide. This directly impacts affordable housing development, public housing authority partnerships, and programs like the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) administered and supported within DHCD's policy area.

The bill provides an exemption from State and local property taxation for qualifying housing authority entities, resulting in a potential minimal decrease in State property tax revenues, an area monitored and collected by the Comptroller's Office.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and managed care organizations cover anesthesia for the entire duration of a procedure without imposing time limitations, directly impacting the department's program administration and Medicaid expenditures.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for a certain beauty salon license in Montgomery County to include a holder of a certain barbershop permit; authorizing a holder of the license to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption in addition to beer and wine; and authorizing the holder to provide not more than 12 ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine, or 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption by a beauty salon or barbershop customer; and requiring an annual license fee of $100.

Applies prior approval ratemaking provisions to the Fund from July 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025. Enforces prior approval ratemaking beginning January 1, 2026, if the Fund fails to maintain required capital. Directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to establish a workgroup studying private passenger automobile insurance affordability. bill_summary: Establishes the Population Health Improvement Fund to support statewide population health targets under the federal AHEAD Model. Authorizes the Health Services Cost Review Commission to assess hospital rates through December 31, 2027, to support the fund. Permits electronic health transaction data to be shared with the State-designated health information exchange for AHEAD Model implementation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit an annual progress report to the General Assembly beginning in 2026. Directs the Department and Commission to hold monthly implementation briefings with designated legislators through December 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Health Services Cost Review Commission; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, electronic health networks, health care payers, and Maryland residents receiving health care services

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with jointly administering the newly established Population Health Improvement Fund, directing fund expenditures in alignment with the Statewide Health Equity Plan, submitting annual reports to the General Assembly, and providing monthly updates on AHEAD model implementation.

HSCRC jointly administers the Population Health Improvement Fund with the Department of Health, is authorized to assess hospital rates (generating an estimated $25 million in special fund revenue), and is required to participate in monthly legislative briefings.

MHCC regulates the State-designated health information exchange (HIE) and electronic health networks; the bill specifically prohibits MHCC regulations from restricting the State's use of electronic claims/financial transaction data for public health purposes under the AHEAD Model.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund separately and invest its moneys pursuant to state investment guidelines.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Population Health Improvement Fund and oversee the fund's accounting under state finance laws.
The bill explicitly establishes that the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits under § 2-1220 of the State Government Article.

bill_summary: Establishes a geriatric parole process for certain incarcerated individuals at least 65 years old who served 20 years. bill_summary: Establishes the Buprenorphine Training Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health. Authorizes counties to apply for grants exclusively to offset costs of training paramedics to administer buprenorphine. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of at least $50,000 from the Opioid Restitution Fund for the program. Expands authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to include the grant program. Directs the Maryland Office of Overdose Response to convene a workgroup studying buprenorphine access and report by December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Office of Overdose Response
stakeholders: counties, county paramedics, local health departments, local behavioral health agencies, and individuals with opioid use disorder
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $56,100 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Office of Overdose Response to staff the workgroup. Opioid Restitution Fund special fund expenditures increase by at least $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2031 due to the mandated appropriation, with no net effect on total fund spending. Local revenues and expenditures may increase for counties receiving grant awards beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Buprenorphine Training Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to provide grants to counties for training paramedics. Additionally, MDH's Behavioral Health Administration is required to participate in the study workgroup, and the department will administer the mandated $50,000 annual appropriation from the Opioid Restitution Fund.

The bill tasks the Maryland Office of Overdose Response (an executive initiative under the Governor) with convening the buprenorphine access workgroup, incurring $56,066 in general fund staffing expenditures in FY 2026 and reporting findings directly to the Governor. The bill also mandates the Governor to include at least $50,000 in the annual budget bill for the grant program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill focuses on training paramedics to administer buprenorphine and explicitly requires a representative of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to serve as a member of the study workgroup.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary multi-stakeholder workgroup to study access to buprenorphine in the State, examine service delivery models, and submit findings and recommendations by December 31, 2025.

The bill establishes a statutory mandated appropriation requiring at least $50,000 annually from the Opioid Restitution Fund from FY 2027 through FY 2031, directly affecting DBM's budget development and oversight duties.
