bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group within the Maryland Department of Health. Requires the advisory group to evaluate Medicaid payment rate sufficiency for homemaker, home health aide, personal care, and habilitation services. Requires the group to study access challenges and examine working conditions for direct care workers. Directs the Deputy Secretary of Health Care Financing to appoint initial members on or before October 1, 2025. Prohibits employers and State agencies from retaliating against direct care workers or consumers for participating in the advisory group. Requires the advisory group to report recommendations annually to the Governor and the General Assembly beginning in 2026.

MDH's Deputy Secretary of Health Care Financing serves as chair and appoints members, and MDH is required to provide staff, logistical, and informational support, maintain a dedicated webpage, supply required rate and access data, and respond to recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent advisory body, the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group, to evaluate Medicaid payment rates, working conditions for direct care workers, and access to home- and community-based services.

The Secretary of Labor (or their designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Advisory Group, and data collected by the Department of Labor regarding the direct care workforce is to be distributed and examined by the group.

The Advisory Group is required to submit an annual report of its activities, findings, and recommendations regarding Medicaid payment rates and workforce issues to the Governor by September 1 each year.

The Secretary of Education (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Collaborative, and the Collaborative's primary focus is studying and recommending policies for school-based dental programs affecting Maryland public school students.

bill_summary: Authorizes prohibiting individuals alleged to have committed assault or bodily injury from using State public transit services or entering stations. Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to convene a workgroup by June 1, 2025. Directs the workgroup to create a rider code of conduct and implement an internal safety program. Mandates ridership bans for assault without requiring a criminal conviction, subject to an appeals process. Authorizes transit use if an assault directly related to a disability and an appropriate caregiver accompanies the individual. Requires the workgroup to report findings and recommendations by October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Maryland Transit Administration transit operators and passengers; individuals accused of assault or bodily injury on State public transit services
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $18,800 in FY 2025 and by $131,200 in FY 2026 for consultant services to staff the workgroup and assist in program implementation. Revenues are not affected, and local finances experience no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MTA is the primary implementing agency under the bill. It is authorized to establish guidelines and an appeals process to exclude individuals who commit assault or bodily injury, and it is mandated to convene a workgroup by June 1, 2025, to create a rider code of conduct and implement a comprehensive internal safety program.

MTA is a modal administration under MDOT, and the bill directly increases Transportation Trust Fund expenditures by $18,800 in FY 2025 and $131,200 in FY 2026 to engage expert consultants to assist in developing the code of conduct and safety program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary workgroup convened by the MTA, consisting of transit representatives and stakeholders, to create a rider code of conduct, design an appeals process, and submit reports to legislative committees.
The bill defines State public transit service to include services operated by any State agency, which may encompass university-operated public transit shuttles (such as Shuttle-UM).
Persons who violate exclusions under the bill are subject to criminal prosecution for trespassing, which would be adjudicated within the Maryland District Court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Individuals arrested and prosecuted for trespassing or assault arising from violations of transit bans could require indigent defense representation provided by OPD.

bill_summary: Establishes waiting periods for alcoholic beverages license applications and issuances in Baltimore County following application denials. Prohibits submitting another license application for the same location for one year after a denial. Prohibits issuing a license for the same location for two years if an application for that location is denied twice. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and commercial property owners in Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. The bill does not materially affect Baltimore County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation specifically alters the local waiting period for alcoholic beverages license applications and re-issuances in Baltimore County and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages regulation in the state.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Behavioral Health Crisis Response System to include a State 9–8–8 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in each jurisdiction or region. Mandates coordination with the national lifeline network to deliver counseling, suicide prevention, crisis intervention, referrals, and direct dispatches. Expands outcome evaluations to include call resolution rates, mobile crisis team response metrics, and crisis stabilization center usage. Directs the Behavioral Health Administration to gather ongoing provider data and track law enforcement involvement and hospital diversions. Requires outcome evaluation data disaggregated by race, gender, age, and zip code to be publicly reported annually by December 1.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration
stakeholders: individuals experiencing behavioral health and suicidal crises, 9-8-8 crisis service providers, mobile crisis teams, and local behavioral health authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $63,100 in FY 2026 and between $55,200 and $62,900 annually through FY 2030 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one part-time epidemiologist to establish data systems and oversee outcome reporting. Local revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its Behavioral Health Administration administer the Maryland Behavioral Health Crisis Response System and oversee the 9-8-8 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. MDH is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, establishing data reporting systems for mobile crisis teams and stabilization centers, and publishing the required annual outcome evaluation report, which requires additional general fund expenditures for staff.

Applies when the prior lapse resulted from an insurer withdrawing from the market. Restricts the prohibition to coverage lapses lasting no longer than 90 days. Authorizes the insurer to require an affidavit stating the applicant incurred no losses during the lapse. Requires the applicant to provide any other documentation required by the insurer. Applies to new residential condominium unit insurance policies issued on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Residential condominium unit owners and insurers issuing residential condominium unit policies in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business impact is minimal.

responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Montgomery County; municipal governments in Montgomery County

fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $12,208 in FY 2026 for District Court programming changes. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the District Court to process citations and handle contested cases resulting from authorized speed monitoring systems, with an estimated fiscal impact of approximately $12,200 in FY 2026 for necessary system reprogramming.

The bill modifies the Transportation Article regarding speed camera placements on roadways identified under the State's Strategic Highway Safety Plan or Vision Zero Plan and prohibits placement on expressways and interstate highways.

MDOT SHA establishes traffic control device standards for speed camera warning signage, designates state and interstate highways, and collaborates on the Strategic Highway Safety Plan and Vision Zero safety evaluations.

The MVA houses the Maryland Highway Safety Office, which develops and administers the State Strategic Highway Safety Plan and Vision Zero programs used to determine high-risk highway eligibility under the bill.
Under the referenced statutory provisions, local jurisdictions must remit any speed monitoring system revenues exceeding 10% of total revenues to the Comptroller for deposit into the General Fund.

bill_summary: Requires federal law enforcement officers to notify specified officials of federal immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations. Requires public schools, public libraries, and executive branch units at sensitive locations to deny nonpublic access for federal immigration enforcement. Permits access only when the individual presents a valid federal court warrant or exigent circumstances exist. Requires the Attorney General to develop and publish guidance regarding immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations. responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: Maryland residents, public schools, public libraries, State and local executive agencies operating at sensitive locations, and federal law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Attorney General to develop and publish formal guidance regarding federal immigration enforcement at sensitive locations, delineate boundaries, minimize liability, and designate additional eligible sensitive locations.

The bill requires each governmental entity to consult directly with the Department of Information Technology to develop and publish procedures preventing the commercial sale and redisclosure of personal records and geolocation data.

Facilities operated by the Comptroller are explicitly defined as 'sensitive locations' under the bill, requiring the Comptroller to deny nonpublic access to federal immigration enforcement absent a judicial warrant and adopt policies aligned with Attorney General guidance.

Health care facilities operated by units of State or local government are classified as sensitive locations under the bill, requiring State health facilities operated by MDH to implement access restriction policies aligned with Attorney General guidance.

Public schools are designated as sensitive locations under the bill, requiring public educational institutions under MSDE's purview to deny nonpublic access to immigration agents without a judicial warrant and adopt conforming policies.
Courthouses are designated as sensitive locations subject to restrictions on immigration enforcement access, directly impacting facility management and operational policies overseen by the Judiciary.

Federal law enforcement officers are statutorily required to notify the appropriate Department of State Police barrack commander when conducting federal immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations.
The bill requires federal law enforcement officers to notify the Secretary of Natural Resources prior to taking federal immigration enforcement actions on property owned, leased, or operated by DNR.
The chief of police of MDTA must be notified by federal law enforcement officers when immigration enforcement actions take place on properties controlled by MDTA, MAA, or MPA.
MAA properties are specifically cited in the statute under the notice requirements when federal immigration enforcement actions are conducted.
MPA properties are specifically cited in the statute under the notice requirements when federal immigration enforcement actions are conducted.

Public libraries are explicitly designated as sensitive locations, requiring them to restrict nonpublic access by federal immigration enforcement officers and adopt policies consistent with Attorney General guidance.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration Waiver Advisory Council within the Developmental Disabilities Administration. Requires the Secretary of Health to appoint voting members representing individuals with lived experience, families, and service providers. Mandates public bi-monthly meetings with video recordings, advance agendas, and designated public comment periods. Requires the Administration to provide staff and host a dedicated Council webpage with meeting records.
responsible_party: Developmental Disabilities Administration; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities participating in Medicaid waiver programs, their families, and developmental disability service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources for travel and expense reimbursements. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1244 establishes the Waiver Advisory Council within the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), a unit of MDH. The Secretary of Health appoints voting members and designates specific staff representatives, and DDA is required to staff the council and host its dedicated webpage.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes in statute a state advisory body, the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration Waiver Advisory Council, to evaluate and advise on Medicaid waiver program policies and service delivery.

The Secretary of Disabilities is required to designate a representative to serve as a nonvoting member on the newly established advisory council, which aligns closely with the department's mission to coordinate services for Marylanders with disabilities.
The State Superintendent of Schools is required to designate a representative from the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) to serve as a nonvoting member on the advisory council.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is required to designate an agency representative to serve as a nonvoting member of the advisory council.
The Secretary of Human Services is required to designate an agency representative to serve as a nonvoting member of the advisory council.

Synopsis: Requiring certain hospitals to adopt certain policies relating to obstetric services and to provide evidence to the Maryland Department of Health that the hospital has the policies; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide certain policies to the public on request; and requiring insurers that issue or deliver medical professional liability insurance policies in the State to provide the Maryland Department of Health, on request, with information regarding the insurer's policy regarding coverage of obstetric services.
Title: Hospitals and Medical Professional Liability Insurers - Obstetric Services Policies (Doula and Birth Policy Transparency Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Requires hospitals providing obstetric care to adopt policies concerning doulas, informed consent for significant medical interventions, and patient transfer acceptance. Requires hospitals to provide evidence of adopted policies to the Maryland Department of Health by January 1, 2026. Requires policies to allow every birthing parent at least one doula present during birth in addition to authorized guests. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to make submitted hospital policies available to the public on request. Requires medical professional liability insurers to provide information regarding obstetric coverage policies to the Department on request.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Hospitals providing obstetric care, birthing parents, doulas, home birth practitioners, licensed direct-entry midwives, and medical professional liability insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,800 in fiscal 2026 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one health facilities nurse surveyor to promulgate regulations, review hospital policies, and investigate complaints, with annualization in subsequent years. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), primarily through the Office of Health Care Quality, to receive obstetric services policies from hospitals, adopt implementing regulations, make policies publicly available upon request, and handle compliance investigations. MDH incurs an ongoing fiscal impact for staffing to execute these requirements.

The bill amends the Insurance Article by requiring medical professional liability insurers to provide information regarding their policies for obstetric services coverage upon request. As the state agency regulating the insurance industry and enforcing compliance with the Insurance Article, MIA has regulatory oversight of these insurers.

Synopsis: Establishing the Department of Social and Economic Mobility; providing for the Secretary of Social and Economic Mobility; providing the purpose of the Department is to provide support for units of State government, individuals, and businesses for the maintenance of social equity policies in the State; establishing the Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill a certain appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund to the Fund; etc.
Title: Department of Social and Economic Mobility - Established

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Department of Social and Economic Mobility as a principal department of the Executive Branch. Designates the department as the successor to three existing State offices regarding social equity programs. Consolidates the Office of Minority Business Enterprises, Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, and Office of Social Equity. Establishes the Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund to finance operations of specified transferred offices. Requires other State units to refer persons interacting with programs for designated populations to the department. Requires the department to submit annual reports on its work and recommended policy changes beginning in 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Social and Economic Mobility
stakeholders: small, minority, and women-owned businesses; individuals from communities disproportionately impacted by the war on drugs; adult-use cannabis business applicants; State personnel in transferred offices
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.3 million in FY 2026 ($2.2 million is budgeted) for nine new positions, moving expenses, and operating costs, with ongoing annual general fund costs ranging from $1.6 million to $1.8 million. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.4 million in FY 2026 and between $4.2 million and $4.4 million annually thereafter due to the redirection of Transportation Trust Fund monies and adult-use cannabis sales tax revenue into the new special fund. No direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally transfers the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, including its staff, duties, and funding, into the newly created Department of Social and Economic Mobility as a constituent unit.

The bill transfers the Office of Social Equity out of the Maryland Cannabis Administration into the newly created department, redirects cannabis tax revenue distributions, and requires ongoing regulatory and technical assistance coordination between MCA and the office.

The bill transfers the Office of Minority Business Enterprises (OMBE) from MDOT to the new department and mandates annual appropriations from the Transportation Trust Fund to cover OMBE's operating and administrative expenses.

The bill establishes a new cabinet-level principal executive department, empowers the Governor to appoint the Secretary and the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, and authorizes the Governor to transfer positions and budget appropriations.

DBM is tasked alongside the Governor with managing the transfer of personnel to minimize state costs and maximize efficiency, and will oversee budget allocations, new positions, and executive pay grade classifications for the new department.

The bill designates the Attorney General as the legal adviser to the newly created department and requires the assignment of Assistant Attorneys General, including a designated Counsel to the Department.

The Comptroller is required to account for the newly created Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund and distribute quarterly shares of adult-use cannabis sales and use tax revenues directly to the fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the newly established Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund separately and invest its moneys.

The bill mandates collaboration between the Department of Commerce and the Office of Social Equity to assist businesses with financing under the Capital Access Program and the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund.
The bill requires annual reports summarizing minority business enterprise participation data to continue being submitted to the Board of Public Works.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Liquor Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue a certain dancing permit to the holder of a Class H beer and wine or beer, wine, and liquor license for a licensed premises located within 1,000 feet of a school located at the Annapolis Mall, rather than prohibiting the Board from doing so; and authorizing the Board to issue a new Class B beer and wine or beer, wine, and liquor license to an establishment located within 1,000 feet of a school located at the Annapolis Mall.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - License and Permit Distance Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners to issue certain licenses and entertainment permits. Exempts establishments located within 1,000 feet of a school at the Annapolis Mall from standard distance restrictions. Authorizes the Board to issue a new Class B on-sale beer and wine or beer, wine, and liquor license. Authorizes the Board to issue a dancing permit to an eligible Class H license holder near that school. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Holders of Class B and Class H alcoholic beverages licenses and restaurant establishments located near the Annapolis Mall in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. The bill does not materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this bill solely alters local distance requirements and licensing exemptions administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal effect, it amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue a limited special event permit to holders of certain alcoholic beverages licenses; and authorizing a permit holder to provide music, dancing, and other legal forms of entertainment.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Limited Special Event Permit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a 1-day limited special event permit in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue the permit to qualifying license holders. Allows permit holders to provide music, dancing, and other legal forms of entertainment on a specific date. Prohibits permit issuance to Class BLX or Class H licenses within 1,000 feet of a place of worship or school. Sets daily permit fees up to $25, with no charge for Class C license holders.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Holders of Class B, Class BLX, Class C, Class D, and Class H alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Anne Arundel County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is tasked with regulatory oversight of the alcohol industry in Maryland. Although this bill pertains specifically to local limited special event permits issued by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages licenses.

Synopsis: Authorizing Charles County to regulate the operation of off-highway recreational vehicles in the county and to impound an off-highway recreational vehicle that is the subject of certain alleged motor vehicle violations.
Title: Charles County - Off-Highway Recreational Vehicles - Regulation and Enforcement

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes Charles County to regulate the operation of off-highway recreational vehicles. Permits the county to require off-highway recreational vehicles to be registered and impose registration fees. Allows the county to impose age restrictions on operating these vehicles. Authorizes the impoundment of vehicles subject to alleged reckless driving, impaired driving, or trespassing violations. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Charles County
stakeholders: Owners and operators of off-highway recreational vehicles in Charles County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Charles County revenues increase minimally if the county exercises its authority to require registration and impose registration fees. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article regarding local authority over highways and vehicle regulations, directly interfacing with the statutory framework overseen by MDOT.

The MVA oversees vehicle titling and registration across the state, including existing titling requirements for off-highway recreational vehicles (OHRVs), and was consulted regarding the interaction between state vehicle registration and county-level regulation.

The Maryland State Police enforces traffic and criminal laws on Maryland roadways, including in Charles County, and has authority regarding vehicle stops, moving violations, and impoundments referenced under the bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court and Circuit Courts, which process citations, trespass violations, and judicial proceedings resulting from the enforcement and impoundment of OHRVs.

Synopsis: Renaming "network directory" to be "provider directory" to conform to a certain federal law; altering the time period from 15 to 2 working days within which certain carriers are required to update the information that must be made available in the carrier's provider directory on the Internet; altering the information required to be included in a provider directory; requiring that a provider directory in printed form include a statement regarding the accuracy of the provider information; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Provider Directory - Required Updates

bill_summary: Renames network directories to provider directories to conform to federal law. Requires health insurance carriers to update online provider directories within two working days after receiving change notifications. Allows dental carriers 15 working days to update directory information after receipt of notification. Requires each carrier to verify and update provider directory information at least once every 90 days. Mandates that printed directories include notices regarding information accuracy dates and directing readers to online versions. Directs the Insurance Commissioner to report on directory accuracy regulations by January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: health insurance carriers, dental plan organizations, participating healthcare providers and facilities, and health benefit plan enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues. The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill and submit the required report using existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers under the Insurance Article, enforces network and provider directory compliance, and the Insurance Commissioner is specifically required by the bill to submit a report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, on regulatory changes regarding provider directory accuracy.

Synopsis: Establishing the Neighborhood Services Unit within the Office of the Sheriff of Baltimore City; requiring the Neighborhood Services Unit and the Board of License Commissioners of Baltimore City to work in partnership to enforce the alcoholic beverages laws of Baltimore City and to enter into a memorandum of understanding that specifies the respective roles and responsibilities of the parties and funding in connection with the partnership; expanding the authorized uses of certain revenue to include the Neighborhood Services Unit; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - Office of the Sheriff - Neighborhood Services Unit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Establishes the Neighborhood Services Unit within the Office of the Sheriff of Baltimore City. Requires the unit and the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to partner in enforcing alcoholic beverages laws. Mandates that both entities enter into a memorandum of understanding specifying roles, responsibilities, and funding sources. Directs the unit to perform any other duties assigned by the Sheriff of Baltimore City. Expands authorized uses of certain District Court filing fee surcharges in Baltimore City to fund the unit.
responsible_party: Office of the Sheriff of Baltimore City; Board of License Commissioners of Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees in Baltimore City, the Office of the Sheriff of Baltimore City, the Board of License Commissioners of Baltimore City, and civil court filers in Baltimore City.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City expenditures may increase significantly, estimated by the city at approximately $1.1 million annually for 10 additional personnel in the Office of the Sheriff, potentially offset by reallocation of existing filing fee surcharges and city general funds. Baltimore City revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions governing civil filing fee surcharges assessed by the Chief Judge of the District Court in Baltimore City and collected by the court, expanding the permissible use of remitted surcharge revenues to fund the new Neighborhood Services Unit.

Synopsis: Subjecting certain earned wage access products to the Maryland Consumer Loan Law and other provisions that regulate entities that provide consumer credit; restricting the acceptance of tips by certain lenders under certain circumstances; providing for the licensing or registration of certain entities offering earned wage access products with certain exemptions; regulating earned wage access service agreements; limiting the costs and fees associated with obtaining an earned wage access product; etc.
Title: Commercial Law - Credit Regulation - Earned Wage Access and Credit Modernization
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 847

bill_summary: Regulates earned wage access products and subjects consumer-directed earned wage access to the Maryland Consumer Loan Law. Requires earned wage access providers to obtain a consumer loan license unless exempt. Prohibits lenders and providers from setting default tips above zero or conditioning credit on tips. Limits delivery fees to $5.00 for advances up to $75.00 and $7.50 for larger advances. Requires providers to offer at least one no-cost option and prohibits charging late fees or interest. Mandates annual reporting by providers to the Office of Financial Regulation beginning July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Earned wage access providers, consumer lenders, employers, and Maryland consumers using earned wage access or consumer credit products
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected because the bill generally codifies existing practice. The Office of Financial Regulation can handle enforcement with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1294 directly regulates earned wage access products under the Maryland Consumer Loan Law, placing licensing, reporting, and regulatory oversight under the Commissioner of Financial Regulation / Office of Financial Regulation, which is a division of the Maryland Department of Labor.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from performing groundwater augmentation except under certain circumstances; establishing the Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program to regulate and evaluate the use of treated reclaimed water as a source for groundwater augmentation through managed aquifer recharge permits; requiring the demonstration facility to address a groundwater supply or quality problem that is anticipated to occur in the next 25 years; etc.
Title: Environment - Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program - Establishment

bill_summary: Establishes the Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment. Prohibits any person from performing groundwater augmentation except under an authorized managed aquifer recharge permit. Authorizes the Department to issue at most one five-year permit under the program. Requires the Department to accept permit applications from January 2, 2026, through January 3, 2028. Mandates rigorous water treatment standards, hydrogeological investigations, and monitoring plans for permit approval. Requires annual reports from the permit holder to the Department and from the Department to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Local governments, water utilities, water treatment contractors, and property owners with drinking water wells near proposed injection sites.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally as early as fiscal 2026 to reimburse the Maryland Department of Health for water testing costs of approximately $17,000 annually, offset by matching Department of Health general fund revenues. The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the program using existing budgeted resources. Local government expenditures may increase significantly if a local jurisdiction chooses to apply for and operate the single permitted demonstration facility.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and regulating the Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program, reviewing permit applications, issuing the single pilot permit, conducting site inspections, and submitting annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

MDH's Laboratories Administration is the primary state laboratory conducting water testing for MDE, and will experience an increase in testing expenditures and reimbursable revenues associated with monitoring water quality parameters under the pilot permit.

OAG represents MDE and is statutorily tasked with prosecuting and defending water pollution control enforcement actions, administrative appeals, and criminal or civil penalties arising under Title 9, Subtitle 3 of the Environment Article.

MDE is mandated to submit comprehensive annual reports directly to the Governor on the status, scientific findings, and legislative recommendations regarding the pilot program beginning December 31, 2028.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, managed care organizations, and certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from requiring prior authorization for a transfer to a special pediatric hospital.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children’s Health Program, and Health Insurance – Transfers to Special Pediatric Hospitals – Prior Authorizations

bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children’s Health Program from requiring prior authorization for special pediatric hospital transfers. Extends this prohibition to managed care organizations, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations. Defines a special pediatric hospital as an in-state facility providing nonacute medical, rehabilitation, therapy, and palliative services. Qualifying facilities serve individuals under age 22, or ages 2 through 22 with co-occurring physical and behavioral health conditions. Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide coverage for transfers to special pediatric hospitals. Applies to all health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Pediatric patients requiring nonacute medical, rehabilitation, therapy, or palliative care; special pediatric hospitals; Medicaid and Maryland Children's Health Program enrollees; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from form filing fees. Medicaid expenditures and federal matching revenues may increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 if transfers lead to an increase in nonmedically necessary hospital days. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), both administered by MDH, prohibiting them and their managed care organizations from requiring prior authorization for transfers to special pediatric hospitals.

The bill adds § 15-861 to the Insurance Article prohibiting private insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs from requiring prior authorization for transfers to special pediatric hospitals. MIA is responsible for reviewing policy form filings and enforcing compliance across regulated health carriers.

DBM oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and was consulted regarding the applicability of the health benefit mandate, though the fiscal note confirmed no fiscal impact on the state plan.

Synopsis: Altering the Prescription Drug Repository Program, including by allowing certain entities located in another state to participate in the Program as drop-off sites and repositories, including over-the-counter drugs under the Program, and altering the individuals who are eligible to receive drugs or medical supplies under the Program; and altering the persons for whom and the activities with respect to which certain immunity is provided under the Program.
Title: Prescription Drug Repository Program - Revisions

bill_summary: Expands the Prescription Drug Repository Program to include over-the-counter drugs and allow participation by qualified out-of-state entities. Defines eligible patients as individuals who self-attest to being indigent, uninsured, underinsured, or enrolled in public health benefits. Permits the acceptance of donated drugs expiring in under 90 days if the drugs are in high demand. Authorizes repositories in the State to charge a fee up to $10 for each over-the-counter drug dispensed. Extends civil and criminal immunity to pharmacy technicians, participating entity staff, volunteers, and over-the-counter drug donors.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Indigent, uninsured, and underinsured patients; individuals enrolled in public health benefits programs; in-state and out-of-state pharmacies; health care facilities; pharmacists; pharmacy technicians
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Pharmacy special fund expenditures increase by $53,844 in FY 2026 to hire one full-time licensing specialist to register out-of-state entities, with costs rising to $69,800 by FY 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Pharmacy, which regulates and administers the Prescription Drug Repository Program, is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The department will oversee program changes, adopt revised regulations, and incur special fund expenditures to register and regulate out-of-state participating entities.

Synopsis: Altering the vaccinations that a pharmacist may administer, subject to certain requirements, to an individual of at least a certain age; and  altering the vaccinations included in the minimum package of child wellness services for which certain health insurers and nonprofit health service plans are required to provide coverage to include those recommended by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention as of December 31, 2024.

bill_summary: Specifies that federal immunization guidelines governing pharmacist vaccination authority reference standards in effect December 31, 2024, or later. Requires pharmacist certification courses to cover federal immunization guidelines in effect on December 31, 2024. Expands required child wellness insurance coverage to include immunizations recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics as of December 31, 2024. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to adopt regulations consistent with specified federal guidance. Applies insurance coverage requirements to policies and contracts issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and insured children and adolescents
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from rate and form filing fees; form reviews can be handled with existing budgeted resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1315 directly amends the Insurance Article regarding mandated health insurance coverage for child wellness immunizations. The Maryland Insurance Administration is authorized to adopt implementing regulations and will experience a minimal special fund revenue increase from reviewing policy form filings.

The bill amends the Health Occupations Article governing pharmacist vaccination protocols, credentialing, training criteria, and reporting to the ImmuNet program, all of which fall under the regulatory purview of the Maryland Department of Health and its health occupations licensing boards (including the State Board of Pharmacy).

As the agency managing the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Plan, DBM monitors health insurance benefit mandates and coverage requirements, though the fiscal note indicates no significant expenditure impact on the State plan.

Title: Natural Resources - Vessels - Carbon Monoxide Warning Labels (Matthew's Law)

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from operating certain gasoline-powered vessels on waters of the State without carbon monoxide warning labels. Applies to vessels manufactured after July 31, 2007, that feature accommodation spaces, swim platforms, or aft lounging areas. Requires warning labels affixed in conspicuous locations in the vicinity of both the transom and the helm. Prohibits the Department of Natural Resources from imposing a penalty on any person who violates the requirement. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: operators and owners of gasoline-powered vessels manufactured after July 31, 2007, with accommodation spaces, swim platforms, or aft lounging areas
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the State Boat Act under the Natural Resources Article, establishing requirements for carbon monoxide warning labels on certain vessels operating on State waters and specifically barring the Department of Natural Resources from imposing penalties for violations.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Garrett County Commissioners or county employees to execute certain contracts without advertising for bids. Applies to purchase or work project contracts for indeterminate goods or services procured on an as-needed basis. Permits these as-needed contracts without bid advertisements regardless of whether cumulative costs exceed $50,000. Authorizes contracts for purchasing one or more vehicles up to $100,000 without advertising for bids. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Garrett County Commissioners
stakeholders: Garrett County government, county procurement personnel, and vendors providing vehicles, goods, or services to Garrett County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Garrett County may experience minimal cost savings from reduced newspaper advertising requirements and improved operational procurement efficiency.

bill_summary: Establishes a rural special event venue beer, wine, and liquor license in Caroline County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Caroline County to issue the license to qualified venue owners. Permits license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption during county-established hours. Sets tiered annual license fees ranging from $250 for up to 10 events to $1,000 for 40 events. Authorizes multiple event license holders to store alcoholic beverages on licensed premises between events in a secured location.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Caroline County
stakeholders: owners of rural special event venues and holders of multiple event licenses in Caroline County
fiscal_impact_summary: Caroline County revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent new licenses are issued. The county can absorb any enforcement activity with existing resources. State finances are unaffected, and specific local revenue estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references authorized personnel of the Comptroller having inspection authority over the alcoholic beverage inventory records and premises of multiple event license holders in Caroline County.

Synopsis: Exempting personal property used in connection with certain large family child care homes from valuation and taxation in Anne Arundel County; authorizing the governing body of Anne Arundel County or the governing body of a municipal corporation in Anne Arundel County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the real property tax owed on the portion of real property used for certain child care centers and day care centers; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax - Day Care Centers and Child Care Centers

bill_summary: Exempts personal property used in connection with certain registered large family child care homes from valuation and taxation in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes Anne Arundel County and municipal corporations in the county to grant a property tax credit for employer-provided child care centers. Requires qualifying employer-owned properties to belong to businesses having at least 25 employees. Authorizes a local property tax credit for property dedicated exclusively to certain child care or adult day care centers. Caps both optional annual property tax credits at the lesser of $10,000 or the property tax attributable to the space.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Anne Arundel County; Municipal corporations in Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Operators of large family child care homes, child care centers, and adult day care centers in Anne Arundel County; businesses with at least 25 employees in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local property tax revenues in Anne Arundel County and its municipalities decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 from the personal property tax exemption and to the extent local credits are granted. Local government expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes registered or licensed under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, which is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (Division of Early Childhood). MSDE also tracked and provided data on licensed child care providers for the fiscal note.

The bill establishes local property tax credit eligibility referencing day care centers for the elderly and day care centers for adults licensed under Title 14 of the Health - General Article, which are regulated by the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services to conduct an assessment of facilities owned by the State and operated by the 16 State agencies the Department supports to evaluate whether the facility or a portion of the facility would be suitable to lease to a child care center;  requiring the Department to report to the General Assembly the results of the assessment and a description of whether each facility is suitable to lease to a child care center by December 1, 2026; and requiring the report to be published on the Department's website.
Title: Department of General Services - Assessment of State-Owned Facilities - Child Care Centers

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to assess certain State-owned facilities for potential child care center leases. Covers all facilities owned by the State and operated by the 16 State agencies supported by the department. Evaluates whether each facility or a portion of it is suitable and available to lease to a child care center. Requires the department to report its findings and facility inventory to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Mandates publication of the report on the department's website. Takes effect July 1, 2025, and terminates June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: Child care center operators, Maryland families seeking child care services, and the 16 State agencies whose facilities are evaluated
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $96,000 in FY 2026 and $35,500 in FY 2027 for a contractual program manager to conduct facility reviews and site visits before terminating on December 1, 2026. State revenues are not affected. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of General Services to conduct an assessment of state-owned facilities across 16 supported agencies to evaluate their suitability and availability for child care center leasing, prepare an inventory, and submit and publish a final report by December 1, 2026, resulting in direct operational and fiscal impacts on the agency.

The bill references child care center standards governed under the Education Article, and the Department of General Services will collaborate with the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)—which licenses child care facilities—to evaluate physical plant standards and suitability.

Synopsis: Providing that a cannabis agent who is employed to provide security services for a cannabis licensee or cannabis registrant as a security guard or by a security guard agency is not required to obtain a State or national criminal history records check if the cannabis agent is authorized to provide security guard services; altering the definition of "security guard employer" for purposes of certain provisions of law to exclude video lottery facilities, sports wagering facility licensees, and health care facilities; etc.
Title: Security Guards and Security Guard Employers - Registration, Certification, and Regulation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Exempts certain cannabis agents providing security services from obtaining a State and national criminal history records check. Applies the exemption when the agent is authorized to provide security guard services under State law. Excludes video lottery operators, sports wagering facility licensees, and health care facilities from the definition of security guard employer. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Department of State Police
stakeholders: Cannabis agents providing security services, cannabis licensees and registrants, video lottery operators, sports wagering facility licensees, health care facilities, and security guards
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2026 for one-time information technology updates to the Department of State Police application portal. General fund revenues, special fund revenues, and special fund expenditures decrease by indeterminate, likely minimal amounts annually beginning in FY 2026 due to forgone certification and background check fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State Police is responsible for licensing security guard agencies and certifying security guards under Title 19 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article. The bill directly impacts MSP operations by requiring a $75,000 IT upgrade to its online application portal and reducing certification fee revenues.

The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article governing the registration of cannabis agents, exempting security guards authorized under Title 19 from duplicate criminal history records checks when registering with MCA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), which conducts State and national criminal history records checks. The bill's exemptions will result in fewer background checks processed, decreasing special fund revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the definition of security guard employer to exclude video lottery operators and sports wagering facility licensees, entities whose employees are regulated and licensed by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission.

The bill excludes health care facilities (as defined under § 19-114 of the Health - General Article, which are regulated by MDH) from the definition of security guard employers under Title 19 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article.

Synopsis: Altering the providers of certain community-based health services that a carrier is prohibited from rejecting for participation on the carrier's provider panel; and altering the period of time in which certain carriers are required to accept or deny certain social workers, counselors, and psychology associates for participation on the carrier's provider panel to within 60 days after the date a carrier receives a completed application.
Title: Health Insurance - Provider Panels - Credentialing for Behavioral Health Care Professionals

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Shortens the deadline for health insurance carriers to decide on credentialing applications for certain behavioral health care professionals. Requires carriers to accept or reject qualifying behavioral health providers within 60 days after receiving a completed application. Applies this timeline when a carrier provides notice of intent to continue processing the application. Covers specified community-based providers, licensed certified social workers-clinical, and licensed clinical professional counselors. Removes licensed graduate social workers from the list of community-based providers that carriers cannot reject based on license. Subjects noncompliant carriers to existing administrative penalties and enforcement sanctions.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, behavioral health care professionals (including licensed master social workers, licensed certified social workers-clinical, licensed clinical professional counselors, graduate counselors and therapists, and registered psychology associates), and accredited community-based behavioral health programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive effect on State activities, operations, revenues, or expenditures. Local government finances and operations are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers in the state. This bill directly amends the Insurance Article by modifying credentialing requirements and timelines for carriers' provider panels, with noncompliance subject to MIA enforcement and administrative penalties.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees behavioral health programs accredited under COMAR 10.63.02 and houses the health occupations boards that license the specific behavioral health practitioners (social workers, counselors, and psychology associates) referenced in the bill.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations are required to provide coverage for medically appropriate and necessary hearing aids for adults to require coverage if the hearing aid is ordered, fitted, and dispensed by a licensed hearing aid dispenser.
Title: Health Insurance - Required Coverage - Hearing Aids

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Expands mandated health insurance coverage for adult hearing aids. Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover adult hearing aids under expanded circumstances. Mandates coverage when hearing aids are ordered, fitted, and dispensed by a licensed hearing aid dispenser. Authorizes carriers to limit benefits to $1,400 per hearing aid for each ear every 36 months. Allows insured individuals to purchase higher-priced hearing aids by paying the cost difference. Applies to all policies, contracts, and plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Adult health insurance policyholders needing hearing aids; licensed hearing aid dispensers; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues from $125 rate and form filing fees in FY 2026 only. No impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs in Maryland. It will review revised policy forms and contracts to enforce the expanded hearing aid coverage requirement and collect associated rate and form filing fees.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. While the fiscal note anticipates no fiscal impact on the State plan, DBM was consulted regarding benefit design and state health plan compliance.
MHBE administers Maryland's health insurance marketplace, where qualified health plans must comply with State benchmark plans and mandated health benefits, including hearing aid coverage.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ODHH promotes the welfare of Deaf and hard of hearing Maryland residents and coordinates policy initiatives to improve accessibility and access to hearing-related services and devices.

Synopsis: Establishing a civil penalty not exceeding $50,000 for a person who falsifies information that is submitted in a report of the results of lead-contaminated dust testing or visual inspection of an affected property.
Title: Lead Testing and Inspections - Falsifying Information - Penalty

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes a civil penalty not exceeding $50,000 for falsifying information submitted in lead testing or inspection reports. Applies the penalty to verified reports of lead-contaminated dust testing or visual inspections. Requires collection of the civil penalty in a civil action. Specifies that each day a violation occurs constitutes a separate violation. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Accredited lead paint inspectors, testing personnel, rental property owners, and tenants of affected properties
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund special fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2026 from civil penalties assessed under the bill. No direct, material effect on State expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE administers the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program under Title 6, Subtitle 8 of the Environment Article. The bill establishes civil penalties for falsifying lead inspection and testing reports submitted to MDE, with collected penalties supporting the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund.
The Office of the Attorney General represents MDE in legal matters and would be responsible for pursuing civil enforcement actions to collect the civil penalties established under the bill.
The bill establishes that penalties are to be collected in a civil action, which falls under the jurisdiction of the state court system administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Motor Vehicle Administration to enter into an agreement to facilitate the issuance, use, and verification of electronic credentials through a national association of motor vehicle agencies; and authorizing an individual who will operate a rented vehicle to use a certain electronic credential showing a representation of a valid driver's license, instead of a driver's license, to rent the vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Driver's Licenses - Electronic Credentials (Maryland Mobile ID Enhancement Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to enter into agreements through a national association of motor vehicle agencies. These agreements facilitate the issuance, use, and verification of electronic credentials issued by Maryland or another state. Authorizes individuals to use qualifying electronic credentials showing a valid driver's license to rent vehicles, trailers, or semitrailers. Allows nonresidents to use electronic credentials if their home state has entered into a facilitation agreement with the Administration. Authorizes vehicle rental lessors to inspect and verify electronic credentials through electronic or digital means.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Vehicle rental businesses, Maryland drivers holding electronic credentials, and nonresident vehicle renters
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on Transportation Trust Fund revenues or expenditures. The Motor Vehicle Administration can enter into facilitation agreements using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is directly authorized by the bill to enter into agreements with a national association of motor vehicle agencies to facilitate the issuance, use, and verification of electronic credentials (mobile IDs) and oversee the credential standards used for vehicle rentals.

As the parent cabinet department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees transportation policy, statutes within the Transportation Article, and the Transportation Trust Fund through which MVA operations are supported.

Synopsis: Authorizing a tow truck to display a portable variable messaging sign mounted on the tow truck while at the scene of a crash or a disabled vehicle; and requiring the portable variable messaging sign to conform to the standards established in the manual on uniform traffic control devices adopted by the State Highway Administration and display only messages approved by the Administration.
Title: Vehicle Equipment - Portable Variable Messaging Signs - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a tow truck to display a mounted portable variable messaging sign at a crash scene or disabled vehicle. Requires the sign to conform to standards in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices. Requires the sign to display only messages approved for use by the State Highway Administration. Restricts tow trucks to displaying portable variable messaging signs only in accordance with these statutory requirements. Establishes an effective date of October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Tow truck operators, private towing businesses, and motorists
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct fiscal impact on State or local revenues or expenditures because the authorization is permissive. Expenditures increase only if State or local agencies choose to purchase equipped tow trucks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the State Highway Administration with establishing standards for the portable variable messaging signs through the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and approving the specific messages authorized for use on tow trucks.

MDOT is the principal department overseeing the state's transportation network and governing modal administrations directly impacted by the bill, including the State Highway Administration and the Maryland Transportation Authority.

MDTA operates toll facilities, patrols roadways, and manages incident response and towing equipment; the fiscal note highlights potential expenditure impacts should MDTA elect to procure tow trucks equipped with these variable messaging signs.
The MVA administers vehicle equipment standards and regulations under the Maryland Vehicle Law amended by this legislation, including authorizations regarding vehicle lighting and signaling devices.

MSP is the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing traffic safety and vehicle equipment laws on Maryland highways, including the proper use and display of authorized lighting and message signs.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to the award of noneconomic damages to a claimant in an action for child sexual abuse; altering certain provisions relating to the liability of the State under the Maryland Tort Claims Act and of a local government under the Local Government Tort Claims Act for certain claims of child sexual abuse; and requiring the Maryland Judiciary to report to the General Assembly by January 31, 2027, and each year thereafter, on the amount of each award and a summary of the sexual abuse claims related to the award.
Title: Civil Actions - Child Sexual Abuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Lowers noneconomic damages caps to $700,000 for previously time-barred child sexual abuse actions filed beginning June 1, 2025. Limits State, local government, and school board liability to $400,000 per claimant for those actions. Alters sovereign immunity protections and mandatory liability insurance minimums for county boards of education. Prohibits filing previously time-barred child sexual abuse claims against the State on or after January 1, 2026. Prohibits counsel from charging or receiving fees exceeding 20% of a settlement or 25% of a judgment.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Supreme Court of Maryland; State Board of Education; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Victims and claimants of child sexual abuse, attorneys representing claimants, the State of Maryland, local governments, and county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures decrease, potentially significantly, due to reduced liability limits for previously time-barred child sexual abuse claims and a filing deadline on claims against the State. Specific dollar estimates cannot be reliably determined in advance. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Judiciary with an annual reporting requirement to the General Assembly detailing each award made under the Act and a summary of underlying claims, and authorizes the Supreme Court of Maryland to adopt rules implementing the Act.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, which covers tort liabilities under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA). The bill alters MTCA liability limits and sets filing deadlines for child sexual abuse claims against the State, directly impacting state liabilities and fund expenditures.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State and its agencies in civil litigation, including hundreds of pending complaints and thousands of potential claims under the Child Victims Act subject to the bill's altered liability caps and limitations.

The bill amends § 4-105 of the Education Article, requiring the State Board of Education to maintain standards for comprehensive liability insurance coverage for county boards of education aligned with the altered statutory liability limits.

Under the amended provisions of Education Article § 4-105, county boards of education that elect to self-insure against liability must comply with rules, regulations, and approvals set by the State Insurance Commissioner.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health, in coordination with the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems, to adopt regulations establishing minimum perinatal care standards for hospitals that meet or exceed the Maryland Perinatal System Standards for each hospital that provides obstetrical services; and requiring each hospital that provides obstetrical services and freestanding birthing centers, as a condition of licensure, to comply with certain minimum perinatal care standards.
Title: Health Care Facilities - Hospitals and Freestanding Birthing Centers - Perinatal Care Standards

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing minimum perinatal care standards. Mandates coordination with the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to develop the regulations. Directs that the standards meet or exceed the Maryland Perinatal System Standards. Applies these standards to each hospital providing obstetrical services and to freestanding birthing centers. Requires covered facilities to comply with the established standards as a condition of licensure. Sets an adoption deadline for the regulations of October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
stakeholders: hospitals providing obstetrical services, freestanding birthing centers, and perinatal patients
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing minimum perinatal care standards for hospitals offering obstetrical services and freestanding birthing centers, and to enforce compliance as a condition of licensure.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Department of Health coordinate directly with MIEMSS in adopting the required regulations establishing minimum perinatal care standards.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law relating to the delivery of alcoholic beverages in Howard County to a holder or an employee of a holder of a Class D license.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class D Licenses - Delivery

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes holders of Class D alcoholic beverages licenses and their employees to deliver alcoholic beverages within Howard County. Applies existing delivery requirements for Class A license holders to Class D licensees. Requires both the deliverer and the recipient to endorse a board-approved certification form upon delivery. Mandates that the purchaser or a designated recipient at least 21 years old be physically present at delivery. Prohibits delivery unless the purchaser pays for the alcoholic beverages at the time of the order.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: holders of Class D alcoholic beverages licenses and their employees in Howard County, and retail alcohol consumers in Howard County
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, and Howard County finances and operations are not materially affected. Small businesses with a Class D license may experience increased sales and revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the regulation and taxation of the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local Class D delivery privileges administered by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates generally to the state's broader alcoholic beverage statutory framework.

Synopsis: Renaming the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund to be the Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund; authorizing funds appropriated to the Catastrophic Event Account to be expended to assist in funding costs connected to a relocation, closure, or mass layoff of a unit of the federal government; establishing the Expedited Hiring Program in the Department of Budget and Management; authorizing an appointing authority to recruit for certain vacant positions in State government; etc.
Title: Support and Protections for Individuals Affected by Federal Actions (Protect Our Federal Workers Act)
