Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Expands the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund to aid former federal employees. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Labor to provide no-interest loans and forgive loans to eligible residents facing financial hardship. Expands the Attorney General's authority to bring legal actions protecting residents from adverse federal actions and federal benefit denials. Increases the Governor's mandated annual budget appropriation to the Attorney General from $1,000,000 to at least $2,500,000. Establishes an Expedited Hiring Program within the Department of Budget and Management to recruit former federal workers for State positions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Budget and Management; Office of the Attorney General; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Current and former federal employees and federal contractors residing in Maryland, and State appointing authorities seeking to fill vacancies
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $7.0 million in FY 2025 and $28.0 million in FY 2026, offset by special fund revenues of $6.5 million in FY 2025 and $10.0 million in FY 2026 from fund transfers. General fund expenditures increase by $1.7 million in FY 2026 for loan administration and $1.5 million annually beginning in FY 2027 for a mandated appropriation increase to the Office of the Attorney General.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary administrator of the renamed Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund (FGEALF), responsible for setting loan criteria, issuing no-interest loans, determining financial hardship, processing loan forgiveness, receiving tax verification data, and completing a study and report on federal worker foreclosure activity.

DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account, which has its funding and usage expanded by the bill, and is charged with establishing and administering the new Expedited Hiring Program for former federal employees filling State Personnel Management System vacancies.

The bill expands the Attorney General's legal authority under the Maryland Defense Act to investigate and initiate litigation regarding adverse federal actions against Maryland residents and increases OAG's statutory mandated appropriation from $1.0 million to at least $2.5 million annually.

The Governor is authorized to execute fund transfers from the Catastrophic Event Account and the Revenue Stabilization Account, is mandated to include increased funding for OAG in the annual budget, and retains statutory review and objection rights regarding OAG lawsuits brought under the Maryland Defense Act.

The Comptroller is statutorily authorized to disclose taxpayer information to MD Labor to administer FGEALF and prevent fraud, and is responsible for accounting for the Catastrophic Event Account and FGEALF.
The Treasurer is statutorily required to hold separately and invest the moneys of the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring circuit courthouses in the State, constructed or renovated on or after October 1, 2025, to maintain on its premises a private lactation room to be used by certain individuals; providing that breast-feeding mothers and certain individuals caring for children under 3 years old may be excused from jury service; and requiring the Maryland Judiciary to collect certain information on jury service excusals and report annually to the Maryland General Assembly beginning by December 31, 2025.
Title: Courts - Parental Accommodations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: Requires circuit courthouses constructed or undergoing major renovations on or after October 1, 2025, to maintain a private lactation room. Specifies the lactation room must include an electrical outlet, a locking door, a sink, and a refrigerator. Authorizes jury judges and jury commissioners to excuse breast-feeding mothers from jury service. Authorizes excusing individuals with legal custody of a child under age three requiring continuous care during court hours. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to report annual data to the General Assembly regarding jury duty excusal requests.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Breastfeeding mothers, primary caregivers of children under age three summoned for jury duty, circuit court employees, courthouse visitors, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $44,844 in fiscal 2026 only for one-time Judiciary form revisions and reporting system updates. Local government expenditures may increase to install compliant lactation rooms in circuit courthouses undergoing new construction or major renovations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary, supported centrally by the Administrative Office of the Courts. It establishes new parental and breastfeeding excusal provisions for jury service and requires the Judiciary to update juror qualification forms, track excusal determinations, and submit an annual reporting metric to the General Assembly, resulting in general fund expenditures of $44,844 in FY 2026.

Synopsis: Requiring the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland to report annually by November 1 to the General Assembly on the Truancy Reduction Pilot Program; and requiring the report to include the number of Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs established in State, the number of participants in each pilot program; information on the outcomes of the participants in each program, and recommendations to improve the function of the current program.
Title: Juveniles - Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs - Report
bill_summary: Alters the contents of the annual report on Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs submitted to the General Assembly. Requires the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland to include the number of established programs. Mandates the reporting of participant counts and participant outcome information for each program. Directs the Chief Justice to provide recommendations to improve the function of current programs. Terminates the expanded reporting requirements on December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Juveniles participating in Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs, public school systems in participating jurisdictions, and the Maryland Judiciary
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Judiciary can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirements for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland regarding Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs (TRPPs). The Administrative Office of the Courts is the operational agency supporting the Maryland Judicial Branch and collects the case management data necessary to compile this report.

Synopsis: Authorizing counties and municipalities to grant a preference in hiring and promotion to eligible veterans, spouses of an eligible service member, spouses of certain eligible veterans and eligible service members, and surviving spouses of deceased eligible veterans; and authorizing counties and municipalities to adopt a local law that allows for the application of a certain credit on a selection test for eligible spouses, eligible veterans, and certain spouses and surviving spouses.
Title: Local Government - Hiring and Promotion Preferences for Veterans and Spouses of Service Members and Veterans (Families Serve Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to grant hiring and promotion preferences to eligible veterans and qualifying spouses. Covers spouses of active-duty service members, spouses of disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of deceased veterans. Permits local governments to adopt local laws awarding 10 credit points on employee selection tests to eligible individuals. Allows an additional two credit points on selection tests for former prisoners of war. Excludes current local government employees and veterans convicted of post-discharge crimes from receiving selection test credits. Clarifies that granting these employment preferences does not violate State or local equal employment opportunity laws.
responsible_party: County and municipal governments
stakeholders: Eligible veterans, spouses of active-duty service members, spouses of veterans with service-connected disabilities, surviving spouses of deceased eligible veterans, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill provides permissive authority for counties and municipalities to award discretionary preferences and test credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts the 'Families Serve Act,' authorizing local governments to establish hiring, promotion, and testing preferences for eligible veterans, active duty spouses, and surviving spouses, aligning directly with the department's mission to advocate for and support veterans and military families.

The bill amends the Maryland Labor and Employment Article (§ 3-714) regarding employer hiring and promotion preferences, which falls within the statutory scope of labor standards overseen by MD Labor.

The bill explicitly provides that granting the authorized hiring and promotion preferences does not violate State or local equal employment opportunity laws, which are enforced by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill incorporates statutory definitions from the State Personnel Management System administered by DBM, though the operational application is restricted entirely to local governments without impacting state personnel.

Synopsis: Establishing an alternative registration process for rental fleet vehicles; requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue distinctive registration plates for rental vehicles registered under the alternative process; and requiring, in addition to an annual registration fee, the owner of a registered rental vehicle to pay a one-time initial registration fee not to exceed $8.50 when the new registration plates are issued.

bill_summary: Establishes an alternative registration process for owners of fleets of five or more rental vehicles. Authorizes eligible fleet owners to register any fleet vehicle under the new process or under existing law. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue distinctive fleet vehicle registration plates for these vehicles. Prohibits the Administration from requiring the attachment, display, or issuance of a validation tab. Requires fleet vehicle registrations to expire on the same date to the extent practicable. Local operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to implement the alternative registration process for rental fleet vehicles, issue distinctive 'Fleet Vehicle' registration plates, eliminate validation tab requirements for these vehicles, and collect the associated registration fees.

The MVA is a modal unit within the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), and the bill directly affects Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures for producing and issuing the new fleet plates.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transportation Authority to establish an installment payment plan program for unpaid video tolls and civil penalties. Authorizes a person who accumulates at least $300 in unpaid video tolls and civil penalties to apply for the program. Directs the Authority to adopt regulations establishing eligibility, payment options, application procedures, and default reporting processes. Authorizes the Authority to refer unpaid amounts to the Central Collection Unit if a person defaults on an approved plan. Expands the Authority's power to recall delinquent toll accounts from the Central Collection Unit.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners with unpaid video tolls and civil penalties
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations because the Maryland Transportation Authority is already implementing a similar program and does not plan to modify its debt recall practices. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDTA is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing the video toll installment payment plan program, adopting regulations, processing applications, and managing referrals to and recalls from the Central Collection Unit.

DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which receives delinquent toll accounts when participants fail to pay according to their installment payment plans and handles account recalls initiated by MDTA.
The MVA is notified by MDTA if a person fails to pay outstanding video tolls or fulfill the terms of an approved installment plan, leading to potential vehicle registration suspension or refusal.
MDOT oversees state transportation administration, including modal administrations like the MVA which are notified regarding vehicle registration actions related to delinquent toll violations.

bill_summary: Requires local legislative bodies to adopt local laws authorizing accessory dwelling unit development by October 1, 2026. Applies to land with a single-family detached dwelling unit as the primary dwelling. Prohibits local laws from establishing setbacks exceeding existing accessory structure setback requirements from lot lines. Excludes accessory dwelling units from residential growth limits and density calculations. Prohibits private land use restrictions from unreasonably limiting the development or rental of accessory dwelling units. Authorizes homeowners association governing bodies to treat accessory dwelling units as separate lots for voting and assessments.
responsible_party: County and Municipal Legislative Bodies; Maryland Historical Trust
stakeholders: Single-family residential property owners, homeowners associations, tenants, local governments, and residential building contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances. Local government expenditures and revenues may experience an indeterminate net impact from adopting local laws, completing required parking studies, and processing accessory dwelling unit permits and associated fee revenues; specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the state's Land Use Article and statewide land use policies regarding local zoning for accessory dwelling units (ADUs). Furthermore, the bill explicitly exempts historic properties listed in or determined eligible by the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is administered within the Department of Planning.

The bill establishes an official state policy to encourage and facilitate the creation of accessory dwelling units to address statewide housing supply and affordability needs, directly intersecting with the department's mission to advance safe and accessible housing.

The bill amends the Real Property Article to invalidate certain restrictive covenants and homeowners association rules that unreasonably restrict ADU development, areas subject to legal interpretation and consumer protection oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring interest earnings on money deposited for a certain taxing and assessment district to be credited to that district; specifying that a certain provision of law governing the petition process for the construction of an erosion prevention project or erosion control project in a certain district in Anne Arundel County does not apply to certain planning, permitting, or cost estimate activities; authorizing certain entities to use tax funds for upkeep or reconstruction of an existing shore erosion control project; etc.

Authorizes entities administering shore erosion control districts statewide to use tax funds to maintain, repair, or restore existing projects. Requires administering entities to conduct a public hearing before using tax funds for project maintenance, repair, or restoration. fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. The Maryland Department of Planning provided information on the bill given its advisory and data role in local comprehensive land use planning and coastal resource management.

Under the statute amended by the bill (§ 8-1815.1), the Critical Area Commission chair may refer enforcement matters to the Office of the Attorney General to initiate legal actions to restrain violations or seek replanting damages.

bill_summary: Expands State equal access requirements to include individuals with disabilities alongside individuals with limited English proficiency. Requires specified State departments, agencies, and programs to develop and biennially update a comprehensive language access plan. Lowers the population threshold triggering mandatory translation of vital documents from 3% to 0.5% statewide. Establishes the Maryland Language Advisory Group, jointly staffed by the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs and Department of Disabilities. Directs the advisory group to develop template plans and recommend an agency for ongoing oversight and enforcement. Sets a full implementation deadline of July 1, 2028, for covered departments and agencies.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs; Maryland Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: Individuals with limited English proficiency; individuals with disabilities; Maryland State departments, agencies, and programs; translation and interpretation service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $56,000 in FY 2026 for the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs to staff the advisory group. Beginning in FY 2027, total State expenditures across affected agencies increase significantly, anticipated to exceed $1.5 million annually for translation services, staffing, and document updates. Department of Human Services may realize an increase in matching federal fund revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) is tasked with co-convening, co-chairing, and sharing staffing responsibilities for the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and is directly involved in developing language access templates and compliance frameworks.

The Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs (an agency within the Executive Department) is mandated to co-convene, co-chair, and staff the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and receives general fund appropriations to support these operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of ODHH is a designated statutory member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group and must be consulted regarding language access and communication accommodations for deaf and hard of hearing individuals.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a designated member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and MSDE is specifically named to achieve full implementation by July 1, 2028, with anticipated costs up to $125,000 annually for translation services.

The Secretary of Human Services is a statutory member of the Advisory Group and collaborates with the OAG to select five independent agencies to comply with the bill. DHS also anticipates substantial system updates and translation costs exceeding $250,000.

The Secretary of Health is a statutory member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and MDH is subject to full implementation as a principal department, with specific vital document exemptions referenced for its health occupations.
The Secretary of Labor is a statutory member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and MD Labor must implement a language access plan and translation of vital documents as a principal department.
The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the Advisory Group, and DoIT is projected to incur $50,000 annually to procure translation and IT communication services.

The OAG is explicitly named to fully implement the bill by July 1, 2028, collaborates with DHS to designate five independent entities, and anticipates annual translation expenditures of at least $25,000.

DSP is explicitly designated to fully implement the bill by July 1, 2028, estimating a potential need for five administrative positions and significant translation costs for public contact, documents, and web services.

MCCR is specifically named to achieve full compliance with language access plans, vital document translations, and annual reporting by July 1, 2028, expecting potentially significant translation costs.
MTA is specifically required to achieve full implementation by July 1, 2028, and anticipates contractual expenses for reporting, assessments, and translation specialists.
WCC is specifically named in the statute to achieve full implementation by July 1, 2028, requiring adoption of a language access plan, document translation, and annual reporting.
The Comptroller is specifically required to fully implement language access plans, document translations, and reporting by July 1, 2028.
As a principal department and the parent agency of MTA and MVA, MDOT is subject to full implementation requirements and reporting under the bill.
MVA is highlighted in the fiscal note regarding required language access plan upgrades, driver licensing translation offerings, and public-facing contact services.
MDoA is a principal department that must comply with language access requirements by July 1, 2028, and is noted in the fiscal note as incurring contractual and printing expenses.
Commerce must comply as a principal department by July 1, 2028, and anticipates ongoing translation expenditures of $14,000 annually plus one-time supply costs.
DNR is a principal department mandated to implement the bill by July 1, 2028, and notes the potential need for an additional staff member and expanded translation contracts.
MDE is required to comply as a principal department by July 1, 2028, and anticipates needing an administrative staff person and translation funds.
MDP must comply as a principal department and anticipates needing additional personnel and resources to translate vital documents and provide in-person public interpretation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory advisory body, the Maryland Language Advisory Group, with authority to convene workgroups and establish statewide language access templates and policies.

MDEM is a principal department subject to the 2028 implementation mandate, and the bill explicitly includes 'emergency preparedness and risk communications' in the definition of vital documents requiring translation.
DBM is an information source and the state's budget and personnel agency responsible for overseeing expenditures and staffing additions requested by affected agencies.
As a principal department under SG § 8-201, MDA must fully implement a language access plan, translate vital documents, and report annually by July 1, 2028.
As a principal department under SG § 8-201, DGS is mandated to comply with the language access and vital documents translation requirements by July 1, 2028.
DHCD is a principal department that must comply with language access requirements by July 1, 2028, including translating benefit eligibility and housing application documents.
DJS is required to implement the language access plan and document translation provisions by July 1, 2028, as a principal department under SG § 8-201.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a principal department subject to the requirement to establish a language access plan, translate vital documents, and report annually by July 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is a principal department under SG § 8-201 required to adopt a language access plan and fulfill the bill's translation requirements by July 1, 2028.
DVMF is a principal department required to establish language access plans and provide translation for veterans' benefits materials and services by July 1, 2028.

Authorizes qualifying out-of-state licensed professional counselors to provide telehealth counseling services in Maryland. Restricts practice to out-of-state students attending higher education institutions who share an existing six-month therapeutic relationship. responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
stakeholders: out-of-state licensed professional counselors and out-of-state students enrolled at Maryland institutions of higher education
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Any special fund revenue impact from temporary telehealth license application fees is assumed to be minimal. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the Department and the Board by requiring them to establish and administer a temporary telehealth licensing process, adopt implementing regulations, and collect application fees.

The bill directly affects mental health service access for out-of-state students enrolled and residing at institutions within the University System of Maryland by allowing their existing out-of-state counselors to provide temporary telehealth services.

responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Howard County

fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in Howard County license revenues depending on the number of Class MT licenses issued and the annual fee established by the Board. Local enforcement and administration can be handled with existing resources. No effect on state finances.

While this bill is administered locally by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages within the state.

bill_summary: Establishes paid family and medical leave benefits at regular pay for all Executive Branch employees, including temporary employees. Authorizes covered employees to request up to 12 weeks of paid leave beginning July 1, 2026. Permits an additional 12 weeks of leave for employees with specified qualifying conditions in the same application year. Repeals existing statutory provisions governing paid parental leave for Executive Branch employees. Requires the Secretary of Budget and Management and higher education governing bodies to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; governing bodies of public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: Executive Branch employees, including temporary employees, of all State units and public institutions of higher education
fiscal_impact_summary: Net state fiscal impact is indeterminate. State expenditures decrease significantly in FY 2026 from avoiding FAMLI employer contributions (estimated annual savings exceeding $35 million in total funds), with an offsetting decline in FAMLI special fund revenues. Beginning in FY 2027, ongoing contribution savings are offset by increased expenditures across all funds to provide and administer fully paid leave. FAMLI special fund expenditures also decrease as FAMLI will not pay benefits to State employees. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM requested this departmental legislation and is the primary implementing agency. The Secretary of Budget and Management is tasked with adopting regulations, administering the new Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) benefits for Executive Branch employees, and reporting employee wage and hour information.

MD Labor administers the statewide Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. Under the bill, quarterly informational wage and hour reports must be filed with MD Labor, appeals of leave denials are adjudicated under FAMLI appeal procedures established by the Secretary of Labor, and the FAMLI Fund experiences significant reductions in special fund revenues and expenditures.
The bill explicitly mandates that the governing body of a public institution of higher education adopt regulations governing PFML benefits, conditions, and procedures for its employees.

As an independent public institution of higher education operating outside the University System of Maryland, its governing body is directly required by the bill to adopt regulations governing PFML benefits for its employees.
As an independent public higher education institution with its own governing board, it is required under the bill to adopt regulations governing PFML benefits for its personnel.

MDOT operates an independent personnel system within the Executive Branch whose workforce is directly covered under the bill's provisions, and the agency provided operational and fiscal input on the measure.

Synopsis: Requiring that notice of the destruction of medical records be provided by first-class mail or by e-mail, rather than by both methods; and providing that if notice is provided by e-mail and no response or delivery receipt is obtained from the e-mail address to which notice was provided, the health care provider shall provide notice via first-class mail at least 10 days before the date on which the record is to be destroyed.

Mandates that this follow-up mail notice occur at least 10 days before the record is destroyed. Applies to notices sent to adult patients or parents and guardians of minor patients. fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1510 amends the Health - General Article regarding medical record retention and notice requirements for destruction by health care providers and facilities, which are regulated by the Maryland Department of Health.

bill_summary: Exempts passive trusts that acquire or are assigned mortgage loans from mortgage lender and installment loan licensing requirements. Exempts trusts established by corporate instrumentalities of the federal government to acquire mortgage loans from mortgage lender licensing. Defines a passive trust as a trust that does not make, broker, or service mortgage loans. Establishes the Maryland Licensing Workgroup to study licensing and registration requirements for financial services providers. Requires the workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: passive trusts acquiring mortgage loans, secondary mortgage market participants, corporate instrumentalities of the federal government, mortgage lenders, and Maryland consumer borrowers
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate net impact on special fund revenues and expenditures for the Office of Financial Regulation due to foregone licensing fees and reduced regulatory costs from exempting passive trusts. The bill clarifies licensing exemptions for passive trusts and federal instrumentality trusts, affects OFR special fund revenues and expenditures, and tasks the Commissioner of Financial Regulation with chairing and staffing the Maryland Licensing Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Maryland Licensing Workgroup, a temporary advisory task force established to study financial service licensing requirements and report findings and recommendations by December 31, 2025.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the Maryland Licensing Workgroup and receiving the workgroup's final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting candidates for appointment to the newly established Maryland Licensing Workgroup.

bill_summary: Amends prior authorizations of State debt across multiple previous capital budgets. Modifies authorized purposes, changes project grantees, and reallocates capital grant funds. Extends deadlines for expending or encumbering grant funds, in many instances through June 1, 2032. Removes matching fund requirements for select local and community projects. Affects capital grants for community centers, healthcare facilities, schools, and cultural institutions statewide.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of General Services
stakeholders: Grant recipients of prior State debt authorizations, including local governments, nonprofit organizations, schools, and health care systems across Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the bill only modifies the conditions, grantees, and deadlines under which previously authorized State grant funds may be used. Local government finances are affected only where a local government entity serves as a grantee.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services administers and manages the execution of State capital grants to local governments and nonprofit organizations authorized through State debt.
The Board of Public Works oversees State capital projects and debt spending, certifies matching funds, and approves grant agreements and expenditure adjustments for State debt authorizations.

The bill directly modifies multiple prior capital debt authorizations specifically allocated to the University of Maryland, College Park (RB22) for the Health and Human Sciences Building, extending termination dates and altering funding amounts.

The bill explicitly redirects a $50,000 capital grant directly to the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families for capital improvements to the Historic White House at the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home.
The bill alters the scope, purpose, and grantees of capital grants authorized under DHCD's Division of Neighborhood Revitalization.
The bill alters a prior capital authorization under DNR's Capital Grants and Loans Administration for a municipal trail/infrastructure project in Salisbury.
The Treasurer's Office manages State debt and bond proceeds, sits on the Board of Public Works, and monitors authorizations of State general obligation bonds.
DBM assists in overseeing State budget execution, capital planning, and fiscal policies related to State-funded debt authorizations.
The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works and functions as the chief financial officer responsible for disbursing State funds and maintaining financial records of State debt appropriations.

bill_summary: Alters the election structure of the Wicomico County Board of Education beginning with the 2026 general election. Requires all seven elected board members to represent individual councilmanic districts, eliminating at-large seats. Adds at least one nonvoting student member serving a one-year term to the county board. Authorizes the county board to grant a scholarship to a student member. Authorizes the Wicomico County Council to set board salaries exceeding statutory compensation minimums. Entitles elected and student board members to reimbursement for travel and other official expenses.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of Education; Wicomico County Council; Wicomico County Board of Elections
stakeholders: Elected members and student members of the Wicomico County Board of Education, high school students in Wicomico County Public Schools, and Wicomico County voters
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Local expenditures increase for the Wicomico County Board of Education if the Wicomico County Council sets salaries higher than current statutory amounts ($4,000 for the chair and $3,700 for other members) or if the board awards scholarships to student members. Expense voucher reimbursements and election administrative adjustments are minimal and absorbable within existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article governing the composition, student representation, and compensation of the Wicomico County Board of Education, which falls under the overarching public education system overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill modifies the election structure for the Wicomico County Board of Education by shifting from five district and two at-large seats to seven single-member councilmanic district seats starting in the 2026 general election, which impacts election administration overseen by the State Board of Elections.

stakeholders: competitively awarded Class B sports wagering facility licensees originally licensed on or before September 30, 2023
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not materially affected. The State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission can handle relocation requests with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly conditions the approval of a sports wagering facility relocation request on review and approval by the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), a statutory state commission.

bill_summary: Requires applicants for barber, barber-stylist, cosmetologist, and limited cosmetology licenses to complete domestic violence awareness training. Directs the Maryland Department of Labor to approve in-person and virtual training programs lasting at least one hour. Requires approved programs to cover recognizing abuse signs, communicating with victims, and connecting clients to support resources. Mandates that existing license and limited license holders complete the training for their next license renewal. Takes effect January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; State Board of Barbers; State Board of Cosmetologists
stakeholders: Applicants for and holders of barber, barber-stylist, cosmetologist, and limited cosmetology licenses; salon and barbershop clients who are victims of domestic violence
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the State Barbers and Cosmetologists Boards' Fund increase by approximately $10,000 in FY 2026 for IT reprogramming. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Labor, which houses both the State Board of Barbers and the State Board of Cosmetologists. The department is mandated to approve domestic violence awareness training programs and implement the new one-hour training requirement for initial licensing and license renewals, requiring special fund expenditures of approximately $10,000 for system reprogramming.

bill_summary: Requires private nonprofit institutions of higher education to submit semi-annual letters of intent for intended new graduate-level programs. Repeals the requirement that the Maryland Higher Education Commission circulate letters of intent among all institutions. Prohibits construing letters of intent to grant an institution a right of first refusal. Authorizes the Commission to notify affected institutions and encourage collaboration when intended programs appear similar. Repeals provisions granting five specified public universities exclusive initial authority to propose emerging workforce need programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: public senior higher education institutions and private nonprofit institutions of higher education in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local finances. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the revisions using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for administering the academic program approval process, receiving and reviewing graduate program letters of intent, identifying program duplication, and updating the State Plan for Higher Education.
As the state's coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission directly oversees the letter of intent requirements and academic program approval revisions enacted by this bill.

USM institutions (including Bowie State University, Coppin State University, UMCP, and UMES) are subject to the graduate program letter of intent process and are directly affected by the repeal of the 90-day exclusive authority to propose emerging workforce need programs.

Morgan State University is a public senior higher education institution directly affected by the letter of intent requirements and the repeal of statutory provisions that previously granted it 90-day exclusive authority to propose emerging workforce need programs.

As an independent public senior higher education institution in Maryland, St. Mary's College is subject to MHEC's academic program approval regulations and the graduate program letter of intent process.

Synopsis: Requiring the District Court to hold a hearing on a tenant holding over within 45 days after a landlord makes a complaint if the landlord or the landlord's spouse is on active duty with the United States military; and authorizing a private process server to serve a certain summons if the constable or sheriff of the county fails to serve the summons within 10 days after the summons is issued by the court.

bill_summary: Requires the District Court to schedule a tenant holding over hearing within 45 days after a landlord files a repossession complaint. Applies when the landlord or spouse is on active military duty, relocates to Maryland, and intends to occupy the property. Requires qualifying service members to submit supporting documentation with their complaint. Authorizes service by a private process server if the sheriff or constable fails to serve the summons within 10 days. Establishes an effective date of October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; county sheriffs and constables
stakeholders: Active duty U.S. military service members and their spouses who lease residential property in Maryland, holdover tenants, private process servers, and county sheriffs and constables
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies District Court procedures for tenant holding over actions involving active duty military service members, requiring the court to issue a summons ordering appearance within 45 days of a complaint and altering service of process requirements.

The bill establishes legal protections and expedited proceedings specifically for active duty service members and their spouses who relocate to Maryland, which pertains to the agency's mission to advocate for and support military families with housing-related needs and resources.

bill_summary: Requires a District Court hearing on a wrongful detainer complaint to be held within 10 business days after filing. Establishes alternative service procedures if a person in possession cannot be found after two good-faith efforts. Directs the authorized process server to file an affidavit describing the good-faith efforts with the court. Requires mailing the complaint by certified and first-class mail and affixing the summons conspicuously to the property. responsible_party: District Court of Maryland

fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures and timelines for wrongful detainer actions in the District Court and appeals to the Circuit Court, including mandating hearings within 10 business days, establishing service and affidavit requirements, and altering appeal timelines.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of General Services to include a notation on a certain identification card indicating that the holder is a veteran under certain circumstances; requiring the Department to obtain the consent of a certain holder of an identification card before transmitting certain information to a certain executive agency; and prohibiting the Department from transmitting certain information obtained on an application for an identification card except under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of General Services to include a veteran status notation on issued identification cards. Requires cardholders seeking the notation to present acceptable veteran certification or documentation. Requires the Department to provide application options to indicate veteran status and consent to benefit outreach. Mandates the transmission of consenting applicants' information to requesting executive agencies regarding veterans' benefits. Prohibits the Department from transmitting veteran status application information without applicant consent unless authorized or required by law.
responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: veterans who are State employees, contractors, regulated lobbyists, media personnel, local government officials, or volunteers holding Department of General Services security identification cards
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of General Services can implement the notation and notification requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of General Services with offering a veteran status notation on its issued identification cards, modifying card application forms to capture veteran status and consent, sharing information with executive agencies upon request, and adopting implementing regulations.

The bill explicitly references veteran status certifications issued by the Department of Veterans and Military Families as acceptable documentation and enables the department to request and receive applicant contact information to conduct outreach regarding state and federal veterans' benefits.

Covers unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, and qualifying portions of soil remains entitled to a State veterans cemetery plot. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires licensed funeral establishments, crematories, and reduction facilities to notify and transfer unclaimed remains of eligible veterans or their dependents to DVMF for appropriate disposition and burial in State veterans' cemeteries, creating an operational and fiscal impact on the department.

The bill amends the Business Regulation Article regarding the disposition of unclaimed remains by crematories and reduction facilities, which are regulated by the Office of Cemetery Oversight housed within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The bill amends the Health Occupations Article relating to licensed funeral establishments and crematories, which fall under the regulatory oversight of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors within the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The health occupations boards are administratively housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status issued by the Department of Veterans and Military Families and establishes a mechanism for health occupations boards to electronically share consenting applicants' information with executive branch agencies to determine eligibility for veterans benefits.

bill_summary: Prohibits committing animal abuse or neglect that results in the death or necessary euthanasia of domestic animals or livestock. Requires a euthanasia decision to be recommended by a licensed veterinarian and validated by a second licensed veterinarian. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to one year imprisonment, a fine up to $5,000, or both. Authorizes courts to order convicted defendants to pay for psychological counseling and animal confiscation, care, or euthanasia costs. Authorizes courts to prohibit defendants from owning, possessing, or residing with animals for a court-determined period.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals charged with or convicted of animal abuse or neglect, owners and custodians of domestic animals or livestock, and licensed veterinarians
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $34,558 in FY 2025 for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs, with potential increases in State and local incarceration expenditures. Local revenues may increase from higher monetary penalties in circuit court cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense and sentencing provisions for animal abuse or neglect resulting in death or euthanasia. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs a direct fiscal impact of $34,558 in fiscal 2025 for one-time computer system reprogramming to track the new offense and dispositions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an increased penalty of up to one year imprisonment for the new misdemeanor, which may result in an increase in state incarceration expenditures for convictions arising from Baltimore City.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants charged with the new offense and increased criminal penalties created by the bill.

The bill explicitly establishes criminal prohibitions and penalties regarding the abuse, neglect, death, and euthanasia of livestock, which falls under the Department of Agriculture's purview regarding animal health and agribusiness oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of the Environment to establish a certain process in collaboration with one or more boards under the Department's direction and control that requires a board to include a notation indicating veteran status on a professional license or certificate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency authorized by the bill to establish the process in collaboration with licensing boards under its direction, update credentialing forms and databases, adopt regulations, and issue professional licenses with veteran notations.

DVMF is specifically cited as a provider of veteran status certifications and is the principal executive agency responsible for connecting veterans with state and federal benefits when data is electronically shared with their consent.

Synopsis: Requiring the local board of elections to send a written notice regarding a request for a State-approved absentee ballot application with a specimen ballot and any other mailings to voters and eligible voters to further awareness of the option of mail-in voting, except under certain circumstances.

Requires inclusion of the notice with mailed specimen ballots and any other mailings to voters or eligible voters. Specifies that the notice must further awareness of the option of mail-in voting. Provides that a local board is not required to send the notice for a vote-by-mail election. Exempts voters with permanent absentee ballot status and limits notices to once per voter per election.
responsible_party: Local boards of elections; Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, eligible voters, and local boards of elections
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) supervises and administers elections in Maryland and oversees local boards of elections. The bill directly impacts election administration by requiring local boards to include notice regarding State-approved absentee ballot applications with specimen ballots and other mailings.

Synopsis: Specifying that property damage that results from an accident that involves any vessel subject to the State Boat Act while on the waters of the State includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers for purposes of a certain reporting requirement.

bill_summary: Specifies that property damage resulting from vessel accidents includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers. Requires vessel operators or owners to report accidents causing such damage within 10 days. Mandates submitting accident reports to the Department of Natural Resources. Excludes vessels required to have a certificate of inspection under federal regulations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: vessel operators and owners on Maryland waters
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 103 directly amends the Natural Resources Article regarding boating accident reporting requirements, specifying that property damage that must be reported to the Department of Natural Resources includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers.

Synopsis: Requiring each school board to certify to the State Ethics Commission, on or before October 1 each year, that the school board is in compliance with certain requirements of the Maryland Public Ethics Law.

bill_summary: Requires each school board to certify annually to the State Ethics Commission compliance with the Maryland Public Ethics Law. Clarifies that the definition of school board includes the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: Members of county boards of education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, as well as local school system officials and employees
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. Requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Ethics Commission by requiring all county school boards and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to annually certify to the Commission by October 1 that they comply with the Maryland Public Ethics Law.
MSDE provides oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 local school systems whose governing school boards are subject to the annual ethics compliance certification requirement under this bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing units in the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a certain process to include a notation of veteran status on an occupational license.

bill_summary: Authorizes units in the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process indicating veteran status on occupational licenses. Requires participating units to allow applicants to request the veteran notation on initial or renewal applications. Permits applicants to affirmatively consent to contact from Executive Branch agencies regarding State or federal veterans' benefits. Requires applicants seeking the notation to submit certified proof of veteran status. Requires units to electronically transmit applicant information to requesting Executive Branch agencies if consent is provided.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Military veterans applying for or renewing occupational licenses and licensing units within the Maryland Department of Labor
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures may increase by a minimal one-time amount of up to $12,000 as early as fiscal 2026 if licensing units choose to modify licenses to include the notation. Revenues and local government operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes occupational and professional licensing units within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process for adding veteran status notations on licenses and transmitting consenting applicant data to relevant executive branch agencies.

The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status issued by the Department of Veterans and Military Families as acceptable documentation and provides a mechanism for MD Labor to transmit consenting veteran licensee information to executive branch agencies such as DVMF to connect veterans with benefits.

Synopsis: Requiring the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty to stop the vessel as close as possible to the scene of the collision, accident, or casualty until the operator has rendered certain assistance and provided certain information; establishing certain criminal penalties for the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty who does not take certain actions in violation of the Act; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the operator of a vessel involved in an accident resulting in bodily injury or death to immediately stop. Mandates that the operator stop as close to the scene as possible to render aid and provide identifying information. Establishes misdemeanor penalties for failing to stop, including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $5,000. Designates failure to stop as a felony if the operator reasonably should have known serious injury or death could occur. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to two months imprisonment and a $500 fine for failing to render aid.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: vessel operators and owners in Maryland, recreational boaters, and victims of boating accidents
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the State Boat Act within the Natural Resources Article, regulating vessel operator duties after accidents and requiring accident reports to be filed with the Department of Natural Resources, whose Natural Resources Police enforce these boating laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new felony and misdemeanor offenses with prison sentences ranging up to 10 years, which may impact state correctional facilities and community supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new criminal penalties and incarceration terms for vessel hit-and-run incidents, requiring legal representation for indigent individuals charged under these provisions.
The Maryland court system will be responsible for adjudicating new misdemeanor and felony charges and processing criminal cases resulting from violations of the bill.

Synopsis: Providing that the Governor appoint members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers with the advice and consent of the Senate.

responsible_party: Governor; Senate of Maryland; State Board of Stationary Engineers; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Nominees and appointed members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers, licensed stationary engineers, and boiler industry representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The Senate confirmation requirement is procedural in nature and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Stationary Engineers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Secretary of Labor provides advice to the Governor regarding member appointments.
The Governor is the appointing authority for members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers, whose appointments will now require the advice and consent of the Senate.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor with the vetting, appointment, and Senate confirmation processes for members of state boards and commissions.

bill_summary: Extends through fiscal 2028 the annual $14,000,000 distribution from unclaimed property funds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million in fiscal 2028 due to the continued distribution of unclaimed property proceeds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Task force administrative duties and member stipends will be absorbed within existing Department of Housing and Community Development resources. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the responsibility to appoint members, designate the chair, provide staff, and authorize stipends for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force to the Secretary and Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill extends the requirement that the Comptroller distribute $14.0 million annually from unclaimed property net proceeds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through FY 2028, and maintain accounting for the fund.
The bill alters the administration of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force by transferring staffing and member appointment authority away from the Office of the Attorney General to DHCD.

The bill extends a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $14.0 million from the ACE Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the State budget through FY 2028, and the Task Force must submit its annual report to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the staffing, membership compensation, appointment authority, and reporting requirements of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and manage the investment of money in the Fund.

Synopsis: Repealing the Department of Agriculture's authority over the identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Cantaloupe growers, packers, shippers, and sellers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or operations, as the Maryland Department of Agriculture does not currently regulate or inspect cantaloupes and regulation occurs at the federal level.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly repeals Title 10, Subtitle 9 of the Agriculture Article, removing the Maryland Department of Agriculture's statutory authority regarding the regulation, identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.

Synopsis: Replacing references to mental hygiene with references to mental health in certain provisions of law governing public health; establishing that, by July 1, 2027, the Department of Health shall conduct a thorough review of Department regulations and adopt regulations to ensure consistency with the Act; and requiring the Department to update all public-facing electronic materials to be consistent with the Act as soon as practicable.

Requires the Maryland Department of Health to review its regulations and adopt conforming changes by July 1, 2027. responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: individuals receiving public mental health services, behavioral health providers, and members of the public accessing Maryland Department of Health materials
fiscal_impact_summary: State impacts are small enough to be absorbed within existing departmental resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

The bill amends Section 24-1105(b) regarding the Comptroller's transfer of proceeds and investment earnings into the renamed Mental Health Community-Based Services Fund, which may require minor administrative or accounting title updates in state financial records.

stakeholders: Maryland veterans and their families; Maryland Department of Disabilities
fiscal_impact_summary: Altering the composition of the Board of Trustees does not materially affect State or local finances. The Secretary of Disabilities or their designee can serve on the board using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 172 directly alters the membership of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust to include the Secretary of Disabilities, ex officio, or the Secretary's designee.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families houses the Maryland Veterans Trust, provides its staff and administrative support, and its Secretary serves as chair of the Board of Trustees being expanded.

The Secretary of Aging is an existing ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust referenced in the amended section.

The Secretary of Human Services is an existing ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust referenced in the amended section.
The Secretary of Labor is an existing ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust referenced in the amended section.

bill_summary: Alters parole consideration standards by requiring the Maryland Parole Commission to consider an incarcerated individual's age and public safety. Establishes a geriatric parole process for individuals at least 65 years old who have served 20 years of confinement. Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to submit names of eligible incarcerated individuals on an ongoing basis. Repeals gubernatorial disapproval authority for Commission decisions granting medical parole to individuals serving life sentences. Authorizes the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board to recommend distributing savings to the Commission to hire risk assessment psychologists.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals eligible for geriatric or medical parole, crime victims, correctional facility staff, and state parole officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,500 in FY 2026 and by $575,600 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Parole Commission to hire three psychologists and one administrative officer to conduct risk assessments and prepare reports. Future years reflect annualized salaries and inflation. General fund costs may be offset if the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board distributes savings from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to the Commission. Potential savings from reduced incarceration cannot be reliably estimated. Local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS and its unit, the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC), are the primary implementing entities. The bill requires DPSCS to regularly submit names of eligible individuals for geriatric parole, requires MPC to conduct risk assessments and parole release hearings, alters medical parole criteria and procedures, and directs DPSCS savings from geriatric parole toward risk assessments, hearings, and reentry services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP houses and supports the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB), which receives annual outcome reports on geriatric parole from MPC and is authorized under the bill to recommend distributing Justice Reinvestment savings to MPC to hire psychologists for risk assessments.

The bill repeals the statutory authority of the Governor to review and disapprove decisions by the Maryland Parole Commission to grant medical parole to incarcerated individuals serving life sentences.

stakeholders: spouses and dependents of eligible veterans, eligible veterans, and participating nonprofit training entities
fiscal_impact_summary: No net state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Veterans and Military Families can handle administrative changes with existing resources, and the bill alters the allowable uses of existing discretionary program funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program is established within and administered by the Department of Veterans and Military Families. This bill expands the program's eligibility, outreach, referral services, and grant-funded support to include spouses and dependents of eligible veterans.

responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the Maryland State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
stakeholders: Maryland State employees participating in or eligible for State supplemental retirement plans

bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to revoke driver's licenses for specified offenses resulting in death or severe injury. Applies to impaired driving that contributes to an accident resulting in death or life-threatening injury. Covers failure to remain at the scene of an accident resulting in death or serious bodily injury. Prohibits issuing a temporary license during an administrative appeal of the revocation. Establishes a five-year waiting period before an individual may apply for license reinstatement. Authorizes application after two years if the Administration finds undue hardship or extenuating circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Drivers convicted of or granted probation before judgment for impaired driving involving death or life-threatening injury, and drivers failing to remain at accident scenes resulting in death or serious bodily injury
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the changes with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for mandatorily revoking driver's licenses for specified impaired driving and hit-and-run offenses, barring temporary licenses during administrative appeals, and processing delayed reinstatement applications and hardship exemptions.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation.

OAH adjudicates administrative appeals of driver's license revocations and suspensions by the MVA, which are directly regulated by the provisions prohibiting temporary licenses during an administrative appeal.
The Maryland Judiciary handles the underlying criminal convictions and probation before judgment dispositions that trigger the required MVA license revocations.

bill_summary: Extends the authorization for certain converted dispensary licensees to deliver medical cannabis until July 1, 2026. Repeals the authorization to issue on-site consumption licenses during the second round of cannabis licensing. Authorizes on-site consumption licensees to repackage and process single-serving products and operate as food service facilities. Prohibits on-site consumption establishments from selling more than single-serving products or permitting removal of cannabis products. Exempts cannabis licensee transfers to employee stock ownership plans from the standard five-year transfer restriction. Clarifies that cannabinoid beverages are excluded from the food exemption under the State sales and use tax.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: licensed cannabis dispensaries, prospective on-site consumption establishment operators, social equity cannabis applicants, medical cannabis patients, and adult-use cannabis consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential unquantified delay or decrease in special fund fee revenues for the Maryland Cannabis Administration due to repealing on-site consumption licenses in the second licensing round. No material impact on overall State expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MCA requested the bill and serves as the primary regulator responsible for administering cannabis licensing, setting standards for on-site consumption establishments and single-serving products, and regulating medical cannabis deliveries and dispensary requirements.

The bill amends the Tax - General Article to exclude cannabinoid beverages from the definition of exempt food, ensuring they are subject to the appropriate sales and use tax collected and administered by the Comptroller.

The bill allows on-site consumption establishments to operate as food service facilities under § 21-301 of the Health - General Article, which are regulated, inspected, and licensed by MDH and local health departments.

The OAG is statutory legal counsel and is specifically required to be consulted by the Administration regarding disparity studies and constitutional licensing requirements.

Requires these instructional programs to be designed to provide a comprehensive and accurate explanation of the product. responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration

It amends the Insurance Article regarding the licensing requirements and instruction programs for limited line credit insurance producers, altering the Insurance Commissioner's approval role and establishing record-retention requirements that insurers must make available to the Commissioner upon request.

bill_summary: Alters provisions of the Public Employee Relations Act governing board staffing, remote meetings, and representation elections. Authorizes the Public Employee Relations Board to appoint up to three deputy directors rather than three specialized directors. Requires appointed deputy directors to be licensed Maryland attorneys or become licensed within 12 months. Allows exclusive representatives to meet with new employees by video technology without demonstrating public health concerns. Restricts the minimum 10-day voting window requirement to elections conducted by mail or electronic voting systems.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board

fiscal_impact_summary: Creates operational efficiencies with no impact on State revenues or local finances. May generate indeterminate State expenditure savings of more than $120,000 annually if the Public Employee Relations Board opts not to hire a third deputy director.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) that directly modifies its internal staffing structure, deputy director qualifications, unfair labor practice complaint handling, and exclusive representation election procedures.

The bill explicitly references the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) regarding unfair labor practice hearings. As noted in the fiscal note, OAH administrative law judges hear PERB-related matters and may require training on the bill's substantive statutory changes.

As the central personnel and human resources agency managing Executive Branch employee policies and collective bargaining relations, DBM is affected by changes governing exclusive representative access and meetings with new state employees.

bill_summary: Increases various environmental fees and penalties and establishes the Private Dam Repair Fund within the Department of the Environment. Raises the maximum emissions-based air quality permit fee from $50 to $200 per ton. Increases the per-barrel oil transfer fee to 9 cents per barrel through June 30, 2030. Requires nonfederal dam owners on the Maryland Dam Inventory to register annually beginning January 1, 2027. Authorizes the Department to provide loans from the Private Dam Repair Fund for repairing unsafe private dams. Authorizes fees up to $575 for on-site sewage disposal and individual well construction permits under specified circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration
stakeholders: Holders of air quality operating permits, oil transfer licensees, owners of nonfederal dams in Maryland, coal combustion by-product generators, and applicants for on-site sewage disposal and well construction permits.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $5.0 million in FY 2026 and between $7.2 million and $7.4 million annually thereafter from increased and newly authorized fees. State special fund expenditures increase by $6.7 million in FY 2026 under contingent budget appropriations, followed by $6.4 million to $6.5 million annually thereafter for program administration and dam assistance. Local government costs increase indeterminately but minimally to pay higher air quality permit fees, dam registration fees, and dam safety permit fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which establishes the Private Dam Repair Fund, sets new registration and safety permit fees for dams, increases air quality and oil transfer fees, adjusts coal combustion by-product fees, and enhances MDE's regulatory and enforcement authorities.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly established Private Dam Repair Fund separately, invest money from the fund, credit interest earnings back to the fund, and facilitate loan pledge withholdings.

The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly established Private Dam Repair Fund and to cause any pledged borrower funds to be withheld and directed toward loan obligations under the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration.
The OAG is authorized under the bill to initiate legal actions against borrowers defaulting on dam repair loan agreements and is consulted annually on MDE's environmental enforcement reporting.
DNR owns dams in Maryland and will experience an operational and fiscal impact by being required to pay the newly established dam registration fees and potential dam safety permit fees.
MDOT may be subject to dam safety permit fees for transportation embankments and water infrastructure projects that fall under the statutory definition of a dam.
