bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment to issue research, development, and demonstration permits for chemical warfare material incineration. Exempts qualifying research facilities from certain controlled hazardous substance requirements when incinerating chemical warfare materials for research purposes. Requires permit applicants to demonstrate capability to protect persons from a maximum credible event and establish emergency preparedness plans. Requires continuous near-real time air emissions monitoring with a lag time of not more than 10 minutes during incineration. Authorizes the Department to order an immediate termination of incineration operations when necessary to protect human health or the environment. Requires permit holders to submit annual operational reports and biennial assessments of impacts on ecosystems and public health.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: U.S. Department of Defense-designated research facilities, including the U.S. Army Chemical Biological Center at Aberdeen Proving Ground, local emergency response personnel, and local governments and residents in potentially impacted jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not anticipated to be materially affected, as the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local governmental operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing and regulatory agency under the bill. It is responsible for evaluating permit applications, establishing research, development, and demonstration (RDD) permit requirements, enforcing emissions and pollution monitoring standards, reviewing operational reports and environmental assessments, and issuing stop orders or revoking permits if public health or the environment is threatened.

This departmental bill was proposed by the Department of Commerce to allow research, development, and demonstration testing of chemical weapon destruction technologies at federal defense facilities such as the U.S. Army Chemical Biological Center at Aberdeen Proving Ground, supporting Maryland's defense industry and economic retention goals.

bill_summary: Requires each local board of elections to submit an election plan at least seven months before each statewide primary election. Mandates that the election plan incorporate a polling place plan, early voting center plan, and ballot drop box plan. Directs local boards to include an analysis of maximizing voter participation in the county and each precinct. Establishes public hearing, website posting, and testimony requirements before a local board votes on a proposed plan. Requires the State Board of Elections to vote on and approve plans meeting specified statutory criteria.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, historically disenfranchised communities, local boards of elections, and local elected officials

bill_summary: Expands the definition of State personnel under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. Adds employees of an office of a sheriff of a county or Baltimore City to the definition. Grants these sheriff office employees immunity from civil tort liability for acts within their public duties. Applies immunity only when tortious acts or omissions occur without malice or gross negligence. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Employees of an office of a sheriff of a county or Baltimore City, county governments, the State Insurance Trust Fund, and tort claimants
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund expenditures for the State Insurance Trust Fund to cover tort claims involving sheriffs' employees. Minimal decrease in local government expenditures for tort litigation, settlements, and insurance premiums. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which pays tort claims filed under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. Expanding the definition of 'State personnel' to include employees of the office of a sheriff results in a direct fiscal impact on SITF expenditures and requires the Treasurer's Office to investigate applicable claims.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State and State personnel in tort litigation under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, and will be tasked with defending claims brought against employees of county and Baltimore City sheriffs' offices.

Synopsis: Establishing for a first offense by a holder of an alcoholic beverages license in Baltimore City of operating the licensed premises outside specified hours of operation without obtaining a certain exemption a fine of not less than $1,000 or suspension of the license or both, and for a second or subsequent offense a fine of not less than $2,000 and not more than $20,000 or suspension of the license or both.

bill_summary: Establishes civil penalties for Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders operating outside specified hours without an exemption. Requires the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to penalize license holders for unauthorized after-hours operation. Mandates a minimum $1,000 fine, license suspension, or both for a first offense. Requires a fine between $2,000 and $20,000, license suspension, or both for second or subsequent offenses. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: holders of alcoholic beverages licenses in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent fines are imposed. Baltimore City expenditures and State finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While enforcement of hours of operation and imposition of civil penalties under this bill are administered locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, the subject matter falls within the broad scope of alcohol regulation overseen at the state level.

bill_summary: Establishes registration and operating requirements for virtual currency kiosk operators in the State. Requires operators to register kiosks annually with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation starting January 1, 2026. Caps daily kiosk transactions at $2,000 for new users and $10,500 for experienced users. Limits transaction fees to the greater of $5 or 15% and mandates fee refunds for verified fraud. Requires specified on-screen risk disclosures, transaction receipts, customer data collection, and live toll-free telephone support. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to enforce compliance and assess civil penalties up to $1,000 daily.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Virtual currency kiosk operators and consumers using virtual currency kiosks in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by an estimated $84,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 from registration and renewal fees. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, with establishing, implementing, and enforcing the regulatory and registration framework for virtual currency kiosks and kiosk operators in Maryland.

Synopsis: Requiring the election director of a local board of elections to designate chief election judges from certain political parties to each polling place except under certain circumstances; and requiring an election director who is unable to designate chief judges for a polling place at least 45 days before the start of early voting to make a certain designation in a certain manner.

bill_summary: Requires polling places to have equal numbers of majority party and principal minority party election judges to the extent practicable. Clarifies that this parity requirement explicitly includes chief judges designated to supervise polling place staff. Repeals existing limits on minor and unaffiliated election judges in precincts with six or more judges. Applies an alternative selection procedure if an election director cannot designate balanced chief judges 45 days before early voting. Requires the director in that circumstance to designate one affiliated chief judge and one chief judge registered with neither party.
responsible_party: Local boards of elections; local election directors
stakeholders: Chief election judges, election judges, unaffiliated voters serving as election judges, and local election directors
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections oversees the administration of state election laws and supervises local boards of elections, which are responsible for appointing and designating chief election judges and election judges in accordance with the bill's party affiliation requirements.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Highway Administration to operate speed monitoring systems on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County. Restricts placement to high-risk crash locations, capped at four systems per direction on Interstate 695 and three on Interstate 83. Prohibits placing systems within 5 miles of another system operating in the same direction. Sets a maximum civil penalty of $40 and mandates warning notices during the first 30 days of operation. Requires citation fines to be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration. Directs fine revenues solely toward system administrative costs and roadway and safety improvements on both highways.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Comptroller of Maryland; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County; registered motor vehicle owners
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures increase, potentially significantly, from fiscal 2026 through 2030 from speed camera fines and roadway safety projects. General fund expenditures increase by $12,208 in fiscal 2026 only for Judiciary system reprogramming.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SHA is the primary implementing agency authorized to place, operate, and maintain speed monitoring systems on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County, receive fine distributions for program cost recovery and safety improvements, and submit a comprehensive evaluation report to the General Assembly and Governor.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration and Motor Vehicle Administration. The bill impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) through increased fine revenues and corresponding expenditures for speed camera administration and highway safety improvements.

The District Court, supported by the AOC, processes contested citations, prescribes uniform citation forms in consultation with SHA, collects civil penalties, remits fine proceeds to the Comptroller, and incurs a fiscal impact ($12,208 in FY 2026) for computer system reprogramming.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to receive fine revenues collected by the District Court from the speed monitoring systems on I-695 and I-83 and distribute them to the State Highway Administration.

As the modal administration overseeing vehicle titling and registration, MVA is authorized to refuse vehicle registration or reregistration for failure to pay speed monitoring citations, while ensuring violations are not assessed points on driving records.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), an entity within DPSCS, is responsible for developing training programs for speed monitoring program administrators and compiling an annual speed monitoring program report incorporating SHA's operations.

bill_summary: Defines visual representation under the State's revenge porn statute to include certain computer-generated images. Excludes drawings, cartoons, sculptures, and paintings from this definition. Establishes a civil cause of action for defamation per se or invasion of privacy against violators. Authorizes courts to award reasonable attorney's fees to a prevailing plaintiff. Prohibits public inspection of visual representations in court records for related criminal and civil cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a civil cause of action for defamation per se or invasion of privacy relating to revenge porn, authorizes courts to award attorney's fees, and modifies procedures regarding the confidentiality and inspection of court records in such cases.

The bill explicitly references the Attorney General or designee regarding access to and inspection of confidential visual representations that are part of a court record in criminal or civil proceedings under the section.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the definition of visual representation under criminal revenge porn statutes (punishable by up to two years imprisonment), which directly impacts indigent defense caseloads and representation in criminal prosecutions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the criminal offense of revenge porn to encompass certain computer-generated visual representations, potentially resulting in commitments and supervision under the department's correctional facilities.

The bill centers on the annual report published by the Independent Investigations Division (IID), a unit within the Office of the Attorney General that investigates police-involved fatalities, requiring its findings to be reviewed and used for policy recommendations.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for State public safety death benefits to include qualifying 9-1-1 specialists. Establishes a line-of-duty death presumption for specified public safety personnel who die by suicide. Triggers the presumption if a licensed medical or mental health professional diagnosed a work-related stress or trauma disorder. Excludes 9-1-1 specialists from eligibility for State public safety funeral benefits. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: 9-1-1 specialists, law enforcement officers, correctional officers, volunteer and career firefighters, rescue squad members, sworn members of the State Fire Marshal, public safety aviation employees, hazardous material response team employees, and their surviving beneficiaries.
fiscal_impact_summary: No immediate material effect on State expenditures because new death benefit claims are expected to occur in limited circumstances and fit within funds typically budgeted; revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not directly affected.

MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and statewide emergency communications infrastructure; the bill explicitly expands eligibility for public safety death benefits to include 9-1-1 specialists.

MSP employs state law enforcement officers, public safety aviation personnel, and sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, all of whom are covered under the public safety death benefit program and affected by the new line-of-duty death presumption for duty-related psychological trauma and suicide.

MDE employs emergency hazardous material response team personnel who are covered public safety employees eligible for line-of-duty death benefits and the bill's expanded duty-related death presumptions.
The statute governs benefits and memorial protocols for Maryland military service members who die in the line of duty, which are coordinated with DVMF.

bill_summary: Exempts specified corridors in Big Savage Mountain, Bear Pen, and Dan's Mountain wildlands from wildland designations. Applies the exemption conditionally if NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic obtains a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Requires the transmission line to run parallel to an existing line and minimize forest and habitat loss. Requires the applicant to replace lost wildland acreage with twice the acreage and implement a conservation plan. Conditions the statutory changes on a 120-day stakeholder process and a recommendation by the Secretary of Natural Resources. Abrogates the act if the Public Service Commission denies the certificate or approves an alternative route.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission; Maryland Department of Natural Resources

fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Department of Natural Resources and the Public Service Commission can handle the review and regulatory requirements using existing resources. In the out-years, federal wildlife restoration grant funding could be jeopardized if lost wildland acreage is not replaced within three years as required by federal regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Public Utilities Article to require the Public Service Commission (PSC) to mandate wildland impact mitigation guarantees for applicants seeking a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) for overhead transmission lines traversing certain wildland areas, and establishes statutory triggers for notifying the Department of Legislative Services upon certain PSC actions.

The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article regarding Type 1 wildland designations (Big Savage Mountain, Bear Pen, and Dan's Mountain Wildlands). It requires DNR consultation on transmission line design, establishes a 90-day deliberation period for DNR, conditions bill provisions on a recommendation by the Secretary of Natural Resources, and requires the applicant to work with DNR to acquire and replace lost wildland acreage at a 2-to-1 ratio.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential consumers in utility and transmission line CPCN proceedings before the Public Service Commission, making the altered conditions and requirements for this major transmission project relevant to its advocacy work.

The Maryland Department of the Environment participates in the state's comprehensive CPCN environmental review process for transmission line siting and was consulted as an information source for the legislation.

Adds the volume of coal combustion by-products disposed of and remaining in storage units or landfills in the State. Requires the Department to use excess fee revenue to increase beneficial reuse and mitigate priority site impacts. Requires the Department to adopt regulations by October 1, 2026, implementing federal legacy coal combustion residual rules.

stakeholders: Generators of coal combustion by-products, electric power plant operators, landfill operators, and communities near coal combustion by-product sites
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2026 due to a contingent budget appropriation, with ongoing expenditures of approximately $204,000 to $216,500 annually. Special fund revenues to the State Coal Combustion By-Products Management Fund increase by $1,031,300 in FY 2027, rising to $1,102,600 by FY 2030 due to fee structure adjustments. Local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including establishing and collecting revised coal combustion by-product fees, adopting updated regulations, utilizing excess fee revenue for mitigation and reuse, and jointly staffing and leading the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is designated as a member of the newly created Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee and is required to jointly provide staff for the committee alongside MDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee to share monitoring results, discuss remediation, and report annually to legislative committees.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development and the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program within the Maryland Department of Labor. Creates the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program and an associated special fund to assist employers with apprenticeship costs. Authorizes the Governor to include at least $5,000,000 in the State budget for the fund each year from fiscal 2027 through 2030. Mandates a minimum ratio of one journeyworker to one apprentice for registered programs approved on or after January 1, 2023. Establishes the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board and repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council; Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board
stakeholders: registered apprentices, apprenticeship sponsors, participating employers, and registered apprenticeship qualified intermediaries
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2026 for 14 staff positions and administrative costs, increasing with inflation in future years. Discretionary general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by indeterminate but potentially significant amounts in FY 2027 through FY 2030 to award program grants. Local impact is minimal to the extent local entities receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with housing the new Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development, administering the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program, operating the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program and its special fund, managing ratio requirements, and staffing the new Advisory Board.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Director of the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to develop the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program.

The bill requires the Director of the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program to consult with the Department of Commerce in developing the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program, and repeals the department's statutory seat on the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new statutory entity, the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board, and repeals the existing Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.

The bill is an Administration initiative that requires the Governor to include annual budget bill appropriations for administrative costs of the new office and authorizes appropriations for the grant fund, as well as appointing members and the chair of the new Advisory Board.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and invest the monies of the newly created Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund.
The Comptroller is required by the bill to account for the newly created Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund and manage associated interest accrual accounting.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, including administering the mandated and discretionary appropriations required by the bill for staffing and program funds.
The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee, on which the State Superintendent of Schools held a statutory seat, affecting interagency youth apprenticeship policy coordination.

The office assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting gubernatorial appointees, including the chair and employer representatives to the newly established Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board.
The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee, on which the Secretary of Juvenile Services previously held a statutory seat.

bill_summary: Alters statutory waiting periods for expungement petitions to run from the completion of the sentence. Defines completion of the sentence as sentence expiration, including probation, parole, or mandatory supervision. Adds misdemeanor convictions for credit card theft and driving without a license to offenses eligible for expungement. Requires courts to evaluate supervision success and restitution payment status before granting expungement petitions. Prohibits Maryland Judiciary Case Search from displaying certain stet charges and treatment-conditioned nolle prosequi dispositions. Prohibits Case Search from displaying electronic records of pardoned cannabis possession convictions.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals seeking expungement of criminal records, individuals with pardoned cannabis convictions or stetted charges, and crime victims entitled to restitution
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $23,824 in FY 2026 for one-time computer programming. Expenditures for the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may also increase minimally if expungement petition volumes require additional staff. State general fund revenues increase minimally from $30 expungement petition filing fees. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary and court operations by expanding expungement eligibility, altering court findings required for expungement petitions, and mandating technical modifications to the Maryland Judiciary Case Search to shield certain records, incurring fiscal and administrative impacts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository and the Division of Parole and Probation. The bill alters definitions around sentence completion, considers probation/parole success, and requires CJIS to process an increased volume of court-ordered record expungements.

This is an Administration bill that specifically incorporates protections for individuals who received gubernatorial pardons for cannabis convictions by prohibiting their display on Maryland Judiciary Case Search.
As the primary state law enforcement agency maintaining police records and booking information, MSP is required to comply with court orders expunging police records for newly eligible offenses.

The bill makes convictions for driving without a license (Transportation Article § 16-101) eligible for expungement, which interacts with driver licensing records and traffic violation tracking managed by the MVA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The expansion of expungement eligibility and modifications to waiting periods and court hearing considerations directly affect post-conviction relief advocacy and client representation provided by the Public Defender.

bill_summary: Reclassifies the crime of transporting a regulated firearm into the State for unlawful sale or trafficking as a felony. Removes the offense from the three-year statute of limitations, allowing prosecution to be instituted at any time. Maintains criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 10 years, a fine up to $25,000, or both. Designates each violation of the transport prohibition as a separate crime. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of State Police; State's Attorneys
stakeholders: firearms dealers, individuals accused of firearm trafficking, law enforcement officers, and prosecutors
fiscal_impact_summary: Not expected to materially affect State or local finances. Reclassifying the offense shifts a minimal number of prosecutions from the District Court to the circuit courts, with no measurable change in revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations, enforcing state firearms laws, and investigating illegal firearms trafficking and straw purchases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation, which manage individuals convicted and incarcerated or supervised under the reclassified felony offense.
Reclassifying the offense from a misdemeanor to a felony shifts filings and proceedings from the District Court to the Circuit Courts, impacting court operations and case administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants charged with firearms trafficking offenses, which will now be handled as felony cases in Circuit Courts.
The Office of the Attorney General advises on state criminal law enforcement and handles criminal appeals stemming from felony convictions in state courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy strategies, including initiatives aimed at reducing gun violence and illegal firearms trafficking.

Synopsis: Altering the deadlines for the completion of the process of review and investigation by a certain investigating unit through disposition by an administrative charging committee under certain circumstances; and requiring a law enforcement agency to file any administrative charges arising out of an investigation of alleged police officer misconduct that is not required to be reviewed by an administrative charging committee within 1 year and 1 day after the date that the appropriate official of the law enforcement agency became aware of the incident.
Title: Public Safety - Police Accountability - Time Limit for Filing Administrative Charges

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Police Conduct -see also- Ethics; Law Enforcement

bill_summary: Alters statutory deadlines for completing investigations and filing administrative charges for alleged police officer misconduct. Requires an investigating unit to forward findings on public complaints to an administrative charging committee within 334 days. Requires the administrative charging committee to make a determination or request further investigation within 30 days of receipt. Requires completion of the review process through disposition within 395 days after an authorized official learns of the incident. Mandates filing administrative charges not reviewed by a charging committee within one year and one day of agency awareness. Establishes a one-year-and-one-day deadline to file administrative charges following the conclusion of related criminal investigations.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies; administrative charging committees
stakeholders: Maryland police officers subject to misconduct allegations, complainants from the public, and State and local law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency in Maryland, MSP directly investigates allegations of police misconduct against its troopers and is governed by the statutory timelines for internal investigations, administrative charging committee proceedings, and the filing of administrative disciplinary charges.

DNR employs the Maryland Natural Resources Police, whose officers and internal affairs investigative units must comply with the altered time limits for investigating misconduct and filing administrative disciplinary charges.
MDTA maintains its own sworn police force that is subject to the statewide police accountability and discipline framework altered by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs sworn law enforcement personnel and works closely with police standards bodies; its investigative units must adhere to statutory requirements regarding internal disciplinary procedures and timelines.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations that employ sworn law enforcement officers who are subject to the statewide police disciplinary process and charging deadlines.
MTA maintains a dedicated sworn transit police force that must abide by the revised timelines for internal investigations and submitting cases to administrative charging committees.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose sworn officers and internal misconduct investigations are directly governed by the statutory deadlines for administrative charges.
USM institutions employ sworn campus police forces that must operate under Maryland's uniform police accountability and disciplinary timelines.
Morgan State University maintains an independent sworn university police department governed by the state's police misconduct and administrative charging statutes.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn regulatory and law enforcement personnel (such as field enforcement agents) who fall within the scope of state police accountability laws.
The Maryland Judiciary handles appeals stemming from police disciplinary trial boards; modifying charging deadlines and procedures may indirectly affect court dockets.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling to study the pooling of public employee health insurance purchasing between the State, counties, municipal corporations, and county boards of education in the State to maximize value and efficiency while maintaining a broad package of benefits and reasonable premiums for public employees; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling to examine pooled public employee health insurance purchasing. Charges the Commission with evaluating health benefit data from the State, counties, municipal corporations, and county boards of education. Requires the Commission to analyze fiscal impacts and identify barriers to implementing pooled purchasing arrangements. Authorizes the Commission to contract with external organizations to provide necessary data analysis. Requires the Commission to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State, county, municipal, and public school employees; the State of Maryland; county governments; municipal corporations; county boards of education; public employee labor unions
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Budget and Management can staff the Commission using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the lead agency responsible for administering state employee health benefits. Under the bill, the Secretary of Budget and Management chairs the Commission, and DBM is required to provide staff support and collect data for the study.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary statutory study body, the Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling, to evaluate pooling public employee health insurance across state and local entities and report findings.
The Procurement Advisor to the Board of Public Works, or the advisor's designee, is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
The Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission to Study Health Insurance Pooling.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner, or the Commissioner's designee, is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
The Governor is responsible for appointing nine members to the Commission and receives the Commission's final report on findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the nine non-legislative/ex-officio seats created on the Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to impose, by law, the general property tax rate and a certain special property tax rate on vacant and abandoned property owned by certain nonprofit organizations that would otherwise be exempt from property tax under certain provisions of law; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - Authority to Impose on Vacant and Abandoned Property Owned by Nonprofit Organizations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to tax certain vacant real property owned by nonprofit organizations. Applies to real property that would otherwise qualify for charitable, educational, or religious property tax exemptions. Permits the city to impose both the general property tax rate and an authorized special rate. Restricts eligible property to vacant lots or improved property cited as vacant and unfit for habitation or other authorized use. Takes effect June 1, 2025, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
stakeholders: nonprofit organizations and religious groups owning vacant lots or cited vacant and unfit improved property in Baltimore City; Baltimore City government
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in Baltimore City property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2026 depending on the number of exempt properties taxed under the bill; local expenditures are not directly affected and State finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under Section 6-302(c)(2) of the Tax - Property Article amended by the bill's framework, jurisdictions enacting special rates on vacant properties are required to submit an annual report to the Department of Housing and Community Development regarding the rates, number of properties, revenue changes, and plans for adaptive reuse.

The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears administrative appeals regarding property tax assessments and exemption determinations. To the extent nonprofit organizations dispute the application of tax rates or loss of exemptions on their vacant properties under this local authorization, appeals may be brought before local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals of real property assessment and exemption decisions arising from the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2029 an appropriation of $5,000,000 to the Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program.
Title: Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $5,000,000 annually for the Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program for fiscal years 2027 through 2029. Reestablishes a multiyear funding mandate for the grant program within the Maryland Department of Health. Directs grant funding to local jurisdictions to establish and expand community behavioral health crisis response systems. Preserves the requirement that at least one-third of the mandated appropriation fund competitive grants for mobile crisis teams.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: local jurisdictions, local behavioral health authorities, mobile crisis teams, community behavioral health providers, and individuals experiencing behavioral health crises
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually from fiscal 2027 through 2029 to provide mandated grant funding, with no effect in fiscal 2026. Local revenues and expenditures increase from fiscal 2027 through 2029 as local behavioral health authorities receive competitive crisis response grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program is established within the Maryland Department of Health, which administers the program and oversees the distribution of grant funds to local jurisdictions.
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include a $5,000,000 appropriation for the program in the annual state operating budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

As the principal agency responsible for preparing and executing the state budget, DBM must incorporate the mandated $5,000,000 general fund appropriation into the state's operating budget for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of stop sign monitoring systems in certain school zones in Baltimore City and the City of Takoma Park under the pilot program authorized for Prince George's County, if authorized by local law; and requiring that a certain percentage of the fines collected under the Act be distributed to the local management board for Baltimore City and be used only to provide youth programming and services for youth living in or attending a school located in the 45th or 46th legislative districts.
Title: Baltimore City and Takoma Park - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems - Authorization of Pilot Program

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes stop sign monitoring systems in school zones in Takoma Park and Baltimore City's 45th and 46th legislative districts. Subjects recorded vehicle owners or drivers to a civil penalty not exceeding $40. Permits local jurisdictions to recover implementation and administrative costs from collected fine revenues. Requires Baltimore City to distribute 50% of collected fines to its local management board. Directs those funds solely to youth programming in the legislative district where the violation occurred. Requires Baltimore City and Takoma Park to submit comprehensive evaluation reports by December 1, 2027.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Baltimore City Department of Transportation; City of Takoma Park; State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers in Baltimore City and the City of Takoma Park; youth living in or attending school in Baltimore City's 45th and 46th legislative districts; local law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,900 in FY 2026 for District Court programming modifications. Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from contested citations through FY 2029. Local revenues and expenditures in Baltimore City and Takoma Park increase to the extent systems are deployed, with revenues used to offset administrative costs and 50% of Baltimore City revenues dedicated to local youth services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The District Court is required to prescribe uniform citation forms, adopt procedures for citations, trial proceedings, and collections, and handle contested cases. The fiscal note also identifies approximately $10,920 in programming costs for the District Court in FY 2026.

MDOT oversees both the State Highway Administration (SHA) and Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), both of which have direct statutory responsibilities under the bill regarding signage, roadway authorization, and vehicle registration sanctions.
SHA must authorize the placement of stop sign monitoring systems on State highways located within school zones and is required to prominently place notice signage on State highways.

As the Administration under the Maryland Vehicle Law, MVA is authorized to suspend or refuse vehicle registration or reregistration for unpaid, uncontested citations, and is prohibited from assessing points or recording violations on driving records.

The bill requires the Baltimore City Department of Transportation and the City of Takoma Park to submit comprehensive implementation and evaluation reports directly to the Governor by December 1, 2027.

Synopsis: Altering the requirements for certification of a U Nonimmigrant Status Petition; altering the individuals eligible to request a certain official to certify victim helpfulness relating to certification of a U Nonimmigrant Status Petition; altering the time periods within which a certain certifying entity shall certify or decline a certain form under certain circumstances; and requiring a certifying entity to develop protocols to assist certain petitioners to take certain actions.
Title: Criminal Procedure - U Nonimmigrant Status Petitions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Alters the procedures and deadlines for certifying entities to process U Nonimmigrant Status petitions for crime victims. Authorizes a victim's attorney, victim advocate, or other representative to request certification of victim helpfulness. Reduces the standard response timeline for certifying entities from 90 days to 45 days. Shortens the response deadline to 7 days for victims facing removal or deportation proceedings. Requires certifying officials to provide written explanations when evidence does not support certification. Mandates that certifying entities establish protocols assisting petitioners who have limited English proficiency.
responsible_party: State and local law enforcement agencies; State's Attorneys' Offices; Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Noncitizen crime victims, their families, and their legal representatives or victim advocates; state and local law enforcement and regulatory agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is explicitly designated by statute as a certifying entity authorized and required to process Form I-918, Supplement B victim helpfulness certifications for U Nonimmigrant Status petitions under the revised statutory guidelines and timelines.

The Maryland Department of Labor is explicitly named in the statute as a certifying entity with investigative and administrative jurisdiction that must adhere to the altered requirements, shorter decision deadlines, and limited English proficiency protocol requirements for U Nonimmigrant Status certifications.

The Department of Human Services oversees Child Protective Services and Adult Protective Services, both of which are explicitly enumerated in the bill as certifying entities responsible for evaluating and certifying victim helpfulness for U visa petitioners.

As the primary state law enforcement agency investigating qualifying criminal activity, the Maryland State Police is a primary certifying entity subject to the shortened response timeframes (e.g., 45 days generally, 7 days if detained or facing removal) and new standards for certifying or denying Form I-918 certifications.

The Office of the Attorney General has investigative and prosecutorial jurisdiction as a certifying entity and is specifically cited in the bill regarding statutory limits on non-disclosure that preserve the Attorney General's duty to disclose exculpatory information to criminal defendants.

Synopsis: Requiring each law enforcement agency, department, or entity providing security at a courthouse facility to submit a report by September 30, 2025, to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland; requiring the report include the current number of court security officers available, the minimum number needed to meet adequate security standards, the current number of vacancies and a viable plan to meet minimum adequate security standards as identified in the Act; etc.
Title: Courtroom Security - Minimum Adequate Security

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Family Law -see also- Adoption; Alimony; Annulment; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Requires law enforcement agencies, departments, and entities providing courthouse security to submit a security assessment report. Mandates submission of the report to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland by September 30, 2025. Directs reporting entities to identify currently available security officers, funded positions, and agency vacancies. Requires entities to calculate staffing levels needed to meet specified courtroom coverage and qualification standards. Requires submission of a viable implementation plan and identification of any obstacles to meeting those standards.
responsible_party: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland; law enforcement agencies, departments, or entities providing security at a courthouse facility
stakeholders: law enforcement agencies, departments, and sheriff's offices providing courthouse security; court security officers; judicial branch personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected, as the Judiciary and local entities can handle the reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judiciary and requires law enforcement agencies and entities providing courthouse security—including the Judiciary for the District Court and appellate courts—to submit reports on staffing, vacancies, and security standards to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland, which is centrally supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to borrow not more than $71,000,000 in order to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public facilities in St. Mary's County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds; etc.
Title: St. Mary's County - Public Facilities Bond

NarrowSubjects.Name: Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Piers and Docks -see also- Marinas; Ports
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of St. Mary’s County to borrow up to $71,000,000 through general obligation bonds. Finances the acquisition, construction, improvement, and development of specified public facilities and public works projects. Limits the maturity date of any issued bond to no later than 30 years from issue. Directs the county to levy annual ad valorem property taxes sufficient to pay bond principal and interest. Exempts the bonds, refunding bonds, and derived income from all Maryland State, county, and municipal taxation.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary’s County
stakeholders: Property owners, taxpayers, and residents in St. Mary’s County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. St. Mary's County bond revenues increase by up to $71.0 million, and county debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $5.0 million annually over a 20-year period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the authorized general obligation bonds, refunding bonds, and any interest or income derived from them are exempt from all State taxation. As the state's principal tax collection and revenue administration agency, the Comptroller oversees state tax compliance and exemptions, though the bill has no direct state fiscal effect.

Synopsis: Requiring certain political organizations to include certain disclaimers and disclosures on certain solicitations; authorizing the State Administrator of Elections to investigate a potential violation of the Act; and authorizing the State Board after the issuance of a public report of its finding to prohibit a person who violated the Act from making further solicitations for a certain period or impose a civil penalty not to exceed $10,000.
Title: Campaign Finance - Political Organizations - Disclosures on Solicitations (Stop Scam PACs Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires certain political committees and independent expenditure entities to include specific disclaimers and expenditure disclosures on solicitations. Mandates disclaimers on solicitations using a candidate's name, image, or likeness without permission. Requires electoral solicitations to disclose the top five expenditure recipients from the previous quarter and their payment amounts. Authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to investigate potential violations and issue subpoenas. Empowers the State Board of Elections to prohibit solicitations or impose civil penalties up to $10,000.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; State Board of Elections
stakeholders: political action committees exclusively making independent expenditures, participating organizations making political disbursements, political candidates, political parties, and political donors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $106,766 in FY 2026 and by ongoing amounts in future years for the State Board of Elections to hire one investigator. Special fund revenues to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase beginning in FY 2026 from civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) and the State Administrator of Elections are the primary implementing entities under the bill. SBE is granted authority to investigate potential violations, issue subpoenas, hold hearings, publish findings, prohibit unauthorized solicitations, assess civil penalties up to $10,000, and promulgate regulations, requiring a new staff position and additional general fund expenditures.
The bill explicitly circumscribes the jurisdiction of the Office of the State Prosecutor by providing that violations of this new section are not subject to investigation by the State Prosecutor.

The bill authorizes the State Administrator to petition the circuit courts to compel compliance with subpoenas issued pursuant to an investigation and mandates that court filings related to those subpoenas be sealed.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 in the annual budget bill to the Department of Housing and Community Development in fiscal years 2027 through 2030 as a grant to community action agencies statewide for measures to combat poverty.
Title: Maryland Community Action Agencies - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2030. Directs the mandated funding to the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires the Department to use the appropriation solely as operating grants to eligible community action agencies. Takes effect July 1, 2025, and terminates on June 30, 2032.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Eligible Maryland community action agencies, local governments operating community action programs, and low-income individuals receiving their services
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually from fiscal 2027 through 2030 for mandated grant funding. The Department can administer the grants with existing resources. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local governmental community action agencies receive and spend grant awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development is the primary implementing agency tasked with receiving the mandated annual appropriation of $250,000 from FY 2027 through FY 2030 and administering the operating grants to eligible community action agencies.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing and supervising the annual state budget and must ensure the mandated $250,000 general fund appropriation is included in the executive budget for FY 2027 through FY 2030.
The bill establishes a statutory mandate directing the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 in the annual budget bill for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Uninsured Employers' Fund Board; and requiring, rather than authorizing, the Board to establish reserves to meet potential losses of the Uninsured Employers' Fund.
Title: Labor and Employment - Uninsured Employers' Fund Board - Membership and Reserves

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Expands the Uninsured Employers' Fund Board from three to five members appointed by the Governor. Requires two members to have substantial experience as officers or employees of a property and casualty insurance company. Requires one member to have substantial experience in accounting or finance. Requires one member to hold a Maryland workers' compensation policy and one to represent the general public. Requires the Board to establish reserves to meet potential losses of the Uninsured Employers' Fund. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Uninsured Employers' Fund Board; Governor
stakeholders: Uninsured Employers' Fund Board members, workers' compensation insurance policyholders, property and casualty insurance professionals, and injured workers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Uninsured Employers' Fund increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 to compensate additional board members. No impact on state revenues or short-term fund operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Uninsured Employers' Fund Board from three to five members and alters their qualifications. Under the statute, the Governor is responsible for appointing all members with the advice and consent of the Senate and holds the authority to remove members for incompetence or misconduct.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. It will be directly responsible for identifying and vetting qualified appointees who meet the newly mandated criteria (such as property and casualty insurance experience, accounting/finance experience, and workers' compensation policyholder status) for the expanded five-member board.

Synopsis: Authorizing each health care facility to screen each patient for information on whether the patient is a service member community member, include on the patient's medical record whether the patient is a service member community member, and  meet certain standards established by The Joint Commission for the purpose of improving health care equity for warrior community members; and defining "service member community member" to mean a service member, a veteran, a certain spouse, a certain child, or a certain stepchild.
Title: Health Care Facilities - Service Member Community Members (SFC Matthew Fast Act )

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes health care facilities to screen patients for eligibility as a service member community member. Authorizes facilities to record service member community member status in patient medical records. Permits facilities to identify these individuals as a vulnerable population to improve health care equity. Authorizes facilities to comply with health care equity standards established by The Joint Commission. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit an annual equity report beginning in 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Service members, veterans, spouses, children, and stepchildren of service members or veterans, and health care facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds Subtitle 25 to the Health - General Article, which applies to health care facilities, including those operated by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its Behavioral Health Administration, authorizing screening of patients for service member status and establishing reporting requirements to the Governor and General Assembly on health care equity progress.

The bill directly amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article, the primary statute governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families, updating definitions for 'service member', 'veteran', 'reserve component', and 'uniformed services'.
The bill mandates an annual report to the Governor by December 1 each year, beginning in 2026, on the health care needs of service member community members and progress toward health care equity.

Synopsis: Establishing certain requirements for elections of the governing body of a condominium or homeowners association; requiring that the governing body of a condominium accommodate unit owner organizing activities relating to the governance of the condominium; prohibiting unit owners and lot owners from being charged for examining certain records of the condominium or homeowners association in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Condominiums and Homeowners Associations - Elections, Financial Statements, and Enforcement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes election procedures for governing bodies of condominiums and homeowners associations. Requires independent parties to conduct elections, collect and count ballots, and certify election results. Requires condominium governing bodies to reasonably accommodate unit owner organizing activities relating to condominium governance. Prohibits condominiums and homeowners associations from charging owners to examine financial statements in person or receive them electronically. Expands the enforcement authority and regulatory powers of the Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General.
responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: condominium unit owners, homeowners association lot owners, condominium councils of unit owners and governing bodies, homeowners associations, and property management companies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly expands the enforcement authority of the Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General to enforce the Maryland Condominium Act and the Maryland Homeowners Association Act, expands the definition of 'consumer' to include unit and lot owners, and grants the Division authority to adopt regulations carrying out these titles.

The Secretary of State has statutory oversight responsibilities regarding condominiums and time-shares in Maryland, and under Section 11-130 of the Real Property Article amended by this bill, local jurisdictions must forward copies of local condominium laws, ordinances, or regulations to the Secretary of State.

Synopsis: Providing that full-time deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of major and below in the Calvert County Sheriff's Office have the right to organize and negotiate with the County Administrator of Calvert County and the Calvert County Sheriff with regard to certain wages and employee benefits in a certain manner.
Title: Calvert County Sheriff - Deputy Sheriffs and Correctional Deputies - Collective Bargaining

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Authorizes full-time Calvert County deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of major and below to bargain collectively. Permits eligible personnel to select an exclusive representative to negotiate wages and employee benefits with the Sheriff and County Administrator. Requires any additional funding under a negotiated agreement to be approved by the Calvert County Commissioners. Prohibits correctional deputies from engaging in a strike. Limits collective bargaining agreements to terms of at least one year and no more than four years.
responsible_party: Calvert County Sheriff; County Administrator of Calvert County; Board of County Commissioners of Calvert County
stakeholders: Full-time deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of major and below in the Calvert County Sheriff's Office, the Calvert County Sheriff, and Calvert County government
fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures may increase to facilitate collective bargaining negotiations and fund potentially higher personnel costs under any approved agreements, though specific figures cannot be reliably estimated; state finances are not materially affected.

Synopsis: Requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to include certain discounts, financial assistance payments, product vouchers, and other out-of-pocket expenses made by or on behalf of an insured or enrollee when calculating certain cost-sharing contributions for certain prescription drugs; providing that a violation of the Act is considered a violation of the Consumer Protection Act; etc.
Title: Health Benefit Plans - Calculation of Cost-Sharing Contribution - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to include prescription drug financial assistance in cost-sharing calculations. Applies to covered drugs lacking preferred generic or biological alternatives, or those obtained through prior authorization, step therapy, or appeals. Excludes the deductible requirement for enrollees covered under high-deductible health plans. Requires noncharitable assistance providers to notify enrollees within seven days of the assistance amount and expiration date. Prohibits carriers from setting or altering coverage terms based on the availability of financial assistance.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Insured individuals and enrollees receiving prescription drug financial assistance, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, pharmacy benefits managers, commercial drug assistance programs, and local governments offering fully insured health plans.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration from the $125 rate and form filing fee in fiscal 2026. Expenditures for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans may increase if insurance costs rise. No impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator of health insurance policies and carriers in the State. The bill amends the Insurance Article to regulate how carriers calculate insureds' cost-sharing contributions for prescription drugs, requiring MIA to review updated policy forms and rate filings.

The bill provides that a failure by financial assistance providers to notify an insured or enrollee of the assistance amount and expiration date constitutes a violation of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that the Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.

bill_summary: Corrects technical errors, omissions, and obsolete references across multiple articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Clarifies statutory language, updates agency and legislative committee names, and reorganizes select provisions. Directs the publishers of the Annotated Code to make nonsubstantive editorial and conforming corrections. Requires publisher corrections to receive approval from the Department of Legislative Services. Confirms that the provisions are intended solely to resolve technical defects without altering substantive law.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
stakeholders: Legal practitioners, state agencies, local governments, and the public using the Annotated Code of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

The bill makes technical corrections to clarify the statutory designation of the Maryland Department of Emergency Management and updates legislative committee reporting references.
The bill corrects statutory naming for the Commission and cleans up stylistic, tabulation, and structural drafting errors within its governing sections in the Health - General Article.
The bill makes technical corrections to provisions governing motor fuel tax rate indexing and account management overseen by the Comptroller.
The bill makes minor technical and stylistic updates referencing the State Treasurer's management and investment of state funds.
The bill updates legislative committee reporting requirements for procurement summaries submitted by the Department of General Services.
The bill corrects internal cross-references, definitions, and designations within economic development programs and accounts administered by the Department.
The bill resolves minor drafting errors, cross-references, and program names (such as the Child Care Scholarship Program) within the Education Article.
The bill amends various sections of the Health - General Article to correct alphabetical order of definitions, obsolete subtitle headings, and cross-references.
The bill updates technical cross-references and aligns nonresident trapping license fee provisions within the Natural Resources Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects facility misnomers (Metropolitan Transition Center and Chesapeake Detention Facility) and capitalization errors within the Correctional Services Article.
The bill corrects a typographical error in the Transportation Article regarding administrator policies for emergency response plans.
The bill corrects the formal statutory name of the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program administered in part with postsecondary institutions.
The bill updates legislative committee names for contract evaluation reporting submitted by the Maryland Environmental Service.
The bill corrects cross-references and internal styling in provisions regarding pension transfers and retirement benefits under the State Personnel and Pensions Article.
The bill corrects cross-references and typographical items in the Public Utilities Article relating to customer education funds and renewable energy portfolio requirements.
The bill updates statutory cross-references relating to Legislative Auditor audits of accounts for small, minority, and women-owned businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor enforces state workplace and labor laws, including the Maryland Parental Leave Act amended by this bill.

stakeholders: Individuals and businesses cited for municipal violations, and Maryland municipal governments

Synopsis: Altering the entities to which a claimant is required to authorize the release in a claim application filed with the Workers' Compensation Commission to include the Uninsured Employers' Fund and the Subsequent Injury Fund; altering the information which a claimant is required to authorize the release in a claim application to include additional claims filed by the claimant and information in the custody of the Commission; etc.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Claims Application Form - Authorization for Release of Information

bill_summary: Expands authorized recipients of workers' compensation claim disclosures to include the Uninsured Employers' Fund and Subsequent Injury Fund. Authorizes the release of information to the agents of those funds. Requires claim forms to authorize the release of relevant medical and financial information. Includes in the authorization additional claims filed by the claimant and information held by the Workers' Compensation Commission. Applies these requirements to claims for accidental personal injury, occupational disease, and resulting death.
responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Workers' compensation claimants and their dependents, employers, workers' compensation insurers, Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the Uninsured Employers' Fund, and the Subsequent Injury Fund
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures for workers' compensation decrease minimally due to administrative savings from issuing fewer subpoenas for claimant records. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures and premium revenues also decrease minimally. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues increase minimally from one-time $125 rate and form filing fees in fiscal 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the required contents of the workers' compensation claim application forms filed with the Commission, expanding the scope of authorized release to include financial information, prior claims, and information held in the custody of the Commission.

The Subsequent Injury Fund is explicitly added to statute as an entity authorized to receive relevant medical and financial information, prior claims, and Commission records, resulting in direct administrative efficiencies in reviewing and adjudicating claims.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity administers workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees; it will experience administrative cost savings by reducing the need to issue costly subpoenas to obtain claimants' medical and financial records.

The agency will experience a minimal special fund revenue increase in FY 2026 from form filing fees as workers' compensation insurers submit updated policy and claim form filings for regulatory review.

responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: private providers of treatment foster care homes
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected because the Department of Human Services can complete the required study with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 833 directly mandates the Department of Human Services to conduct a study on appropriate and beneficial State support for private providers of treatment foster care homes and submit a final report with recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
