Requires electronic smoking devices wholesaler distributors and wholesaler importers to maintain detailed transaction and monthly inventory records. Mandates that wholesaler distributors and wholesaler importers preserve these records for up to six years for Commission examination. Repeals the authority of licensed electronic smoking devices manufacturers to sell devices directly to consumers.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Electronic smoking devices manufacturers, wholesaler distributors, wholesaler importers, retailers, vape shop vendors, and consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission can implement the bill's enforcement, seizure, and hearing requirements with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, and may represent the agency in contested seizure hearings, license actions, and litigation to recover enforcement expenses and attorney's fees authorized by the bill.

The Maryland Judiciary is responsible for adjudicating criminal misdemeanor violations under Title 16.7 and hearing potential judicial appeals arising from administrative seizures and final forfeiture determinations.

The Comptroller of Maryland regulates and taxes tobacco and related products and shares overlapping interest and statutory framework regarding contraband tobacco seizures, though primary regulatory enforcement of electronic smoking devices under this bill is conducted by the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.

Requires a verified mail notice if an electronic notice receives no confirmation at least five days before sale. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Self-service storage facility operators and storage unit occupants
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection and commercial laws through its Consumer Protection Division, which reviews and ensures compliance with statutory notice and lien enforcement requirements such as those in the Maryland Self-Service Storage Act.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

While the Public Service Commission regulates traditional telephone utilities, cellular and wireless carriers are specifically excluded from its regulatory jurisdiction under state law as noted in the bill's fiscal analysis.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment and partner agencies to develop a website and informational pamphlet on mold. Requires landlords to provide the pamphlet to tenants at lease signing and every two years upon request. Mandates that landlords perform a mold assessment within 15 days after receiving written notice of mold detection. Requires landlords to perform mold remediation within 45 days after completing an assessment that detects mold. Directs the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations establishing uniform mold assessment and remediation standards by June 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Labor; Department of General Services
stakeholders: residential landlords, residential tenants, local governments and local housing authorities that own or manage residential property, and mold assessment and remediation contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $125,000 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire a consultant to assist in developing regulations. State revenues are not affected. Local expenditures increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 for local governments and housing authorities that own or manage residential properties to meet assessment, remediation, and property maintenance standards, as well as for local code enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing a centralized website and informational pamphlet on mold, adopting comprehensive regulations by June 1, 2027 establishing uniform standards for mold assessment and remediation, and incurs a fiscal impact of $125,000 for contractual consultant assistance.

MDH is specifically mandated to coordinate with MDE to develop and update the centralized website and tenant mold informational pamphlet, and must be consulted during the promulgation of uniform mold assessment and remediation regulations.

DHCD is statutorily required to coordinate with MDE on developing the mold website and tenant pamphlet, and must be consulted by MDE in establishing the uniform standards and regulations for mold assessment and remediation in residential housing.

MD Labor is required to coordinate with MDE on the development of the centralized website and informational pamphlet, and administers the state's Minimum Livability Code referenced in the landlord maintenance requirements.

DGS is required to coordinate with MDE in developing the centralized website and informational pamphlet, as well as consult on the development of uniform standards and regulations for mold assessment, remediation, and building codes.

Repeals the mandated annual $99,000 appropriation for talent pipeline management. Requires the Program to award competitive workforce development grants or contracts beginning in fiscal year 2026. Expands eligible grant recipients to include employers, registered apprenticeship sponsors, local workforce boards, labor unions, and local governments. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $3,100,000 for the Fund in fiscal year 2026. Alters the composition of the Cyber Maryland Board and establishes new annual reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Cyber Maryland Board
stakeholders: Cybersecurity employers, job seekers, students, elementary and secondary schools, higher education institutions, registered apprenticeship sponsors, labor unions, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State net general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026, reflecting a $99,000 reduction for TEDCO and a $3.1 million increase for the Maryland Department of Labor. Potential increase in grant revenues for eligible local government entities and local workforce development boards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the Cyber Maryland Program, the Cyber Maryland Fund, and the Cyber Maryland Board from TEDCO to the Maryland Department of Labor, making it the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the program, issuing grants and contracts, and submitting required annual reports.

TEDCO currently houses and operates the Cyber Maryland Program and Fund; the bill transfers the program and associated funding out of TEDCO to MD Labor, while retaining the TEDCO CEO on the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Secretary of Information Technology serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the statutory purposes of the program include supporting DoIT to improve the State government's overall cybersecurity posture.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board is tasked with coordinating with the Department of Commerce on cybersecurity workforce and economic development efforts.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and program funds support initiatives specifically aimed at transitioning military veterans with cyber skills.
The State Superintendent of Schools is added as an ex-officio member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and elementary and secondary schools are eligible grant recipients under the Cyber Maryland Fund.
The Secretary of Higher Education is added to the Cyber Maryland Board, and institutions of higher education are eligible recipients for cybersecurity workforce development grants.
The Adjutant General (or designee) is added as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board to help advise on cybersecurity workforce and defense-related cyber capabilities.

The Governor is authorized to provide annual budget appropriations for the fund and program, appoints several members to the Cyber Maryland Board, and receives required annual reports on program operations and performance.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the special, nonlapsing Cyber Maryland Fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the Cyber Maryland Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State moneys.

bill_summary: Directs state agencies to coordinate cybersecurity planning, regulation, and assessments for community water and sewerage systems. Requires water and sewerage providers serving over 3,300 customers or using operational technology to adopt minimum cybersecurity standards. Mandates that these providers commit to a zero-trust model and complete biennial third-party cybersecurity maturity assessments by July 1, 2026. Requires all community water and sewerage providers to designate a cybersecurity contact, attend annual trainings, and report cyber incidents. Prohibits public inspection under the Public Information Act of records regarding operational technology or critical infrastructure security.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Information Technology; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: Community water system and community sewerage system providers, local emergency management organizations, certified waterworks and waste system operators, and cybersecurity service contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $271,700 in FY 2026 for one DoIT operational technology cybersecurity manager and MDEM contractual support, growing to $340,479 by FY 2030. Potential significant increase in local government expenditures beginning in FY 2026 for local water and sewerage systems to comply with standards, zero-trust implementation, and biennial third-party assessments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory agency responsible for coordinating cybersecurity efforts within community water and sewerage systems, updating regulations to establish cybersecurity standards, requiring incident reporting, approving training programs, and submitting progress reports to the General Assembly.

DoIT is assigned major operational and regulatory duties, including hiring an operational technology cybersecurity specialist, establishing cyber incident reporting protocols through the State Security Operations Center, collecting provider compliance certifications, and developing guidance documents.

MDEM and its Cyber Preparedness Unit are tasked with developing crisis and emergency risk communication guidance, assisting local emergency managers with water/wastewater cyber incident planning, and hosting annual tabletop cybersecurity exercises tailored to the water and wastewater sector.

As an independent state entity that manages and operates water and wastewater treatment facilities across Maryland, MES may be subject to the bill's cybersecurity standards, maturity assessments, zero-trust planning, and incident reporting requirements for systems it operates.

The bill amends the Maryland Public Information Act to shield records relating to operational technology and critical infrastructure security from public disclosure, affecting legal advice and PIA interpretation provided by the OAG.

bill_summary: Requires the Office of Social Equity to oversee the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund with assistance from the Comptroller. Repeals requirements for the Office to solicit public input and report annually on fund allocations. Allows local governments to dedicate up to 15% of received funds toward local administrative expenses. Requires each county to develop a distribution plan after consulting stakeholders and holding a public hearing. Mandates that counties hold distributions separately as special funds and submit annual implementation reports starting October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Office of Social Equity; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland counties, community-based organizations providing services in low-income or disproportionately impacted communities, and individuals and families in areas affected by historical cannabis prohibition enforcement
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Office of Social Equity increase by $65,986 in FY 2026 for a part-time administrator, funded by cannabis sales tax revenues redirected to the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund. Consequently, FY 2026 distributions decrease by $32,993 for the general fund, $23,095 for the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, and $3,299 for direct county allocations. Counties may retain up to 15% of fund distributions to cover administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Social Equity (OSE) is an independent office operating within the Maryland Cannabis Administration. The bill expands OSE's oversight responsibilities over the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, resulting in increased administrative expenditures funded through MCA's Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund.

The bill alters the administration of the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund from the Comptroller to the Executive Director of OSE, with the Comptroller providing assistance and continuing to account for the Fund and distribute cannabis sales and use tax revenues.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund separately and invest the money in the Fund in the same manner as other State money.
The Office of Social Equity must consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine which communities were most impacted by disproportionate enforcement of cannabis prohibition.
The bill explicitly maintains that the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, who administers the Fund and oversees its distribution.

The Department of Commerce administers the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which experiences a minor decrease in special fund revenue distributions due to increased administrative expenditures for OSE.

The Department of Health administers the Cannabis Public Health Fund, which sees a minor reduction in special fund tax revenue distributions as adult-use cannabis tax revenues are diverted to cover OSE administrative costs.

bill_summary: Establishes an extended producer responsibility program for packaging and paper products across Maryland. Requires covered producers to submit producer responsibility plans to the Department of the Environment by July 1, 2028. Prohibits selling or distributing covered materials without an approved producer responsibility plan on file. Directs producer responsibility organizations to reimburse registered service providers for collecting, transporting, and processing covered materials. Requires the Department to establish a statewide list of recyclable and compostable materials by July 1, 2027. Directs the Office of Recycling to conduct regular statewide recycling needs assessments funded by producer fees.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: producers and brand owners of packaging and paper products; producer responsibility organizations; local governments; waste and recycling service providers; materials recovery and composting facility operators
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $212,800 in FY 2026, rising to $572,322 in FY 2029 for Maryland Department of the Environment staffing and administration. Special fund revenues increase by $667,000 in FY 2026 from an initial assessment fee and match administrative costs in subsequent fiscal years via producer registration and oversight fees. Local government revenues increase beginning around FY 2029 through reimbursements for covered recycling and collection services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for overseeing the producer responsibility program, reviewing and approving producer responsibility plans, developing the statewide list of covered materials, adopting regulations, collecting fees, and enforcing compliance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the purpose, membership, and responsibilities of the Producer Responsibility Advisory Council, which provides input on producer responsibility plans, annual reports, and program implementation.

The Comptroller is statutorily designated under the bill to account for the State Recycling Trust Fund, including the separate account established for fees and penalties collected from producer responsibility organizations.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the State Recycling Trust Fund separately and invest the money in the fund, which receives fees and penalties established under the bill.

The OAG is responsible for prosecuting enforcement actions under the referenced statutory enforcement provisions (§§ 9-334 through 9-344) and is implicated by provisions providing immunity under State antitrust and trade restraint laws.
The bill requires the Department of the Environment's Office of Recycling to report the findings of statewide recycling needs assessments to the Governor.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to develop a list of similar boys' and girls' high school sports. Directs the Department and the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association to update this list every three years. Mandates that county boards of education ensure equal pay for officials in similar high school sports officiating roles. Requires county boards to reject procurement bids resulting in disparate pay or fees for similar sports. fiscal_impact_summary: State implementation can be handled with existing resources. Local school system expenditures increase in counties that must equalize pay for boys' and girls' sports officials, though total figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), in consultation with the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association, to develop and update every three years a list of similar boys' and girls' high school sports to ensure pay parity for sports officials across local school systems.

bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to pay identical commission rates to insurance producers for selling certain Medicare supplement policies. Applies this requirement regardless of whether a policy is underwritten or sold during an open enrollment period. Prohibits commission differences for policies issued within 30 days following an individual's birthday. Covers Medicare supplement policies sold to individuals at least 65 years old. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers selling Medicare supplement policies, licensed insurance producers, and Medicare-eligible individuals purchasing supplement coverage
fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive effect on State activities or operations and no local government fiscal effect. Small business insurance brokers that sell Medicare supplement policies may see increased commission earnings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance market, including Medicare supplement carriers and insurance producers, and is responsible for enforcing compliance with the state's insurance laws and commission requirements.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange was consulted as an information source regarding health insurance market impacts, though it does not directly regulate Medicare supplement policies or broker commissions.

bill_summary: Exempts any municipality with annual revenues of less than $100,000 from annual audit requirements for that fiscal year. Retains the requirement that exempt municipalities file an annual financial report with the Department of Legislative Services. Authorizes the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee to require an audit if the report indicates financial irregularities or concerns. Requires any mandated audit to be conducted by an approved certified public accountant.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee
stakeholders: Municipalities with annual revenues under $100,000
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Indeterminate minimal reduction in local government audit expenditures for the limited number of municipalities qualifying for the exemption; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies municipal audit requirements under § 16-305 of the Local Government Article, which the Legislative Auditor oversees. The Office of Legislative Audits reviews local government audit filings, grants four-year audit waivers under existing law, and retains authority to review or audit financial records.

bill_summary: Requires qualifying accommodations intermediaries to collect and remit local hotel rental taxes to the Comptroller instead of local governments. Applies this collection mandate to intermediaries facilitating at least $100,000 in gross transactions or 200 bookings annually. Directs the Comptroller to distribute monthly proceeds to local jurisdictions while retaining up to 1.5% for administrative costs. Prohibits counties and municipalities from imposing higher tax rates on short-term rental units than on other accommodations. Authorizes Howard County to increase its room rental tax cap from 7% to 8%. Increases the monthly late-payment interest rate in Garrett County and accelerates penalties in Talbot County.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Accommodations intermediaries, short-term rental platforms, accommodations providers, hotels, transient guests, and Maryland county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $1,264,815 in FY 2028 and $438,100 in FY 2030 for five administrative positions and computer programming expenses. Special fund revenues increase beginning in FY 2028 through a retained administrative fee of up to 1.5% of local hotel tax collections. County and municipal revenues may increase from centralized collection compliance, and Howard County revenues may increase by approximately $828,600 annually if the county exercises authority to raise its rate to 8%.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with establishing a centralized collection and remittance process for local hotel rental taxes from accommodations intermediaries, distributing revenues to local jurisdictions, conducting audits and investigations, and developing unified tax forms.

The Office of the Attorney General will provide legal counsel and litigation support for tax enforcement, audits, and appeals under the bill, including the staffing of an Assistant Attorney General position identified in the fiscal note.
The judicial branch may handle civil actions, enforcement of subpoenas, distraint proceedings, and judicial reviews of tax determinations initiated by the Comptroller or taxpayers.
The Maryland Tax Court may hear administrative appeals arising from hotel rental tax assessments, revisions, and refund determinations under Title 13 of the Tax - General Article.

Synopsis: Extending until the end of July 1, 2026, the expiration of an alcoholic beverages license issued for the 5700 block of Falls Road in Baltimore City for transfer and renewal purposes.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - License Extension
bill_summary: Extends the expiration of a Class B-D-7 alcoholic beverages license in Baltimore City. Applies specifically to a license issued for a premises on the 5700 block of Falls Road. Considers the license unexpired until the end of July 1, 2026. Authorizes the completion of an ownership transfer and license renewal at the same location. Takes effect July 1, 2025, and abrogates at the end of July 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: The license holder and prospective transferee of the Class B-D-7 alcoholic beverages license for the premises on the 5700 block of Falls Road in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and collecting related excise taxes. While this legislation specifically extends the expiration of a single local Class B-D-7 license administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it touches upon the broader statutory framework of alcoholic beverage regulation overseen at the state level.

bill_summary: Authorizes up to five highest-ranking officers of a specified nonprofit volunteer emergency medical organization to equip privately owned vehicles with lighting devices. Applies to organizations in Baltimore County or Baltimore City operating under Hatzalah of Baltimore's commercial ambulance service license. Permits equipped vehicles to have red or red and white lights or signal devices. Restricts the display of these devices exclusively to travel toward or presence at an emergency scene. Takes effect October 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Up to five highest-ranking officers of Hatzalah of Baltimore operating in Baltimore City and Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and does not directly affect Baltimore City or Baltimore County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law concerning vehicle lighting equipment and standards authorized by the Motor Vehicle Administrator under Section 22-218 of the Transportation Article.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which regulates vehicle equipment and operations under the Transportation Article.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing traffic and motor vehicle equipment laws on Maryland highways, including regulations governing unauthorized or authorized emergency vehicle lighting devices.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates emergency medical services and licenses commercial ambulance services in Maryland; the bill specifically applies to volunteer EMS officers operating under a commercial ambulance service license.

Synopsis: Increasing the percentage of beer not produced by the holder of a Class 5 brewery license that the license holder is permitted to sell for on-premises consumption if the holder also holds an applicable on-site consumption permit or a Class D license.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 5 Breweries - On-Premises Consumption
bill_summary: Increases the maximum percentage of certain off-site brewed beer that eligible Class 5 breweries may sell for on-premises consumption. Raises the sales allowance from 25% to 35% of total barrels sold on-premises in a calendar year. Applies to beer brewed off-site when owned or manufactured by the licensee or an affiliate. Maintains the alternative volume threshold of 1.2% of total finished production under the license. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; local licensing boards
stakeholders: Class 5 brewery license holders (specifically Open Gate Brewery in Baltimore County) and brewery patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and administering alcoholic beverage taxes and enforcement. This bill alters the regulations governing the on-premises sale and consumption of beer produced off-site by Class 5 brewery licensees.
